passages.vernacular: 「我以前聽過嗰個聲音,」福爾摩斯講,凝視住燈光昏暗嘅街道。「而家,我想知道嗰到底會係邊個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以前聽過那個聲音,」福爾摩斯說,凝視著燈光昏暗的街道。「現在,我想知道那到底會是誰。」

passages.original: I slept at Baker Street that night, and we were engaged upon our toast and coffee in the morning when the King of Bohemia rushed into the room.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上我瞓喺貝克街,朝早我哋正在食吐司、飲咖啡時,波希米亞國王衝進咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上我睡在貝克街,早上我們正在吃吐司、喝咖啡時,波希米亞國王衝進了房間。

passages.original: “You have really got it!” he cried, grasping Sherlock Holmes by either shoulder and looking eagerly into his face.
passages.vernacular: 「你真嘅攞到喇!」佢喊道,抓住夏洛克·福爾摩斯嘅雙肩,急切地睇住佢嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真的拿到了!」他喊道,抓住夏洛克·福爾摩斯的雙肩,急切地看著他的臉。

passages.original: “Not yet.”
passages.vernacular: 「仲冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還沒有。」

passages.original: “But you have hopes?”
passages.vernacular: 「但你有希望嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你有希望嗎?」

passages.original: “I have hopes.”
passages.vernacular: 「我有希望。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有希望。」

passages.original: “Then, come. I am all impatience to be gone.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就嚟吧。我迫不及待要走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就來吧。我迫不及待要走了。」

passages.original: “We must have a cab.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋得叫一輛出租馬車。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們得叫一輛出租馬車。」

passages.original: “No, my brougham is waiting.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔使,我嘅四輪馬車喺等住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不用,我的四輪馬車在等著。」

passages.original: “Then that will simplify matters.” We descended and started off once more for Briony Lodge.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就簡化事情喇。」我哋下樓,再次出發前往布里奧尼莊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就簡化事情了。」我們下樓,再次出發前往布里奧尼莊。

passages.original: “Irene Adler is married,” remarked Holmes.
passages.vernacular: 「艾琳·艾德勒結婚喇,」福爾摩斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「艾琳·艾德勒結婚了,」福爾摩斯說。

passages.original: “Married! When?”
passages.vernacular: 「結婚喇!乜嘢時候?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「結婚了!什麼時候?」

passages.original: “Yesterday.”
passages.vernacular: 「尋日。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「昨天。」

passages.original: “But to whom?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過嫁畀邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是嫁給誰?」

passages.original: “To an English lawyer named Norton.”
passages.vernacular: 「一個名叫諾頓嘅英國律師。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個名叫諾頓的英國律師。」

passages.original: “But she could not love him.”
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢唔可能愛佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是她不可能愛他。」

passages.original: “I am in hopes that she does.”
passages.vernacular: 「我希望佢愛佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望她愛他。」

passages.original: “And why in hopes?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解希望?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼希望?」

passages.original: “Because it would spare your Majesty all fear of future annoyance. If the lady loves her husband, she does not love your Majesty. If she does not love your Majesty, there is no reason why she should interfere with your Majesty’s plan.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為咁樣可以讓陛下免於對將來被騷擾嘅一切恐懼。如果呢位女士愛佢嘅丈夫,佢就不愛陛下。如果佢不愛陛下,佢就冇理由干涉陛下嘅計畫。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為這樣可以讓陛下免於對將來被騷擾的一切恐懼。如果這位女士愛她的丈夫,她就不愛陛下。如果她不愛陛下,她就沒有理由干涉陛下的計畫。」

passages.original: “It is true. And yet—! Well! I wish she had been of my own station! What a queen she would have made!” He relapsed into a moody silence, which was not broken until we drew up in Serpentine Avenue.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係真嘅。不過——!唉!我真希望佢同我同一地位!佢會成為幾咁出色嘅王后啊!」佢陷入憂鬱嘅沉默,直到我哋喺蛇形大道停下才打破。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是真的。可是——!唉!我真希望她與我同一地位!她會成為多麼出色的王后啊!」他陷入憂鬱的沉默,直到我們在蛇形大道停下才打破。

passages.original: The door of Briony Lodge was open, and an elderly woman stood upon the steps. She watched us with a sardonic eye as we stepped from the brougham.
passages.vernacular: 布里奧尼莊嘅門開住,一位年長嘅婦人站喺台階上。我哋從四輪馬車上下嚟時,佢以譏諷嘅眼神睇住我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布里奧尼莊的門開著,一位年長的婦人站在台階上。我們從四輪馬車上下來時,她以譏諷的眼神看著我們。

passages.original: “Mr. Sherlock Holmes, I believe?” said she.
passages.vernacular: 「我想係夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生吧?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生吧?」她說。

passages.original: “I am Mr. Holmes,” answered my companion, looking at her with a questioning and rather startled gaze.
passages.vernacular: 「我係福爾摩斯先生,」我嘅同伴回答,以疑問而頗為食驚嘅目光睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是福爾摩斯先生,」我的同伴回答,以疑問而頗為吃驚的目光看著她。

passages.original: “Indeed! My mistress told me that you were likely to call. She left this morning with her husband by the 5:15 train from Charing Cross for the Continent.”
passages.vernacular: 「果然!我嘅女主人告訴我您可能會嚟拜訪。佢今早同佢丈夫乘五點十五分從查令十字嘅火車,去歐洲大陸喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「果然!我的女主人告訴我您可能會來拜訪。她今早同她丈夫乘五點十五分從查令十字的火車,去歐洲大陸了。」

passages.original: “What!” Sherlock Holmes staggered back, white with chagrin and surprise. “Do you mean that she has left England?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢!」夏洛克·福爾摩斯踉蹌後退,又懊惱又食驚,臉色蒼白。「你係講佢已離開英國?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼!」夏洛克·福爾摩斯踉蹌後退,又懊惱又吃驚,臉色蒼白。「你是說她已離開英國?」

passages.original: “Never to return.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔再回嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不再回來了。」

passages.original: “And the papers?” asked the King hoarsely. “All is lost.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰啲文件呢?」國王嘶啞地問。「一切都完喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那些文件呢?」國王嘶啞地問。「一切都完了。」

passages.original: “We shall see.” He pushed past the servant and rushed into the drawing-room, followed by the King and myself. The furniture was scattered about in every direction, with dismantled shelves and open drawers, as if the lady had hurriedly ransacked them before her flight. Holmes rushed at the bell-pull, tore back a small sliding shutter, and, plunging in his hand, pulled out a photograph and a letter. The photograph was of Irene Adler herself in evening dress, the letter was superscribed to “Sherlock Holmes, Esq. To be left till called for.” My friend tore it open, and we all three read it together. It was dated at midnight of the preceding night and ran in this way:
passages.vernacular: 「我哋睇睇。」佢推開女僕,衝進客廳,國王同我跟喺後面。家具四處散亂,書架被拆開,抽屜敞開,好像嗰位女士逃走前匆忙洗劫過佢哋。福爾摩斯衝向拉鈴繩,扯開一小塊滑動護板,把手伸進去,取出一張照片同一封信。照片係艾琳·艾德勒本人穿住晚禮服嘅樣子,信嘅封面寫住「夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生收。待領。」我嘅朋友撕開信,我哋三人一起讀。信嘅日期係前一天晚上午夜,內容如下:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們看看。」他推開女僕,衝進客廳,國王和我跟在後面。家具四處散亂,書架被拆開,抽屜敞開,好像那位女士逃走前匆忙洗劫過它們。福爾摩斯衝向拉鈴繩,扯開一小塊滑動護板,把手伸進去,取出一張照片和一封信。照片是艾琳·艾德勒本人穿著晚禮服的樣子,信的封面寫著「夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生收。待領。」我的朋友撕開信,我們三人一起讀。信的日期是前一天晚上午夜,內容如下:

passages.original: “MY DEAR MR. SHERLOCK HOLMES,—You really did it very well. You took me in completely. Until after the alarm of fire, I had not a suspicion. But then, when I found how I had betrayed myself, I began to think. I had been warned against you months ago. I had been told that, if the King employed an agent, it would certainly be you. And your address had been given me. Yet, with all this, you made me reveal what you wanted to know. Even after I became suspicious, I found it hard to think evil of such a dear, kind old clergyman. But, you know, I have been trained as an actress myself. Male costume is nothing new to me. I often take advantage of the freedom which it gives. I sent John, the coachman, to watch you, ran upstairs, got into my walking clothes, as I call them, and came down just as you departed.
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生:你真嘅做得好漂亮。你完全騙過咗我。直到起火嘅警報之後,我都毫無懷疑。但後來,當我發現自己點樣暴露咗自己,我開始思考。幾個月前就有人警告過我提防你。有人告訴我,如果國王雇用一個代理人,嗰一定係你。而且你嘅地址都有人畀咗我。然而,儘管如此,你定係讓我顯露咗你想知道嘅嘢。即使我開始起疑之後,我仍好難對咁樣一位親切和藹嘅老牧師作壞嘅想像。但係,你知道,我自己都受過演員訓練。男裝對我並不新鮮。我常常利用佢所畀予嘅自由。我派車夫約翰去監視你,自己跑上樓,換上我稱為外出服嘅衣服,正好喺你離開時下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生:你真的做得很漂亮。你完全騙過了我。直到起火的警報之後,我都毫無懷疑。但後來,當我發現自己怎樣暴露了自己,我開始思考。幾個月前就有人警告過我提防你。有人告訴我,如果國王雇用一個代理人,那一定是你。而且你的地址也有人給了我。然而,儘管如此,你還是讓我顯露了你想知道的東西。即使我開始起疑之後,我仍很難對這樣一位親切和藹的老牧師作壞的想像。但是,你知道,我自己也受過演員訓練。男裝對我並不新鮮。我常常利用它所給予的自由。我派車夫約翰去監視你,自己跑上樓,換上我稱為外出服的衣服,正好在你離開時下來。

passages.original: “Well, I followed you to your door, and so made sure that I was really an object of interest to the celebrated Mr. Sherlock Holmes. Then I, rather imprudently, wished you good-night, and started for the Temple to see my husband.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,我跟住你到咗你嘅門口,咁樣便確定我確實係著名嘅夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生感興趣嘅對象。然後我相當輕率地向你道咗晚安,動身前往內殿去見我嘅丈夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,我跟著你到了你的門口,這樣便確定我確實是著名的夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生感興趣的對象。然後我相當輕率地向你道了晚安,動身前往內殿去見我的丈夫。

passages.original: “We both thought the best resource was flight, when pursued by so formidable an antagonist; so you will find the nest empty when you call to-morrow. As to the photograph, your client may rest in peace. I love and am loved by a better man than he. The King may do what he will without hindrance from one whom he has cruelly wronged. I keep it only to safeguard myself, and to preserve a weapon which will always secure me from any steps which he might take in the future. I leave a photograph which he might care to possess; and I remain, dear Mr. Sherlock Holmes,
passages.vernacular: 「我哋兩人都認為,面對咁樣厲害嘅對手追趕,最好嘅辦法就係逃走;所以你聽日嚟拜訪時,會發現巢已空喇。至於照片,你嘅委託人可以安心。我愛一個比佢更好嘅人,都被佢所愛。國王可以隨意行事,唔會受到佢曾殘酷虧待過嘅人嘅阻撓。我保留佢只係為了保護自己,並保留一件武器,使我永遠不受佢將來可能採取嘅任何措施嘅傷害。我留下一張佢或者想擁有嘅照片;我仍然係,親愛嘅夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們兩人都認為,面對這樣厲害的對手追趕,最好的辦法就是逃走;所以你明天來拜訪時,會發現巢已空了。至於照片,你的委託人可以安心。我愛一個比他更好的人,也被他所愛。國王可以隨意行事,不會受到他曾殘酷虧待過的人的阻撓。我保留它只是為了保護自己,並保留一件武器,使我永遠不受他將來可能採取的任何措施的傷害。我留下一張他也許想擁有的照片;我仍然是,親愛的夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生,

passages.original: “Very truly yours,
passages.vernacular: 「您真誠嘅,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您真誠的,

passages.original: “IRENE NORTON, née ADLER.”
passages.vernacular: 「艾琳·諾頓,原姓艾德勒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「艾琳·諾頓,原姓艾德勒。」

passages.original: “What a woman—oh, what a woman!” cried the King of Bohemia, when we had all three read this epistle. “Did I not tell you how quick and resolute she was? Would she not have made an admirable queen? Is it not a pity that she was not on my level?”
passages.vernacular: 「幾咁了不起嘅女人——哦,幾咁了不起嘅女人!」波希米亞國王喊道,我哋三人讀完呢封信之後。「我唔係告訴過你佢幾咁敏捷而堅決嗎?佢唔係會成為一位令人欽佩嘅王后嗎?佢唔係同我地位不同,真係可惜嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多麼了不起的女人——哦,多麼了不起的女人!」波希米亞國王喊道,我們三人讀完這封信之後。「我不是告訴過你她多麼敏捷而堅決嗎?她不是會成為一位令人欽佩的王后嗎?她不是與我地位不同,真是可惜嗎?」

passages.original: “From what I have seen of the lady, she seems, indeed, to be on a very different level to your Majesty,” said Holmes coldly. “I am sorry that I have not been able to bring your Majesty’s business to a more successful conclusion.”
passages.vernacular: 「從我對呢位女士所見嘅嚟睇,佢似乎確實同陛下處於一個好不同嘅層次,」福爾摩斯冷冷地講。「我好抱歉冇能把陛下嘅事辦得更成功。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從我對這位女士所見的來看,她似乎確實與陛下處於一個非常不同的層次,」福爾摩斯冷冷地說。「我很抱歉沒能把陛下的事辦得更成功。」

passages.original: “On the contrary, my dear sir,” cried the King; “nothing could be more successful. I know that her word is inviolate. The photograph is now as safe as if it were in the fire.”
passages.vernacular: 「恰恰相反,親愛嘅先生,」國王喊道;「冇乜嘢比呢更成功喇。我知道佢嘅話係不可違背嘅。照片而家就像放喺火裡一樣安全。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「恰恰相反,親愛的先生,」國王喊道;「沒有什麼比這更成功了。我知道她的話是不可違背的。照片現在就像放在火裡一樣安全。」

passages.original: “I am glad to hear your Majesty say so.”
passages.vernacular: 「聽陛下咁樣講我好高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽陛下這樣說我很高興。」

passages.original: “I am immensely indebted to you. Pray tell me in what way I can reward you. This ring—” He slipped an emerald snake ring from his finger and held it out upon the palm of his hand.
passages.vernacular: 「我對你感激不盡。請告訴我,我可以點樣酬謝你。呢枚戒指——」佢從手指上褪下一枚翡翠蛇形戒指,放喺手掌上伸出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我對你感激不盡。請告訴我,我可以怎樣酬謝你。這枚戒指——」他從手指上褪下一枚翡翠蛇形戒指,放在手掌上伸出來。

passages.original: “Your Majesty has something which I should value even more highly,” said Holmes.
passages.vernacular: 「陛下有一樣嘢,我會更加珍視,」福爾摩斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「陛下有一樣東西,我會更加珍視,」福爾摩斯說。

passages.original: “You have but to name it.”
passages.vernacular: 「你只需講出嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你只需說出來。」

passages.original: “This photograph!”
passages.vernacular: 「呢張照片!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這張照片!」

passages.original: The King stared at him in amazement.
passages.vernacular: 國王驚訝地瞪住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王驚訝地瞪著他。

passages.original: “Irene’s photograph!” he cried. “Certainly, if you wish it.”
passages.vernacular: 「艾琳嘅照片!」佢喊道。「當然,如果你想要嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「艾琳的照片!」他喊道。「當然,如果你想要的話。」

passages.original: “I thank your Majesty. Then there is no more to be done in the matter. I have the honour to wish you a very good morning.” He bowed, and, turning away without observing the hand which the King had stretched out to him, he set off in my company for his chambers.
passages.vernacular: 「我感謝陛下。咁呢件事就冇乜嘢要做嘅喇。謹祝您早安。」佢鞠咗一躬,轉身離去,冇注意到國王向佢伸出嘅手,同我一起動身回佢嘅寓所。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我感謝陛下。那麼這件事就沒有什麼要做的了。謹祝您早安。」他鞠了一躬,轉身離去,沒有注意到國王向他伸出的手,與我一起動身回他的寓所。

passages.original: And that was how a great scandal threatened to affect the kingdom of Bohemia, and how the best plans of Mr. Sherlock Holmes were beaten by a woman’s wit. He used to make merry over the cleverness of women, but I have not heard him do it of late. And when he speaks of Irene Adler, or when he refers to her photograph, it is always under the honourable title of the woman.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣,一樁大醜聞險些影響波希米亞王國,夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生嘅最佳計畫都被一個女人嘅機智所挫敗。佢以前常常嘲笑女人嘅聰明,但近來我冇再聽佢咁樣做。而當佢談到艾琳·艾德勒,或提到佢嘅照片時,總是用嗰個光榮嘅稱號:「嗰位女子」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣,一樁大醜聞險些影響波希米亞王國,夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生的最佳計畫也被一個女人的機智所挫敗。他以前常常嘲笑女人的聰明,但近來我沒有再聽他這樣做。而當他談到艾琳·艾德勒,或提到她的照片時,總是用那個光榮的稱號:「那位女子」。

passages.original: I had called upon my friend, Mr. Sherlock Holmes, one day in the autumn of last year and found him in deep conversation with a very stout, florid-faced, elderly gentleman with fiery red hair. With an apology for my intrusion, I was about to withdraw when Holmes pulled me abruptly into the room and closed the door behind me.
passages.vernacular: 去年秋天嘅一天,我去拜訪我嘅朋友夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生,發現佢正同一位好肥胖、面色紅潤、有住火紅頭髮嘅年長先生深談。我為打擾道咗歉,正要退出,福爾摩斯卻突然把我拉進房間,並喺我身後關上咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去年秋天的一天,我去拜訪我的朋友夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生,發現他正與一位非常肥胖、面色紅潤、有著火紅頭髮的年長先生深談。我為打擾道了歉,正要退出,福爾摩斯卻突然把我拉進房間,並在我身後關上了門。

passages.original: “You could not possibly have come at a better time, my dear Watson,” he said cordially.
passages.vernacular: 「你嚟得再好不過喇,親愛嘅華生,」佢親切地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你來得再好不過了,親愛的華生,」他親切地說。

passages.original: “I was afraid that you were engaged.”
passages.vernacular: 「我仲怕你有事呢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我還怕你有事呢。」

passages.original: “So I am. Very much so.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係有事。而且好忙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是有事。而且很忙。」

passages.original: “Then I can wait in the next room.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我可以喺隔壁房間等。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我可以在隔壁房間等。」

passages.original: “Not at all. This gentleman, Mr. Wilson, has been my partner and helper in many of my most successful cases, and I have no doubt that he will be of the utmost use to me in yours also.”
passages.vernacular: 「啲都唔使。呢位威爾遜先生,喺我最成功嘅許多案子裡都曾係我嘅夥伴同助手,我毫不懷疑佢對我處理你嘅案子都會有極大嘅用處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一點也不用。這位威爾遜先生,在我最成功的許多案子裡都曾是我的夥伴和助手,我毫不懷疑他對我處理你的案子也會有極大的用處。」

passages.original: The stout gentleman half rose from his chair and gave a bob of greeting, with a quick little questioning glance from his small fat-encircled eyes.
passages.vernacular: 嗰位肥胖嘅先生從椅子上半站起嚟,點咗點頭問候,佢嗰被脂肪圈住嘅小眼睛匆匆投嚟疑問嘅一瞥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位肥胖的先生從椅子上半站起來,點了點頭問候,他那被脂肪圈住的小眼睛匆匆投來疑問的一瞥。

passages.original: “Try the settee,” said Holmes, relapsing into his armchair and putting his fingertips together, as was his custom when in judicial moods. “I know, my dear Watson, that you share my love of all that is bizarre and outside the conventions and humdrum routine of everyday life. You have shown your relish for it by the enthusiasm which has prompted you to chronicle, and, if you will excuse my saying so, somewhat to embellish so many of my own little adventures.”
passages.vernacular: 「試試嗰張長椅吧,」福爾摩斯講,佢靠回扶手椅,把指尖合喺一起,呢個係佢處於斷案心情時嘅習慣。「我知道,親愛嘅華生,你同我一樣喜愛一切奇異嘅、超出日常生活常規同單調例行公事嘅事物。你嘅熱情促使你記錄,並且——恕我直言——有些仲加以潤飾我嘅許多小冒險,呢顯示咗你對此嘅喜愛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「試試那張長椅吧,」福爾摩斯說,他靠回扶手椅,把指尖合在一起,這是他處於斷案心情時的習慣。「我知道,親愛的華生,你同我一樣喜愛一切奇異的、超出日常生活常規和單調例行公事的事物。你的熱情促使你記錄,並且——恕我直言——有些還加以潤飾我的許多小冒險,這顯示了你對此的喜愛。」

passages.original: “Your cases have indeed been of the greatest interest to me,” I observed.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅案子對我確實好有趣,」我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的案子對我確實非常有趣,」我說。

passages.original: “You will remember that I remarked the other day, just before we went into the very simple problem presented by Miss Mary Sutherland, that for strange effects and extraordinary combinations we must go to life itself, which is always far more daring than any effort of the imagination.”
passages.vernacular: 「你會記得,前幾天,就喺我哋著手處理瑪麗·薩瑟蘭小姐提出嘅嗰個好簡單嘅問題之前,我講過,要找離奇嘅效果同不尋常嘅組合,我哋必須到生活本身中去,因為生活總是比任何想像力嘅努力都大膽得多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會記得,前幾天,就在我們著手處理瑪麗·薩瑟蘭小姐提出的那個很簡單的問題之前,我說過,要找離奇的效果和不尋常的組合,我們必須到生活本身中去,因為生活總是比任何想像力的努力都大膽得多。」

passages.original: “A proposition which I took the liberty of doubting.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個命題我冒昧地表示過懷疑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個命題我冒昧地表示過懷疑。」

passages.original: “You did, Doctor, but none the less you must come round to my view, for otherwise I shall keep on piling fact upon fact on you until your reason breaks down under them and acknowledges me to be right. Now, Mr. Jabez Wilson here has been good enough to call upon me this morning, and to begin a narrative which promises to be one of the most singular which I have listened to for some time. You have heard me remark that the strangest and most unique things are very often connected not with the larger but with the smaller crimes, and occasionally, indeed, where there is room for doubt whether any positive crime has been committed. As far as I have heard, it is impossible for me to say whether the present case is an instance of crime or not, but the course of events is certainly among the most singular that I have ever listened to. Perhaps, Mr. Wilson, you would have the great kindness to recommence your narrative. I ask you not merely because my friend Dr. Watson has not heard the opening part but also because the peculiar nature of the story makes me anxious to have every possible detail from your lips. As a rule, when I have heard some slight indication of the course of events, I am able to guide myself by the thousands of other similar cases which occur to my memory. In the present instance I am forced to admit that the facts are, to the best of my belief, unique.”
passages.vernacular: 「你確實懷疑過,醫生,但你終究必須接受我嘅觀點,否則我會不斷把事實堆喺你身上,直到你嘅理性喺佢哋下面崩潰,承認我係對嘅。而家,呢位賈貝茲·威爾遜先生今日早晨好心嚟拜訪我,開始講述一個好可能係我近來聽過嘅最奇特嘅故事。你聽我講過,最奇怪、最獨特嘅事物,往往同較小嘅罪行有關,而唔係同較大嘅罪行有關,而且有時確實同係咪真有犯罪都值得懷疑嘅情況有關。就我所聽到嘅,我無法講而家呢個案子係唔係犯罪嘅例子,但事件嘅經過肯定係我所聽過嘅最奇特嘅之一。威爾遜先生,或者你肯好心重新開始你嘅敘述。我請你咁樣做,不僅因為我嘅朋友華生醫生冇聽到開頭部分,仲因為呢個故事嘅特殊性質使我渴望從你口中得到每一個可能嘅細節。通常,當我聽到事件經過嘅啲輕微跡象時,我能憑記憶中浮現嘅成千上萬類似案例嚟指引自己。喺呢個案子裡,我唔得不承認,據我所信,事實係獨一無二嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你確實懷疑過,醫生,但你終究必須接受我的觀點,否則我會不斷把事實堆在你身上,直到你的理性在它們下面崩潰,承認我是對的。現在,這位賈貝茲·威爾遜先生今天早晨好心來拜訪我,開始講述一個很可能是我近來聽過的最奇特的故事。你聽我說過,最奇怪、最獨特的事物,往往與較小的罪行有關,而不是與較大的罪行有關,而且有時確實與是否真有犯罪都值得懷疑的情況有關。就我所聽到的,我無法說現在這個案子是不是犯罪的例子,但事件的經過肯定是我所聽過的最奇特的之一。威爾遜先生,也許你肯好心重新開始你的敘述。我請你這樣做,不僅因為我的朋友華生醫生沒有聽到開頭部分,還因為這個故事的特殊性質使我渴望從你口中得到每一個可能的細節。通常,當我聽到事件經過的一點輕微跡象時,我能憑記憶中浮現的成千上萬類似案例來指引自己。在這個案子裡,我不得不承認,據我所信,事實是獨一無二的。」

passages.original: The portly client puffed out his chest with an appearance of some little pride and pulled a dirty and wrinkled newspaper from the inside pocket of his greatcoat. As he glanced down the advertisement column, with his head thrust forward and the paper flattened out upon his knee, I took a good look at the man and endeavoured, after the fashion of my companion, to read the indications which might be presented by his dress or appearance.
passages.vernacular: 嗰位肥胖嘅委託人帶住啲驕傲嘅神氣挺起胸膛,從大衣嘅內袋裡掏出一張又髒又皺嘅報紙。佢把頭向前伸,報紙攤平放喺膝上,瀏覽住廣告欄,我趁機仔細打量呢個人,並學住我同伴嘅方式,試圖從佢嘅衣住或外表睇出些跡象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位肥胖的委託人帶著一點驕傲的神氣挺起胸膛,從大衣的內袋裡掏出一張又髒又皺的報紙。他把頭向前伸,報紙攤平放在膝上,瀏覽著廣告欄,我趁機仔細打量這個人,並學著我同伴的方式,試圖從他的衣著或外表看出些跡象。

passages.original: I did not gain very much, however, by my inspection. Our visitor bore every mark of being an average commonplace British tradesman, obese, pompous, and slow. He wore rather baggy grey shepherd’s check trousers, a not over-clean black frock-coat, unbuttoned in the front, and a drab waistcoat with a heavy brassy Albert chain, and a square pierced bit of metal dangling down as an ornament. A frayed top-hat and a faded brown overcoat with a wrinkled velvet collar lay upon a chair beside him. Altogether, look as I would, there was nothing remarkable about the man save his blazing red head, and the expression of extreme chagrin and discontent upon his features.
passages.vernacular: 不過我嘅觀察並冇得到太多收穫。我哋嘅訪客具備一個普通平庸嘅英國商人嘅一切特徵:肥胖、自負而遲鈍。佢穿一條相當寬鬆嘅灰色牧羊格子褲,一件不太乾淨嘅黑色長禮服外套,前面冇扣,仲有一件灰暗嘅背心,配住一條粗大嘅黃銅色艾伯特錶鏈,下面吊住一塊方形穿孔嘅金屬片作裝飾。一頂磨損嘅高帽同一件褪咗色嘅棕色大衣,帶住皺巴巴嘅天鵝絨領子,放喺佢身旁嘅椅子上。總而言之,不管我點睇,呢個人除咗火紅嘅頭髮同臉上極度懊惱不滿嘅表情之外,冇任何引人注目之處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我的觀察並沒有得到太多收穫。我們的訪客具備一個普通平庸的英國商人的一切特徵:肥胖、自負而遲鈍。他穿一條相當寬鬆的灰色牧羊格子褲,一件不太乾淨的黑色長禮服外套,前面沒有扣,還有一件灰暗的背心,配著一條粗大的黃銅色艾伯特錶鏈,下面吊著一塊方形穿孔的金屬片作裝飾。一頂磨損的高帽和一件褪了色的棕色大衣,帶著皺巴巴的天鵝絨領子,放在他身旁的椅子上。總而言之,不管我怎麼看,這個人除了火紅的頭髮和臉上極度懊惱不滿的表情之外,沒有任何引人注目之處。

passages.original: Sherlock Holmes’ quick eye took in my occupation, and he shook his head with a smile as he noticed my questioning glances. “Beyond the obvious facts that he has at some time done manual labour, that he takes snuff, that he is a Freemason, that he has been in China, and that he has done a considerable amount of writing lately, I can deduce nothing else.”
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯嘅敏銳眼睛睇到咗我嘅所作所為,佢注意到我疑問嘅眼神,微笑住搖咗搖頭。「除咗明顯嘅事實:佢曾喺某個時期做過體力勞動,佢吸鼻煙,佢係共濟會員,佢去過中國,而且最近寫咗好多嘢之外,我推論不出別嘅喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯的敏銳眼睛看到了我的所作所為,他注意到我疑問的眼神,微笑著搖了搖頭。「除了明顯的事實:他曾在某個時期做過體力勞動,他吸鼻煙,他是共濟會員,他去過中國,而且最近寫了很多東西之外,我推論不出別的了。」

passages.original: Mr. Jabez Wilson started up in his chair, with his forefinger upon the paper, but his eyes upon my companion.
passages.vernacular: 賈貝茲·威爾遜先生喺椅子上猛然一動,食指按喺報紙上,眼睛卻盯住我嘅同伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 賈貝茲·威爾遜先生在椅子上猛然一動,食指按在報紙上,眼睛卻盯著我的同伴。

passages.original: “How, in the name of good-fortune, did you know all that, Mr. Holmes?” he asked. “How did you know, for example, that I did manual labour. It’s as true as gospel, for I began as a ship’s carpenter.”
passages.vernacular: 「福爾摩斯先生,睇喺老天份上,你係點知道呢一切嘅?」佢問。「比如講,你點知道我做過體力勞動?呢千真萬確,因為我係從船上嘅木匠做起嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「福爾摩斯先生,看在老天份上,你是怎麼知道這一切的?」他問。「比如說,你怎麼知道我做過體力勞動?這千真萬確,因為我是從船上的木匠做起的。」

passages.original: “Your hands, my dear sir. Your right hand is quite a size larger than your left. You have worked with it, and the muscles are more developed.”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅手,親愛嘅先生。你嘅右手比左手大咗一號。你用佢幹過活,肌肉更發達。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的手,親愛的先生。你的右手比左手大了一號。你用它幹過活,肌肉更發達。」

passages.original: “Well, the snuff, then, and the Freemasonry?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁,鼻煙同共濟會呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,鼻煙和共濟會呢?」

passages.original: “I won’t insult your intelligence by telling you how I read that, especially as, rather against the strict rules of your order, you use an arc-and-compass breastpin.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔想用告訴你我係點睇出嚟嘅嚟侮辱你嘅智力,尤其係你違背咗你哋會所嘅嚴格規定,戴咗一枚弧形同圓規嘅胸針。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不想用告訴你我是怎麼看出來的來侮辱你的智力,尤其是你違背了你們會所的嚴格規定,戴了一枚弧形和圓規的胸針。」

passages.original: “Ah, of course, I forgot that. But the writing?”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,當然,我忘咗呢個。嗰寫作呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,當然,我忘了這個。那寫作呢?」

passages.original: “What else can be indicated by that right cuff so very shiny for five inches, and the left one with the smooth patch near the elbow where you rest it upon the desk?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰右邊嘅袖口有五英寸咁亮,而左邊嘅袖口喺你擱喺桌上嘅肘部附近有一塊光滑嘅地方,呢仲能講明別嘅乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那右邊的袖口有五英寸那麼亮,而左邊的袖口在你擱在桌上的肘部附近有一塊光滑的地方,這還能說明別的什麼?」

passages.original: “Well, but China?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,咁中國呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那麼中國呢?」

passages.original: “The fish that you have tattooed immediately above your right wrist could only have been done in China. I have made a small study of tattoo marks and have even contributed to the literature of the subject. That trick of staining the fishes’ scales of a delicate pink is quite peculiar to China. When, in addition, I see a Chinese coin hanging from your watch-chain, the matter becomes even more simple.”
passages.vernacular: 「你右手腕正上方紋嘅嗰條魚,只可能係喺中國紋嘅。我對紋身圖案做過啲研究,甚至為呢個題目的文獻作過貢獻。把魚鱗染成淡粉色嘅嗰種手法,係中國所特有嘅。此外,當我睇到你嘅錶鏈上掛住一枚中國銅錢,呢件事就更簡單喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你右手腕正上方紋的那條魚,只可能是在中國紋的。我對紋身圖案做過一點研究,甚至為這個題目的文獻作過貢獻。把魚鱗染成淡粉色的那種手法,是中國所特有的。此外,當我看到你的錶鏈上掛著一枚中國銅錢,這件事就更簡單了。」

passages.original: Mr. Jabez Wilson laughed heavily. “Well, I never!” said he. “I thought at first that you had done something clever, but I see that there was nothing in it after all.”
passages.vernacular: 賈貝茲·威爾遜先生沉重地笑喇。「哎呀,真冇想到!」佢講。「我起先以為你做咗乜嘢聰明嘅事,不過我睇出嚟其實都冇乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 賈貝茲·威爾遜先生沉重地笑了。「哎呀,真沒想到!」他說。「我起先以為你做了什麼聰明的事,可是我看出來其實也沒什麼。」

passages.original: “I begin to think, Watson,” said Holmes, “that I make a mistake in explaining. ‘Omne ignotum pro magnifico,’ you know, and my poor little reputation, such as it is, will suffer shipwreck if I am so candid. Can you not find the advertisement, Mr. Wilson?”
passages.vernacular: 「我開始覺得,華生,」福爾摩斯講,「我解釋係個錯誤。你知道,『凡未知者皆顯神奇』,如果我咁樣坦率,我嗰可憐嘅小名聲,不管佢係乜嘢,就要遭到船難喇。威爾遜先生,你找唔到嗰則廣告嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我開始覺得,華生,」福爾摩斯說,「我解釋是個錯誤。你知道,『凡未知者皆顯神奇』,如果我這樣坦率,我那可憐的小名聲,不管它是什麼,就要遭到船難了。威爾遜先生,你找不到那則廣告嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, I have got it now,” he answered with his thick red finger planted halfway down the column. “Here it is. This is what began it all. You just read it for yourself, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「找到喇,我而家找到喇,」佢回答,佢粗壯嘅紅手指按喺欄目中間。「喺呢兒。呢個就係一切嘅開始。先生,你自己讀吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「找到了,我現在找到了,」他回答,他粗壯的紅手指按在欄目中間。「在這兒。這就是一切的開始。先生,你自己讀吧。」

passages.original: I took the paper from him and read as follows:
passages.vernacular: 我從佢手裡接過報紙,讀到如下內容:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從他手裡接過報紙,讀到如下內容:

passages.original: “TO THE RED-HEADED LEAGUE: On account of the bequest of the late Ezekiah Hopkins, of Lebanon, Pennsylvania, U.S.A., there is now another vacancy open which entitles a member of the League to a salary of £ 4 a week for purely nominal services. All red-headed men who are sound in body and mind and above the age of twenty-one years, are eligible. Apply in person on Monday, at eleven o’clock, to Duncan Ross, at the offices of the League, 7 Pope’s Court, Fleet Street.”
passages.vernacular: 「致紅髮會:由於已故嘅美國賓夕法尼亞州黎巴嫩嘅以西結·霍普金斯嘅遺贈,現有一個新嘅空缺,使本會會員有權領取每週四英鎊嘅薪金,只需名義上嘅服務。所有身體同精神健全、年滿二十一歲嘅紅頭髮男子均有資格。請於星期一十啲親自前嚟,面見鄧肯·羅斯,地點為本會辦事處,艦隊街教皇院七號。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「致紅髮會:由於已故的美國賓夕法尼亞州黎巴嫩的以西結·霍普金斯的遺贈,現有一個新的空缺,使本會會員有權領取每週四英鎊的薪金,只需名義上的服務。所有身體和精神健全、年滿二十一歲的紅頭髮男子均有資格。請於星期一十一點親自前來,面見鄧肯·羅斯,地點為本會辦事處,艦隊街教皇院七號。」

passages.original: “What on earth does this mean?” I ejaculated after I had twice read over the extraordinary announcement.
passages.vernacular: 「呢到底係乜嘢意思?」我讀咗兩遍呢則非同尋常嘅廣告之後,脫口而出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這到底是什麼意思?」我讀了兩遍這則非同尋常的廣告之後,脫口而出。

passages.original: Holmes chuckled and wriggled in his chair, as was his habit when in high spirits. “It is a little off the beaten track, isn’t it?” said he. “And now, Mr. Wilson, off you go at scratch and tell us all about yourself, your household, and the effect which this advertisement had upon your fortunes. You will first make a note, Doctor, of the paper and the date.”
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯咯咯地笑住,喺椅子上扭動身子,呢個係佢心情特別好時嘅習慣。「呢有點離經叛道,係吧?」佢講。「而家,威爾遜先生,你從頭開始,告訴我哋你自己、你嘅家庭,以及呢則廣告對你嘅命運所產生嘅影響。醫生,你先記下報紙同日期。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯咯咯地笑著,在椅子上扭動身子,這是他心情特別好時的習慣。「這有點離經叛道,是吧?」他說。「現在,威爾遜先生,你從頭開始,告訴我們你自己、你的家庭,以及這則廣告對你的命運所產生的影響。醫生,你先記下報紙和日期。」

passages.original: “It is The Morning Chronicle of April 27, 1890. Just two months ago.”
passages.vernacular: 「係1890年4月27日嘅《晨報》。剛好兩個月前。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是1890年4月27日的《晨報》。剛好兩個月前。」

passages.original: “Very good. Now, Mr. Wilson?”
passages.vernacular: 「好好。而家,威爾遜先生,請講?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好。現在,威爾遜先生,請說?」

passages.original: “Well, it is just as I have been telling you, Mr. Sherlock Holmes,” said Jabez Wilson, mopping his forehead; “I have a small pawnbroker’s business at Coburg Square, near the City. It’s not a very large affair, and of late years it has not done more than just give me a living. I used to be able to keep two assistants, but now I only keep one; and I would have a job to pay him but that he is willing to come for half wages so as to learn the business.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,正如我一直喺告訴你嘅,夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生,」賈貝茲·威爾遜擦住前額講;「我喺城區附近嘅科堡廣場開咗一家小當鋪。佢唔係個好大嘅買賣,近年嚟只夠勉強維持我嘅生活。我以前能養兩個助手,而家只養一個;要唔係佢願意攞半薪嚟學呢行生意,我連佢都付不起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,正如我一直在告訴你的,夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生,」賈貝茲·威爾遜擦著前額說;「我在城區附近的科堡廣場開了一家小當鋪。它不是個很大的買賣,近年來只夠勉強維持我的生活。我以前能養兩個助手,現在只養一個;要不是他願意拿半薪來學這行生意,我連他都付不起。」

passages.original: “What is the name of this obliging youth?” asked Sherlock Holmes.
passages.vernacular: 「呢位樂於助人嘅青年叫乜嘢名字?」夏洛克·福爾摩斯問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這位樂於助人的青年叫什麼名字?」夏洛克·福爾摩斯問。

passages.original: “His name is Vincent Spaulding, and he’s not such a youth, either. It’s hard to say his age. I should not wish a smarter assistant, Mr. Holmes; and I know very well that he could better himself and earn twice what I am able to give him. But, after all, if he is satisfied, why should I put ideas in his head?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢叫文森特·斯波爾丁,而且佢都不算係青年。好難講佢嘅年齡。福爾摩斯先生,我唔想要一個更聰明嘅助手;我都好清楚,佢可以去找更好嘅工作,賺嘅錢係我能畀佢嘅兩倍。但係,畢竟,如果佢滿意,我點解要讓佢有別嘅念頭呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他叫文森特·斯波爾丁,而且他也不算是青年。很難說他的年齡。福爾摩斯先生,我不想要一個更聰明的助手;我也很清楚,他可以去找更好的工作,賺的錢是我能給他的兩倍。但是,畢竟,如果他滿意,我為什麼要讓他有別的念頭呢?」

passages.original: “Why, indeed? You seem most fortunate in having an employé who comes under the full market price. It is not a common experience among employers in this age. I don’t know that your assistant is not as remarkable as your advertisement.”
passages.vernacular: 「確實,點解呢?你似乎好幸運,有一個低於市場價格就肯受雇嘅雇員。喺呢個時代嘅雇主之間,呢唔係常見嘅經歷。我唔知道你嘅助手係咪不如你嘅廣告咁出色。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「確實,為什麼呢?你似乎很幸運,有一個低於市場價格就肯受雇的雇員。在這個時代的雇主之間,這不是常見的經歷。我不知道你的助手是否不如你的廣告那麼出色。」

passages.original: “Oh, he has his faults, too,” said Mr. Wilson. “Never was such a fellow for photography. Snapping away with a camera when he ought to be improving his mind, and then diving down into the cellar like a rabbit into its hole to develop his pictures. That is his main fault, but on the whole he’s a good worker. There’s no vice in him.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢都有佢嘅缺點,」威爾遜先生講。「從來冇人咁迷攝影。應該提高自己嘅頭腦時,卻攞住照相機啪啪啪地拍,然後像兔子鑽洞一樣鑽進地窖去沖洗照片。呢個係佢嘅主要缺點,但總嘅來講佢係個好工人。佢冇惡習。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,他也有他的缺點,」威爾遜先生說。「從來沒有人那麼迷攝影。應該提高自己的頭腦時,卻拿著照相機啪啪啪地拍,然後像兔子鑽洞一樣鑽進地窖去沖洗照片。這是他的主要缺點,但總的來說他是個好工人。他沒有惡習。」

passages.original: “He is still with you, I presume?”
passages.vernacular: 「我想佢仲喺你身邊吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想他還在你身邊吧?」

passages.original: “Yes, sir. He and a girl of fourteen, who does a bit of simple cooking and keeps the place clean—that’s all I have in the house, for I am a widower and never had any family. We live very quietly, sir, the three of us; and we keep a roof over our heads and pay our debts, if we do nothing more.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生。佢同一個十四歲嘅女孩,佢做些簡單嘅飯菜,把地方打掃乾淨——呢個就係我家裡所有嘅人,因為我係鰥夫,從來冇過家人。我哋過得好安靜,先生,我哋三個人;我哋有個遮頭嘅屋頂,仲清債務,雖然別嘅乜嘢都不做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生。他和一個十四歲的女孩,她做些簡單的飯菜,把地方打掃乾淨——這就是我家裡所有的人,因為我是鰥夫,從來沒有過家人。我們過得很安靜,先生,我們三個人;我們有個遮頭的屋頂,還清債務,雖然別的什麼都不做。

passages.original: “The first thing that put us out was that advertisement. Spaulding, he came down into the office just this day eight weeks, with this very paper in his hand, and he says:
passages.vernacular: 「第一件打亂我哋嘅事就係嗰則廣告。斯波爾丁,佢喺八個星期前嘅今日下到辦公室,手裡攞住呢同一份報紙,佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「第一件打亂我們的事就是那則廣告。斯波爾丁,他在八個星期前的今天下到辦公室,手裡拿著這同一份報紙,他說:

passages.original: “‘I wish to the Lord, Mr. Wilson, that I was a red-headed man.’
passages.vernacular: 「『老天,威爾遜先生,我真希望我係個紅頭髮嘅人。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『老天,威爾遜先生,我真希望我是個紅頭髮的人。』

passages.original: “‘Why that?’ I asks.
passages.vernacular: 「『點解?』我問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『為什麼?』我問。

passages.original: “‘Why,’ says he, ‘here’s another vacancy on the League of the Red-headed Men. It’s worth quite a little fortune to any man who gets it, and I understand that there are more vacancies than there are men, so that the trustees are at their wits’ end what to do with the money. If my hair would only change colour, here’s a nice little crib all ready for me to step into.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,』佢講,『紅髮會又有一個空缺。對得到呢個空缺嘅人來講,呢值一筆不小嘅財富,而且我知道,空缺比人仲多,所以受託人唔知道該點處理呢啲錢。要係我嘅頭髮能變顏色,呢兒就有個現成嘅好差事讓我去做。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,』他說,『紅髮會又有一個空缺。對得到這個空缺的人來說,這值一筆不小的財富,而且我知道,空缺比人還多,所以受託人不知道該怎麼處理這些錢。要是我的頭髮能變顏色,這兒就有個現成的好差事讓我去做。』

passages.original: “‘Why, what is it, then?’ I asked. You see, Mr. Holmes, I am a very stay-at-home man, and as my business came to me instead of my having to go to it, I was often weeks on end without putting my foot over the door-mat. In that way I didn’t know much of what was going on outside, and I was always glad of a bit of news.
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,嗰個係乜嘢?』我問。福爾摩斯先生,你要知道,我係個好宅嘅人,而且因為我嘅生意係客人上門,而唔係我出去找,所以我常常一連幾個星期都不跨出門墊一步。咁樣我對外面發生嘅事了解不多,總是好高興聽到啲消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,那是什麼?』我問。福爾摩斯先生,你要知道,我是個很宅的人,而且因為我的生意是客人上門,而不是我出去找,所以我常常一連幾個星期都不跨出門墊一步。這樣我對外面發生的事了解不多,總是很高興聽到一點消息。

passages.original: “‘Have you never heard of the League of the Red-headed Men?’ he asked with his eyes open.
passages.vernacular: 「『你從冇聽講過紅髮會嗎?』佢睜大眼睛問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你從沒聽說過紅髮會嗎?』他睜大眼睛問。

passages.original: “‘Never.’
“‘Why, I wonder at that, for you are eligible yourself for one of the vacancies.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哎呀,我好奇怪,因為你自己就有資格得到其中一個空缺。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哎呀,我很奇怪,因為你自己就有資格得到其中一個空缺。』

passages.original: “‘And what are they worth?’ I asked.
passages.vernacular: 「『嗰值多少錢?』我問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『那值多少錢?』我問。

passages.original: “‘Oh, merely a couple of hundred a year, but the work is slight, and it need not interfere very much with one’s other occupations.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,一年不過二百鎊左右,但工作好輕鬆,唔會好妨礙一個人嘅其他職業。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,一年不過二百鎊左右,但工作很輕鬆,不會很妨礙一個人的其他職業。』

passages.original: “Well, you can easily think that that made me prick up my ears, for the business has not been over good for some years, and an extra couple of hundred would have been very handy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你可以輕易想到,呢使我豎起耳朵,因為生意已經好幾年不太好喇,多出二百鎊會好方便。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你可以輕易想到,這使我豎起耳朵,因為生意已經好幾年不太好了,多出二百鎊會非常方便。

passages.original: “‘Tell me all about it,’ said I.
passages.vernacular: 「『都告訴我吧,』我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『都告訴我吧,』我說。

passages.original: “‘Well,’ said he, showing me the advertisement, ‘you can see for yourself that the League has a vacancy, and there is the address where you should apply for particulars. As far as I can make out, the League was founded by an American millionaire, Ezekiah Hopkins, who was very peculiar in his ways. He was himself red-headed, and he had a great sympathy for all red-headed men; so, when he died, it was found that he had left his enormous fortune in the hands of trustees, with instructions to apply the interest to the providing of easy berths to men whose hair is of that colour. From all I hear it is splendid pay and very little to do.’
passages.vernacular: 「『好吧,』佢講,畀我睇嗰則廣告,『你自己睇得出,本會有一個空缺,嗰兒有你該去詢問詳情嘅地址。據我所知,呢個協會係由一位美國百萬富翁以西結·霍普金斯創辦嘅,佢嘅行為好古怪。佢自己係紅頭髮,對所有紅頭髮嘅人都有極大同情;所以佢死後,人哋發現佢把巨額財產留畀咗受託人,吩咐佢哋用利息為頭髮係呢種顏色嘅人提供輕鬆嘅差事。據我所聽講,薪水極好,事情卻好少。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『好吧,』他說,給我看那則廣告,『你自己看得出,本會有一個空缺,那兒有你該去詢問詳情的地址。據我所知,這個協會是由一位美國百萬富翁以西結·霍普金斯創辦的,他的行為很古怪。他自己是紅頭髮,對所有紅頭髮的人都有極大同情;所以他死後,人們發現他把巨額財產留給了受託人,吩咐他們用利息為頭髮是這種顏色的人提供輕鬆的差事。據我所聽說,薪水極好,事情卻很少。』

passages.original: “‘But,’ said I, ‘there would be millions of red-headed men who would apply.’
passages.vernacular: 「『不過,』我講,『會有成百萬紅頭髮嘅人去申請嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『可是,』我說,『會有成百萬紅頭髮的人去申請的。』

passages.original: “‘Not so many as you might think,’ he answered. ‘You see it is really confined to Londoners, and to grown men. This American had started from London when he was young, and he wanted to do the old town a good turn. Then, again, I have heard it is no use your applying if your hair is light red, or dark red, or anything but real bright, blazing, fiery red. Now, if you cared to apply, Mr. Wilson, you would just walk in; but perhaps it would hardly be worth your while to put yourself out of the way for the sake of a few hundred pounds.’
passages.vernacular: 「『冇你想嘅咁多,』佢回答。『你睇,佢實際上只限於倫敦人,而且係成年男子。呢位美國人年輕時係從倫敦出發嘅,佢想為呢座老城做點好事。仲有,我聽講,如果你嘅頭髮係淺紅色,或深紅色,或任何唔係真正鮮亮、熾烈、火焰般嘅紅色,申請都冇用。而家,威爾遜先生,如果你想申請,你只管走進去就行;但或者為了幾百鎊而特地麻煩自己,不太值得。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『沒有你想的那麼多,』他回答。『你看,它實際上只限於倫敦人,而且是成年男子。這位美國人年輕時是從倫敦出發的,他想為這座老城做點好事。還有,我聽說,如果你的頭髮是淺紅色,或深紅色,或任何不是真正鮮亮、熾烈、火焰般的紅色,申請也沒用。現在,威爾遜先生,如果你想申請,你只管走進去就行;但也許為了幾百鎊而特地麻煩自己,不太值得。』

passages.original: “Now, it is a fact, gentlemen, as you may see for yourselves, that my hair is of a very full and rich tint, so that it seemed to me that if there was to be any competition in the matter I stood as good a chance as any man that I had ever met. Vincent Spaulding seemed to know so much about it that I thought he might prove useful, so I just ordered him to put up the shutters for the day and to come right away with me. He was very willing to have a holiday, so we shut the business up and started off for the address that was given us in the advertisement.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,先生哋,事實係,你哋可以自己睇出嚟,我嘅頭髮顏色好濃厚豐富,所以我覺得,如果呢件事要有任何競爭,我嘅機會不比我遇到過嘅任何人差。文森特·斯波爾丁似乎對呢件事知道得咁多,我想佢可能有用,所以就吩咐佢當天關上店門,即刻跟我一起去。佢好願意放假,於是我哋關咗店,動身前往廣告上畀嘅地址。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,先生們,事實是,你們可以自己看出來,我的頭髮顏色非常濃厚豐富,所以我覺得,如果這件事要有任何競爭,我的機會不比我遇到過的任何人差。文森特·斯波爾丁似乎對這件事知道得那麼多,我想他可能有用,所以就吩咐他當天關上店門,立刻跟我一起去。他非常願意放假,於是我們關了店,動身前往廣告上給的地址。

passages.original: “I never hope to see such a sight as that again, Mr. Holmes. From north, south, east, and west every man who had a shade of red in his hair had tramped into the city to answer the advertisement. Fleet Street was choked with red-headed folk, and Pope’s Court looked like a coster’s orange barrow. I should not have thought there were so many in the whole country as were brought together by that single advertisement. Every shade of colour they were—straw, lemon, orange, brick, Irish-setter, liver, clay; but, as Spaulding said, there were not many who had the real vivid flame-coloured tint. When I saw how many were waiting, I would have given it up in despair; but Spaulding would not hear of it. How he did it I could not imagine, but he pushed and pulled and butted until he got me through the crowd, and right up to the steps which led to the office. There was a double stream upon the stair, some going up in hope, and some coming back dejected; but we wedged in as well as we could and soon found ourselves in the office.”
passages.vernacular: 「福爾摩斯先生,我再都不指望睇到嗰樣嘅景象喇。從北面、南面、東面同西面,每一個頭髮帶有啲紅色嘅人都步行進城嚟應徵嗰則廣告。艦隊街被紅頭髮嘅人堵塞喇,教皇院睇起嚟像一輛賣橘子嘅小販手推車。我真冇想到全國有咁多紅頭髮嘅人,竟被嗰一則廣告聚集喺一起。各種顏色都有——稻草色、檸檬色、橙色、磚色、愛爾蘭塞特犬色、肝色、黏土色;但係,正如斯波爾丁所講,真正鮮明嘅火焰般顏色嘅人並不多。當我睇到有咁多人喺等,我本想絕望地放棄;但斯波爾丁完全不聽。我想像不出佢係點做到嘅,佢推、拉、頂,直到把我擠過人群,走到通往辦公室嘅台階前。樓梯上有兩股人流,有些人懷住希望往上走,有些人垂頭喪氣往下走;但我哋盡可能擠進去,好快就到咗辦公室。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「福爾摩斯先生,我再也不指望看到那樣的景象了。從北面、南面、東面和西面,每一個頭髮帶有一點紅色的人都步行進城來應徵那則廣告。艦隊街被紅頭髮的人堵塞了,教皇院看起來像一輛賣橘子的小販手推車。我真沒想到全國有那麼多紅頭髮的人,竟被那一則廣告聚集在一起。各種顏色都有——稻草色、檸檬色、橙色、磚色、愛爾蘭塞特犬色、肝色、黏土色;但是,正如斯波爾丁所說,真正鮮明的火焰般顏色的人並不多。當我看到有那麼多人在等,我本想絕望地放棄;但斯波爾丁完全不聽。我想像不出他是怎麼做到的,他推、拉、頂,直到把我擠過人群,走到通往辦公室的台階前。樓梯上有兩股人流,有些人懷著希望往上走,有些人垂頭喪氣往下走;但我們盡可能擠進去,很快就到了辦公室。」

passages.original: “Your experience has been a most entertaining one,” remarked Holmes as his client paused and refreshed his memory with a huge pinch of snuff. “Pray continue your very interesting statement.”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅經歷好有趣,」福爾摩斯喺佢嘅委託人停下嚟、用一大撮鼻煙嚟喚起記憶時講。「請繼續你呢個好有趣嘅陳述。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的經歷非常有趣,」福爾摩斯在他的委託人停下來、用一大撮鼻煙來喚起記憶時說。「請繼續你這非常有趣的陳述。」

passages.original: “There was nothing in the office but a couple of wooden chairs and a deal table, behind which sat a small man with a head that was even redder than mine. He said a few words to each candidate as he came up, and then he always managed to find some fault in them which would disqualify them. Getting a vacancy did not seem to be such a very easy matter, after all. However, when our turn came the little man was much more favourable to me than to any of the others, and he closed the door as we entered, so that he might have a private word with us.
passages.vernacular: 「辦公室裡除咗幾張木椅同一張杉木桌子之外乜嘢都冇,桌子後面坐住一個小個子,佢嘅頭髮甚至比我嘅仲要紅。佢喺每個應徵者上前時對佢講幾句話,然後總能喺佢哋身上找出啲缺點,使佢哋不合格。睇來,得到一個空缺畢竟唔係咁容易嘅事。不過,輪到我哋時,嗰個小個子對我比對其他任何人都友好得多,我哋一進去佢就關上咗門,以便同我哋私下講幾句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「辦公室裡除了幾張木椅和一張杉木桌子之外什麼也沒有,桌子後面坐著一個小個子,他的頭髮甚至比我的還要紅。他在每個應徵者上前時對他說幾句話,然後總能在他們身上找出一些缺點,使他們不合格。看來,得到一個空缺畢竟不是那麼容易的事。不過,輪到我們時,那個小個子對我比對其他任何人都友好得多,我們一進去他就關上了門,以便同我們私下說幾句話。

passages.original: “‘This is Mr. Jabez Wilson,’ said my assistant, ‘and he is willing to fill a vacancy in the League.’
passages.vernacular: 「『呢位係賈貝茲·威爾遜先生,』我嘅助手講,『佢願意填補協會嘅一個空缺。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『這位是賈貝茲·威爾遜先生,』我的助手說,『他願意填補協會的一個空缺。』

passages.original: “‘And he is admirably suited for it,’ the other answered. ‘He has every requirement. I cannot recall when I have seen anything so fine.’ He took a step backward, cocked his head on one side, and gazed at my hair until I felt quite bashful. Then suddenly he plunged forward, wrung my hand, and congratulated me warmly on my success.
passages.vernacular: 「『而且佢好合適,』另一人回答。『佢具備所有條件。我想不起乜嘢時候見過咁好嘅。』佢往後退一步,把頭歪向一邊,盯住我嘅頭髮睇,睇得我好不好意思。然後佢突然衝上嚟,緊握我嘅手,熱烈地祝賀我成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『而且他非常合適,』另一人回答。『他具備所有條件。我想不起什麼時候見過這麼好的。』他往後退一步,把頭歪向一邊,盯著我的頭髮看,看得我很不好意思。然後他突然衝上來,緊握我的手,熱烈地祝賀我成功。

passages.original: “‘It would be injustice to hesitate,’ said he. ‘You will, however, I am sure, excuse me for taking an obvious precaution.’ With that he seized my hair in both his hands, and tugged until I yelled with the pain. ‘There is water in your eyes,’ said he as he released me. ‘I perceive that all is as it should be. But we have to be careful, for we have twice been deceived by wigs and once by paint. I could tell you tales of cobbler’s wax which would disgust you with human nature.’ He stepped over to the window and shouted through it at the top of his voice that the vacancy was filled. A groan of disappointment came up from below, and the folk all trooped away in different directions until there was not a red-head to be seen except my own and that of the manager.
passages.vernacular: 「『猶豫就不公平喇,』佢講。『不過,我確信你會原諒我採取一個顯而易見嘅預防措施。』講住佢用雙手抓住我嘅頭髮,一直拉到我痛得喊叫起嚟。『你眼裡有淚水,』佢放開我時講。『我睇出一切都正常。但我哋必須小心,因為我哋曾兩次被假髮欺騙,一次被顏料欺騙。我可以畀你講些鞋匠蠟嘅故事,會使你厭惡人性。』佢走到窗邊,對住窗外用盡全力喊,空缺已經填補喇。樓下傳嚟一陣失望嘅呻吟,人哋朝不同方向成群散去,直到睇唔到一個紅頭髮,除咗我自己嘅同經理嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『猶豫就不公平了,』他說。『不過,我確信你會原諒我採取一個顯而易見的預防措施。』說著他用雙手抓住我的頭髮,一直拉到我痛得喊叫起來。『你眼裡有淚水,』他放開我時說。『我看出一切都正常。但我們必須小心,因為我們曾兩次被假髮欺騙,一次被顏料欺騙。我可以給你講些鞋匠蠟的故事,會使你厭惡人性。』他走到窗邊,對著窗外用盡全力喊,空缺已經填補了。樓下傳來一陣失望的呻吟,人們朝不同方向成群散去,直到看不到一個紅頭髮,除了我自己的和經理的。

passages.original: “‘My name,’ said he, ‘is Mr. Duncan Ross, and I am myself one of the pensioners upon the fund left by our noble benefactor. Are you a married man, Mr. Wilson? Have you a family?’
passages.vernacular: 「『我嘅名字,』佢講,『係鄧肯·羅斯先生,我自己都係我哋嗰位高貴嘅施主所留基金嘅領取人之一。威爾遜先生,你結婚咗嗎?有家庭嗎?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我的名字,』他說,『是鄧肯·羅斯先生,我自己也是我們那位高貴的施主所留基金的領取人之一。威爾遜先生,你結婚了嗎?有家庭嗎?』

passages.original: “I answered that I had not.
passages.vernacular: 「我回答講冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我回答說沒有。

passages.original: “His face fell immediately.
passages.vernacular: 「佢嘅臉即刻沉咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他的臉立刻沉了下來。

passages.original: “‘Dear me!’ he said gravely, ‘that is very serious indeed! I am sorry to hear you say that. The fund was, of course, for the propagation and spread of the red-heads as well as for their maintenance. It is exceedingly unfortunate that you should be a bachelor.’
passages.vernacular: 「『天呀!』佢嚴肅地講,『嗰真嘅好嚴重!聽你咁樣講我好抱歉。呢筆基金當然係為了紅頭髮者嘅繁衍同傳播,以及佢哋嘅生活費用。你偏偏係個單身漢,實在太不幸喇。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『天哪!』他嚴肅地說,『那真的非常嚴重!聽你這樣說我很抱歉。這筆基金當然是為了紅頭髮者的繁衍和傳播,以及他們的生活費用。你偏偏是個單身漢,實在太不幸了。』

passages.original: “My face lengthened at this, Mr. Holmes, for I thought that I was not to have the vacancy after all; but after thinking it over for a few minutes he said that it would be all right.
passages.vernacular: 「福爾摩斯先生,我聽咗呢話,臉拉長喇,因為我以為呢個空缺畢竟唔會係我嘅喇;但佢考慮咗幾分鐘之後講,咁樣都行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「福爾摩斯先生,我聽了這話,臉拉長了,因為我以為這個空缺畢竟不會是我的了;但他考慮了幾分鐘之後說,這樣也行。

passages.original: “‘In the case of another,’ said he, ‘the objection might be fatal, but we must stretch a point in favour of a man with such a head of hair as yours. When shall you be able to enter upon your new duties?’
passages.vernacular: 「『換咗別人,』佢講,『呢個反對理由可能係致命嘅,但對一個有您咁樣一頭頭髮嘅人,我哋必須通融一下。您乜嘢時候能開始履行您嘅新職責?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『換了別人,』他說,『這個反對理由可能是致命的,但對一個有您這樣一頭頭髮的人,我們必須通融一下。您什麼時候能開始履行您的新職責?』

passages.original: “‘Well, it is a little awkward, for I have a business already,’ said I.
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,有點不方便,因為我已經有一份生意喇,』我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,有點不方便,因為我已經有一份生意了,』我說。

passages.original: “‘Oh, never mind about that, Mr. Wilson!’ said Vincent Spaulding. ‘I should be able to look after that for you.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,唔使管嗰個,威爾遜先生!』文森特·斯波爾丁講。『我可以替您照睇嗰邊。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,不用管那個,威爾遜先生!』文森特·斯波爾丁說。『我可以替您照看那邊。』

passages.original: “‘What would be the hours?’ I asked.
passages.vernacular: 「『時間係點樣嘅?』我問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『時間是怎樣的?』我問。

passages.original: “‘Ten to two.’
passages.vernacular: 「『十點到兩點。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『十點到兩點。』

passages.original: “Now a pawnbroker’s business is mostly done of an evening, Mr. Holmes, especially Thursday and Friday evening, which is just before pay-day; so it would suit me very well to earn a little in the mornings. Besides, I knew that my assistant was a good man, and that he would see to anything that turned up.
passages.vernacular: 「福爾摩斯先生,當鋪嘅生意大多係喺晚上做嘅,尤其係星期四同星期五晚上,嗰正是發薪日之前;所以朝早賺點錢對我好合適。此外,我知道我嘅助手係個好人,有乜嘢事發生佢都會照料。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「福爾摩斯先生,當鋪的生意大多是在晚上做的,尤其是星期四和星期五晚上,那正是發薪日之前;所以早上賺點錢對我很合適。此外,我知道我的助手是個好人,有什麼事發生他都會照料。

passages.original: “‘That would suit me very well,’ said I. ‘And the pay?’
passages.vernacular: 「『呢對我好合適,』我講。『嗰報酬呢?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『這對我很合適,』我說。『那報酬呢?』

passages.original: “‘Is £ 4 a week.’
passages.vernacular: 「『每週四鎊。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『每週四鎊。』

passages.original: “‘And the work?’
passages.vernacular: 「『工作呢?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『工作呢?』

passages.original: “‘Is purely nominal.’
passages.vernacular: 「『純屬名義上嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『純屬名義上的。』

passages.original: “‘What do you call purely nominal?’
passages.vernacular: 「『你講嘅純屬名義上係乜嘢意思?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你說的純屬名義上是什麼意思?』

passages.original: “‘Well, you have to be in the office, or at least in the building, the whole time. If you leave, you forfeit your whole position forever. The will is very clear upon that point. You don’t comply with the conditions if you budge from the office during that time.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,您必須整段時間都待喺辦公室,或者至少待喺呢幢樓裡。如果您離開,就永遠失去您嘅職位。遺囑喺呢啲上好明確。如果喺嗰段時間內您從辦公室移開一步,就不符合條件。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,您必須整段時間都待在辦公室,或者至少待在這幢樓裡。如果您離開,就永遠失去您的職位。遺囑在這一點上很明確。如果在那段時間內您從辦公室移開一步,就不符合條件。』

passages.original: “‘It’s only four hours a day, and I should not think of leaving,’ said
passages.vernacular: 「『每天只有四小時,我絕唔會想到要離開嘅,』我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『每天只有四小時,我絕不會想到要離開的,』我說。

passages.original: “‘No excuse will avail,’ said Mr. Duncan Ross; ‘neither sickness nor business nor anything else. There you must stay, or you lose your billet.’
passages.vernacular: 「『任何藉口都冇用,』鄧肯·羅斯先生講;『不論生病、生意定係別嘅乜嘢。您必須待喺嗰度,否則就丟咗差事。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『任何藉口都沒用,』鄧肯·羅斯先生說;『不論生病、生意還是別的什麼。您必須待在那裡,否則就丟了差事。』

passages.original: “‘And the work?’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗰工作呢?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『那工作呢?』

passages.original: “‘Is to copy out the Encyclopædia Britannica. There is the first volume of it in that press. You must find your own ink, pens, and blotting-paper, but we provide this table and chair. Will you be ready to-morrow?’
passages.vernacular: 「『係抄寫《大英百科全書》。第一卷就喺嗰個櫃子裡。墨水、筆同吸墨紙您得自己準備,但呢張桌子同椅子由我哋提供。您聽日能準備好嗎?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『是抄寫《大英百科全書》。第一卷就在那個櫃子裡。墨水、筆和吸墨紙您得自己準備,但這張桌子和椅子由我們提供。您明天能準備好嗎?』

passages.original: “‘Certainly,’ I answered.
passages.vernacular: 「『當然,』我回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『當然,』我回答。

passages.original: “‘Then, good-bye, Mr. Jabez Wilson, and let me congratulate you once more on the important position which you have been fortunate enough to gain.’ He bowed me out of the room and I went home with my assistant, hardly knowing what to say or do, I was so pleased at my own good fortune.
passages.vernacular: 「『咁再見,賈貝茲·威爾遜先生,讓我再次祝賀您幸運地得到咗呢個重要職位。』佢鞠躬送我出房間,我同我嘅助手回家,高興得幾乎唔知道該講乜嘢、做乜嘢,為我自己嘅好運而歡喜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『那麼再見,賈貝茲·威爾遜先生,讓我再次祝賀您幸運地得到了這個重要職位。』他鞠躬送我出房間,我同我的助手回家,高興得幾乎不知道該說什麼、做什麼,為我自己的好運而歡喜。

passages.original: “Well, I thought over the matter all day, and by evening I was in low spirits again; for I had quite persuaded myself that the whole affair must be some great hoax or fraud, though what its object might be I could not imagine. It seemed altogether past belief that anyone could make such a will, or that they would pay such a sum for doing anything so simple as copying out the Encyclopædia Britannica. Vincent Spaulding did what he could to cheer me up, but by bedtime I had reasoned myself out of the whole thing. However, in the morning I determined to have a look at it anyhow, so I bought a penny bottle of ink, and with a quill-pen, and seven sheets of foolscap paper, I started off for Pope’s Court.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我整天思考呢件事,到傍晚我又情緒低落喇;因為我已經完全講服自己,整件事一定係個大騙局或詐騙,雖然我想像不出佢嘅目的係乜嘢。似乎完全令人難以置信,居然有人立下咁樣嘅遺囑,或者願意付咁一筆錢,只做抄寫《大英百科全書》咁樣簡單嘅事。文森特·斯波爾丁盡力使我振作,但到瞓覺時我已用推理講服自己放棄整件事。不過,早晨我決定無論如何去睇一睇,於是買咗一便士嘅墨水,帶住一支羽毛筆同七張大張稿紙,動身前往教皇院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我整天思考這件事,到傍晚我又情緒低落了;因為我已經完全說服自己,整件事一定是個大騙局或詐騙,雖然我想像不出它的目的是什麼。似乎完全令人難以置信,居然有人立下這樣的遺囑,或者願意付這麼一筆錢,只做抄寫《大英百科全書》這樣簡單的事。文森特·斯波爾丁盡力使我振作,但到睡覺時我已用推理說服自己放棄整件事。不過,早晨我決定無論如何去看一看,於是買了一便士的墨水,帶著一支羽毛筆和七張大張稿紙,動身前往教皇院。

passages.original: “Well, to my surprise and delight, everything was as right as possible. The table was set out ready for me, and Mr. Duncan Ross was there to see that I got fairly to work. He started me off upon the letter A, and then he left me; but he would drop in from time to time to see that all was right with me. At two o’clock he bade me good-day, complimented me upon the amount that I had written, and locked the door of the office after me.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,令我又驚又喜嘅係,一切都盡可能地正常。桌子已為我擺好,鄧肯·羅斯先生喺嗰度,睇我公平地開始工作。佢讓我從字母A開始,然後離開咗我;但佢時不時會進嚟睇睇我一切係咪正常。兩點鐘佢向我道別,稱讚我寫嘅數量,並喺我身後鎖上辦公室嘅門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,令我又驚又喜的是,一切都盡可能地正常。桌子已為我擺好,鄧肯·羅斯先生在那裡,看我公平地開始工作。他讓我從字母A開始,然後離開了我;但他時不時會進來看看我一切是否正常。兩點鐘他向我道別,稱讚我寫的數量,並在我身後鎖上辦公室的門。

passages.original: “This went on day after day, Mr. Holmes, and on Saturday the manager came in and planked down four golden sovereigns for my week’s work. It was the same next week, and the same the week after. Every morning I was there at ten, and every afternoon I left at two. By degrees Mr. Duncan Ross took to coming in only once of a morning, and then, after a time, he did not come in at all. Still, of course, I never dared to leave the room for an instant, for I was not sure when he might come, and the billet was such a good one, and suited me so well, that I would not risk the loss of it.
passages.vernacular: 「福爾摩斯先生,咁樣一天又一天地過去,星期六經理進嚟,把四個金索維林砰地放下,作為我一週嘅工作報酬。下週都係如此,再下一週都一樣。每天早晨我十點到嗰度,每天下午兩點離開。漸漸地,鄧肯·羅斯先生變成每個早晨只嚟一次,然後過咗一段時間,佢乾脆不嚟喇。當然,我始終唔敢離開房間一瞬間,因為我不確定佢乜嘢時候會嚟,而且呢份差事咁好,咁適合我,我唔願冒失去佢嘅風險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「福爾摩斯先生,這樣一天又一天地過去,星期六經理進來,把四個金索維林砰地放下,作為我一週的工作報酬。下週也是如此,再下一週也一樣。每天早晨我十點到那裡,每天下午兩點離開。漸漸地,鄧肯·羅斯先生變成每個早晨只來一次,然後過了一段時間,他乾脆不來了。當然,我始終不敢離開房間一瞬間,因為我不確定他什麼時候會來,而且這份差事那麼好,那麼適合我,我不願冒失去它的風險。

passages.original: “Eight weeks passed away like this, and I had written about Abbots and Archery and Armour and Architecture and Attica, and hoped with diligence that I might get on to the B’s before very long. It cost me something in foolscap, and I had pretty nearly filled a shelf with my writings. And then suddenly the whole business came to an end.”
passages.vernacular: 「八個星期就咁樣過去喇,我寫咗修道院長、射箭、盔甲、建築同阿提卡,並且希望勤奮啲,不久就可以寫到B。呢花咗我啲大張稿紙嘅費用,而且我寫嘅嘢差不多堆滿咗一個書架。然後突然間,整件事結束喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「八個星期就這樣過去了,我寫了修道院長、射箭、盔甲、建築和阿提卡,並且希望勤奮一點,不久就可以寫到B。這花了我一點大張稿紙的費用,而且我寫的東西差不多堆滿了一個書架。然後突然間,整件事結束了。」

passages.original: “To an end?”
passages.vernacular: 「結束喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「結束了?」

passages.original: “Yes, sir. And no later than this morning. I went to my work as usual at ten o’clock, but the door was shut and locked, with a little square of cardboard hammered on to the middle of the panel with a tack. Here it is, and you can read for yourself.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生。就喺今日朝早。我照常十點去上班,但門關住而且鎖住,門板中央用一枚圖釘釘住一小塊方形硬紙板。就喺呢兒,你可以自己讀。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生。就在今天早上。我照常十點去上班,但門關著而且鎖著,門板中央用一枚圖釘釘著一小塊方形硬紙板。就在這兒,你可以自己讀。」

passages.original: He held up a piece of white cardboard about the size of a sheet of note-paper. It read in this fashion:
passages.vernacular: 佢舉起一塊白色嘅硬紙板,大小像一張信紙。上面係咁樣寫嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他舉起一塊白色的硬紙板,大小像一張信紙。上面是這樣寫的:

passages.original: “THE RED-HEADED LEAGUE IS DISSOLVED. October 9, 1890.”
passages.vernacular: 「紅髮會已解散。1890年10月9日。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「紅髮會已解散。1890年10月9日。」

passages.original: Sherlock Holmes and I surveyed this curt announcement and the rueful face behind it, until the comical side of the affair so completely overtopped every other consideration that we both burst out into a roar of laughter.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯同我審視住呢句簡短嘅通告,同佢後面嗰張憂傷嘅臉,直到事情滑稽嘅一面完全壓倒咗其他一切考慮,我哋兩個都爆發出一陣大笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯和我審視著這句簡短的通告,和它後面那張憂傷的臉,直到事情滑稽的一面完全壓倒了其他一切考慮,我們兩個都爆發出一陣大笑。

passages.original: “I cannot see that there is anything very funny,” cried our client, flushing up to the roots of his flaming head. “If you can do nothing better than laugh at me, I can go elsewhere.”
passages.vernacular: 「我睇不出有乜嘢好笑嘅,」我哋嘅委託人喊道,臉紅到佢嗰火紅頭髮嘅根部。「如果你除咗笑我之外冇更好嘅辦法,我可以去別處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看不出有什麼好笑的,」我們的委託人喊道,臉紅到他那火紅頭髮的根部。「如果你除了笑我之外沒有更好的辦法,我可以去別處。」

passages.original: “No, no,” cried Holmes, shoving him back into the chair from which he had half risen. “I really wouldn’t miss your case for the world. It is most refreshingly unusual. But there is, if you will excuse my saying so, something just a little funny about it. Pray what steps did you take when you found the card upon the door?”
passages.vernacular: 「不,不,」福爾摩斯喊道,把佢推回佢剛半站起嚟嘅椅子上。「我真嘅無論如何都唔會錯過你嘅案子。佢係令人耳目一新嘅不尋常。但係,恕我直言,其中有啲點滑稽。請問你發現門上嘅卡片後採取咗乜嘢行動?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不,」福爾摩斯喊道,把他推回他剛半站起來的椅子上。「我真的無論如何都不會錯過你的案子。它是令人耳目一新的不尋常。但是,恕我直言,其中有一點點滑稽。請問你發現門上的卡片後採取了什麼行動?」

passages.original: “I was staggered, sir. I did not know what to do. Then I called at the offices round, but none of them seemed to know anything about it. Finally, I went to the landlord, who is an accountant living on the ground floor, and I asked him if he could tell me what had become of the Red-headed League. He said that he had never heard of any such body. Then I asked him who Mr. Duncan Ross was. He answered that the name was new to him.
passages.vernacular: 「我嚇呆喇,先生。我唔知道該點算。然後我拜訪咗周圍嘅辦事處,但似乎冇一個知道呢件事。最後,我去找房東,佢係住喺一樓嘅會計師,我問佢能唔能夠告訴我紅髮會點喇。佢講佢從冇聽講過任何咁樣嘅團體。然後我問佢鄧肯·羅斯先生係邊個。佢回答講呢個名字佢冇聽過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我嚇呆了,先生。我不知道該怎麼辦。然後我拜訪了周圍的辦事處,但似乎沒有一個知道這件事。最後,我去找房東,他是住在一樓的會計師,我問他能不能告訴我紅髮會怎麼了。他說他從沒聽說過任何這樣的團體。然後我問他鄧肯·羅斯先生是誰。他回答說這個名字他沒聽過。

passages.original: “‘Well,’ said I, ‘the gentleman at No. 4.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,』我講,『四號嘅嗰位先生。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,』我說,『四號的那位先生。』

passages.original: “‘What, the red-headed man?’
passages.vernacular: 「『乜嘢,嗰個紅頭髮嘅人?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『什麼,那個紅頭髮的人?』

passages.original: “‘Yes.’
“‘Oh,’ said he, ‘his name was William Morris. He was a solicitor and was using my room as a temporary convenience until his new premises were ready. He moved out yesterday.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,』佢講,『佢嘅名字叫威廉·莫里斯。佢係個事務律師,臨時借用我嘅房間,等佢嘅新辦公室準備好。佢尋日搬走喇。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,』他說,『他的名字叫威廉·莫里斯。他是個事務律師,臨時借用我的房間,等他的新辦公室準備好。他昨天搬走了。』

passages.original: “‘Where could I find him?’
passages.vernacular: 「『我喺邊度能找到佢?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我在哪裡能找到他?』

passages.original: “‘Oh, at his new offices. He did tell me the address. Yes, 17 King Edward Street, near St. Paul’s.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,喺佢嘅新辦事處。佢確實告訴過我地址。對,聖保羅教堂附近嘅愛德華國王街十七號。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,在他的新辦事處。他確實告訴過我地址。對,聖保羅教堂附近的愛德華國王街十七號。』

passages.original: “I started off, Mr. Holmes, but when I got to that address it was a manufactory of artificial knee-caps, and no one in it had ever heard of either Mr. William Morris or Mr. Duncan Ross.”
passages.vernacular: 「福爾摩斯先生,我出發喇,但到咗嗰個地址,嗰個係一家製造人工膝蓋骨嘅工廠,裡面冇人聽講過威廉·莫里斯先生或鄧肯·羅斯先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「福爾摩斯先生,我出發了,但到了那個地址,那是一家製造人工膝蓋骨的工廠,裡面沒有人聽說過威廉·莫里斯先生或鄧肯·羅斯先生。」

passages.original: “And what did you do then?” asked Holmes.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你後來做咗乜嘢?」福爾摩斯問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你後來做了什麼?」福爾摩斯問。

passages.original: “I went home to Saxe-Coburg Square, and I took the advice of my assistant. But he could not help me in any way. He could only say that if I waited I should hear by post. But that was not quite good enough, Mr. Holmes. I did not wish to lose such a place without a struggle, so, as I had heard that you were good enough to give advice to poor folk who were in need of it, I came right away to you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我回到薩克斯-科堡廣場嘅家,聽取我助手嘅建議。但佢無法以任何方式幫我。佢只能講,如果我等住,我會收到郵件。但福爾摩斯先生,嗰仲唔夠好。我唔願不經一番掙扎就失去咁樣嘅職位,所以,由於聽講你好心畀需要嘅窮人提供建議,我就即刻嚟找你喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我回到薩克斯-科堡廣場的家,聽取我助手的建議。但他無法以任何方式幫我。他只能說,如果我等著,我會收到郵件。但福爾摩斯先生,那還不夠好。我不願不經一番掙扎就失去這樣的職位,所以,由於聽說你好心給需要的窮人提供建議,我就立刻來找你了。」

passages.original: “And you did very wisely,” said Holmes. “Your case is an exceedingly remarkable one, and I shall be happy to look into it. From what you have told me I think that it is possible that graver issues hang from it than might at first sight appear.”
passages.vernacular: 「你做得好明智,」福爾摩斯講。「你嘅案子極不尋常,我好樂意調查。根據你所告訴我嘅,我認為呢件事有可能牽涉到比乍睇之下更嚴重嘅問題。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你做得非常明智,」福爾摩斯說。「你的案子極不尋常,我很樂意調查。根據你所告訴我的,我認為這件事有可能牽涉到比乍看之下更嚴重的問題。」

passages.original: “Grave enough!” said Mr. Jabez Wilson. “Why, I have lost four pound a week.”
passages.vernacular: 「夠嚴重嘅喇!」賈貝茲·威爾遜先生講。「哎呀,我每週損失咗四鎊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夠嚴重的了!」賈貝茲·威爾遜先生說。「哎呀,我每週損失了四鎊。」

passages.original: “As far as you are personally concerned,” remarked Holmes, “I do not see that you have any grievance against this extraordinary league. On the contrary, you are, as I understand, richer by some £ 30, to say nothing of the minute knowledge which you have gained on every subject which comes under the letter A. You have lost nothing by them.”
passages.vernacular: 「就你個人而言,」福爾摩斯講,「我睇不出你對呢個奇特嘅協會有乜嘢可抱怨嘅。相反,據我所知,你富咗大約三十鎊,更唔使講你喺以字母A開頭嘅每一個題目上所獲得嘅詳盡知識。你冇因佢哋而損失任何嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就你個人而言,」福爾摩斯說,「我看不出你對這個奇特的協會有什麼可抱怨的。相反,據我所知,你富了大約三十鎊,更不用說你在以字母A開頭的每一個題目上所獲得的詳盡知識。你沒有因他們而損失任何東西。」

passages.original: “No, sir. But I want to find out about them, and who they are, and what their object was in playing this prank—if it was a prank—upon me. It was a pretty expensive joke for them, for it cost them two and thirty pounds.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,先生。但我想弄清楚佢哋係邊個,以及佢哋對我開呢個玩笑——如果係玩笑嘅話——嘅目的係乜嘢。呢對佢哋來講係個相當昂貴嘅玩笑,因為佢花咗佢哋三十二鎊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,先生。但我想弄清楚他們是誰,以及他們對我開這個玩笑——如果是玩笑的話——的目的是什麼。這對他們來說是個相當昂貴的玩笑,因為它花了他們三十二鎊。」

passages.original: “We shall endeavour to clear up these points for you. And, first, one or two questions, Mr. Wilson. This assistant of yours who first called your attention to the advertisement—how long had he been with you?”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋會努力為你弄清呢幾點。首先,威爾遜先生,有一兩個問題。你呢位首先使你注意到廣告嘅助手——佢跟你有多久喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們會努力為你弄清這幾點。首先,威爾遜先生,有一兩個問題。你這位首先使你注意到廣告的助手——他跟你有多久了?」

passages.original: “About a month then.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰時大約一個月。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那時大約一個月。」

passages.original: “How did he come?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係點樣嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是怎樣來的?」

passages.original: “In answer to an advertisement.”
passages.vernacular: 「回應一則廣告。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「回應一則廣告。」

passages.original: “Was he the only applicant?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係唯一嘅應徵者嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是唯一的應徵者嗎?」

passages.original: “No, I had a dozen.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,我有十幾個應徵者。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我有十幾個應徵者。」

passages.original: “Why did you pick him?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點解挑佢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼挑他?」

passages.original: “Because he was handy and would come cheap.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為佢手腳靈便,而且肯攞低薪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為他手腳靈便,而且肯拿低薪。」

passages.original: “At half wages, in fact.”
passages.vernacular: 「實際上係半薪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「實際上是半薪。」

passages.original: “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。」

passages.original: “What is he like, this Vincent Spaulding?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個文森特·斯波爾丁長乜嘢樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個文森特·斯波爾丁長什麼樣?」

passages.original: “Small, stout-built, very quick in his ways, no hair on his face, though he’s not short of thirty. Has a white splash of acid upon his forehead.”
passages.vernacular: 「個子小,體格結實,動作好敏捷,臉上冇鬍子,雖然佢不止三十歲。額頭上有一塊酸液燒嘅白斑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「個子小,體格結實,動作很敏捷,臉上沒有鬍子,雖然他不止三十歲。額頭上有一塊酸液燒的白斑。」

passages.original: Holmes sat up in his chair in considerable excitement. “I thought as much,” said he. “Have you ever observed that his ears are pierced for earrings?”
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯喺椅子上興奮地坐直喇。「我就料到係咁樣,」佢講。「你有冇注意到佢嘅耳朵穿咗耳環孔?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯在椅子上興奮地坐直了。「我就料到是這樣,」他說。「你有沒有注意到他的耳朵穿了耳環孔?」

passages.original: “Yes, sir. He told me that a gipsy had done it for him when he was a lad.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生。佢告訴我係佢小時候一個吉普賽人畀佢穿嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生。他告訴我是他小時候一個吉普賽人給他穿的。」

passages.original: “Hum!” said Holmes, sinking back in deep thought. “He is still with you?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯!」福爾摩斯講,陷入沉思中。「佢仲喺你嗰度嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯!」福爾摩斯說,陷入沉思中。「他還在你那裡嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, sir; I have only just left him.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,先生;我剛離開佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,先生;我剛離開他。」

passages.original: “And has your business been attended to in your absence?”
passages.vernacular: 「你不喺嘅時候,你嘅生意有人照料嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不在的時候,你的生意有人照料嗎?」

passages.original: “Nothing to complain of, sir. There’s never very much to do of a morning.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇乜嘢可抱怨嘅,先生。早晨從來冇好多事做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒什麼可抱怨的,先生。早晨從來沒有很多事做。」

passages.original: “That will do, Mr. Wilson. I shall be happy to give you an opinion upon the subject in the course of a day or two. To-day is Saturday, and I hope that by Monday we may come to a conclusion.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢就夠喇,威爾遜先生。我好樂意喺一兩天內就呢個問題畀你一個意見。今日係星期六,我希望到星期一我哋就能得出結論。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就夠了,威爾遜先生。我很樂意在一兩天內就這個問題給你一個意見。今天是星期六,我希望到星期一我們就能得出結論。」

passages.original: “Well, Watson,” said Holmes when our visitor had left us, “what do you make of it all?”
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,華生,」福爾摩斯喺我哋嘅訪客離開後講,「你點睇呢一切?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,華生,」福爾摩斯在我們的訪客離開後說,「你怎麼看這一切?」

passages.original: “I make nothing of it,” I answered frankly. “It is a most mysterious business.”
passages.vernacular: 「我乜嘢都睇不出嚟,」我坦率地回答。「呢個係樁最神秘嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我什麼也看不出來,」我坦率地回答。「這是樁最神秘的事。」

passages.original: “As a rule,” said Holmes, “the more bizarre a thing is the less mysterious it proves to be. It is your commonplace, featureless crimes which are really puzzling, just as a commonplace face is the most difficult to identify. But I must be prompt over this matter.”
passages.vernacular: 「一般來講,」福爾摩斯講,「一件事越奇特,佢就越不神秘。真正令人困惑嘅係嗰啲平淡無奇、冇特徵嘅罪行,正如平凡嘅臉最難辨認。但我必須對呢件事迅速行動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一般來說,」福爾摩斯說,「一件事越奇特,它就越不神秘。真正令人困惑的是那些平淡無奇、沒有特徵的罪行,正如平凡的臉最難辨認。但我必須對這件事迅速行動。」

passages.original: “What are you going to do, then?” I asked.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你打算做乜嘢?」我問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你打算做什麼?」我問。

passages.original: “To smoke,” he answered. “It is quite a three pipe problem, and I beg that you won’t speak to me for fifty minutes.” He curled himself up in his chair, with his thin knees drawn up to his hawk-like nose, and there he sat with his eyes closed and his black clay pipe thrusting out like the bill of some strange bird. I had come to the conclusion that he had dropped asleep, and indeed was nodding myself, when he suddenly sprang out of his chair with the gesture of a man who has made up his mind and put his pipe down upon the mantelpiece.
passages.vernacular: 「抽煙,」佢回答。「呢個係個要抽三斗煙嘅問題,我請求你喺五好鐘內唔好同我講話。」佢喺椅子上蜷成一團,瘦削嘅膝蓋抵到佢鷹鉤似嘅鼻子,就嗰樣閉住眼睛坐住,黑色嘅陶土煙斗像某種奇怪鳥類嘅喙一樣伸出嚟。我得出結論,佢瞓住喇,而我自己都喺打盹,呢陣佢突然從椅子上跳起嚟,帶住下定決心嘅人嘅姿態,把煙斗放喺壁爐台上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「抽煙,」他回答。「這是個要抽三斗煙的問題,我請求你在五十分鐘內不要同我說話。」他在椅子上蜷成一團,瘦削的膝蓋抵到他鷹鉤似的鼻子,就那樣閉著眼睛坐著,黑色的陶土煙斗像某種奇怪鳥類的喙一樣伸出來。我得出結論,他睡著了,而我自己也在打盹,這時他突然從椅子上跳起來,帶著下定決心的人的姿態,把煙斗放在壁爐台上。

passages.original: “Sarasate plays at the St. James’s Hall this afternoon,” he remarked. “What do you think, Watson? Could your patients spare you for a few hours?”
passages.vernacular: 「薩拉薩泰今日下午喺聖詹姆斯大廳演奏,」佢講。「華生,你覺得呢?你嘅病人能放你幾個小時嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「薩拉薩泰今天下午在聖詹姆斯大廳演奏,」他說。「華生,你覺得呢?你的病人能放你幾個小時嗎?」

passages.original: “I have nothing to do to-day. My practice is never very absorbing.”
passages.vernacular: 「我今日冇事。我嘅診所從來不太忙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我今天沒事。我的診所從來不太忙。」

passages.original: “Then put on your hat and come. I am going through the City first, and we can have some lunch on the way. I observe that there is a good deal of German music on the programme, which is rather more to my taste than Italian or French. It is introspective, and I want to introspect. Come along!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就戴上帽子嚟吧。我先要穿過倫敦城,我哋可以喺路上食點午飯。我注意到節目單上有好多德國音樂,比意大利或法國音樂更合我嘅口味。佢係內省嘅,而我想內省。走吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就戴上帽子來吧。我先要穿過倫敦城,我們可以在路上吃點午飯。我注意到節目單上有很多德國音樂,比意大利或法國音樂更合我的口味。它是內省的,而我想內省。走吧!」

passages.original: We travelled by the Underground as far as Aldersgate; and a short walk took us to Saxe-Coburg Square, the scene of the singular story which we had listened to in the morning. It was a poky, little, shabby-genteel place, where four lines of dingy two-storied brick houses looked out into a small railed-in enclosure, where a lawn of weedy grass and a few clumps of faded laurel bushes made a hard fight against a smoke-laden and uncongenial atmosphere. Three gilt balls and a brown board with “JABEZ WILSON” in white letters, upon a corner house, announced the place where our red-headed client carried on his business. Sherlock Holmes stopped in front of it with his head on one side and looked it all over, with his eyes shining brightly between puckered lids. Then he walked slowly up the street, and then down again to the corner, still looking keenly at the houses. Finally he returned to the pawnbroker’s, and, having thumped vigorously upon the pavement with his stick two or three times, he went up to the door and knocked. It was instantly opened by a bright-looking, clean-shaven young fellow, who asked him to step in.
passages.vernacular: 我哋乘地鐵到奧爾德斯蓋特;走咗一小段路就到咗薩克斯-科堡廣場,就係我哋朝早聽到嘅嗰個奇特故事發生嘅地方。嗰個係個狹小、破舊而裝腔作勢嘅地方,四排灰暗嘅兩層磚房朝向一個小小嘅有欄杆嘅圍場,裡面係長滿雜草嘅草坪同幾叢褪色嘅月桂樹,喺煙霧瀰漫、令人不快嘅空氣中艱難地掙扎。一個角落房子上掛住三個鍍金球同一塊棕色嘅牌子,上面用白字寫住「賈貝茲·威爾遜」,表明我哋嗰位紅頭髮嘅委託人做生意嘅地方。夏洛克·福爾摩斯喺佢前面停下,把頭歪向一邊,眯住眼,眼睛喺皺起嘅眼皮之間明亮地閃住,把佢全部打量咗一番。然後佢慢慢沿街走上去,又走下到街角,仍然銳利地睇住嗰啲房子。最後佢回到當鋪,用手杖喺人行道上用力敲咗兩三下,然後走到門前敲門。門立即被一個神采奕奕、臉刮得乾乾淨淨嘅年輕人打開,佢請佢進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們乘地鐵到奧爾德斯蓋特;走了一小段路就到了薩克斯-科堡廣場,就是我們早上聽到的那個奇特故事發生的地方。那是個狹小、破舊而裝腔作勢的地方,四排灰暗的兩層磚房朝向一個小小的有欄杆的圍場,裡面是長滿雜草的草坪和幾叢褪色的月桂樹,在煙霧瀰漫、令人不快的空氣中艱難地掙扎。一個角落房子上掛著三個鍍金球和一塊棕色的牌子,上面用白字寫著「賈貝茲·威爾遜」,表明我們那位紅頭髮的委託人做生意的地方。夏洛克·福爾摩斯在它前面停下,把頭歪向一邊,眯著眼,眼睛在皺起的眼皮之間明亮地閃著,把它全部打量了一番。然後他慢慢沿街走上去,又走下到街角,仍然銳利地看著那些房子。最後他回到當鋪,用手杖在人行道上用力敲了兩三下,然後走到門前敲門。門立即被一個神采奕奕、臉刮得乾乾淨淨的年輕人打開,他請他進去。

passages.original: “Thank you,” said Holmes, “I only wished to ask you how you would go from here to the Strand.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝,」福爾摩斯講,「我只想問您,從呢度點去河濱路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝,」福爾摩斯說,「我只想問您,從這裡怎麼去河濱路。」

passages.original: “Third right, fourth left,” answered the assistant promptly, closing the door.
passages.vernacular: 「第三條右轉,第四條左轉,」助手即刻回答,關上咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「第三條右轉,第四條左轉,」助手立刻回答,關上了門。

passages.original: “Smart fellow, that,” observed Holmes as we walked away. “He is, in my judgment, the fourth smartest man in London, and for daring I am not sure that he has not a claim to be third. I have known something of him before.”
passages.vernacular: 「聰明嘅傢伙,」我哋走開時,福爾摩斯講。「依我判斷,佢係倫敦第四聰明嘅人,若論膽量,我不確定佢冇資格排第三。我以前對佢有些了解。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聰明的傢伙,」我們走開時,福爾摩斯說。「依我判斷,他是倫敦第四聰明的人,若論膽量,我不確定他沒有資格排第三。我以前對他有些了解。」

passages.original: “Evidently,” said I, “Mr. Wilson’s assistant counts for a good deal in this mystery of the Red-headed League. I am sure that you inquired your way merely in order that you might see him.”
passages.vernacular: 「顯然,」我講,「威爾遜先生嘅助手喺呢個紅髮會之謎中好重要。我肯定你問路只係為了睇佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「顯然,」我說,「威爾遜先生的助手在這個紅髮會之謎中很重要。我肯定你問路只是為了看他。」

passages.original: “Not him.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係睇佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是看他。」

passages.original: “What then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼?」

passages.original: “The knees of his trousers.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢褲子嘅膝蓋部分。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他褲子的膝蓋部分。」

passages.original: “And what did you see?”
passages.vernacular: 「你睇見咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看見了什麼?」

passages.original: “What I expected to see.”
passages.vernacular: 「我預料會睇見嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我預料會看見的東西。」

passages.original: “Why did you beat the pavement?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點解敲人行道?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼敲人行道?」

passages.original: “My dear doctor, this is a time for observation, not for talk. We are spies in an enemy’s country. We know something of Saxe-Coburg Square. Let us now explore the parts which lie behind it.”
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅醫生,呢個係觀察嘅時候,唔係講話嘅時候。我哋係敵國裡嘅間諜。我哋對薩克斯-科堡廣場已有些了解。而家讓我哋探索佢後面嘅部分。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的醫生,這是觀察的時候,不是說話的時候。我們是敵國裡的間諜。我們對薩克斯-科堡廣場已有些了解。現在讓我們探索它後面的部分。」

passages.original: The road in which we found ourselves as we turned round the corner from the retired Saxe-Coburg Square presented as great a contrast to it as the front of a picture does to the back. It was one of the main arteries which conveyed the traffic of the City to the north and west. The roadway was blocked with the immense stream of commerce flowing in a double tide inward and outward, while the footpaths were black with the hurrying swarm of pedestrians. It was difficult to realise as we looked at the line of fine shops and stately business premises that they really abutted on the other side upon the faded and stagnant square which we had just quitted.
passages.vernacular: 我哋從呢個隱蔽嘅薩克斯-科堡廣場轉過街角,所嚟到嘅呢條路同佢形成強烈對比,就像一幅畫嘅正面對背面。佢係把倫敦城嘅交通運往北面同西面嘅主要幹道之一。路面被大量商業車流堵塞,往內往外兩股潮水流動,而人行道上則擠滿咗匆匆嘅行人,一片漆黑。睇住嗰一排精美嘅商店同堂皇嘅商業建築,好難想像佢哋嘅另一面確實就緊靠住我哋剛離開嘅嗰個褪色而停滯嘅廣場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們從這個隱蔽的薩克斯-科堡廣場轉過街角,所來到的這條路與它形成強烈對比,就像一幅畫的正面對背面。它是把倫敦城的交通運往北面和西面的主要幹道之一。路面被大量商業車流堵塞,往內往外兩股潮水流動,而人行道上則擠滿了匆匆的行人,一片漆黑。看著那一排精美的商店和堂皇的商業建築,很難想像它們的另一面確實就緊靠著我們剛離開的那個褪色而停滯的廣場。

passages.original: “Let me see,” said Holmes, standing at the corner and glancing along the line, “I should like just to remember the order of the houses here. It is a hobby of mine to have an exact knowledge of London. There is Mortimer’s, the tobacconist, the little newspaper shop, the Coburg branch of the City and Suburban Bank, the Vegetarian Restaurant, and McFarlane’s carriage-building depot. That carries us right on to the other block. And now, Doctor, we’ve done our work, so it’s time we had some play. A sandwich and a cup of coffee, and then off to violin-land, where all is sweetness and delicacy and harmony, and there are no red-headed clients to vex us with their conundrums.”
passages.vernacular: 「讓我想想,」福爾摩斯站喺街角,沿住一排房子睇去,講,「我只想記住呢度房子嘅次序。準確了解倫敦係我嘅一種愛好。呢度有莫蒂默嘅煙草店、小報攤、城市及郊區銀行嘅科堡分行、素食餐廳,同麥克法倫嘅馬車製造倉庫。呢就一直連到另一排。而家,醫生,我哋工作做完喇,係時候玩一玩喇。一個三明治同一杯咖啡,然後去小提琴嘅國度,嗰度一切都係甜美、細膩同和諧,冇紅頭髮嘅委託人嚟用謎題嚟煩我哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我想想,」福爾摩斯站在街角,沿著一排房子看去,說,「我只想記住這裡房子的次序。準確了解倫敦是我的一種愛好。這裡有莫蒂默的煙草店、小報攤、城市及郊區銀行的科堡分行、素食餐廳,和麥克法倫的馬車製造倉庫。這就一直連到另一排。現在,醫生,我們工作做完了,是時候玩一玩了。一個三明治和一杯咖啡,然後去小提琴的國度,那裡一切都是甜美、細膩與和諧,沒有紅頭髮的委託人來用謎題來煩我們。」

passages.original: My friend was an enthusiastic musician, being himself not only a very capable performer but a composer of no ordinary merit. All the afternoon he sat in the stalls wrapped in the most perfect happiness, gently waving his long, thin fingers in time to the music, while his gently smiling face and his languid, dreamy eyes were as unlike those of Holmes the sleuth-hound, Holmes the relentless, keen-witted, ready-handed criminal agent, as it was possible to conceive. In his singular character the dual nature alternately asserted itself, and his extreme exactness and astuteness represented, as I have often thought, the reaction against the poetic and contemplative mood which occasionally predominated in him. The swing of his nature took him from extreme languor to devouring energy; and, as I knew well, he was never so truly formidable as when, for days on end, he had been lounging in his armchair amid his improvisations and his black-letter editions. Then it was that the lust of the chase would suddenly come upon him, and that his brilliant reasoning power would rise to the level of intuition, until those who were unacquainted with his methods would look askance at him as on a man whose knowledge was not that of other mortals. When I saw him that afternoon so enwrapped in the music at St. James’s Hall I felt that an evil time might be coming upon those whom he had set himself to hunt down.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅朋友係個熱情嘅音樂家,佢自己不僅係好能幹嘅演奏者,而且係個作曲水準不凡嘅作曲家。整個下午佢坐喺前排座位上,沉浸喺最完美嘅幸福中,修長瘦削嘅手指隨住音樂輕輕揮動,佢溫和微笑嘅臉同慵懶夢幻嘅眼睛,同偵探犬般嘅福爾摩斯、無情、機智敏銳、動作迅速嘅罪犯追捕者福爾摩斯,所能想像嘅相差之大,無以復加。喺佢獨特嘅性格中,雙重本性交替地表現出嚟,我常想,佢極端嘅準確同精明,代表咗對偶爾佔上風嘅詩意同沉思情緒嘅反作用。佢天性嘅擺動使佢從極端嘅倦怠走向吞噬一切嘅精力;而且我好清楚,佢從來冇像連續幾天喺扶手椅上懶散度日、沉浸喺即興曲同黑體字版書籍中之後嗰樣真正令人畏懼。呢陣追獵嘅欲望會突然降臨到佢身上,佢輝煌嘅推理能力會上升到直覺嘅水平,以致不了解他方法嘅人會斜眼睇佢,像睇一個其知識不屬於凡人嘅人。當我嗰天下午睇到佢咁樣被聖詹姆斯大廳嘅音樂所包裹,我覺得嗰啲被佢決心追捕嘅人,一個厄運嘅時刻可能要降臨喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的朋友是個熱情的音樂家,他自己不僅是非常能幹的演奏者,而且是個作曲水準不凡的作曲家。整個下午他坐在前排座位上,沉浸在最完美的幸福中,修長瘦削的手指隨著音樂輕輕揮動,他溫和微笑的臉和慵懶夢幻的眼睛,與偵探犬般的福爾摩斯、無情、機智敏銳、動作迅速的罪犯追捕者福爾摩斯,所能想像的相差之大,無以復加。在他獨特的性格中,雙重本性交替地表現出來,我常想,他極端的準確和精明,代表了對偶爾佔上風的詩意與沉思情緒的反作用。他天性的擺動使他從極端的倦怠走向吞噬一切的精力;而且我很清楚,他從來沒有像連續幾天在扶手椅上懶散度日、沉浸在即興曲和黑體字版書籍中之後那樣真正令人畏懼。這時追獵的欲望會突然降臨到他身上,他輝煌的推理能力會上升到直覺的水平,以致不了解他方法的人會斜眼看他,像看一個其知識不屬於凡人的人。當我那天下午看到他這樣被聖詹姆斯大廳的音樂所包裹,我覺得那些被他決心追捕的人,一個厄運的時刻可能要降臨了。

passages.original: “You want to go home, no doubt, Doctor,” he remarked as we emerged.
passages.vernacular: 「你想回家,無疑,醫生,」我哋走出嚟時佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想回家,無疑,醫生,」我們走出來時他說。

passages.original: “Yes, it would be as well.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,咁樣都好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,這樣也好。」

passages.original: “And I have some business to do which will take some hours. This business at Coburg Square is serious.”
passages.vernacular: 「而我有些事要辦,要花幾個小時。科堡廣場呢件事係嚴重嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而我有些事要辦,要花幾個小時。科堡廣場這件事是嚴重的。」

passages.original: “Why serious?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解嚴重?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼嚴重?」

passages.original: “A considerable crime is in contemplation. I have every reason to believe that we shall be in time to stop it. But to-day being Saturday rather complicates matters. I shall want your help to-night.”
passages.vernacular: 「有一件重大嘅罪行正在醞釀。我有充分理由相信我哋嚟得及阻止佢。但今日係星期六,事情就稍微複雜喇。今晚我需要你嘅幫助。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一件重大的罪行正在醞釀。我有充分理由相信我們來得及阻止它。但今天是星期六,事情就稍微複雜了。今晚我需要你的幫助。」

passages.original: “At what time?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢時候?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼時候?」

passages.original: “Ten will be early enough.”
passages.vernacular: 「十點就夠早喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「十點就夠早了。」

passages.original: “I shall be at Baker Street at ten.”
passages.vernacular: 「我十點會到貝克街。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我十點會到貝克街。」

passages.original: “Very well. And, I say, Doctor, there may be some little danger, so kindly put your army revolver in your pocket.” He waved his hand, turned on his heel, and disappeared in an instant among the crowd.
passages.vernacular: 「好好。仲有,我講,醫生,可能有啲小危險,所以請把你嘅軍用左輪手槍放進口袋。」佢揮咗揮手,轉身,即刻消失喺人群中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好。還有,我說,醫生,可能有一點小危險,所以請把你的軍用左輪手槍放進口袋。」他揮了揮手,轉身,立刻消失在人群中。

passages.original: I trust that I am not more dense than my neighbours, but I was always oppressed with a sense of my own stupidity in my dealings with Sherlock Holmes. Here I had heard what he had heard, I had seen what he had seen, and yet from his words it was evident that he saw clearly not only what had happened but what was about to happen, while to me the whole business was still confused and grotesque. As I drove home to my house in Kensington I thought over it all, from the extraordinary story of the red-headed copier of the Encyclopædia down to the visit to Saxe-Coburg Square, and the ominous words with which he had parted from me. What was this nocturnal expedition, and why should I go armed? Where were we going, and what were we to do? I had the hint from Holmes that this smooth-faced pawnbroker’s assistant was a formidable man—a man who might play a deep game. I tried to puzzle it out, but gave it up in despair and set the matter aside until night should bring an explanation.
passages.vernacular: 我相信我並不比我嘅鄰居更遲鈍,但每次同夏洛克·福爾摩斯打交道時,我總是被自己愚蠢嘅感覺壓得喘不過氣嚟。呢一次,我聽到咗佢聽到嘅,睇到咗佢睇到嘅,但從佢嘅話睇來,佢顯然不僅清楚地睇出咗已經發生嘅事,仲睇出咗即將發生嘅事,而喺我睇來,整件事仍然混亂而怪誕。我乘車回到肯辛頓嘅家時,把呢一切想咗一遍,從嗰個抄寫百科全書嘅紅頭髮人嘅非凡故事,到薩克斯-科堡廣場之行,以及佢同我分手時嗰啲不祥嘅話。呢次夜間行動係乜嘢?我點解要帶武器去?我哋要去邊度,要做乜嘢?福爾摩斯暗示過,呢個臉光滑嘅當鋪助手係個可怕嘅人——一個可能玩大陰謀嘅人。我試圖想通呢件事,但絕望地放棄喇,把事情擱喺一邊,等夜晚帶嚟答案。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信我並不比我的鄰居更遲鈍,但每次同夏洛克·福爾摩斯打交道時,我總是被自己愚蠢的感覺壓得喘不過氣來。這一次,我聽到了他聽到的,看到了他看到的,但從他的話看來,他顯然不僅清楚地看出了已經發生的事,還看出了即將發生的事,而在我看來,整件事仍然混亂而怪誕。我乘車回到肯辛頓的家時,把這一切想了一遍,從那個抄寫百科全書的紅頭髮人的非凡故事,到薩克斯-科堡廣場之行,以及他同我分手時那些不祥的話。這次夜間行動是什麼?我為什麼要帶武器去?我們要去哪裡,要做什麼?福爾摩斯暗示過,這個臉光滑的當鋪助手是個可怕的人——一個可能玩大陰謀的人。我試圖想通這件事,但絕望地放棄了,把事情擱在一邊,等夜晚帶來答案。

passages.original: It was a quarter-past nine when I started from home and made my way across the Park, and so through Oxford Street to Baker Street. Two hansoms were standing at the door, and as I entered the passage I heard the sound of voices from above. On entering his room, I found Holmes in animated conversation with two men, one of whom I recognised as Peter Jones, the official police agent, while the other was a long, thin, sad-faced man, with a very shiny hat and oppressively respectable frock-coat.
passages.vernacular: 我九點一刻從家裡出發,穿過公園,然後經牛津街到貝克街。門口停住兩輛雙輪馬車,我走進走廊時,聽到樓上傳來講話聲。進入佢嘅房間,我發現福爾摩斯正同兩個人熱烈交談,其中一個我認出係官方警探彼得·瓊斯,另一個係個又高又瘦、面帶愁容嘅人,戴住一頂好光亮嘅帽子,穿住令人壓抑嘅體面長禮服外套。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我九點一刻從家裡出發,穿過公園,然後經牛津街到貝克街。門口停著兩輛雙輪馬車,我走進走廊時,聽到樓上傳來說話聲。進入他的房間,我發現福爾摩斯正同兩個人熱烈交談,其中一個我認出是官方警探彼得·瓊斯,另一個是個又高又瘦、面帶愁容的人,戴著一頂很光亮的帽子,穿著令人壓抑的體面長禮服外套。

passages.original: “Ha! Our party is complete,” said Holmes, buttoning up his pea-jacket and taking his heavy hunting crop from the rack. “Watson, I think you know Mr. Jones, of Scotland Yard? Let me introduce you to Mr. Merryweather, who is to be our companion in to-night’s adventure.”
passages.vernacular: 「哈!我哋嘅隊伍齊喇,」福爾摩斯講,扣上佢嘅粗呢短外套,從架子上取下佢嗰沉重嘅獵鞭。「華生,我想你認識蘇格蘭場嘅瓊斯先生吧?讓我畀你介紹梅里韋瑟先生,佢係我哋今晚冒險嘅同伴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈!我們的隊伍齊了,」福爾摩斯說,扣上他的粗呢短外套,從架子上取下他那沉重的獵鞭。「華生,我想你認識蘇格蘭場的瓊斯先生吧?讓我給你介紹梅里韋瑟先生,他是我們今晚冒險的同伴。」

passages.original: “We’re hunting in couples again, Doctor, you see,” said Jones in his consequential way. “Our friend here is a wonderful man for starting a chase. All he wants is an old dog to help him to do the running down.”
passages.vernacular: 「醫生,你睇,我哋又成對打獵喇,」瓊斯以佢自命不凡嘅口氣講。「我哋呢位朋友係個發動追逐嘅奇才。佢只需要一隻老獵犬嚟幫佢追捕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「醫生,你看,我們又成對打獵了,」瓊斯以他自命不凡的口氣說。「我們這位朋友是個發動追逐的奇才。他只需要一隻老獵犬來幫他追捕。」

passages.original: “I hope a wild goose may not prove to be the end of our chase,” observed Mr. Merryweather gloomily.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望追逐嘅結果唔會係一場白費力氣,」梅里韋瑟先生憂鬱地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望追逐的結果不會是一場白費力氣,」梅里韋瑟先生憂鬱地說。

passages.original: “You may place considerable confidence in Mr. Holmes, sir,” said the police agent loftily. “He has his own little methods, which are, if he won’t mind my saying so, just a little too theoretical and fantastic, but he has the makings of a detective in him. It is not too much to say that once or twice, as in that business of the Sholto murder and the Agra treasure, he has been more nearly correct than the official force.”
passages.vernacular: 「您可以對福爾摩斯先生有相當嘅信心,先生,」警探傲慢地講。「佢有佢自己嘅小方法,如果佢不介意我咁講,嗰啲方法有點過於理論化同異想天開,但佢具備偵探嘅潛質。可以毫不誇張地講,一兩次,例如肖爾托謀殺案同阿格拉寶藏嗰件事,佢比官方警力更接近正確。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您可以對福爾摩斯先生有相當的信心,先生,」警探傲慢地說。「他有他自己的小方法,如果他不介意我這麼說,那些方法有點過於理論化和異想天開,但他具備偵探的潛質。可以毫不誇張地說,一兩次,例如肖爾托謀殺案和阿格拉寶藏那件事,他比官方警力更接近正確。」
