passages.original: Sherlock Holmes closed his eyes and placed his elbows upon the arms of his chair, with his finger-tips together. “The ideal reasoner,” he remarked, “would, when he had once been shown a single fact in all its bearings, deduce from it not only all the chain of events which led up to it but also all the results which would follow from it. As Cuvier could correctly describe a whole animal by the contemplation of a single bone, so the observer who has thoroughly understood one link in a series of incidents should be able to accurately state all the other ones, both before and after. We have not yet grasped the results which the reason alone can attain to. Problems may be solved in the study which have baffled all those who have sought a solution by the aid of their senses. To carry the art, however, to its highest pitch, it is necessary that the reasoner should be able to utilise all the facts which have come to his knowledge; and this in itself implies, as you will readily see, a possession of all knowledge, which, even in these days of free education and encyclopædias, is a somewhat rare accomplishment. It is not so impossible, however, that a man should possess all knowledge which is likely to be useful to him in his work, and this I have endeavoured in my case to do. If I remember rightly, you on one occasion, in the early days of our friendship, defined my limits in a very precise fashion.”
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯閉上眼睛,把手肘放喺椅子扶手上,指尖合喺一起。「理想嘅推理者,」佢講,「一旦被展示咗一個事實嘅全部關係,就會從中推論出不僅導致佢嘅整條事件鏈,而且仲有從佢引出嘅所有結果。正如居維葉能夠通過觀察一根骨頭正確地描述整隻動物,一個徹底理解咗一系列事件中一環嘅觀察者,應該能夠準確地講出前後所有其他各環。我哋仲冇領會單靠理性可以達到嘅結果。喺書房裡可以解決嗰啲難倒所有試圖借助感官尋求答案嘅人嘅問題。不過,要把呢門藝術推到最高點,推理者必須能夠利用佢所知嘅一切事實;而呢本身就意味住,正如你好容易睇到嘅,擁有一切知識,即使喺呢個免費教育同百科全書嘅時代,呢都係一種相當罕見嘅成就。然而,一個人擁有對佢工作可能有用嘅所有知識,並非咁唔可能,而我就一直喺努力咁樣做。如果我冇記錯嘅話,喺我哋友誼嘅早期,你曾有一次以好精確嘅方式界定咗我嘅局限。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯閉上眼睛,把手肘放在椅子扶手上,指尖合在一起。「理想的推理者,」他說,「一旦被展示了一個事實的全部關係,就會從中推論出不僅導致它的整條事件鏈,而且還有從它引出的所有結果。正如居維葉能夠通過觀察一根骨頭正確地描述整隻動物,一個徹底理解了一系列事件中一環的觀察者,應該能夠準確地說出前後所有其他各環。我們還沒有領會單靠理性可以達到的結果。在書房裡可以解決那些難倒所有試圖借助感官尋求答案的人的問題。不過,要把這門藝術推到最高點,推理者必須能夠利用他所知的一切事實;而這本身就意味著,正如你很容易看到的,擁有一切知識,即使在這個免費教育和百科全書的時代,這也是一種相當罕見的成就。然而,一個人擁有對他工作可能有用的所有知識,並非那麼不可能,而我就一直在努力這樣做。如果我沒記錯的話,在我們友誼的早期,你曾有一次以非常精確的方式界定了我的局限。」

passages.original: “Yes,” I answered, laughing. “It was a singular document. Philosophy, astronomy, and politics were marked at zero, I remember. Botany variable, geology profound as regards the mud-stains from any region within fifty miles of town, chemistry eccentric, anatomy unsystematic, sensational literature and crime records unique, violin-player, boxer, swordsman, lawyer, and self-poisoner by cocaine and tobacco. Those, I think, were the main points of my analysis.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」我笑住回答。「嗰個係份奇特嘅文件。我記得,哲學、天文學同政治都被標為零。植物學不定,地質學對於離城五十英里之內任何地區嘅泥漬好精深,化學古怪,解剖學不系統,聳動文學同犯罪記錄獨一無二,小提琴手、拳擊手、劍客、律師,以及靠古柯鹼同煙草嘅自我毒害者。呢啲,我想,係我分析嘅要點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」我笑著回答。「那是份奇特的文件。我記得,哲學、天文學和政治都被標為零。植物學不定,地質學對於離城五十英里之內任何地區的泥漬很精深,化學古怪,解剖學不系統,聳動文學和犯罪記錄獨一無二,小提琴手、拳擊手、劍客、律師,以及靠古柯鹼和煙草的自我毒害者。這些,我想,是我分析的要點。」

passages.original: Holmes grinned at the last item. “Well,” he said, “I say now, as I said then, that a man should keep his little brain-attic stocked with all the furniture that he is likely to use, and the rest he can put away in the lumber-room of his library, where he can get it if he wants it. Now, for such a case as the one which has been submitted to us to-night, we need certainly to muster all our resources. Kindly hand me down the letter K of the American Encyclopædia which stands upon the shelf beside you. Thank you. Now let us consider the situation and see what may be deduced from it. In the first place, we may start with a strong presumption that Colonel Openshaw had some very strong reason for leaving America. Men at his time of life do not change all their habits and exchange willingly the charming climate of Florida for the lonely life of an English provincial town. His extreme love of solitude in England suggests the idea that he was in fear of someone or something, so we may assume as a working hypothesis that it was fear of someone or something which drove him from America. As to what it was he feared, we can only deduce that by considering the formidable letters which were received by himself and his successors. Did you remark the postmarks of those letters?”
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯對最後一項咧嘴而笑。「嗯,」佢講,「我而家講,像當時講嘅一樣,一個人應該讓佢嘅小小腦閣樓裡儲滿佢可能用到嘅所有家具,其餘嘅佢可以放進佢圖書館嘅雜物間裡,需要嘅時候可以去攞。而家,對於今晚向我哋提出嘅咁樣嘅案子,我哋當然需要集結我哋所有嘅資源。請把你旁邊架子上《美國百科全書》嘅字母K嗰一卷遞畀我。謝謝。而家讓我哋考慮呢個局勢,睇睇可以從中推論出乜嘢。首先,我哋可以從一個強烈嘅假定開始:奧彭肖上校有好強烈嘅理由離開美國。佢嗰個年紀嘅人唔會改變所有習慣,心甘情願地用佛羅里達迷人嘅氣候去換英國外省小鎮嘅孤獨生活。佢喺英國極端喜愛獨處,暗示佢害怕某個人或某件事,所以我哋可以假設,作為一個工作假講,係對某人或某事嘅恐懼把佢從美國趕走。至於佢害怕嘅係乜嘢,我哋只能通過考慮佢本人同佢嘅繼承人收到嘅嗰啲可怕嘅信嚟推論。你有冇注意到嗰啲信嘅郵戳?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯對最後一項咧嘴而笑。「嗯,」他說,「我現在說,像當時說的一樣,一個人應該讓他的小小腦閣樓裡儲滿他可能用到的所有家具,其餘的他可以放進他圖書館的雜物間裡,需要的時候可以去拿。現在,對於今晚向我們提出的這樣的案子,我們當然需要集結我們所有的資源。請把你旁邊架子上《美國百科全書》的字母K那一卷遞給我。謝謝。現在讓我們考慮這個局勢,看看可以從中推論出什麼。首先,我們可以從一個強烈的假定開始:奧彭肖上校有非常強烈的理由離開美國。他那個年紀的人不會改變所有習慣,心甘情願地用佛羅里達迷人的氣候去換英國外省小鎮的孤獨生活。他在英國極端喜愛獨處,暗示他害怕某個人或某件事,所以我們可以假設,作為一個工作假說,是對某人或某事的恐懼把他從美國趕走。至於他害怕的是什麼,我們只能通過考慮他本人和他的繼承人收到的那些可怕的信來推論。你有沒有注意到那些信的郵戳?」

passages.original: “The first was from Pondicherry, the second from Dundee, and the third from London.”
passages.vernacular: 「第一封來自本地治里,第二封來自鄧迪,第三封來自倫敦。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「第一封來自本地治里,第二封來自鄧迪,第三封來自倫敦。」

passages.original: “From East London. What do you deduce from that?”
passages.vernacular: 「來自倫敦東區。你從中推論出乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來自倫敦東區。你從中推論出什麼?」

passages.original: “They are all seaports. That the writer was on board of a ship.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋都係海港。寫信嘅人喺一艘船上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們都是海港。寫信的人在一艘船上。」

passages.original: “Excellent. We have already a clue. There can be no doubt that the probability—the strong probability—is that the writer was on board of a ship. And now let us consider another point. In the case of Pondicherry, seven weeks elapsed between the threat and its fulfilment, in Dundee it was only some three or four days. Does that suggest anything?”
passages.vernacular: 「好極喇。我哋已經有咗一條線索。毫無疑問,可能性——好強嘅可能性——係寫信嘅人喺一艘船上。而家讓我哋考慮另啲。本地治里嗰一次,從威脅到實現相隔咗七個星期,鄧迪嗰一次只有三四天。呢暗示咗乜嘢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好極了。我們已經有了一條線索。毫無疑問,可能性——很強的可能性——是寫信的人在一艘船上。現在讓我們考慮另一點。本地治里那一次,從威脅到實現相隔了七個星期,鄧迪那一次只有三四天。這暗示了什麼嗎?」

passages.original: “A greater distance to travel.”
passages.vernacular: 「要走嘅路更遠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要走的路更遠。」

passages.original: “But the letter had also a greater distance to come.”
passages.vernacular: 「但係信都有更遠嘅路要嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是信也有更遠的路要來。」

passages.original: “Then I do not see the point.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我睇不出重點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我看不出重點。」

passages.original: “There is at least a presumption that the vessel in which the man or men are is a sailing-ship. It looks as if they always send their singular warning or token before them when starting upon their mission. You see how quickly the deed followed the sign when it came from Dundee. If they had come from Pondicherry in a steamer they would have arrived almost as soon as their letter. But, as a matter of fact, seven weeks elapsed. I think that those seven weeks represented the difference between the mail-boat which brought the letter and the sailing vessel which brought the writer.”
passages.vernacular: 「至少有一個推測,嗰個人或嗰啲人所在嘅船係帆船。睇來佢哋喺開始執行任務時,總是把佢哋嘅奇特警告或標記先寄出去。你睇來自鄧迪嘅標記之後,行動跟住嚟得多快。如果佢哋係從本地治里乘輪船嚟嘅,佢哋幾乎會同信同時到達。但事實上,相隔咗七個星期。我想嗰七個星期代表咗送信嘅郵船同送寫信人嘅帆船之間嘅差別。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「至少有一個推測,那個人或那些人所在的船是帆船。看來他們在開始執行任務時,總是把他們的奇特警告或標記先寄出去。你看來自鄧迪的標記之後,行動跟著來得多快。如果他們是從本地治里乘輪船來的,他們幾乎會與信同時到達。但事實上,相隔了七個星期。我想那七個星期代表了送信的郵船與送寫信人的帆船之間的差別。」

passages.original: “It is possible.”
passages.vernacular: 「有可能。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有可能。」

passages.original: “More than that. It is probable. And now you see the deadly urgency of this new case, and why I urged young Openshaw to caution. The blow has always fallen at the end of the time which it would take the senders to travel the distance. But this one comes from London, and therefore we cannot count upon delay.”
passages.vernacular: 「不止如此。係好有可能。而家你睇出呢個新案子嘅致命緊迫性,以及我點解力勸年輕嘅奧彭肖謹慎。打擊總是落喺寄信人走完呢段距離所需時間結束嘅時候。但呢一次係從倫敦嚟嘅,因此我哋唔能夠指望有所延遲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不止如此。是很有可能。現在你看出這個新案子的致命緊迫性,以及我為什麼力勸年輕的奧彭肖謹慎。打擊總是落在寄信人走完這段距離所需時間結束的時候。但這一次是從倫敦來的,因此我們不能指望有所延遲。」

passages.original: “Good God!” I cried. “What can it mean, this relentless persecution?”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅上帝!」我喊道。「呢種無情嘅迫害係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的上帝!」我喊道。「這種無情的迫害是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “The papers which Openshaw carried are obviously of vital importance to the person or persons in the sailing-ship. I think that it is quite clear that there must be more than one of them. A single man could not have carried out two deaths in such a way as to deceive a coroner’s jury. There must have been several in it, and they must have been men of resource and determination. Their papers they mean to have, be the holder of them who it may. In this way you see K. K. K. ceases to be the initials of an individual and becomes the badge of a society.”
passages.vernacular: 「奧彭肖持有嘅文件顯然對帆船上嘅嗰個人或嗰啲人至關重要。我想好明顯,佢哋一定不止一個人。單獨一個人唔可能以欺騙驗屍官陪審團嘅方式造成兩起死亡。一定有好幾個人參與其中,而且佢哋一定係足智多謀同意志堅定嘅人。佢哋要攞到佢哋嘅文件,不管持有人係邊個。咁樣,你睇K. K. K.就唔再係一個人嘅姓名縮寫,而成咗一個社團嘅標誌。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奧彭肖持有的文件顯然對帆船上的那個人或那些人至關重要。我想很明顯,他們一定不止一個人。單獨一個人不可能以欺騙驗屍官陪審團的方式造成兩起死亡。一定有好幾個人參與其中,而且他們一定是足智多謀和意志堅定的人。他們要拿到他們的文件,不管持有人是誰。這樣,你看K. K. K.就不再是一個人的姓名縮寫,而成了一個社團的標誌。」

passages.original: “But of what society?”
passages.vernacular: 「但係乜嘢社團?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是什麼社團?」

passages.original: “Have you never—” said Sherlock Holmes, bending forward and sinking his voice—“have you never heard of the Ku Klux Klan?”
passages.vernacular: 「你難道從冇——」夏洛克·福爾摩斯講,身體前傾並壓低聲音——「你難道從冇聽講過三K黨?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你難道從沒——」夏洛克·福爾摩斯說,身體前傾並壓低聲音——「你難道從沒聽說過三K黨?」

passages.original: “I never have.”
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇聽講過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒聽說過。」

passages.original: Holmes turned over the leaves of the book upon his knee. “Here it is,” said he presently:
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯翻動佢膝上嗰本書嘅書頁。「喺呢度,」佢一會兒講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯翻動他膝上那本書的書頁。「在這裡,」他一會兒說:

passages.original: “‘Ku Klux Klan. A name derived from the fanciful resemblance to the sound produced by cocking a rifle. This terrible secret society was formed by some ex-Confederate soldiers in the Southern states after the Civil War, and it rapidly formed local branches in different parts of the country, notably in Tennessee, Louisiana, the Carolinas, Georgia, and Florida. Its power was used for political purposes, principally for the terrorising of the negro voters and the murdering and driving from the country of those who were opposed to its views. Its outrages were usually preceded by a warning sent to the marked man in some fantastic but generally recognised shape—a sprig of oak-leaves in some parts, melon seeds or orange pips in others. On receiving this the victim might either openly abjure his former ways, or might fly from the country. If he braved the matter out, death would unfailingly come upon him, and usually in some strange and unforeseen manner. So perfect was the organisation of the society, and so systematic its methods, that there is hardly a case upon record where any man succeeded in braving it with impunity, or in which any of its outrages were traced home to the perpetrators. For some years the organisation flourished in spite of the efforts of the United States government and of the better classes of the community in the South. Eventually, in the year 1869, the movement rather suddenly collapsed, although there have been sporadic outbreaks of the same sort since that date.’
passages.vernacular: 「『三K黨。呢個名字來源於佢同扳起步槍擊錘發出聲音嘅奇妙相似。呢個可怕嘅秘密社團係由啲前南方邦聯士兵在內戰之後於南方各州成立嘅,佢迅速喺全國不同地方設立地方分會,特別係喺田納西、路易斯安嗰、卡羅嚟納、喬治亞同佛羅里達。佢嘅力量被用於政治目的,主要係恐嚇黑人選民,謀殺並把反對其觀點嘅人驅逐出國。佢嘅暴行通常先畀被標記嘅人送去一個警告,形式離奇但一般為人所知——有嘅地方係一枝橡樹葉,有嘅地方係甜瓜籽或橘子核。收到呢個警告後,受害者可以公開放棄佢以前嘅作風,或者逃離呢個國家。如果佢硬撐到底,死亡必然降臨喺佢身上,通常係以某種奇怪而意想唔到嘅方式。呢個社團嘅組織如此完善,方法如此系統,以致記錄上幾乎冇一個案例,有人成功地硬撐而不受懲罰,或者其暴行中有任何一件被追查到肇事者身上。儘管美國政府同南方較上等階層做咗努力,呢個組織仍興旺咗好幾年。最後,喺1869年,呢個運動相當突然地瓦解,雖然嗰以後仍有同類零星嘅爆發。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『三K黨。這個名字來源於它與扳起步槍擊錘發出聲音的奇妙相似。這個可怕的秘密社團是由一些前南方邦聯士兵在內戰之後於南方各州成立的,它迅速在全國不同地方設立地方分會,特別是在田納西、路易斯安那、卡羅來納、喬治亞和佛羅里達。它的力量被用於政治目的,主要是恐嚇黑人選民,謀殺並把反對其觀點的人驅逐出國。它的暴行通常先給被標記的人送去一個警告,形式離奇但一般為人所知——有的地方是一枝橡樹葉,有的地方是甜瓜籽或橘子核。收到這個警告後,受害者可以公開放棄他以前的作風,或者逃離這個國家。如果他硬撐到底,死亡必然降臨在他身上,通常是以某種奇怪而意想不到的方式。這個社團的組織如此完善,方法如此系統,以致記錄上幾乎沒有一個案例,有人成功地硬撐而不受懲罰,或者其暴行中有任何一件被追查到肇事者身上。儘管美國政府和南方較上等階層做了努力,這個組織仍興旺了好幾年。最後,在1869年,這個運動相當突然地瓦解,雖然那以後仍有同類零星的爆發。』

passages.original: “You will observe,” said Holmes, laying down the volume, “that the sudden breaking up of the society was coincident with the disappearance of Openshaw from America with their papers. It may well have been cause and effect. It is no wonder that he and his family have some of the more implacable spirits upon their track. You can understand that this register and diary may implicate some of the first men in the South, and that there may be many who will not sleep easy at night until it is recovered.”
passages.vernacular: 「你會注意到,」福爾摩斯講,放下嗰本書,「呢個社團嘅突然解散,同奧彭肖帶住佢哋嘅文件從美國消失係同時發生嘅。好可能係因果關係。難怪佢同佢嘅家人被某些更唔肯罷休嘅人盯上。你可以理解,呢份登記簿同日記可能牽連南方嘅啲首要人物,可能有許多人不攞回佢哋,夜晚就唔能夠安瞓。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會注意到,」福爾摩斯說,放下那本書,「這個社團的突然解散,與奧彭肖帶著他們的文件從美國消失是同時發生的。很可能是因果關係。難怪他和他的家人被某些更不肯罷休的人盯上。你可以理解,這份登記簿和日記可能牽連南方的一些首要人物,可能有許多人不拿回它們,夜晚就不能安睡。」

passages.original: “Then the page we have seen—”
passages.vernacular: 「咁我哋睇到嘅嗰一頁——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼我們看到的那一頁——」

passages.original: “Is such as we might expect. It ran, if I remember right, ‘sent the pips to A, B, and C’—that is, sent the society’s warning to them. Then there are successive entries that A and B cleared, or left the country, and finally that C was visited, with, I fear, a sinister result for C. Well, I think, Doctor, that we may let some light into this dark place, and I believe that the only chance young Openshaw has in the meantime is to do what I have told him. There is nothing more to be said or to be done to-night, so hand me over my violin and let us try to forget for half an hour the miserable weather and the still more miserable ways of our fellow men.”
passages.vernacular: 「正是我哋可以預料嘅。如果我冇記錯,佢寫嘅係『把橘子核寄畀A、B同C』——都就係講,把社團嘅警告寄畀佢哋。然後有連續嘅記載,講A同B解決喇,或離開咗呢個國家,最後講C被拜訪喇,恐怕對C來講結果不祥。嗯,醫生,我想我哋可以讓啲光射進呢個黑暗嘅地方,我相信年輕嘅奧彭肖喺此期間唯一嘅機會就係照我告訴佢嘅去做。今晚冇更多可以講或可以做嘅喇,所以把我嘅小提琴遞畀我,讓我哋試住忘記半小時呢糟糕嘅天氣同我哋同胞更糟糕嘅行為。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「正是我們可以預料的。如果我沒記錯,它寫的是『把橘子核寄給A、B和C』——也就是說,把社團的警告寄給他們。然後有連續的記載,說A和B解決了,或離開了這個國家,最後說C被拜訪了,恐怕對C來說結果不祥。嗯,醫生,我想我們可以讓一點光射進這個黑暗的地方,我相信年輕的奧彭肖在此期間唯一的機會就是照我告訴他的去做。今晚沒有更多可以說或可以做的了,所以把我的小提琴遞給我,讓我們試著忘記半小時這糟糕的天氣和我們同胞更糟糕的行為。」

passages.original: It had cleared in the morning, and the sun was shining with a subdued brightness through the dim veil which hangs over the great city. Sherlock Holmes was already at breakfast when I came down.
passages.vernacular: 早晨天晴喇,太陽透過籠罩呢座大城市嘅朦朧面紗,閃耀住柔和嘅亮光。我下樓時,夏洛克·福爾摩斯已經喺食早餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨天晴了,太陽透過籠罩這座大城市的朦朧面紗,閃耀著柔和的亮光。我下樓時,夏洛克·福爾摩斯已經在吃早餐。

passages.original: “You will excuse me for not waiting for you,” said he; “I have, I foresee, a very busy day before me in looking into this case of young Openshaw’s.”
passages.vernacular: 「請原諒我冇等你,」佢講;「我預見今日有一個好忙碌嘅日子,要調查年輕嘅奧彭肖呢個案子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請原諒我沒有等你,」他說;「我預見今天有一個非常忙碌的日子,要調查年輕的奧彭肖這個案子。」

passages.original: “What steps will you take?” I asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你會採取乜嘢步驟?」我問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會採取什麼步驟?」我問。

passages.original: “It will very much depend upon the results of my first inquiries. I may have to go down to Horsham, after all.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個好大程度上取決於我第一批詢問嘅結果。我或者終究要去霍舍姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這很大程度上取決於我第一批詢問的結果。我也許終究要去霍舍姆。」

passages.original: “You will not go there first?”
passages.vernacular: 「你不先去嗰度嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不先去那裡嗎?」

passages.original: “No, I shall commence with the City. Just ring the bell and the maid will bring up your coffee.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,我先從倫敦城開始。只需按鈴,女傭就會把你嘅咖啡端上嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我先從倫敦城開始。只需按鈴,女傭就會把你的咖啡端上來。」

passages.original: As I waited, I lifted the unopened newspaper from the table and glanced my eye over it. It rested upon a heading which sent a chill to my heart.
passages.vernacular: 等待時,我從桌上攞起嗰份冇打開嘅報紙,瞥咗一眼。我嘅目光停喺一個標題上,使我心裡一陣發冷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等待時,我從桌上拿起那份沒打開的報紙,瞥了一眼。我的目光停在一個標題上,使我心裡一陣發冷。

passages.original: “Holmes,” I cried, “you are too late.”
passages.vernacular: 「福爾摩斯,」我喊道,「你嚟晚喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「福爾摩斯,」我喊道,「你來晚了。」

passages.original: “Ah!” said he, laying down his cup, “I feared as much. How was it done?” He spoke calmly, but I could see that he was deeply moved.
passages.vernacular: 「啊!」佢講,放下杯子,「我擔心會咁樣。係點發生嘅?」佢講得好平靜,但我睇得出佢深受震動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!」他說,放下杯子,「我擔心會這樣。是怎麼發生的?」他說得很平靜,但我看得出他深受震動。

passages.original: “My eye caught the name of Openshaw, and the heading ‘Tragedy Near Waterloo Bridge.’ Here is the account:
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅眼睛抓住咗奧彭肖呢個名字,同標題『滑鐵盧橋附近嘅悲劇』。報導如下:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的眼睛抓住了奧彭肖這個名字,和標題『滑鐵盧橋附近的悲劇』。報導如下:

passages.original: “‘Between nine and ten last night Police-Constable Cook, of the H Division, on duty near Waterloo Bridge, heard a cry for help and a splash in the water. The night, however, was extremely dark and stormy, so that, in spite of the help of several passers-by, it was quite impossible to effect a rescue. The alarm, however, was given, and, by the aid of the water-police, the body was eventually recovered. It proved to be that of a young gentleman whose name, as it appears from an envelope which was found in his pocket, was John Openshaw, and whose residence is near Horsham. It is conjectured that he may have been hurrying down to catch the last train from Waterloo Station, and that in his haste and the extreme darkness he missed his path and walked over the edge of one of the small landing-places for river steamboats. The body exhibited no traces of violence, and there can be no doubt that the deceased had been the victim of an unfortunate accident, which should have the effect of calling the attention of the authorities to the condition of the riverside landing-stages.’”
passages.vernacular: 「『昨夜九點到十點之間,H分局嘅警員庫克喺滑鐵盧橋附近執勤時,聽到呼救聲同落水聲。然而夜晚極其黑暗,風雨交加,儘管有幾個路人協助,救援完全唔可能。不過警報發出喇,喺水上警察嘅協助下,屍體最終被撈起。證實係一位年輕紳士,根據佢口袋裡發現嘅一個信封,名叫約翰·奧彭肖,住所在霍舍姆附近。據推測,佢可能係匆匆趕去趕滑鐵盧車站嘅最後一班火車,由於匆忙同極度黑暗,佢走錯咗路,從河上輪船嘅一個小碼頭邊緣走咗下去。屍體冇顯示暴力痕跡,毫無疑問死者係一次不幸意外嘅受害者,呢應該使當局注意河邊碼頭嘅狀況。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『昨夜九點到十點之間,H分局的警員庫克在滑鐵盧橋附近執勤時,聽到呼救聲和落水聲。然而夜晚極其黑暗,風雨交加,儘管有幾個路人協助,救援完全不可能。不過警報發出了,在水上警察的協助下,屍體最終被撈起。證實是一位年輕紳士,根據他口袋裡發現的一個信封,名叫約翰·奧彭肖,住所在霍舍姆附近。據推測,他可能是匆匆趕去趕滑鐵盧車站的最後一班火車,由於匆忙和極度黑暗,他走錯了路,從河上輪船的一個小碼頭邊緣走了下去。屍體沒有顯示暴力痕跡,毫無疑問死者是一次不幸意外的受害者,這應該使當局注意河邊碼頭的狀況。』」

passages.original: We sat in silence for some minutes, Holmes more depressed and shaken than I had ever seen him.
passages.vernacular: 我哋默默坐咗幾分鐘,福爾摩斯比我所見過嘅任何時候都更沮喪、更震動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們默默坐了幾分鐘,福爾摩斯比我所見過的任何時候都更沮喪、更震動。

passages.original: “That hurts my pride, Watson,” he said at last. “It is a petty feeling, no doubt, but it hurts my pride. It becomes a personal matter with me now, and, if God sends me health, I shall set my hand upon this gang. That he should come to me for help, and that I should send him away to his death—!” He sprang from his chair and paced about the room in uncontrollable agitation, with a flush upon his sallow cheeks and a nervous clasping and unclasping of his long thin hands.
passages.vernacular: 「呢傷咗我嘅自尊,華生,」佢終於講。「呢無疑係種瑣碎嘅感情,但係佢傷咗我嘅自尊。而家呢成咗我個人嘅事,如果上帝賜我健康,我要把手按喺呢夥人身上。佢嚟向我求助,而我卻把佢送去送死——!」佢從椅子上跳起嚟,喺房間裡走嚟走去,激動得無法控制,蠟黃嘅雙頰泛住紅暈,長而瘦嘅雙手神經質地緊握又鬆開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這傷了我的自尊,華生,」他終於說。「這無疑是種瑣碎的感情,但是它傷了我的自尊。現在這成了我個人的事,如果上帝賜我健康,我要把手按在這夥人身上。他來向我求助,而我卻把他送去送死——!」他從椅子上跳起來,在房間裡走來走去,激動得無法控制,蠟黃的雙頰泛著紅暈,長而瘦的雙手神經質地緊握又鬆開。

passages.original: “They must be cunning devils,” he exclaimed at last. “How could they have decoyed him down there? The Embankment is not on the direct line to the station. The bridge, no doubt, was too crowded, even on such a night, for their purpose. Well, Watson, we shall see who will win in the long run. I am going out now!”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋一定係狡猾嘅魔鬼,」佢終於喊道。「佢哋係點把佢誘騙到嗰度嘅?河堤不喺通往車站嘅直線上。橋,無疑,即使喺嗰樣嘅夜晚,對佢哋嘅目的來講都太擁擠喇。好,華生,我哋走住瞧到最後邊個會贏。我而家出去!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們一定是狡猾的魔鬼,」他終於喊道。「他們是怎麼把他誘騙到那裡的?河堤不在通往車站的直線上。橋,無疑,即使在那樣的夜晚,對他們的目的來說也太擁擠了。好,華生,我們走著瞧到最後誰會贏。我現在出去!」

passages.original: “To the police?”
passages.vernacular: 「去找警察?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去找警察?」

passages.original: “No; I shall be my own police. When I have spun the web they may take the flies, but not before.”
passages.vernacular: 「不;我自己做自己嘅警察。等我織好網,佢哋可以去抓蒼蠅,但唔能夠喺嗰以前。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不;我自己做自己的警察。等我織好網,他們可以去抓蒼蠅,但不能在那以前。」

passages.original: All day I was engaged in my professional work, and it was late in the evening before I returned to Baker Street. Sherlock Holmes had not come back yet. It was nearly ten o’clock before he entered, looking pale and worn. He walked up to the sideboard, and tearing a piece from the loaf he devoured it voraciously, washing it down with a long draught of water.
passages.vernacular: 我整天忙於我嘅專業工作,直到深夜才回到貝克街。夏洛克·福爾摩斯仲冇回嚟。將近十點佢才進嚟,睇起嚟蒼白而疲憊。佢走到餐具櫃前,撕下一塊麵包,貪婪地吞下去,用長長嘅一口水沖下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我整天忙於我的專業工作,直到深夜才回到貝克街。夏洛克·福爾摩斯還沒有回來。將近十點他才進來,看起來蒼白而疲憊。他走到餐具櫃前,撕下一塊麵包,貪婪地吞下去,用長長的一口水沖下去。

passages.original: “You are hungry,” I remarked.
passages.vernacular: 「你餓喇,」我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你餓了,」我說。

passages.original: “Starving. It had escaped my memory. I have had nothing since breakfast.”
passages.vernacular: 「餓壞喇。我忘記喇。我從早餐後乜嘢都冇食。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「餓壞了。我忘記了。我從早餐後什麼也沒吃。」

passages.original: “Nothing?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢都冇食?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼也沒吃?」

passages.original: “Not a bite. I had no time to think of it.”
passages.vernacular: 「一口都冇。我冇時間想到佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一口也沒有。我沒時間想到它。」

passages.original: “And how have you succeeded?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你進行得點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你進行得怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “Well.”
passages.vernacular: 「好好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好。」

passages.original: “You have a clue?”
passages.vernacular: 「你有線索喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有線索了?」

passages.original: “I have them in the hollow of my hand. Young Openshaw shall not long remain unavenged. Why, Watson, let us put their own devilish trade-mark upon them. It is well thought of!”
passages.vernacular: 「我已把佢哋握喺手心裡。年輕嘅奧彭肖唔會長久得唔到報仇。哎呀,華生,讓我哋把佢哋自己嘅魔鬼商標打喺佢哋身上。想得好!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我已把它們握在手心裡。年輕的奧彭肖不會長久得不到報仇。哎呀,華生,讓我們把他們自己的魔鬼商標打在他們身上。想得好!」

passages.original: “What do you mean?”
passages.vernacular: 「你係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是什麼意思?」

passages.original: He took an orange from the cupboard, and tearing it to pieces he squeezed out the pips upon the table. Of these he took five and thrust them into an envelope. On the inside of the flap he wrote “S. H. for J. O.” Then he sealed it and addressed it to “Captain James Calhoun, Barque Lone Star, Savannah, Georgia.”
passages.vernacular: 佢從櫥櫃裡攞出一個橘子,把佢撕開,把橘子核擠喺桌上。其中佢取咗五粒,塞進一個信封裡。喺信封內蓋上佢寫咗「S. H.致J. O.」然後佢封好,地址寫「喬治亞州薩凡納,三桅帆船孤星號,詹姆斯·卡爾霍恩船長」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他從櫥櫃裡拿出一個橘子,把它撕開,把橘子核擠在桌上。其中他取了五粒,塞進一個信封裡。在信封內蓋上他寫了「S. H.致J. O.」然後他封好,地址寫「喬治亞州薩凡納,三桅帆船孤星號,詹姆斯·卡爾霍恩船長」。

passages.original: “That will await him when he enters port,” said he, chuckling. “It may give him a sleepless night. He will find it as sure a precursor of his fate as Openshaw did before him.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢進港時佢就喺等住佢,」佢咯咯笑住講。「佢可能使佢失眠一夜。佢會發現佢像奧彭肖之前嗰樣,係佢命運嘅一個確定嘅先兆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他進港時它就在等著他,」他咯咯笑著說。「它可能使他失眠一夜。他會發現它像奧彭肖之前那樣,是他命運的一個確定的先兆。」

passages.original: “And who is this Captain Calhoun?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢位卡爾霍恩船長係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這位卡爾霍恩船長是誰?」

passages.original: “The leader of the gang. I shall have the others, but he first.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢夥人嘅頭目。其他人我都要抓,但佢係第一個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這夥人的頭目。其他人我也要抓,但他是第一個。」

passages.original: “How did you trace it, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你係點樣追蹤到嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你是怎樣追蹤到的?」

passages.original: He took a large sheet of paper from his pocket, all covered with dates and names.
passages.vernacular: 佢從口袋裡攞出一張大紙,上面寫滿咗日期同名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他從口袋裡拿出一張大紙,上面寫滿了日期和名字。

passages.original: “I have spent the whole day,” said he, “over Lloyd’s registers and files of the old papers, following the future career of every vessel which touched at Pondicherry in January and February in ’83. There were thirty-six ships of fair tonnage which were reported there during those months. Of these, one, the Lone Star, instantly attracted my attention, since, although it was reported as having cleared from London, the name is that which is given to one of the states of the Union.”
passages.vernacular: 「我花咗整整一天,」佢講,「喺勞埃德船舶登記冊同舊報紙嘅檔案裡,追蹤1883年1月同2月停靠過本地治里嘅每一艘船嘅後來嘅經歷。喺嗰幾個月裡,有三十六艘噸位相當嘅船被報告喺嗰度。其中有一艘,孤星號,即刻吸引咗我嘅注意,因為雖然報告講佢從倫敦出港,呢個名字卻係聯邦裡一個州嘅別稱。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我花了整整一天,」他說,「在勞埃德船舶登記冊和舊報紙的檔案裡,追蹤1883年1月和2月停靠過本地治里的每一艘船的後來的經歷。在那幾個月裡,有三十六艘噸位相當的船被報告在那裡。其中有一艘,孤星號,立刻吸引了我的注意,因為雖然報告說它從倫敦出港,這個名字卻是聯邦裡一個州的別稱。」

passages.original: “Texas, I think.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想係德克薩斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是德克薩斯。」

passages.original: “I was not and am not sure which; but I knew that the ship must have an American origin.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不確定係邊個,而家都不確定;但我知道嗰艘船一定源於美國。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不確定是哪個,現在也不確定;但我知道那艘船一定源於美國。」

passages.original: “What then?”
passages.vernacular: 「然後呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後呢?」

passages.original: “I searched the Dundee records, and when I found that the barque Lone Star was there in January, ’85, my suspicion became a certainty. I then inquired as to the vessels which lay at present in the port of London.”
passages.vernacular: 「我查咗鄧迪嘅記錄,當我發現孤星號三桅帆船喺1885年1月喺嗰度時,我嘅懷疑變成咗確定。然後我詢問咗目前停泊喺倫敦港嘅船隻。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我查了鄧迪的記錄,當我發現孤星號三桅帆船在1885年1月在那裡時,我的懷疑變成了確定。然後我詢問了目前停泊在倫敦港的船隻。」

passages.original: “Yes?”
passages.vernacular: 「點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “The Lone Star had arrived here last week. I went down to the Albert Dock and found that she had been taken down the river by the early tide this morning, homeward bound to Savannah. I wired to Gravesend and learned that she had passed some time ago, and as the wind is easterly I have no doubt that she is now past the Goodwins and not very far from the Isle of Wight.”
passages.vernacular: 「孤星號上星期到達呢度。我去咗阿爾伯特碼頭,發現佢今日早晨乘早潮被拖下河,返航薩凡納。我發電報到格雷夫森德,得知佢已喺一段時間前通過喇,由於風向偏東,我毫不懷疑佢而家已經過咗古德溫沙洲,離懷特島不遠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「孤星號上星期到達這裡。我去了阿爾伯特碼頭,發現她今天早晨乘早潮被拖下河,返航薩凡納。我發電報到格雷夫森德,得知她已在一段時間前通過了,由於風向偏東,我毫不懷疑她現在已經過了古德溫沙洲,離懷特島不遠。」

passages.original: “What will you do, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你要點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你要怎麼辦?」

passages.original: “Oh, I have my hand upon him. He and the two mates, are as I learn, the only native-born Americans in the ship. The others are Finns and Germans. I know, also, that they were all three away from the ship last night. I had it from the stevedore who has been loading their cargo. By the time that their sailing-ship reaches Savannah the mail-boat will have carried this letter, and the cable will have informed the police of Savannah that these three gentlemen are badly wanted here upon a charge of murder.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我已把手按喺佢身上。據我了解,佢同兩個大副係船上僅有嘅土生美國人。其他人係芬蘭人同德國人。我仲知道,佢哋三個琴晚都離開咗船。呢個係我從畀佢哋裝貨嘅碼頭工人嗰度得知嘅。當佢哋嘅帆船到達薩凡納時,郵船將已經把呢封信帶到,電報將已經通知薩凡納警方,呢三位先生喺呢度因謀殺罪被嚴重通緝。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我已把手按在他身上。據我了解,他和兩個大副是船上僅有的土生美國人。其他人是芬蘭人和德國人。我還知道,他們三個昨晚都離開了船。這是我從給他們裝貨的碼頭工人那裡得知的。當他們的帆船到達薩凡納時,郵船將已經把這封信帶到,電報將已經通知薩凡納警方,這三位先生在這裡因謀殺罪被嚴重通緝。」

passages.original: There is ever a flaw, however, in the best laid of human plans, and the murderers of John Openshaw were never to receive the orange pips which would show them that another, as cunning and as resolute as themselves, was upon their track. Very long and very severe were the equinoctial gales that year. We waited long for news of the Lone Star of Savannah, but none ever reached us. We did at last hear that somewhere far out in the Atlantic a shattered stern-post of a boat was seen swinging in the trough of a wave, with the letters “L. S.” carved upon it, and that is all which we shall ever know of the fate of the Lone Star.
passages.vernacular: 然而,人類最周密嘅計畫總有缺陷,殺害約翰·奧彭肖嘅兇手永遠收唔到嗰啲橘子核,佢哋本會告訴佢哋,另一個同佢哋同樣狡猾、同樣堅決嘅人,正在追蹤佢哋。嗰一年嘅秋分風暴好長,都好猛烈。我哋等咗好久孤星號嘅消息,但從來冇消息傳到我哋呢度。我哋最後確實聽講,喺遙遠嘅大西洋某處,有人睇到一根破碎嘅船尾柱,喺浪谷中搖擺,上面刻住字母「L. S.」,呢個就係我哋永遠能知道嘅孤星號嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,人類最周密的計畫總有缺陷,殺害約翰·奧彭肖的兇手永遠收不到那些橘子核,它們本會告訴他們,另一個與他們同樣狡猾、同樣堅決的人,正在追蹤他們。那一年的秋分風暴非常長,也非常猛烈。我們等了很久孤星號的消息,但從來沒有消息傳到我們這裡。我們最後確實聽說,在遙遠的大西洋某處,有人看到一根破碎的船尾柱,在浪谷中搖擺,上面刻著字母「L. S.」,這就是我們永遠能知道的孤星號的命運。

chapters.title: The Man with the Twisted Lip 歪嘴男人

passages.original: Isa Whitney, brother of the late Elias Whitney, D.D., Principal of the Theological College of St. George’s, was much addicted to opium. The habit grew upon him, as I understand, from some foolish freak when he was at college; for having read De Quincey’s description of his dreams and sensations, he had drenched his tobacco with laudanum in an attempt to produce the same effects. He found, as so many more have done, that the practice is easier to attain than to get rid of, and for many years he continued to be a slave to the drug, an object of mingled horror and pity to his friends and relatives. I can see him now, with yellow, pasty face, drooping lids, and pin-point pupils, all huddled in a chair, the wreck and ruin of a noble man.
passages.vernacular: 伊薩·惠特尼,已故嘅神學博士以利亞·惠特尼嘅弟弟,聖喬治神學院嘅院長,佢對鴉片好上癮。據我了解,呢個習慣係由於佢上大學時一時愚蠢嘅怪念頭而日益加深嘅;佢讀咗德昆西對自己夢境同感覺嘅描寫之後,就把佢嘅煙草浸滿咗鴉片酊,企圖產生同樣嘅效果。佢發現,像許多其他人一樣,呢種做法容易染上卻難以戒除,多年嚟佢一直係呢種毒品嘅奴隸,成咗佢嘅朋友同親戚既恐懼又憐憫嘅對象。我而家仲能睇見佢:黃色嘅麵糊般嘅臉、下垂嘅眼瞼同針尖般嘅瞳孔,整個人蜷縮喺椅子裡,係一個高貴之人嘅殘骸同廢墟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伊薩·惠特尼,已故的神學博士以利亞·惠特尼的弟弟,聖喬治神學院的院長,他對鴉片十分上癮。據我了解,這個習慣是由於他上大學時一時愚蠢的怪念頭而日益加深的;他讀了德昆西對自己夢境和感覺的描寫之後,就把他的煙草浸滿了鴉片酊,企圖產生同樣的效果。他發現,像許多其他人一樣,這種做法容易染上卻難以戒除,多年來他一直是這種毒品的奴隸,成了他的朋友和親戚既恐懼又憐憫的對象。我現在還能看見他:黃色的麵糊般的臉、下垂的眼瞼和針尖般的瞳孔,整個人蜷縮在椅子裡,是一個高貴之人的殘骸和廢墟。

passages.original: One night—it was in June, ’89—there came a ring to my bell, about the hour when a man gives his first yawn and glances at the clock. I sat up in my chair, and my wife laid her needle-work down in her lap and made a little face of disappointment.
passages.vernacular: 一天晚上——嗰個係1889年6月——我嘅門鈴響喇,時間大約係一個人第一次打呵欠、瞥一眼時鐘嘅時候。我喺椅子上坐直,我妻子把佢嘅針線活放到膝上,做咗一個失望嘅鬼臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天晚上——那是1889年6月——我的門鈴響了,時間大約是一個人第一次打呵欠、瞥一眼時鐘的時候。我在椅子上坐直,我妻子把她的針線活放到膝上,做了一個失望的鬼臉。

passages.original: “A patient!” said she. “You’ll have to go out.”
passages.vernacular: 「病人!」佢講。「你得出去喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「病人!」她說。「你得出去了。」

passages.original: I groaned, for I was newly come back from a weary day.
passages.vernacular: 我呻吟咗一聲,因為我剛從疲倦嘅一天中回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我呻吟了一聲,因為我剛從疲倦的一天中回來。

passages.original: We heard the door open, a few hurried words, and then quick steps upon the linoleum. Our own door flew open, and a lady, clad in some dark-coloured stuff, with a black veil, entered the room.
passages.vernacular: 我哋聽到門打開,講咗幾句急促嘅話,然後係喺油氈上嘅急步聲。我哋自己嘅門被猛然推開,一位穿住深色衣料、戴住黑面紗嘅女士走進房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們聽到門打開,說了幾句急促的話,然後是在油氈上的急步聲。我們自己的門被猛然推開,一位穿著深色衣料、戴著黑面紗的女士走進房間。

passages.original: “You will excuse my calling so late,” she began, and then, suddenly losing her self-control, she ran forward, threw her arms about my wife’s neck, and sobbed upon her shoulder. “Oh, I’m in such trouble!” she cried; “I do so want a little help.”
passages.vernacular: 「請原諒我咁晚嚟,」佢開始講,然後突然失去自制,跑上前,雙臂摟住我妻子嘅脖子,伏喺佢肩上啜泣。「哦,我遇到咁樣嘅麻煩!」佢喊道;「我真嘅好需要啲幫助。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請原諒我這麼晚來,」她開始說,然後突然失去自制,跑上前,雙臂摟住我妻子的脖子,伏在她肩上啜泣。「哦,我遇到這樣的麻煩!」她喊道;「我真的很需要一點幫助。」

passages.original: “Why,” said my wife, pulling up her veil, “it is Kate Whitney. How you startled me, Kate! I had not an idea who you were when you came in.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,」我妻子講,掀起佢嘅面紗,「係凱特·惠特尼。你嚇咗我一跳,凱特!你進嚟時我完全唔知道你係邊個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,」我妻子說,掀起她的面紗,「是凱特·惠特尼。你嚇了我一跳,凱特!你進來時我完全不知道你是誰。」

passages.original: “I didn’t know what to do, so I came straight to you.” That was always the way. Folk who were in grief came to my wife like birds to a lighthouse.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道該點算,所以直接嚟找你喇。」總是咁樣。悲傷嘅人嚟找我妻子,就像鳥飛向燈塔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道該怎麼辦,所以直接來找你了。」總是這樣。悲傷的人來找我妻子,就像鳥飛向燈塔。

passages.original: “It was very sweet of you to come. Now, you must have some wine and water, and sit here comfortably and tell us all about it. Or should you rather that I sent James off to bed?”
passages.vernacular: 「你嚟真係太好喇。而家,你必須飲些酒同水,舒舒服服地坐喺呢度,把一切都告訴我哋。定係你寧願我叫詹姆斯去瞓覺?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你來真是太好了。現在,你必須喝些酒和水,舒舒服服地坐在這裡,把一切都告訴我們。還是你寧願我叫詹姆斯去睡覺?」

passages.original: “Oh, no, no! I want the doctor’s advice and help, too. It’s about Isa. He has not been home for two days. I am so frightened about him!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不,不!我都需要醫生嘅建議同幫助。係關於伊薩嘅。佢兩天冇回家喇。我為佢擔心得要命!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不,不!我也需要醫生的建議和幫助。是關於伊薩的。他兩天沒回家了。我為他擔心得要命!」

passages.original: It was not the first time that she had spoken to us of her husband’s trouble, to me as a doctor, to my wife as an old friend and school companion. We soothed and comforted her by such words as we could find. Did she know where her husband was? Was it possible that we could bring him back to her?
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係佢第一次向我哋談起佢丈夫嘅麻煩,向我呢個醫生,向我妻子呢位老朋友同同學。我哋用我哋能找到嘅話安慰、勸慰佢。佢知道佢丈夫喺邊度嗎?我哋有可能把佢帶回畀佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是她第一次向我們談起她丈夫的麻煩,向我這個醫生,向我妻子這位老朋友和同學。我們用我們能找到的話安慰、勸慰她。她知道她丈夫在哪裡嗎?我們有可能把他帶回給她嗎?

passages.original: It seems that it was. She had the surest information that of late he had, when the fit was on him, made use of an opium den in the farthest east of the City. Hitherto his orgies had always been confined to one day, and he had come back, twitching and shattered, in the evening. But now the spell had been upon him eight-and-forty hours, and he lay there, doubtless among the dregs of the docks, breathing in the poison or sleeping off the effects. There he was to be found, she was sure of it, at the Bar of Gold, in Upper Swandam Lane. But what was she to do? How could she, a young and timid woman, make her way into such a place and pluck her husband out from among the ruffians who surrounded him?
passages.vernacular: 睇來有可能。佢得到最可靠嘅消息,佢最近喺發病時,去咗倫敦城最東邊嘅一家鴉片館。到目前為止,佢嘅狂歡一向只限於一天,晚上就回嚟,抽搐住、一副崩潰嘅樣子。但呢次發作已經持續咗四十八小時,佢無疑躺喺碼頭渣滓之間,吸住毒或瞓住以消除其影響。喺嗰度可以找到佢,佢確信,喺上斯旺丹巷嘅金酒吧。但佢該點算?佢一個年輕膽怯嘅女人,怎能走進咁樣嘅地方,把佢嘅丈夫從周圍嘅惡棍當中拉出嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看來有可能。她得到最可靠的消息,他最近在發病時,去了倫敦城最東邊的一家鴉片館。到目前為止,他的狂歡一向只限於一天,晚上就回來,抽搐著、一副崩潰的樣子。但這次發作已經持續了四十八小時,他無疑躺在碼頭渣滓之間,吸著毒或睡著以消除其影響。在那裡可以找到他,她確信,在上斯旺丹巷的金酒吧。但她該怎麼辦?她一個年輕膽怯的女人,怎能走進這樣的地方,把她的丈夫從周圍的惡棍當中拉出來?

passages.original: There was the case, and of course there was but one way out of it. Might I not escort her to this place? And then, as a second thought, why should she come at all? I was Isa Whitney’s medical adviser, and as such I had influence over him. I could manage it better if I were alone. I promised her on my word that I would send him home in a cab within two hours if he were indeed at the address which she had given me. And so in ten minutes I had left my armchair and cheery sitting-room behind me, and was speeding eastward in a hansom on a strange errand, as it seemed to me at the time, though the future only could show how strange it was to be.
passages.vernacular: 情況就係咁樣,當然只有一條出路。我能唔能夠陪佢去嗰個地方?然後,轉念一想,佢點解要去呢?我係伊薩·惠特尼嘅醫療顧問,作為咁樣嘅人,我對佢有影響力。如果我一個人去,我能處理得更好。我向佢保證,如果佢真嘅喺佢畀我嘅嗰個地址,我會喺兩小時內用馬車把佢送回家。於是好鐘後,我離開咗我嘅扶手椅同愉快嘅起居室,乘住一輛雙輪馬車向東疾馳,去做一件喺當時睇來好奇怪嘅差事,雖然只有將來才能顯示佢會有多奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 情況就是這樣,當然只有一條出路。我能不能陪她去那個地方?然後,轉念一想,她為什麼要去呢?我是伊薩·惠特尼的醫療顧問,作為這樣的人,我對他有影響力。如果我一個人去,我能處理得更好。我向她保證,如果他真的在她給我的那個地址,我會在兩小時內用馬車把他送回家。於是十分鐘後,我離開了我的扶手椅和愉快的起居室,乘著一輛雙輪馬車向東疾馳,去做一件在當時看來很奇怪的差事,雖然只有將來才能顯示它會有多奇怪。

passages.original: But there was no great difficulty in the first stage of my adventure. Upper Swandam Lane is a vile alley lurking behind the high wharves which line the north side of the river to the east of London Bridge. Between a slop-shop and a gin-shop, approached by a steep flight of steps leading down to a black gap like the mouth of a cave, I found the den of which I was in search. Ordering my cab to wait, I passed down the steps, worn hollow in the centre by the ceaseless tread of drunken feet; and by the light of a flickering oil-lamp above the door I found the latch and made my way into a long, low room, thick and heavy with the brown opium smoke, and terraced with wooden berths, like the forecastle of an emigrant ship.
passages.vernacular: 但我冒險嘅第一階段冇太大困難。上斯旺丹巷係一條骯髒嘅小巷,潛伏喺沿倫敦橋東邊河北岸排列嘅高大碼頭後面。喺一家舊衣店同一家杜松子酒店之間,通過一段陡峭嘅台階走下去,通到一個像洞口一樣嘅黑暗缺口,我找到咗我所尋找嘅嗰個窩。我吩咐馬車等住,走下台階,台階中央被醉漢不停嘅腳步磨出咗凹陷;借住門上方一盞搖曳嘅油燈嘅光,我找到門閂,走進一個又長又低嘅房間,裡面充滿咗濃重而沉悶嘅棕色鴉片煙霧,並且有木製嘅鋪位呈階梯狀排列,像移民船嘅前艙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我冒險的第一階段沒有太大困難。上斯旺丹巷是一條骯髒的小巷,潛伏在沿倫敦橋東邊河北岸排列的高大碼頭後面。在一家舊衣店和一家杜松子酒店之間,通過一段陡峭的台階走下去,通到一個像洞口一樣的黑暗缺口,我找到了我所尋找的那個窩。我吩咐馬車等著,走下台階,台階中央被醉漢不停的腳步磨出了凹陷;借著門上方一盞搖曳的油燈的光,我找到門閂,走進一個又長又低的房間,裡面充滿了濃重而沉悶的棕色鴉片煙霧,並且有木製的鋪位呈階梯狀排列,像移民船的前艙。

passages.original: Through the gloom one could dimly catch a glimpse of bodies lying in strange fantastic poses, bowed shoulders, bent knees, heads thrown back, and chins pointing upward, with here and there a dark, lack-lustre eye turned upon the newcomer. Out of the black shadows there glimmered little red circles of light, now bright, now faint, as the burning poison waxed or waned in the bowls of the metal pipes. The most lay silent, but some muttered to themselves, and others talked together in a strange, low, monotonous voice, their conversation coming in gushes, and then suddenly tailing off into silence, each mumbling out his own thoughts and paying little heed to the words of his neighbour. At the farther end was a small brazier of burning charcoal, beside which on a three-legged wooden stool there sat a tall, thin old man, with his jaw resting upon his two fists, and his elbows upon his knees, staring into the fire.
passages.vernacular: 喺昏暗中可以隱約瞥見躺喺奇怪幻想姿勢中嘅身體:彎曲嘅肩膀、屈起嘅膝蓋、向後仰嘅頭同朝上嘅下巴,呢度嗰度有一隻暗淡無神嘅眼睛轉向新嚟者。從黑暗嘅陰影中,閃爍住小小嘅紅色光圈,時亮時暗,隨住金屬煙斗碗中燃燒嘅毒物漲落。大多數人沉默躺住,但有些人自言自語,另啲人用奇怪、低沉、單調嘅聲音交談,談話一陣一陣湧出,然後突然沉入寂靜,每個人都喃喃講住自己嘅想法,好少注意鄰居嘅話。喺遠端有一個燃燒木炭嘅小火盆,旁邊三腳木凳上坐住一個又高又瘦嘅老人,下巴靠喺兩個拳頭上,手肘放喺膝蓋上,凝視住火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在昏暗中可以隱約瞥見躺在奇怪幻想姿勢中的身體:彎曲的肩膀、屈起的膝蓋、向後仰的頭和朝上的下巴,這裡那裡有一隻暗淡無神的眼睛轉向新來者。從黑暗的陰影中,閃爍著小小的紅色光圈,時亮時暗,隨著金屬煙斗碗中燃燒的毒物漲落。大多數人沉默躺著,但有些人自言自語,另一些人用奇怪、低沉、單調的聲音交談,談話一陣一陣湧出,然後突然沉入寂靜,每個人都喃喃說著自己的想法,很少注意鄰居的話。在遠端有一個燃燒木炭的小火盆,旁邊三腳木凳上坐著一個又高又瘦的老人,下巴靠在兩個拳頭上,手肘放在膝蓋上,凝視著火。

passages.original: As I entered, a sallow Malay attendant had hurried up with a pipe for me and a supply of the drug, beckoning me to an empty berth.
passages.vernacular: 我進去時,一個臉色蠟黃嘅馬嚟服務員已匆匆走嚟,畀我送上一支煙斗同一份毒品,向我示意一個空鋪位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我進去時,一個臉色蠟黃的馬來服務員已匆匆走來,給我送上一支煙斗和一份毒品,向我示意一個空鋪位。

passages.original: “Thank you. I have not come to stay,” said I. “There is a friend of mine here, Mr. Isa Whitney, and I wish to speak with him.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝。我唔係嚟待住嘅,」我講。「我有個朋友喺呢度,伊薩·惠特尼先生,我想同佢講話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝。我不是來待著的,」我說。「我有個朋友在這裡,伊薩·惠特尼先生,我想同他說話。」

passages.original: There was a movement and an exclamation from my right, and peering through the gloom, I saw Whitney, pale, haggard, and unkempt, staring out at me.
passages.vernacular: 我右邊有動靜同一聲驚叫,透過昏暗望去,我睇見惠特尼,蒼白、憔悴、頭髮蓬亂,正瞪住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我右邊有動靜和一聲驚叫,透過昏暗望去,我看見惠特尼,蒼白、憔悴、頭髮蓬亂,正瞪著我。

passages.original: “My God! It’s Watson,” said he. He was in a pitiable state of reaction, with every nerve in a twitter. “I say, Watson, what o’clock is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅上帝!係華生,」佢講。佢處於可憐嘅反應狀態,每根神經都喺顫抖。「我講,華生,而家幾點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的上帝!是華生,」他說。他處於可憐的反應狀態,每根神經都在顫抖。「我說,華生,現在幾點了?」

passages.original: “Nearly eleven.”
passages.vernacular: 「快十啲喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「快十一點了。」

passages.original: “Of what day?”
passages.vernacular: 「邊一天?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哪一天?」

passages.original: “Of Friday, June 19th.”
passages.vernacular: 「6月19日,星期五。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「6月19日,星期五。」

passages.original: “Good heavens! I thought it was Wednesday. It is Wednesday. What d’you want to frighten a chap for?” He sank his face onto his arms and began to sob in a high treble key.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!我以為係星期三。就係星期三。你點解要嚇唬人?」佢把臉埋喺手臂上,開始以高音嗚咽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!我以為是星期三。就是星期三。你為什麼要嚇唬人?」他把臉埋在手臂上,開始以高音嗚咽。

passages.original: “I tell you that it is Friday, man. Your wife has been waiting this two days for you. You should be ashamed of yourself!”
passages.vernacular: 「我告訴你係星期五,老兄。你妻子已經等咗你兩天。你應該為自己感到羞愧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我告訴你是星期五,老兄。你妻子已經等了你兩天。你應該為自己感到羞愧!」

passages.original: “So I am. But you’ve got mixed, Watson, for I have only been here a few hours, three pipes, four pipes—I forget how many. But I’ll go home with you. I wouldn’t frighten Kate—poor little Kate. Give me your hand! Have you a cab?”
passages.vernacular: 「我係羞愧。不過你弄混喇,華生,因為我只喺呢度待咗幾個小時,三斗煙,四斗煙——我忘咗多少。但我同你回家。我唔想嚇凱特——可憐嘅小凱特。把你嘅手畀我!你有馬車嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是羞愧。可是你弄混了,華生,因為我只在這裡待了幾個小時,三斗煙,四斗煙——我忘了多少。但我同你回家。我不想嚇凱特——可憐的小凱特。把你的手給我!你有馬車嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, I have one waiting.”
passages.vernacular: 「有,我有一輛喺等住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有,我有一輛在等著。」

passages.original: “Then I shall go in it. But I must owe something. Find what I owe, Watson. I am all off colour. I can do nothing for myself.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我就乘佢。但我一定欠咗點乜嘢。查一查我欠咗乜嘢,華生。我全身不舒服。我自己乜嘢都做不喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我就乘它。但我一定欠了點什麼。查一查我欠了什麼,華生。我全身不舒服。我自己什麼也做不了。」

passages.original: I walked down the narrow passage between the double row of sleepers, holding my breath to keep out the vile, stupefying fumes of the drug, and looking about for the manager. As I passed the tall man who sat by the brazier I felt a sudden pluck at my skirt, and a low voice whispered, “Walk past me, and then look back at me.” The words fell quite distinctly upon my ear. I glanced down. They could only have come from the old man at my side, and yet he sat now as absorbed as ever, very thin, very wrinkled, bent with age, an opium pipe dangling down from between his knees, as though it had dropped in sheer lassitude from his fingers. I took two steps forward and looked back. It took all my self-control to prevent me from breaking out into a cry of astonishment. He had turned his back so that none could see him but I. His form had filled out, his wrinkles were gone, the dull eyes had regained their fire, and there, sitting by the fire and grinning at my surprise, was none other than Sherlock Holmes. He made a slight motion to me to approach him, and instantly, as he turned his face half round to the company once more, subsided into a doddering, loose-lipped senility.
passages.vernacular: 我沿住兩排瞓者之間嘅窄通道走下去,屏住呼吸,以擋住嗰毒品令人作嘔、使人麻木嘅煙氣,四處找管事嘅人。當我經過坐喺火盆邊嘅嗰個高個子時,我感到有人突然拉咗一下我嘅衣擺,一個低沉嘅聲音低語:「從我身邊走過去,然後回頭睇我。」呢啲話好清楚地落入我耳中。我低頭睇咗一眼。佢哋只可能來自我身邊嘅嗰位老人,然而佢而家依然全神貫注地坐住,好瘦,好多皺紋,因年老而彎曲,一支鴉片煙斗從佢兩膝之間垂下嚟,好像係由於徹底嘅疲倦從佢手指間掉下嘅。我向前走咗兩步,回頭睇。我費盡全部自制力,才冇爆發出一聲驚叫。佢已轉過背,除咗我之外冇人能睇見佢。佢嘅身形已經豐滿起嚟,皺紋唔見喇,暗淡嘅眼睛恢復咗火光,而坐喺火邊、對我嘅驚訝咧嘴笑嘅,正是夏洛克·福爾摩斯。佢向我做咗個輕微嘅動作,示意我走近佢,隨即,當佢再次把臉半轉向眾人時,又沉入搖搖晃晃、嘴唇鬆垮嘅老態中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沿著兩排睡者之間的窄通道走下去,屏住呼吸,以擋住那毒品令人作嘔、使人麻木的煙氣,四處找管事的人。當我經過坐在火盆邊的那個高個子時,我感到有人突然拉了一下我的衣擺,一個低沉的聲音低語:「從我身邊走過去,然後回頭看我。」這些話非常清楚地落入我耳中。我低頭看了一眼。它們只可能來自我身邊的那位老人,然而他現在依然全神貫注地坐著,非常瘦,非常多皺紋,因年老而彎曲,一支鴉片煙斗從他兩膝之間垂下來,好像是由於徹底的疲倦從他手指間掉下的。我向前走了兩步,回頭看。我費盡全部自制力,才沒有爆發出一聲驚叫。他已轉過背,除了我之外沒有人能看見他。他的身形已經豐滿起來,皺紋不見了,暗淡的眼睛恢復了火光,而坐在火邊、對我的驚訝咧嘴笑的,正是夏洛克·福爾摩斯。他向我做了個輕微的動作,示意我走近他,隨即,當他再次把臉半轉向眾人時,又沉入搖搖晃晃、嘴唇鬆垮的老態中。

passages.original: “Holmes!” I whispered, “what on earth are you doing in this den?”
passages.vernacular: 「福爾摩斯!」我低聲講,「你到底喺呢個窩裡做乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「福爾摩斯!」我低聲說,「你到底在這個窩裡做什麼?」

passages.original: “As low as you can,” he answered; “I have excellent ears. If you would have the great kindness to get rid of that sottish friend of yours I should be exceedingly glad to have a little talk with you.”
passages.vernacular: 「盡量小聲,」佢回答;「我耳朵好好。如果你能好心打發走你嗰個酒鬼朋友,我會好高興同你談一談。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「盡量小聲,」他回答;「我耳朵非常好。如果你能好心打發走你那個酒鬼朋友,我會非常高興同你談一談。」

passages.original: “I have a cab outside.”
passages.vernacular: 「我有一輛馬車喺外面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有一輛馬車在外面。」

passages.original: “Then pray send him home in it. You may safely trust him, for he appears to be too limp to get into any mischief. I should recommend you also to send a note by the cabman to your wife to say that you have thrown in your lot with me. If you will wait outside, I shall be with you in five minutes.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就請用佢送佢回家。你可以放心信任佢,因為佢似乎太軟弱,幹不咗乜嘢壞事。我仲建議你通過車夫畀你妻子捎一張便條,講你已同我共命運喇。如果你喺外面等,我五分鐘後就同你會合。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就請用它送他回家。你可以放心信任他,因為他似乎太軟弱,幹不了什麼壞事。我還建議你通過車夫給你妻子捎一張便條,說你已和我共命運了。如果你在外面等,我五分鐘後就同你會合。」

passages.original: It was difficult to refuse any of Sherlock Holmes’ requests, for they were always so exceedingly definite, and put forward with such a quiet air of mastery. I felt, however, that when Whitney was once confined in the cab my mission was practically accomplished; and for the rest, I could not wish anything better than to be associated with my friend in one of those singular adventures which were the normal condition of his existence. In a few minutes I had written my note, paid Whitney’s bill, led him out to the cab, and seen him driven through the darkness. In a very short time a decrepit figure had emerged from the opium den, and I was walking down the street with Sherlock Holmes. For two streets he shuffled along with a bent back and an uncertain foot. Then, glancing quickly round, he straightened himself out and burst into a hearty fit of laughter.
passages.vernacular: 好難拒絕夏洛克·福爾摩斯嘅任何要求,因為佢哋總是咁明確,並且以嗰樣一種平靜嘅主宰氣度提出。不過,我覺得一旦惠特尼被關進馬車,我嘅任務就基本完成喇;至於其餘嘅,我唔能夠希望有比同我朋友一起參與嗰啲奇特冒險更好嘅事,嗰個係佢生活嘅常態。幾分鐘內,我寫好咗便條,付咗惠特尼嘅賬,領佢出去上咗馬車,睇住佢喺黑暗中被趕走。好快,一個老態龍鍾嘅身影從鴉片館出嚟,我便同夏洛克·福爾摩斯一起沿街走去。走咗兩條街,佢一直彎住背、步履不穩地拖住腳走。然後,佢迅速四下一睇,挺直咗身子,爆發出一陣痛快嘅笑聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很難拒絕夏洛克·福爾摩斯的任何要求,因為它們總是那麼明確,並且以那樣一種平靜的主宰氣度提出。不過,我覺得一旦惠特尼被關進馬車,我的任務就基本完成了;至於其餘的,我不能希望有比和我朋友一起參與那些奇特冒險更好的事,那是他生活的常態。幾分鐘內,我寫好了便條,付了惠特尼的賬,領他出去上了馬車,看著他在黑暗中被趕走。很快,一個老態龍鍾的身影從鴉片館出來,我便與夏洛克·福爾摩斯一起沿街走去。走了兩條街,他一直彎著背、步履不穩地拖著腳走。然後,他迅速四下一看,挺直了身子,爆發出一陣痛快的笑聲。

passages.original: “I suppose, Watson,” said he, “that you imagine that I have added opium-smoking to cocaine injections, and all the other little weaknesses on which you have favoured me with your medical views.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想,華生,」佢講,「你大概以為我喺古柯鹼注射之外,又添咗抽鴉片,以及所有其他你曾賜畀我你嘅醫學意見嘅小弱點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想,華生,」他說,「你大概以為我在古柯鹼注射之外,又添了抽鴉片,以及所有其他你曾賜給我你的醫學意見的小弱點。」

passages.original: “I was certainly surprised to find you there.”
passages.vernacular: 「我喺嗰度發現你,確實好驚訝。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在那裡發現你,確實很驚訝。」

passages.original: “But not more so than I to find you.”
passages.vernacular: 「但不及我發現你嗰樣驚訝。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但不及我發現你那樣驚訝。」

passages.original: “I came to find a friend.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係嚟找一個朋友嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是來找一個朋友的。」

passages.original: “And I to find an enemy.”
passages.vernacular: 「而我係嚟找一個敵人嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而我是來找一個敵人的。」

passages.original: “An enemy?”
passages.vernacular: 「敵人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「敵人?」

passages.original: “Yes; one of my natural enemies, or, shall I say, my natural prey. Briefly, Watson, I am in the midst of a very remarkable inquiry, and I have hoped to find a clue in the incoherent ramblings of these sots, as I have done before now. Had I been recognised in that den my life would not have been worth an hour’s purchase; for I have used it before now for my own purposes, and the rascally Lascar who runs it has sworn to have vengeance upon me. There is a trap-door at the back of that building, near the corner of Paul’s Wharf, which could tell some strange tales of what has passed through it upon the moonless nights.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅;我嘅天敵之一,或者講,我嘅天然獵物。簡單地講,華生,我正處喺一項好了不起嘅調查中,我希望能像以前嗰樣,從呢啲酒鬼語無倫次嘅喃喃自語中找到線索。如果我喺嗰個窩裡被認出,我嘅命連一小時都不值;因為我以前為了自己嘅目的用過佢,而經營佢嘅嗰個無賴拉斯卡人已發誓要向我報仇。喺嗰幢建築嘅後面,靠近保羅碼頭嘅拐角處有一個活板門,佢可以講述啲喺無月之夜通過佢嘅怪事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的;我的天敵之一,或者說,我的天然獵物。簡單地說,華生,我正處在一項非常了不起的調查中,我希望能像以前那樣,從這些酒鬼語無倫次的喃喃自語中找到線索。如果我在那個窩裡被認出,我的命連一小時都不值;因為我以前為了自己的目的用過它,而經營它的那個無賴拉斯卡人已發誓要向我報仇。在那幢建築的後面,靠近保羅碼頭的拐角處有一個活板門,它可以講述一些在無月之夜通過它的怪事。」

passages.original: “What! You do not mean bodies?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢!你唔係講屍體吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼!你不是說屍體吧?」

passages.original: “Ay, bodies, Watson. We should be rich men if we had £ 1000 for every poor devil who has been done to death in that den. It is the vilest murder-trap on the whole riverside, and I fear that Neville St. Clair has entered it never to leave it more. But our trap should be here.” He put his two forefingers between his teeth and whistled shrilly—a signal which was answered by a similar whistle from the distance, followed shortly by the rattle of wheels and the clink of horses’ hoofs.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,屍體,華生。如果每個喺嗰個窩裡被殺害嘅可憐蟲我哋都能得到一千鎊,我哋就係富人喇。佢係整個河邊最卑劣嘅謀殺陷阱,我恐怕內維爾·聖克萊爾走進去再都冇出嚟。但我哋嘅馬車應該就喺呢度。」佢把兩根食指放進牙齒之間,尖銳地吹咗聲口哨——遠處有一聲相似嘅口哨回應,隨後不久就係車輪嘅嘎嘎聲同馬蹄嘅叮噹聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,屍體,華生。如果每個在那個窩裡被殺害的可憐蟲我們都能得到一千鎊,我們就是富人了。它是整個河邊最卑劣的謀殺陷阱,我恐怕內維爾·聖克萊爾走進去再也沒有出來。但我們的馬車應該就在這裡。」他把兩根食指放進牙齒之間,尖銳地吹了聲口哨——遠處有一聲相似的口哨回應,隨後不久就是車輪的嘎嘎聲和馬蹄的叮噹聲。

passages.original: “Now, Watson,” said Holmes, as a tall dog-cart dashed up through the gloom, throwing out two golden tunnels of yellow light from its side lanterns. “You’ll come with me, won’t you?”
passages.vernacular: 「而家,華生,」福爾摩斯講,一輛高高嘅雙輪輕馬車從昏暗中疾馳而嚟,側燈投射出兩條金黃色嘅光隧道。「你會同我一起去,對嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,華生,」福爾摩斯說,一輛高高的雙輪輕馬車從昏暗中疾馳而來,側燈投射出兩條金黃色的光隧道。「你會同我一起去,對嗎?」

passages.original: “If I can be of use.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果我能有用嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我能有用的話。」

passages.original: “Oh, a trusty comrade is always of use; and a chronicler still more so. My room at The Cedars is a double-bedded one.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,一個忠實嘅夥伴總是有用嘅;一個記錄者更係如此。我喺雪松莊嘅房間係雙人床嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,一個忠實的夥伴總是有用的;一個記錄者更是如此。我在雪松莊的房間是雙人床的。」

passages.original: “The Cedars?”
passages.vernacular: 「雪松莊?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「雪松莊?」

passages.original: “Yes; that is Mr. St. Clair’s house. I am staying there while I conduct the inquiry.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅;嗰個係聖克萊爾先生嘅房子。我喺進行調查期間住喺嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的;那是聖克萊爾先生的房子。我在進行調查期間住在那裡。」

passages.original: “Where is it, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係喺邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是在哪裡?」

passages.original: “Near Lee, in Kent. We have a seven-mile drive before us.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺肯特嘅李鎮附近。我哋前面有七英里嘅路程。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在肯特的李鎮附近。我們前面有七英里的路程。」

passages.original: “But I am all in the dark.”
passages.vernacular: 「但我完全摸不住頭腦。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我完全摸不著頭腦。」

passages.original: “Of course you are. You’ll know all about it presently. Jump up here. All right, John; we shall not need you. Here’s half a crown. Look out for me to-morrow, about eleven. Give her her head. So long, then!”
passages.vernacular: 「當然你係咁樣。你好快就會知道一切。跳上嚟。好喇,約翰;我哋不需要你喇。呢度有半克朗。聽日十啲左右留意我。放開牠。咁再見!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然你是這樣。你很快就會知道一切。跳上來。好了,約翰;我們不需要你了。這裡有半克朗。明天十一點左右留意我。放開牠。那麼再見!」

passages.original: He flicked the horse with his whip, and we dashed away through the endless succession of sombre and deserted streets, which widened gradually, until we were flying across a broad balustraded bridge, with the murky river flowing sluggishly beneath us. Beyond lay another dull wilderness of bricks and mortar, its silence broken only by the heavy, regular footfall of the policeman, or the songs and shouts of some belated party of revellers. A dull wrack was drifting slowly across the sky, and a star or two twinkled dimly here and there through the rifts of the clouds. Holmes drove in silence, with his head sunk upon his breast, and the air of a man who is lost in thought, while I sat beside him, curious to learn what this new quest might be which seemed to tax his powers so sorely, and yet afraid to break in upon the current of his thoughts. We had driven several miles, and were beginning to get to the fringe of the belt of suburban villas, when he shook himself, shrugged his shoulders, and lit up his pipe with the air of a man who has satisfied himself that he is acting for the best.
passages.vernacular: 佢用鞭子輕拂馬,我哋飛馳穿過無窮無盡嘅、陰暗而荒涼嘅街道,街道逐漸變寬,直到我哋飛越一座有欄杆嘅寬闊橋樑,渾濁嘅河水喺我哋下面緩緩流動。橋外係另一片沉悶嘅磚瓦荒原,其寂靜只被警察沉重而有規律嘅腳步聲,或某夥晚歸狂歡者嘅歌聲同喊聲所打破。一片昏暗嘅雲層緩緩飄過天空,一兩顆星星從雲隙間呢度嗰度暗淡地閃爍。福爾摩斯沉默地駕車,頭垂喺胸前,一副陷入沉思嘅神態,而我坐喺佢旁邊,好奇地想知道呢個新探索係乜嘢,似乎極大地考驗佢嘅能力,但又怕打斷佢嘅思路。我哋已駛咗好幾英里,開始接近郊區別墅帶嘅邊緣,呢陣佢抖咗抖身子,聳聳肩,點燃煙斗,神情像一個講服咗自己係喺做最佳安排嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他用鞭子輕拂馬,我們飛馳穿過無窮無盡的、陰暗而荒涼的街道,街道逐漸變寬,直到我們飛越一座有欄杆的寬闊橋樑,渾濁的河水在我們下面緩緩流動。橋外是另一片沉悶的磚瓦荒原,其寂靜只被警察沉重而有規律的腳步聲,或某夥晚歸狂歡者的歌聲和喊聲所打破。一片昏暗的雲層緩緩飄過天空,一兩顆星星從雲隙間這裡那裡暗淡地閃爍。福爾摩斯沉默地駕車,頭垂在胸前,一副陷入沉思的神態,而我坐在他旁邊,好奇地想知道這個新探索是什麼,似乎極大地考驗他的能力,但又怕打斷他的思路。我們已駛了好幾英里,開始接近郊區別墅帶的邊緣,這時他抖了抖身子,聳聳肩,點燃煙斗,神情像一個說服了自己是在做最佳安排的人。

passages.original: “You have a grand gift of silence, Watson,” said he. “It makes you quite invaluable as a companion. ’Pon my word, it is a great thing for me to have someone to talk to, for my own thoughts are not over-pleasant. I was wondering what I should say to this dear little woman to-night when she meets me at the door.”
passages.vernacular: 「你有高超嘅沉默天賦,華生,」佢講。「呢使你成為一個極其寶貴嘅同伴。講真嘅,有個人可以講話,對我來講係件大事,因為我自己嘅想法不太愉快。我喺想,今晚呢位親愛嘅小女士喺門口迎接我時,我該對佢講乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有高超的沉默天賦,華生,」他說。「這使你成為一個極其寶貴的同伴。說真的,有個人可以說話,對我來說是件大事,因為我自己的想法不太愉快。我在想,今晚這位親愛的小女士在門口迎接我時,我該對她說什麼。」

passages.original: “You forget that I know nothing about it.”
passages.vernacular: 「你忘咗我對此一無所知。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你忘了我對此一無所知。」

passages.original: “I shall just have time to tell you the facts of the case before we get to Lee. It seems absurdly simple, and yet, somehow I can get nothing to go upon. There’s plenty of thread, no doubt, but I can’t get the end of it into my hand. Now, I’ll state the case clearly and concisely to you, Watson, and maybe you can see a spark where all is dark to me.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺到達李鎮之前,我正好有時間告訴你呢個案子嘅事實。佢睇起嚟荒唐地簡單,但唔知點嘅,我乜嘢都抓不住。線頭無疑好多,但我攞唔到線嘅末端。而家,華生,我會清楚簡明地向你陳述呢個案子,或者你能喺我睇來一片黑暗嘅地方睇到啲火花。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在到達李鎮之前,我正好有時間告訴你這個案子的事實。它看起來荒唐地簡單,但不知怎麼的,我什麼也抓不住。線頭無疑很多,但我拿不到線的末端。現在,華生,我會清楚簡明地向你陳述這個案子,也許你能在我看來一片黑暗的地方看到一點火花。」

passages.original: “Proceed, then.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁請講吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼請說吧。」

passages.original: “Some years ago—to be definite, in May, 1884—there came to Lee a gentleman, Neville St. Clair by name, who appeared to have plenty of money. He took a large villa, laid out the grounds very nicely, and lived generally in good style. By degrees he made friends in the neighbourhood, and in 1887 he married the daughter of a local brewer, by whom he now has two children. He had no occupation, but was interested in several companies and went into town as a rule in the morning, returning by the 5:14 from Cannon Street every night. Mr. St. Clair is now thirty-seven years of age, is a man of temperate habits, a good husband, a very affectionate father, and a man who is popular with all who know him. I may add that his whole debts at the present moment, as far as we have been able to ascertain, amount to £ 88 10s., while he has £ 220 standing to his credit in the Capital and Counties Bank. There is no reason, therefore, to think that money troubles have been weighing upon his mind.
passages.vernacular: 「幾年前——確切地講,1884年5月——有一位紳士嚟到李鎮,名叫內維爾·聖克萊爾,佢似乎好有錢。佢租咗一幢大別墅,把場地佈置得好漂亮,總嘅來講生活得好有格調。漸漸地,佢喺附近結交咗朋友,1887年佢娶咗當地一個釀酒商嘅女兒,而家佢哋有兩個細路。佢冇職業,但對幾家公司有興趣,一般早晨進城,每晚乘五點十四分從坎農街出發嘅車回嚟。聖克萊爾先生而家三十七歲,係個生活有節制嘅人,好丈夫,好慈愛嘅父親,並且係所有認識佢嘅人都鍾意嘅人。我可以補充,就我哋所能確定嘅,佢目前所有嘅債務共計八十八鎊十先令,而佢喺首都同郡縣銀行有二百二十鎊嘅存款。因此,冇理由認為金錢上嘅麻煩一直壓喺佢心頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「幾年前——確切地說,1884年5月——有一位紳士來到李鎮,名叫內維爾·聖克萊爾,他似乎很有錢。他租了一幢大別墅,把場地佈置得非常漂亮,總的來說生活得很有格調。漸漸地,他在附近結交了朋友,1887年他娶了當地一個釀酒商的女兒,現在他們有兩個孩子。他沒有職業,但對幾家公司有興趣,一般早晨進城,每晚乘五點十四分從坎農街出發的車回來。聖克萊爾先生現在三十七歲,是個生活有節制的人,好丈夫,非常慈愛的父親,並且是所有認識他的人都喜歡的人。我可以補充,就我們所能確定的,他目前所有的債務共計八十八鎊十先令,而他在首都與郡縣銀行有二百二十鎊的存款。因此,沒有理由認為金錢上的麻煩一直壓在他心頭。

passages.original: “Last Monday Mr. Neville St. Clair went into town rather earlier than usual, remarking before he started that he had two important commissions to perform, and that he would bring his little boy home a box of bricks. Now, by the merest chance, his wife received a telegram upon this same Monday, very shortly after his departure, to the effect that a small parcel of considerable value which she had been expecting was waiting for her at the offices of the Aberdeen Shipping Company. Now, if you are well up in your London, you will know that the office of the company is in Fresno Street, which branches out of Upper Swandam Lane, where you found me to-night. Mrs. St. Clair had her lunch, started for the City, did some shopping, proceeded to the company’s office, got her packet, and found herself at exactly 4:35 walking through Swandam Lane on her way back to the station. Have you followed me so far?”
passages.vernacular: 「上星期一,內維爾·聖克萊爾先生比平常早啲進城,出發前講佢有兩件重要事務要辦,並講佢會畀佢嘅小兒子帶一盒積木回家。而家,純屬偶然,佢嘅妻子就喺同一個星期一,佢離開後不久,收到一封電報,講佢一直喺等嘅一個價值相當高嘅小包裹,喺阿伯丁航運公司嘅辦事處等佢。而家,如果你對倫敦好熟,你就會知道呢家公司嘅辦事處喺弗雷斯諾街,佢從今晚你找到我嘅上斯旺丹巷分出去。聖克萊爾太太食咗午飯,動身進城,買咗些嘢,前往公司辦事處,攞到包裹,恰好喺四點三十五分發現自己正走過斯旺丹巷,回車站。你到目前為止都跟上咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「上星期一,內維爾·聖克萊爾先生比平常早一些進城,出發前說他有兩件重要事務要辦,並說他會給他的小兒子帶一盒積木回家。現在,純屬偶然,他的妻子就在同一個星期一,他離開後不久,收到一封電報,說她一直在等的一個價值相當高的小包裹,在阿伯丁航運公司的辦事處等她。現在,如果你對倫敦很熟,你就會知道這家公司的辦事處在弗雷斯諾街,它從今晚你找到我的上斯旺丹巷分出去。聖克萊爾太太吃了午飯,動身進城,買了些東西,前往公司辦事處,拿到包裹,恰好在四點三十五分發現自己正走過斯旺丹巷,回車站。你到目前為止都跟上了嗎?」

passages.original: “It is very clear.”
passages.vernacular: 「好清楚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「非常清楚。」

passages.original: “If you remember, Monday was an exceedingly hot day, and Mrs. St. Clair walked slowly, glancing about in the hope of seeing a cab, as she did not like the neighbourhood in which she found herself. While she was walking in this way down Swandam Lane, she suddenly heard an ejaculation or cry, and was struck cold to see her husband looking down at her and, as it seemed to her, beckoning to her from a second-floor window. The window was open, and she distinctly saw his face, which she describes as being terribly agitated. He waved his hands frantically to her, and then vanished from the window so suddenly that it seemed to her that he had been plucked back by some irresistible force from behind. One singular point which struck her quick feminine eye was that although he wore some dark coat, such as he had started to town in, he had on neither collar nor necktie.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你記得,星期一係個異常炎熱嘅日子,聖克萊爾太太走得好慢,環顧四周,希望睇到馬車,因為佢不鍾意自己所在嘅呢個地區。佢咁樣沿住斯旺丹巷走時,突然聽到一聲驚叫或呼喊,並震驚地睇到佢丈夫從二樓嘅一扇窗子向下睇住佢,喺佢睇來,似乎喺向佢招手。窗子係開住嘅,佢清楚地睇見佢嘅臉,佢描述講嗰張臉驚恐得可怕。佢瘋狂地向佢揮手,然後從窗口消失得咁突然,喺佢睇來,好像佢被某種不可抗拒嘅力量從後面拉咗回去。一個引起佢敏銳女性眼光嘅奇特之處係,雖然佢穿住佢進城時穿嘅嗰件深色外套,但佢既冇戴領子,都冇打領帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你記得,星期一是個異常炎熱的日子,聖克萊爾太太走得很慢,環顧四周,希望看到馬車,因為她不喜歡自己所在的這個地區。她這樣沿著斯旺丹巷走時,突然聽到一聲驚叫或呼喊,並震驚地看到她丈夫從二樓的一扇窗子向下看著她,在她看來,似乎在向她招手。窗子是開著的,她清楚地看見他的臉,她描述說那張臉驚恐得可怕。他瘋狂地向她揮手,然後從窗口消失得那麼突然,在她看來,好像他被某種不可抗拒的力量從後面拉了回去。一個引起她敏銳女性眼光的奇特之處是,雖然他穿著他進城時穿的那件深色外套,但他既沒有戴領子,也沒有打領帶。

passages.original: “Convinced that something was amiss with him, she rushed down the steps—for the house was none other than the opium den in which you found me to-night—and running through the front room she attempted to ascend the stairs which led to the first floor. At the foot of the stairs, however, she met this Lascar scoundrel of whom I have spoken, who thrust her back and, aided by a Dane, who acts as assistant there, pushed her out into the street. Filled with the most maddening doubts and fears, she rushed down the lane and, by rare good-fortune, met in Fresno Street a number of constables with an inspector, all on their way to their beat. The inspector and two men accompanied her back, and in spite of the continued resistance of the proprietor, they made their way to the room in which Mr. St. Clair had last been seen. There was no sign of him there. In fact, in the whole of that floor there was no one to be found save a crippled wretch of hideous aspect, who, it seems, made his home there. Both he and the Lascar stoutly swore that no one else had been in the front room during the afternoon. So determined was their denial that the inspector was staggered, and had almost come to believe that Mrs. St. Clair had been deluded when, with a cry, she sprang at a small deal box which lay upon the table and tore the lid from it. Out there fell a cascade of children’s bricks. It was the toy which he had promised to bring home.
passages.vernacular: 「確信佢出咗乜嘢事,佢衝下台階——因為嗰幢房子正是今晚你找到我嘅嗰個鴉片館——跑過前屋,試圖登上通往一樓嘅樓梯。然而喺樓梯腳,佢遇到我講過嘅呢個拉斯卡惡棍,佢把佢推回去,並喺嗰度擔任助手嘅一個丹麥人嘅幫助下,把佢推到咗街上。佢心中充滿咗最令人發狂嘅疑慮同恐懼,衝下巷子,極其幸運地喺弗雷斯諾街遇到啲警察同一名督察,都喺巡邏嘅路上。督察同兩個人陪佢回去,儘管老闆仍喺抵抗,佢哋定係嚟到聖克萊爾先生最後被睇見嘅嗰個房間。嗰度冇佢嘅蹤影。事實上,整個嗰一層樓除咗一個外表可怕嘅跛腳可憐蟲之外,邊個都找唔到,佢似乎以嗰度為家。佢同拉斯卡人都堅決發誓下午前屋冇別人。佢哋否認得咁堅決,督察唔知所措,幾乎相信聖克萊爾太太係受咗迷惑,呢陣佢叫咗一聲,撲向放喺桌上嘅一個小杉木盒,扯下盒蓋。裡面落出一堆小細路嘅積木。嗰個係佢答應帶回家嘅玩具。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「確信他出了什麼事,她衝下台階——因為那幢房子正是今晚你找到我的那個鴉片館——跑過前屋,試圖登上通往一樓的樓梯。然而在樓梯腳,她遇到我說過的這個拉斯卡惡棍,他把她推回去,並在那裡擔任助手的一個丹麥人的幫助下,把她推到了街上。她心中充滿了最令人發狂的疑慮和恐懼,衝下巷子,極其幸運地在弗雷斯諾街遇到一些警察和一名督察,都在巡邏的路上。督察和兩個人陪她回去,儘管老闆仍在抵抗,他們還是來到聖克萊爾先生最後被看見的那個房間。那裡沒有他的蹤影。事實上,整個那一層樓除了一個外表可怕的跛腳可憐蟲之外,誰也找不到,他似乎以那裡為家。他和拉斯卡人都堅決發誓下午前屋沒有別人。他們否認得那麼堅決,督察不知所措,幾乎相信聖克萊爾太太是受了迷惑,這時她叫了一聲,撲向放在桌上的一個小杉木盒,扯下盒蓋。裡面落出一堆小孩子的積木。那是他答應帶回家的玩具。

passages.original: “This discovery, and the evident confusion which the cripple showed, made the inspector realise that the matter was serious. The rooms were carefully examined, and results all pointed to an abominable crime. The front room was plainly furnished as a sitting-room and led into a small bedroom, which looked out upon the back of one of the wharves. Between the wharf and the bedroom window is a narrow strip, which is dry at low tide but is covered at high tide with at least four and a half feet of water. The bedroom window was a broad one and opened from below. On examination traces of blood were to be seen upon the windowsill, and several scattered drops were visible upon the wooden floor of the bedroom. Thrust away behind a curtain in the front room were all the clothes of Mr. Neville St. Clair, with the exception of his coat. His boots, his socks, his hat, and his watch—all were there. There were no signs of violence upon any of these garments, and there were no other traces of Mr. Neville St. Clair. Out of the window he must apparently have gone for no other exit could be discovered, and the ominous bloodstains upon the sill gave little promise that he could save himself by swimming, for the tide was at its very highest at the moment of the tragedy.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個發現同跛子明顯表現出嘅慌亂,使督察意識到事情嚴重。房間被仔細檢查,結果都指向一樁可憎嘅罪行。前屋布置得好簡單,像個起居室,通向一間小臥室,窗子對住一個碼頭嘅後面。碼頭同臥室窗子之間有一條窄帶,退潮時係乾嘅,但漲潮時被至少四英尺半嘅水覆蓋。臥室嘅窗子好寬,從下面往上開。檢查時,窗台上可以睇到血跡,臥室嘅木地板上可見幾滴散落嘅血滴。喺前屋嘅一幅窗簾後面塞住內維爾·聖克萊爾先生所有嘅衣服,除咗佢嘅外套。佢嘅靴子、襪子、帽子同錶——全都喺嗰度。呢啲衣服上都冇暴力嘅跡象,都冇內維爾·聖克萊爾先生嘅其他痕跡。佢顯然一定係從窗子出去嘅,因為找唔到其他出口,而窗台上不祥嘅血跡幾乎不畀佢游泳自救嘅希望,因為悲劇發生時潮水正處於最高點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個發現和跛子明顯表現出的慌亂,使督察意識到事情嚴重。房間被仔細檢查,結果都指向一樁可憎的罪行。前屋布置得很簡單,像個起居室,通向一間小臥室,窗子對著一個碼頭的後面。碼頭和臥室窗子之間有一條窄帶,退潮時是乾的,但漲潮時被至少四英尺半的水覆蓋。臥室的窗子很寬,從下面往上開。檢查時,窗台上可以看到血跡,臥室的木地板上可見幾滴散落的血滴。在前屋的一幅窗簾後面塞著內維爾·聖克萊爾先生所有的衣服,除了他的外套。他的靴子、襪子、帽子和錶——全都在那裡。這些衣服上都沒有暴力的跡象,也沒有內維爾·聖克萊爾先生的其他痕跡。他顯然一定是從窗子出去的,因為找不到其他出口,而窗台上不祥的血跡幾乎不給他游泳自救的希望,因為悲劇發生時潮水正處於最高點。

passages.original: “And now as to the villains who seemed to be immediately implicated in the matter. The Lascar was known to be a man of the vilest antecedents, but as, by Mrs. St. Clair’s story, he was known to have been at the foot of the stair within a very few seconds of her husband’s appearance at the window, he could hardly have been more than an accessory to the crime. His defence was one of absolute ignorance, and he protested that he had no knowledge as to the doings of Hugh Boone, his lodger, and that he could not account in any way for the presence of the missing gentleman’s clothes.
passages.vernacular: 「而家談嗰啲似乎同此事直接有牽連嘅惡棍。拉斯卡人係個出咗名嚟歷最卑劣嘅人,但由於根據聖克萊爾太太嘅講法,佢丈夫喺窗口出現後幾秒鐘內,佢就被發而家樓梯腳,佢幾乎唔可能只係呢樁罪行嘅從犯。佢嘅辯護係完全唔知情,佢抗議講佢唔知道佢嘅房客休·布恩嘅所作所為,都無法以任何方式解釋失蹤紳士嘅衣服為何喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在談那些似乎與此事直接有牽連的惡棍。拉斯卡人是個出了名來歷最卑劣的人,但由於根據聖克萊爾太太的說法,她丈夫在窗口出現後幾秒鐘內,他就被發現在樓梯腳,他幾乎不可能只是這樁罪行的從犯。他的辯護是完全不知情,他抗議說他不知道他的房客休·布恩的所作所為,也無法以任何方式解釋失蹤紳士的衣服為何在那裡。

passages.original: “So much for the Lascar manager. Now for the sinister cripple who lives upon the second floor of the opium den, and who was certainly the last human being whose eyes rested upon Neville St. Clair. His name is Hugh Boone, and his hideous face is one which is familiar to every man who goes much to the City. He is a professional beggar, though in order to avoid the police regulations he pretends to a small trade in wax vestas. Some little distance down Threadneedle Street, upon the left-hand side, there is, as you may have remarked, a small angle in the wall. Here it is that this creature takes his daily seat, cross-legged with his tiny stock of matches on his lap, and as he is a piteous spectacle a small rain of charity descends into the greasy leather cap which lies upon the pavement beside him. I have watched the fellow more than once before ever I thought of making his professional acquaintance, and I have been surprised at the harvest which he has reaped in a short time. His appearance, you see, is so remarkable that no one can pass him without observing him. A shock of orange hair, a pale face disfigured by a horrible scar, which, by its contraction, has turned up the outer edge of his upper lip, a bulldog chin, and a pair of very penetrating dark eyes, which present a singular contrast to the colour of his hair, all mark him out from amid the common crowd of mendicants and so, too, does his wit, for he is ever ready with a reply to any piece of chaff which may be thrown at him by the passers-by. This is the man whom we now learn to have been the lodger at the opium den, and to have been the last man to see the gentleman of whom we are in quest.”
passages.vernacular: 「拉斯卡人管事嘅就講咁多。而家講嗰個住喺鴉片館二樓嘅陰險跛子,佢肯定係最後一個目光落在內維爾·聖克萊爾身上嘅人。佢嘅名字叫休·布恩,佢嗰可怕嘅臉,係每個常去倫敦城嘅人都熟悉嘅。佢係個職業乞丐,不過為了避開警察規定,佢假裝做啲蠟火柴嘅小買賣。喺針線街沿路下去一小段,左手邊,你或者注意過,牆上有個小角落。呢個傢伙每天就坐喺呢度,盤住腿,小小嘅火柴存貨放喺膝上,而由於佢係個可憐嘅景象,一陣小雨般嘅施捨落進咗放喺人行道上佢旁邊嘅嗰頂油膩嘅皮帽裡。喺我想到要同佢結識職業關係之前,我就不止一次觀察過呢個傢伙,我對佢喺短時間內收獲嘅數目感到驚訝。你睇,佢嘅外表如此引人注目,冇人能經過佢而不注意到佢。一頭橙色嘅亂髮,一張被可怕疤痕毀容嘅蒼白臉,嗰疤痕嘅收縮使佢上唇嘅外緣翹咗起嚟,一個鬥牛犬般嘅下巴,同一雙好有穿透力嘅黑眼睛,同佢頭髮嘅顏色形成奇特嘅對比,呢一切使佢從普通嘅乞丐群中顯出;佢嘅機智都係,因為路人對佢拋出嘅任何嘲弄,佢總是隨時準備好回答。呢個就係我哋而家得知係鴉片館房客嘅人,都係最後一個睇見我哋所尋找嘅嗰位紳士嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「拉斯卡人管事的就說這麼多。現在說那個住在鴉片館二樓的陰險跛子,他肯定是最後一個目光落在內維爾·聖克萊爾身上的人。他的名字叫休·布恩,他那可怕的臉,是每個常去倫敦城的人都熟悉的。他是個職業乞丐,不過為了避開警察規定,他假裝做一點蠟火柴的小買賣。在針線街沿路下去一小段,左手邊,你也許注意過,牆上有個小角落。這個傢伙每天就坐在這裡,盤著腿,小小的火柴存貨放在膝上,而由於他是個可憐的景象,一陣小雨般的施捨落進了放在人行道上他旁邊的那頂油膩的皮帽裡。在我想到要同他結識職業關係之前,我就不止一次觀察過這個傢伙,我對他在短時間內收獲的數目感到驚訝。你看,他的外表如此引人注目,沒有人能經過他而不注意到他。一頭橙色的亂髮,一張被可怕疤痕毀容的蒼白臉,那疤痕的收縮使他上唇的外緣翹了起來,一個鬥牛犬般的下巴,和一雙非常有穿透力的黑眼睛,與他頭髮的顏色形成奇特的對比,這一切使他從普通的乞丐群中顯出;他的機智也是,因為路人對他拋出的任何嘲弄,他總是隨時準備好回答。這就是我們現在得知是鴉片館房客的人,也是最後一個看見我們所尋找的那位紳士的人。」

passages.original: “But a cripple!” said I. “What could he have done single-handed against a man in the prime of life?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢係個跛子!」我講。「佢一個人對付一個正值壯年嘅男人,能做乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是他是個跛子!」我說。「他一個人對付一個正值壯年的男人,能做什麼?」

passages.original: “He is a cripple in the sense that he walks with a limp; but in other respects he appears to be a powerful and well-nurtured man. Surely your medical experience would tell you, Watson, that weakness in one limb is often compensated for by exceptional strength in the others.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係跛子,意思係佢走路有點瘸;但喺其他方面,佢似乎係個強壯、營養良好嘅人。華生,你嘅醫學經驗肯定會告訴你,一條肢體嘅虛弱往往由其他肢體嘅非凡力量所補償。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是跛子,意思是他走路有點瘸;但在其他方面,他似乎是個強壯、營養良好的人。華生,你的醫學經驗肯定會告訴你,一條肢體的虛弱往往由其他肢體的非凡力量所補償。」

passages.original: “Pray continue your narrative.”
passages.vernacular: 「請繼續你嘅敘述。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請繼續你的敘述。」

passages.original: “Mrs. St. Clair had fainted at the sight of the blood upon the window, and she was escorted home in a cab by the police, as her presence could be of no help to them in their investigations. Inspector Barton, who had charge of the case, made a very careful examination of the premises, but without finding anything which threw any light upon the matter. One mistake had been made in not arresting Boone instantly, as he was allowed some few minutes during which he might have communicated with his friend the Lascar, but this fault was soon remedied, and he was seized and searched, without anything being found which could incriminate him. There were, it is true, some blood-stains upon his right shirt-sleeve, but he pointed to his ring-finger, which had been cut near the nail, and explained that the bleeding came from there, adding that he had been to the window not long before, and that the stains which had been observed there came doubtless from the same source. He denied strenuously having ever seen Mr. Neville St. Clair and swore that the presence of the clothes in his room was as much a mystery to him as to the police. As to Mrs. St. Clair’s assertion that she had actually seen her husband at the window, he declared that she must have been either mad or dreaming. He was removed, loudly protesting, to the police-station, while the inspector remained upon the premises in the hope that the ebbing tide might afford some fresh clue.
passages.vernacular: 「聖克萊爾太太睇到窗子上嘅血就暈過去喇,警察用馬車護送佢回家,因為佢在場對佢哋嘅調查幫不上乜嘢忙。負責此案嘅巴頓督察對呢個地方做咗好仔細嘅檢查,但冇找到任何能講明呢件事嘅嘢。有一個錯誤係冇即刻逮捕布恩,因為佢被允許有幾分鐘時間,可以同佢嘅朋友拉斯卡人溝通,但呢個過失好快就被糾正喇,佢被抓住並被搜身,冇發現任何可以使佢入罪嘅嘢。確實,佢嘅右襯衫袖子上有啲血跡,但佢指住佢嘅無名指,嗰度靠近指甲處被割傷喇,解釋講血係從嗰度流嘅,並補充講佢不久前去過窗口,嗰度觀察到嘅血跡無疑都來自同一個來源。佢極力否認曾經見過內維爾·聖克萊爾先生,並發誓佢房間裡有嗰啲衣服,對佢來講同對警察一樣係個謎。至於聖克萊爾太太斷言佢確實在窗口睇到佢丈夫,佢宣稱佢一定係瘋咗或喺做夢。佢大聲抗議住被帶到咗警察局,而督察留喺現場,希望退潮能提供啲新嘅線索。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聖克萊爾太太看到窗子上的血就暈過去了,警察用馬車護送她回家,因為她在場對他們的調查幫不上什麼忙。負責此案的巴頓督察對這個地方做了非常仔細的檢查,但沒有找到任何能說明這件事的東西。有一個錯誤是沒有立刻逮捕布恩,因為他被允許有幾分鐘時間,可以與他的朋友拉斯卡人溝通,但這個過失很快就被糾正了,他被抓住並被搜身,沒有發現任何可以使他入罪的東西。確實,他的右襯衫袖子上有一些血跡,但他指著他的無名指,那裡靠近指甲處被割傷了,解釋說血是從那裡流的,並補充說他不久前去過窗口,那裡觀察到的血跡無疑也來自同一個來源。他極力否認曾經見過內維爾·聖克萊爾先生,並發誓他房間裡有那些衣服,對他來說和對警察一樣是個謎。至於聖克萊爾太太斷言她確實在窗口看到她丈夫,他宣稱她一定是瘋了或在做夢。他大聲抗議著被帶到了警察局,而督察留在現場,希望退潮能提供一些新的線索。

passages.original: “And it did, though they hardly found upon the mud-bank what they had feared to find. It was Neville St. Clair’s coat, and not Neville St. Clair, which lay uncovered as the tide receded. And what do you think they found in the pockets?”
passages.vernacular: 「確實有,雖然佢哋喺泥灘上幾乎冇找到佢哋所害怕找到嘅嘢。隨住潮水退去而裸露出嚟嘅,係內維爾·聖克萊爾嘅外套,而唔係內維爾·聖克萊爾。你猜佢哋喺口袋裡發現咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「確實有,雖然他們在泥灘上幾乎沒有找到他們所害怕找到的東西。隨著潮水退去而裸露出來的,是內維爾·聖克萊爾的外套,而不是內維爾·聖克萊爾。你猜他們在口袋裡發現了什麼?」

passages.original: “I cannot imagine.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想像不出。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想像不出。」

passages.original: “No, I don’t think you would guess. Every pocket stuffed with pennies and half-pennies—421 pennies and 270 half-pennies. It was no wonder that it had not been swept away by the tide. But a human body is a different matter. There is a fierce eddy between the wharf and the house. It seemed likely enough that the weighted coat had remained when the stripped body had been sucked away into the river.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我想你猜唔到。每個口袋都塞滿咗便士同半便士——四百二十一個便士同二百七十個半便士。難怪佢冇被潮水沖走。但係人嘅身體就不同喇。喺碼頭同房子之間有一股猛烈嘅漩渦。好可能係,有重量嘅外套留咗下嚟,而被剝光衣服嘅身體被吸進咗河裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我想你猜不到。每個口袋都塞滿了便士和半便士——四百二十一個便士和二百七十個半便士。難怪它沒有被潮水沖走。但是人的身體就不同了。在碼頭和房子之間有一股猛烈的漩渦。很可能是,有重量的外套留了下來,而被剝光衣服的身體被吸進了河裡。」

passages.original: “But I understand that all the other clothes were found in the room. Would the body be dressed in a coat alone?”
passages.vernacular: 「但我了解到其他所有衣服都喺嗰個房間裡找到。屍體只穿住外套嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我了解到其他所有衣服都在那個房間裡找到。屍體只穿著外套嗎?」

passages.original: “No, sir, but the facts might be met speciously enough. Suppose that this man Boone had thrust Neville St. Clair through the window, there is no human eye which could have seen the deed. What would he do then? It would of course instantly strike him that he must get rid of the tell-tale garments. He would seize the coat, then, and be in the act of throwing it out, when it would occur to him that it would swim and not sink. He has little time, for he has heard the scuffle downstairs when the wife tried to force her way up, and perhaps he has already heard from his Lascar confederate that the police are hurrying up the street. There is not an instant to be lost. He rushes to some secret hoard, where he has accumulated the fruits of his beggary, and he stuffs all the coins upon which he can lay his hands into the pockets to make sure of the coat’s sinking. He throws it out, and would have done the same with the other garments had not he heard the rush of steps below, and only just had time to close the window when the police appeared.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,先生,但事實可以相當似係而非地配合。假設呢個人布恩把內維爾·聖克萊爾推出咗窗外,冇人嘅眼睛能睇到呢個行為。嗰佢會點做?當然佢會即刻想到,佢必須擺脫嗰啲泄露真相嘅衣服。咁佢會抓起外套,正要把佢扔出去時,佢想到佢會浮喺水面而唔會沉下去。佢時間好少,因為佢聽到樓下妻子試圖強行上樓嘅扭打聲,或者佢已從佢嘅拉斯卡同夥嗰度聽到警察正沿街趕嚟。一刻都唔能夠浪費。佢衝到某個秘密嘅藏處,嗰度有佢乞討所得嘅積蓄,把佢能攞到嘅所有硬幣塞進口袋,以確保外套會沉下去。佢把佢扔出去,本來都會對其他衣服做同樣嘅事,只係佢聽到樓下嘅奔跑聲,剛好有時間關上窗子,警察就出現喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,先生,但事實可以相當似是而非地配合。假設這個人布恩把內維爾·聖克萊爾推出了窗外,沒有人的眼睛能看到這個行為。那他會怎麼做?當然他會立刻想到,他必須擺脫那些泄露真相的衣服。那麼他會抓起外套,正要把它扔出去時,他想到它會浮在水面而不會沉下去。他時間很少,因為他聽到樓下妻子試圖強行上樓的扭打聲,也許他已從他的拉斯卡同夥那裡聽到警察正沿街趕來。一刻也不能浪費。他衝到某個秘密的藏處,那裡有他乞討所得的積蓄,把他能拿到的所有硬幣塞進口袋,以確保外套會沉下去。他把它扔出去,本來也會對其他衣服做同樣的事,只是他聽到樓下的奔跑聲,剛好有時間關上窗子,警察就出現了。」

passages.original: “It certainly sounds feasible.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢聽起嚟確實可行。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這聽起來確實可行。」

passages.original: “Well, we will take it as a working hypothesis for want of a better. Boone, as I have told you, was arrested and taken to the station, but it could not be shown that there had ever before been anything against him. He had for years been known as a professional beggar, but his life appeared to have been a very quiet and innocent one. There the matter stands at present, and the questions which have to be solved—what Neville St. Clair was doing in the opium den, what happened to him when there, where is he now, and what Hugh Boone had to do with his disappearance—are all as far from a solution as ever. I confess that I cannot recall any case within my experience which looked at the first glance so simple and yet which presented such difficulties.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,由於冇更好嘅,我哋就把佢當作一個工作假講。布恩,正如我告訴過你嘅,被逮捕並帶到咗警局,但無法顯示佢以前有任何對佢不利嘅記錄。多年嚟佢一直被認為係職業乞丐,但佢嘅生活似乎一直好安靜、無辜。事情目前就停喺嗰度,需要解決嘅問題——內維爾·聖克萊爾喺鴉片館做乜嘢,佢喺嗰度發生咗乜嘢事,佢而家喺邊度,休·布恩同佢嘅失蹤有乜嘢關係——都像以前一樣離解決仲遠。我承認,喺我嘅經驗中,我想不起有邊一個案子乍睇如此簡單,卻呈現咁樣嘅困難。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,由於沒有更好的,我們就把它當作一個工作假說。布恩,正如我告訴過你的,被逮捕並帶到了警局,但無法顯示他以前有任何對他不利的記錄。多年來他一直被認為是職業乞丐,但他的生活似乎一直很安靜、無辜。事情目前就停在那裡,需要解決的問題——內維爾·聖克萊爾在鴉片館做什麼,他在那裡發生了什麼事,他現在在哪裡,休·布恩與他的失蹤有什麼關係——都像以前一樣離解決還遠。我承認,在我的經驗中,我想不起有哪一個案子乍看如此簡單,卻呈現這樣的困難。」

passages.original: While Sherlock Holmes had been detailing this singular series of events, we had been whirling through the outskirts of the great town until the last straggling houses had been left behind, and we rattled along with a country hedge upon either side of us. Just as he finished, however, we drove through two scattered villages, where a few lights still glimmered in the windows.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯詳細敘述呢一連串奇特事件時,我哋一直喺大城市嘅郊區飛馳,直到最後幾幢零散嘅房子被拋喺後面,我哋兩邊都係鄉村樹籬,嘎嘎地前進。不過,就喺佢講完時,我哋駛過兩個零星嘅村莊,窗子裡仲有幾盞燈光閃爍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯詳細敘述這一連串奇特事件時,我們一直在大城市的郊區飛馳,直到最後幾幢零散的房子被拋在後面,我們兩邊都是鄉村樹籬,嘎嘎地前進。不過,就在他說完時,我們駛過兩個零星的村莊,窗子裡還有幾盞燈光閃爍。

passages.original: “We are on the outskirts of Lee,” said my companion. “We have touched on three English counties in our short drive, starting in Middlesex, passing over an angle of Surrey, and ending in Kent. See that light among the trees? That is The Cedars, and beside that lamp sits a woman whose anxious ears have already, I have little doubt, caught the clink of our horse’s feet.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋喺李鎮嘅郊區喇,」我嘅同伴講。「我哋喺短短嘅車程中觸及咗英格蘭三個郡,從米德爾塞克斯出發,越過薩里嘅一個角,喺肯特結束。睇到樹叢中嘅嗰盞燈嗎?嗰個就係雪松莊,嗰盞燈旁邊坐住一個女人,我毫不懷疑,佢焦急嘅耳朵已經捕捉到我哋馬蹄嘅叮噹聲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們在李鎮的郊區了,」我的同伴說。「我們在短短的車程中觸及了英格蘭三個郡,從米德爾塞克斯出發,越過薩里的一個角,在肯特結束。看到樹叢中的那盞燈嗎?那就是雪松莊,那盞燈旁邊坐著一個女人,我毫不懷疑,她焦急的耳朵已經捕捉到我們馬蹄的叮噹聲。」

passages.original: “But why are you not conducting the case from Baker Street?” I asked.
passages.vernacular: 「但你點解不喺貝克街指揮呢個案子?」我問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你為什麼不在貝克街指揮這個案子?」我問。

passages.original: “Because there are many inquiries which must be made out here. Mrs. St. Clair has most kindly put two rooms at my disposal, and you may rest assured that she will have nothing but a welcome for my friend and colleague. I hate to meet her, Watson, when I have no news of her husband. Here we are. Whoa, there, whoa!”
passages.vernacular: 「因為有許多詢問必須喺呢度進行。聖克萊爾太太好好心地讓我使用兩個房間,你可以放心,佢對我嘅朋友同同事只會有歡迎。華生,當我冇佢丈夫嘅消息時,我討厭見佢。到喇。籲,停,籲!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為有許多詢問必須在這裡進行。聖克萊爾太太非常好心地讓我使用兩個房間,你可以放心,她對我的朋友和同事只會有歡迎。華生,當我沒有她丈夫的消息時,我討厭見她。到了。籲,停,籲!」

passages.original: We had pulled up in front of a large villa which stood within its own grounds. A stable-boy had run out to the horse’s head, and springing down, I followed Holmes up the small, winding gravel-drive which led to the house. As we approached, the door flew open, and a little blonde woman stood in the opening, clad in some sort of light mousseline de soie, with a touch of fluffy pink chiffon at her neck and wrists. She stood with her figure outlined against the flood of light, one hand upon the door, one half-raised in her eagerness, her body slightly bent, her head and face protruded, with eager eyes and parted lips, a standing question.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺一幢位於自己園地內嘅大別墅前停下。一個馬房小子跑到馬頭前,我跳下車,跟住福爾摩斯沿住通往房子嘅曲折小碎石路上去。我哋走近時,門被猛地推開,一位金髮嘅小個子女人站喺門口,穿住某種輕薄嘅絲質薄紗,頸部同手腕有啲蓬鬆嘅粉紅雪紡。佢站喺嗰度,身影映喺湧出嘅光中,一隻手扶住門,一隻手因急切而半舉,身體微微前傾,頭同臉伸出去,眼睛急切,嘴唇微張,係一個站住嘅問號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在一幢位於自己園地內的大別墅前停下。一個馬房小子跑到馬頭前,我跳下車,跟著福爾摩斯沿著通往房子的曲折小碎石路上去。我們走近時,門被猛地推開,一位金髮的小個子女人站在門口,穿著某種輕薄的絲質薄紗,頸部和手腕有一點蓬鬆的粉紅雪紡。她站在那裡,身影映在湧出的光中,一隻手扶著門,一隻手因急切而半舉,身體微微前傾,頭和臉伸出去,眼睛急切,嘴唇微張,是一個站著的問號。

passages.original: “Well?” she cried, “well?” And then, seeing that there were two of us, she gave a cry of hope which sank into a groan as she saw that my companion shook his head and shrugged his shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 「點樣?」佢喊道,「點樣?」然後,睇到我哋有兩個人,佢發出一聲充滿希望嘅喊聲,卻喺睇到我嘅同伴搖頭聳肩時沉成咗呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼樣?」她喊道,「怎麼樣?」然後,看到我們有兩個人,她發出一聲充滿希望的喊聲,卻在看到我的同伴搖頭聳肩時沉成了呻吟。

passages.original: “No good news?”
passages.vernacular: 「冇好消息?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有好消息?」

passages.original: “None.”
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有。」

passages.original: “No bad?”
passages.vernacular: 「都冇壞消息?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也沒有壞消息?」

passages.original: “No.”
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有。」

passages.original: “Thank God for that. But come in. You must be weary, for you have had a long day.”
passages.vernacular: 「感謝上帝。但請進嚟。你一定累喇,因為你忙咗一整天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「感謝上帝。但請進來。你一定累了,因為你忙了一整天。」

passages.original: “This is my friend, Dr. Watson. He has been of most vital use to me in several of my cases, and a lucky chance has made it possible for me to bring him out and associate him with this investigation.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我嘅朋友華生醫生。佢喺我嘅幾個案子裡幫咗極為重要嘅忙,一個幸運嘅機緣使我能夠帶佢出嚟,讓佢參與呢次調查。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我的朋友華生醫生。他在我的幾個案子裡幫了極為重要的忙,一個幸運的機緣使我能夠帶他出來,讓他參與這次調查。」

passages.original: “I am delighted to see you,” said she, pressing my hand warmly. “You will, I am sure, forgive anything that may be wanting in our arrangements, when you consider the blow which has come so suddenly upon us.”
passages.vernacular: 「見到你我好高興,」佢講,熱情地握住我嘅手。「我相信你會原諒我哋嘅安排中可能有嘅任何不周,如果你考慮到突然降臨喺我哋身上嘅打擊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「見到你我很高興,」她說,熱情地握著我的手。「我相信你會原諒我們的安排中可能有的任何不周,如果你考慮到突然降臨在我們身上的打擊。」

passages.original: “My dear madam,” said I, “I am an old campaigner, and if I were not I can very well see that no apology is needed. If I can be of any assistance, either to you or to my friend here, I shall be indeed happy.”
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅夫人,」我講,「我係個老戰士,即使唔係,我都完全睇得出不需要道歉。如果我能對你或我嘅朋友有任何幫助,我會好高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的夫人,」我說,「我是個老戰士,即使不是,我也完全看得出不需要道歉。如果我能對你或我的朋友有任何幫助,我會非常高興。」
