passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個高大的人,圓肩,大頭,寬闊而聰明的臉,下巴逐漸變尖,留著斑白褐色的尖鬍子。鼻子和面頰有一點紅,伸出的手有輕微顫抖,使人想起福爾摩斯對他習慣的推測。他那件生鏽的黑色長禮服外套前面一直扣上,領子翻起,瘦長的手腕從袖子裡伸出,看不到袖口或襯衫的痕跡。他說話緩慢而斷續,小心地選擇字眼,總體上給人的印象是一個學者和文人,在命運手中遭受了不公平的對待。

passages.original: “We have retained these things for some days,” said Holmes, “because we expected to see an advertisement from you giving your address. I am at a loss to know now why you did not advertise.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋保留呢啲嘢好幾天喇,」福爾摩斯講,「因為我哋期待睇到您登廣告留下地址。我而家不明白點解您冇登廣告。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們保留這些東西好幾天了,」福爾摩斯說,「因為我們期待看到您登廣告留下地址。我現在不明白為什麼您沒有登廣告。」

passages.original: Our visitor gave a rather shamefaced laugh. “Shillings have not been so plentiful with me as they once were,” he remarked. “I had no doubt that the gang of roughs who assaulted me had carried off both my hat and the bird. I did not care to spend more money in a hopeless attempt at recovering them.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅訪客有些羞愧地笑喇。「我手裡嘅先令不像從前咁多喇,」佢講。「我毫不懷疑襲擊我嘅嗰夥流氓把我嘅帽子同鵝都攞走喇。我唔願為一個無望嘅追回企圖花更多嘅錢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的訪客有些羞愧地笑了。「我手裡的先令不像從前那麼多了,」他說。「我毫不懷疑襲擊我的那夥流氓把我的帽子和鵝都拿走了。我不願為一個無望的追回企圖花更多的錢。」

passages.original: “Very naturally. By the way, about the bird, we were compelled to eat it.”
passages.vernacular: 「好自然。順便講,關於嗰隻鵝,我哋被迫把佢食喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很自然。順便說,關於那隻鵝,我們被迫把它吃了。」

passages.original: “To eat it!” Our visitor half rose from his chair in his excitement.
passages.vernacular: 「食喇!」我哋嘅訪客激動得從椅子上半站起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吃了!」我們的訪客激動得從椅子上半站起來。

passages.original: “Yes, it would have been of no use to anyone had we not done so. But I presume that this other goose upon the sideboard, which is about the same weight and perfectly fresh, will answer your purpose equally well?”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,如果我哋不咁樣做,佢對邊個都冇用。但我想,餐具櫃上嘅呢另一隻鵝,重量差不多,而且完全新鮮,對您同樣合用吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,如果我們不這樣做,它對誰都沒有用。但我想,餐具櫃上的這另一隻鵝,重量差不多,而且完全新鮮,對您同樣合用吧?」

passages.original: “Oh, certainly, certainly,” answered Mr. Baker with a sigh of relief.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,當然,當然,」貝克先生鬆咗一口氣回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,當然,當然,」貝克先生鬆了一口氣回答。

passages.original: “Of course, we still have the feathers, legs, crop, and so on of your own bird, so if you wish—”
passages.vernacular: 「當然,我哋仲保留住您嗰隻鵝嘅羽毛、腿、嗉囊等等,所以如果您想要嘅話——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,我們還保留著您那隻鵝的羽毛、腿、嗉囊等等,所以如果您想要的話——」

passages.original: The man burst into a hearty laugh. “They might be useful to me as relics of my adventure,” said he, “but beyond that I can hardly see what use the disjecta membra of my late acquaintance are going to be to me. No, sir, I think that, with your permission, I will confine my attentions to the excellent bird which I perceive upon the sideboard.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰人爆發出一陣痛快嘅笑聲。「佢哋作為我冒險嘅紀念品或者對我有用,」佢講,「但除此之外,我好難睇出我已故相識嘅殘肢對我有乜嘢用處。不,先生,我想,經您允許,我只把注意力放喺我睇到餐具櫃上嘅嗰隻優質嘅鵝上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人爆發出一陣痛快的笑聲。「它們作為我冒險的紀念品也許對我有用,」他說,「但除此之外,我很難看出我已故相識的殘肢對我有什麼用處。不,先生,我想,經您允許,我只把注意力放在我看到餐具櫃上的那隻優質的鵝上。」

passages.original: Sherlock Holmes glanced sharply across at me with a slight shrug of his shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯銳利地瞥咗我一眼,輕輕聳咗聳肩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯銳利地瞥了我一眼,輕輕聳了聳肩。

passages.original: “There is your hat, then, and there your bird,” said he. “By the way, would it bore you to tell me where you got the other one from? I am somewhat of a fowl fancier, and I have seldom seen a better grown goose.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁,您嘅帽子喺呢度,您嘅鵝喺嗰度,」佢講。「順便講,您能唔能夠不嫌煩地告訴我,另一隻您係從邊度得嚟嘅?我有點愛好家禽,好少見到長得更好嘅鵝。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,您的帽子在這裡,您的鵝在那裡,」他說。「順便說,您能不能不嫌煩地告訴我,另一隻您是從哪裡得來的?我有點愛好家禽,很少見到長得更好的鵝。」

passages.original: “Certainly, sir,” said Baker, who had risen and tucked his newly gained property under his arm. “There are a few of us who frequent the Alpha Inn, near the Museum—we are to be found in the Museum itself during the day, you understand. This year our good host, Windigate by name, instituted a goose club, by which, on consideration of some few pence every week, we were each to receive a bird at Christmas. My pence were duly paid, and the rest is familiar to you. I am much indebted to you, sir, for a Scotch bonnet is fitted neither to my years nor my gravity.” With a comical pomposity of manner he bowed solemnly to both of us and strode off upon his way.
passages.vernacular: 「當然,先生,」貝克講,佢已起身,把新得到嘅財物夾喺腋下。「我哋有幾個人常去博物館附近嘅阿爾法旅店——您知道,白天我哋可以喺博物館裡找到。今年我哋嘅好老闆,名叫溫迪蓋特,成立咗一個鵝俱樂部,每週付幾便士,我哋每人喺聖誕節得到一隻鵝。我嘅便士按時付喇,其餘嘅您都知道。先生,我好感謝您,因為蘇格蘭軟帽既不適合我嘅年紀,都不適合我嘅莊重。」佢以一種滑稽嘅誇張姿態,莊重地向我哋兩人鞠咗一躬,大步走上佢嘅路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,先生,」貝克說,他已起身,把新得到的財物夾在腋下。「我們有幾個人常去博物館附近的阿爾法旅店——您知道,白天我們可以在博物館裡找到。今年我們的好老闆,名叫溫迪蓋特,成立了一個鵝俱樂部,每週付幾便士,我們每人在聖誕節得到一隻鵝。我的便士按時付了,其餘的您都知道。先生,我非常感謝您,因為蘇格蘭軟帽既不適合我的年紀,也不適合我的莊重。」他以一種滑稽的誇張姿態,莊重地向我們兩人鞠了一躬,大步走上他的路。

passages.original: “So much for Mr. Henry Baker,” said Holmes when he had closed the door behind him. “It is quite certain that he knows nothing whatever about the matter. Are you hungry, Watson?”
passages.vernacular: 「亨利·貝克先生就講咁多,」福爾摩斯喺佢身後關上門時講。「完全可以肯定佢對呢件事一無所知。你餓嗎,華生?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「亨利·貝克先生就說這麼多,」福爾摩斯在他身後關上門時說。「完全可以肯定他對這件事一無所知。你餓嗎,華生?」

passages.original: “Not particularly.”
passages.vernacular: 「不特別餓。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不特別餓。」

passages.original: “Then I suggest that we turn our dinner into a supper and follow up this clue while it is still hot.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁我建議我哋把晚餐改成夜宵,趁熱追蹤呢條線索。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼我建議我們把晚餐改成夜宵,趁熱追蹤這條線索。」

passages.original: “By all means.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然可以。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然可以。」

passages.original: It was a bitter night, so we drew on our ulsters and wrapped cravats about our throats. Outside, the stars were shining coldly in a cloudless sky, and the breath of the passers-by blew out into smoke like so many pistol shots. Our footfalls rang out crisply and loudly as we swung through the doctors’ quarter, Wimpole Street, Harley Street, and so through Wigmore Street into Oxford Street. In a quarter of an hour we were in Bloomsbury at the Alpha Inn, which is a small public-house at the corner of one of the streets which runs down into Holborn. Holmes pushed open the door of the private bar and ordered two glasses of beer from the ruddy-faced, white-aproned landlord.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一個刺骨嘅夜晚,所以我哋穿上長大衣,脖子上圍上領巾。外面,星星喺無雲嘅天空中冷冷地閃住光,行人嘅呼吸像許多手槍嘅槍聲一樣噴成煙霧。我哋走過醫生區域,韋爾貝克街、哈利街,然後經威格莫爾街進入牛津街時,腳步聲清脆而響亮。一刻鐘內,我哋到咗布盧姆茨伯里嘅阿爾法旅店,呢個係一家小酒館,位於一條通往霍爾本嘅街角。福爾摩斯推開私人酒吧嘅門,向紅臉、穿白圍裙嘅老闆要咗兩杯啤酒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一個刺骨的夜晚,所以我們穿上長大衣,脖子上圍上領巾。外面,星星在無雲的天空中冷冷地閃著光,行人的呼吸像許多手槍的槍聲一樣噴成煙霧。我們走過醫生區域,韋爾貝克街、哈利街,然後經威格莫爾街進入牛津街時,腳步聲清脆而響亮。一刻鐘內,我們到了布盧姆茨伯里的阿爾法旅店,這是一家小酒館,位於一條通往霍爾本的街角。福爾摩斯推開私人酒吧的門,向紅臉、穿白圍裙的老闆要了兩杯啤酒。

passages.original: “Your beer should be excellent if it is as good as your geese,” said he.
passages.vernacular: 「如果您嘅啤酒像您嘅鵝一樣好,嗰就應該好棒,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果您的啤酒像您的鵝一樣好,那就應該非常棒,」他說。

passages.original: “My geese!” The man seemed surprised.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅鵝!」嗰人似乎好驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的鵝!」那人似乎很驚訝。

passages.original: “Yes. I was speaking only half an hour ago to Mr. Henry Baker, who was a member of your goose club.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。半小時前我剛同亨利·貝克先生講過話,佢係您鵝俱樂部嘅成員。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。半小時前我剛同亨利·貝克先生說過話,他是您鵝俱樂部的成員。」

passages.original: “Ah! yes, I see. But you see, sir, them’s not our geese.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊!係嘅,我明白喇。但係您睇,先生,嗰啲唔係我哋嘅鵝。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!是的,我明白了。但是您看,先生,那些不是我們的鵝。」

passages.original: “Indeed! Whose, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅!咁係邊個嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的!那麼是誰的?」

passages.original: “Well, I got the two dozen from a salesman in Covent Garden.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我從科文特花園嘅一個推銷員嗰度攞咗兩打。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我從科文特花園的一個推銷員那裡拿了兩打。」

passages.original: “Indeed? I know some of them. Which was it?”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅?我認識佢哋中嘅啲人。係邊一個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的?我認識他們中的一些人。是哪一個?」

passages.original: “Breckinridge is his name.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢嘅名字係布雷肯里奇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他的名字是布雷肯里奇。」

passages.original: “Ah! I don’t know him. Well, here’s your good health landlord, and prosperity to your house. Good-night.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊!我不認識佢。好,祝您健康,老闆,祝您嘅店生意興隆。晚安。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!我不認識他。好,祝您健康,老闆,祝您的店生意興隆。晚安。」

passages.original: “Now for Mr. Breckinridge,” he continued, buttoning up his coat as we came out into the frosty air. “Remember, Watson that though we have so homely a thing as a goose at one end of this chain, we have at the other a man who will certainly get seven years’ penal servitude unless we can establish his innocence. It is possible that our inquiry may but confirm his guilt; but, in any case, we have a line of investigation which has been missed by the police, and which a singular chance has placed in our hands. Let us follow it out to the bitter end. Faces to the south, then, and quick march!”
passages.vernacular: 「而家去找布雷肯里奇先生,」佢繼續講,我哋走到結霜嘅空氣中時,佢扣上外套。「記住,華生,雖然我哋喺呢條鏈子嘅一端有鵝咁樣家常嘅嘢,喺另一端卻有一個人,除非我哋能證明佢無辜,否則佢肯定會被判七年苦役。我哋嘅調查可能只係證實佢有罪;但無論如何,我哋有一條警察錯過嘅調查線索,係一個奇特嘅機緣放喺我哋手中嘅。讓我哋追到底。咁面向南,快步前進!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在去找布雷肯里奇先生,」他繼續說,我們走到結霜的空氣中時,他扣上外套。「記住,華生,雖然我們在這條鏈子的一端有鵝這樣家常的東西,在另一端卻有一個人,除非我們能證明他無辜,否則他肯定會被判七年苦役。我們的調查可能只是證實他有罪;但無論如何,我們有一條警察錯過的調查線索,是一個奇特的機緣放在我們手中的。讓我們追到底。那麼面向南,快步前進!」

passages.original: We passed across Holborn, down Endell Street, and so through a zigzag of slums to Covent Garden Market. One of the largest stalls bore the name of Breckinridge upon it, and the proprietor a horsey-looking man, with a sharp face and trim side-whiskers was helping a boy to put up the shutters.
passages.vernacular: 我哋穿過霍爾本,走下恩德爾街,然後穿過曲折嘅貧民窟,到科文特花園市場。一個最大嘅攤位上有布雷肯里奇嘅名字,店主係個像馬販子模樣嘅人,臉尖,留住整齊嘅絡腮鬍,正在幫一個男孩關百葉板。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們穿過霍爾本,走下恩德爾街,然後穿過曲折的貧民窟,到科文特花園市場。一個最大的攤位上有布雷肯里奇的名字,店主是個像馬販子模樣的人,臉尖,留著整齊的絡腮鬍,正在幫一個男孩關百葉板。

passages.original: “Good-evening. It’s a cold night,” said Holmes.
passages.vernacular: 「晚上好。今晚好冷,」福爾摩斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「晚上好。今晚很冷,」福爾摩斯說。

passages.original: The salesman nodded and shot a questioning glance at my companion.
passages.vernacular: 推銷員點點頭,向我嘅同伴投去一個詢問嘅眼光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 推銷員點點頭,向我的同伴投去一個詢問的眼光。

passages.original: “Sold out of geese, I see,” continued Holmes, pointing at the bare slabs of marble.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇鵝賣完喇,」福爾摩斯繼續講,指住光禿禿嘅大理石板。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看鵝賣完了,」福爾摩斯繼續說,指著光禿禿的大理石板。

passages.original: “Let you have five hundred to-morrow morning.”
passages.vernacular: 「聽日早晨可以畀你五百隻。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「明天早晨可以給你五百隻。」

passages.original: “That’s no good.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰冇用。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那沒用。」

passages.original: “Well, there are some on the stall with the gas-flare.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰個有煤氣燈嘅攤位上有啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那個有煤氣燈的攤位上有一些。」

passages.original: “Ah, but I was recommended to you.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,但有人向我推薦你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,但有人向我推薦你。」

passages.original: “Who by?”
passages.vernacular: 「邊個推薦嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰推薦的?」

passages.original: “The landlord of the Alpha.”
passages.vernacular: 「阿爾法旅店嘅老闆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「阿爾法旅店的老闆。」

passages.original: “Oh, yes; I sent him a couple of dozen.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅;我畀咗佢兩打。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的;我給了他兩打。」

passages.original: “Fine birds they were, too. Now where did you get them from?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰啲鵝都係好鵝。而家你係從邊度弄嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那些鵝也是好鵝。現在你是從哪裡弄來的?」

passages.original: To my surprise the question provoked a burst of anger from the salesman.
passages.vernacular: 令我食驚嘅係,呢個問題引起推銷員一陣怒氣爆發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令我吃驚的是,這個問題引起推銷員一陣怒氣爆發。

passages.original: “Now, then, mister,” said he, with his head cocked and his arms akimbo, “what are you driving at? Let’s have it straight, now.”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,先生,」佢講,頭歪向一邊,雙手叉腰,「你想講乜嘢?而家直講吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,先生,」他說,頭歪向一邊,雙手叉腰,「你想說什麼?現在直說吧。」

passages.original: “It is straight enough. I should like to know who sold you the geese which you supplied to the Alpha.”
passages.vernacular: 「已經夠直喇。我想知道係邊個把你供應畀阿爾法嘅鵝賣畀你嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「已經夠直了。我想知道是誰把你供應給阿爾法的鵝賣給你的。」

passages.original: “Well then, I shan’t tell you. So now!”
passages.vernacular: 「哼,嗰我不告訴你。就咁樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,那我不告訴你。就這樣!」

passages.original: “Oh, it is a matter of no importance; but I don’t know why you should be so warm over such a trifle.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,呢個係無關緊要嘅事;但我唔知道你點解為咁樣嘅小事咁火大。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,這是無關緊要的事;但我不知道你為什麼為這樣的小事這麼火大。」

passages.original: “Warm! You’d be as warm, maybe, if you were as pestered as I am. When I pay good money for a good article there should be an end of the business; but it’s ‘Where are the geese?’ and ‘Who did you sell the geese to?’ and ‘What will you take for the geese?’ One would think they were the only geese in the world, to hear the fuss that is made over them.”
passages.vernacular: 「火大!如果你像我一樣被糾纏,或者你都會咁火大。我付咗好錢買好貨,事情就該了結;但卻係『鵝喺邊度?』、『你把鵝賣畀邊個喇?』、『你要乜嘢價賣鵝?』聽人哋為佢哋大驚小怪,你仲以為佢哋係世上唯一嘅鵝呢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「火大!如果你像我一樣被糾纏,也許你也會這麼火大。我付了好錢買好貨,事情就該了結;但卻是『鵝在哪裡?』、『你把鵝賣給誰了?』、『你要什麼價賣鵝?』聽人們為它們大驚小怪,你還以為它們是世上唯一的鵝呢。」

passages.original: “Well, I have no connection with any other people who have been making inquiries,” said Holmes carelessly. “If you won’t tell us the bet is off, that is all. But I’m always ready to back my opinion on a matter of fowls, and I have a fiver on it that the bird I ate is country bred.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我同其他進行詢問嘅人毫無關係,」福爾摩斯漫不經心地講。「如果你不告訴我哋,嗰賭就取消,就係咁樣。但我總是準備好喺家禽嘅事情上支持我嘅睇法,我賭五鎊,我食嘅嗰隻鵝係鄉下養嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我和其他進行詢問的人毫無關係,」福爾摩斯漫不經心地說。「如果你不告訴我們,那賭就取消,就是這樣。但我總是準備好在家禽的事情上支持我的看法,我賭五鎊,我吃的那隻鵝是鄉下養的。」

passages.original: “Well, then, you’ve lost your fiver, for it’s town bred,” snapped the salesman.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰你輸咗你嘅五鎊,因為係城裡養嘅,」推銷員厲聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那你輸了你的五鎊,因為是城裡養的,」推銷員厲聲說。

passages.original: “It’s nothing of the kind.”
passages.vernacular: 「根本唔係咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「根本不是這樣。」

passages.original: “I say it is.”
passages.vernacular: 「我講係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說是。」

passages.original: “I don’t believe it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不信。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不信。」

passages.original: “D’you think you know more about fowls than I, who have handled them ever since I was a nipper? I tell you, all those birds that went to the Alpha were town bred.”
passages.vernacular: 「你以為你比我更懂家禽嗎?我從定係小細路起就經手佢哋。我告訴你,所有送到阿爾法嘅鵝都係城裡養嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你以為你比我更懂家禽嗎?我從還是小孩子起就經手它們。我告訴你,所有送到阿爾法的鵝都是城裡養的。」

passages.original: “You’ll never persuade me to believe that.”
passages.vernacular: 「你永遠講服不咗我相信呢個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你永遠說服不了我相信這個。」

passages.original: “Will you bet, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你賭嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你賭嗎?」

passages.original: “It’s merely taking your money, for I know that I am right. But I’ll have a sovereign on with you, just to teach you not to be obstinate.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢只係攞你嘅錢,因為我知道我係對嘅。但我跟你賭一個索維林,只係教你唔好固執。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這只是拿你的錢,因為我知道我是對的。但我跟你賭一個索維林,只是教你不要固執。」

passages.original: The salesman chuckled grimly. “Bring me the books, Bill,” said he.
passages.vernacular: 推銷員陰沉地咯咯笑喇。「把賬本攞嚟,比爾,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 推銷員陰沉地咯咯笑了。「把賬本拿來,比爾,」他說。

passages.original: The small boy brought round a small thin volume and a great greasy-backed one, laying them out together beneath the hanging lamp.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個小男孩攞嚟一本小而薄嘅簿子同一本背面油膩嘅大簿子,把佢哋一起放喺吊燈下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個小男孩拿來一本小而薄的簿子和一本背面油膩的大簿子,把它們一起放在吊燈下。

passages.original: “Now then, Mr. Cocksure,” said the salesman, “I thought that I was out of geese, but before I finish you’ll find that there is still one left in my shop. You see this little book?”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,自以為係先生,」推銷員講,「我以為我嘅鵝賣完喇,但喺我講完之前,你會發現我店裡仲剩一隻。你睇到呢本小簿子嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,自以為是先生,」推銷員說,「我以為我的鵝賣完了,但在我說完之前,你會發現我店裡還剩一隻。你看到這本小簿子嗎?」

passages.original: “Well?”
passages.vernacular: 「點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了?」

passages.original: “That’s the list of the folk from whom I buy. D’you see? Well, then, here on this page are the country folk, and the numbers after their names are where their accounts are in the big ledger. Now, then! You see this other page in red ink? Well, that is a list of my town suppliers. Now, look at that third name. Just read it out to me.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我從中買貨嘅人嘅名單。你睇見咗嗎?嗯,呢一頁係鄉下人,佢哋名字後面嘅數字係佢哋嘅賬目喺大賬本裡嘅位置。而家!你睇到呢另一頁用紅墨水寫嘅嗎?嗯,嗰個係我嘅城裡供應商嘅名單。而家,睇第三個名字。念畀我聽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我從中買貨的人的名單。你看見了嗎?嗯,這一頁是鄉下人,他們名字後面的數字是他們的賬目在大賬本裡的位置。現在!你看到這另一頁用紅墨水寫的嗎?嗯,那是我的城裡供應商的名單。現在,看第三個名字。念給我聽。」

passages.original: “Mrs. Oakshott, 117, Brixton Road—249,” read Holmes.
passages.vernacular: 「奧克肖特太太,布里克斯頓路117號——249,」福爾摩斯念道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奧克肖特太太,布里克斯頓路117號——249,」福爾摩斯念道。

passages.original: “Quite so. Now turn that up in the ledger.”
passages.vernacular: 「完全正確。而家喺大賬本裡翻到嗰個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「完全正確。現在在大賬本裡翻到那個。」

passages.original: Holmes turned to the page indicated. “Here you are, ‘Mrs. Oakshott, 117, Brixton Road, egg and poultry supplier.’”
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯翻到指定嘅嗰一頁。「喺呢度,『奧克肖特太太,布里克斯頓路117號,蛋類同家禽供應商。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯翻到指定的那一頁。「在這裡,『奧克肖特太太,布里克斯頓路117號,蛋類和家禽供應商。』」

passages.original: “Now, then, what’s the last entry?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁,最後一項係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,最後一項是什麼?」

passages.original: “‘December 22nd. Twenty-four geese at 7s. 6d.’”
passages.vernacular: 「『12月22日。二十四隻鵝,每隻七先令六便士。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『12月22日。二十四隻鵝,每隻七先令六便士。』」

passages.original: “Quite so. There you are. And underneath?”
passages.vernacular: 「完全正確。就係咁樣。下面呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「完全正確。就是這樣。下面呢?」

passages.original: “‘Sold to Mr. Windigate of the Alpha, at 12s.’”
passages.vernacular: 「『以十二先令嘅價格賣畀阿爾法嘅溫迪蓋特先生。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『以十二先令的價格賣給阿爾法的溫迪蓋特先生。』」

passages.original: “What have you to say now?”
passages.vernacular: 「你而家有乜嘢好講嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你現在有什麼好說的?」

passages.original: Sherlock Holmes looked deeply chagrined. He drew a sovereign from his pocket and threw it down upon the slab, turning away with the air of a man whose disgust is too deep for words. A few yards off he stopped under a lamp-post and laughed in the hearty, noiseless fashion which was peculiar to him.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯顯得好懊惱。佢從口袋裡攞出一個索維林,扔喺大理石板上,轉身離去,神態像一個厭惡得無法用言語表達嘅人。喺幾碼外,佢喺一根燈柱下停下,以佢特有嘅嗰種痛快而無聲嘅方式笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯顯得非常懊惱。他從口袋裡拿出一個索維林,扔在大理石板上,轉身離去,神態像一個厭惡得無法用言語表達的人。在幾碼外,他在一根燈柱下停下,以他特有的那種痛快而無聲的方式笑了。

passages.original: “When you see a man with whiskers of that cut and the ‘Pink ’un’ protruding out of his pocket, you can always draw him by a bet,” said he. “I daresay that if I had put £ 100 down in front of him, that man would not have given me such complete information as was drawn from him by the idea that he was doing me on a wager. Well, Watson, we are, I fancy, nearing the end of our quest, and the only point which remains to be determined is whether we should go on to this Mrs. Oakshott to-night, or whether we should reserve it for to-morrow. It is clear from what that surly fellow said that there are others besides ourselves who are anxious about the matter, and I should—”
passages.vernacular: 「當你睇到一個留住嗰種形狀嘅絡腮鬍、口袋裡露出《粉紅報》嘅人,你總是可以用打賭引佢上鉤,」佢講。「我敢講,即使我喺佢面前放一百鎊,嗰人都唔會畀我像佢因為以為喺打賭中贏我而被引出嘅咁完整嘅資料。好,華生,我想我哋嘅探索接近尾聲喇,剩下需要決定嘅唯一啲係,我哋今晚係咪要去找呢位奧克肖特太太,定係留到聽日。從嗰個脾氣壞嘅傢伙所講嘅話睇得好清楚,除咗我哋之外,仲有別人都為呢件事焦急,而我應該——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當你看到一個留著那種形狀的絡腮鬍、口袋裡露出《粉紅報》的人,你總是可以用打賭引他上鉤,」他說。「我敢說,即使我在他面前放一百鎊,那人也不會給我像他因為以為在打賭中贏我而被引出的那麼完整的資料。好,華生,我想我們的探索接近尾聲了,剩下需要決定的唯一一點是,我們今晚是否要去找這位奧克肖特太太,還是留到明天。從那個脾氣壞的傢伙所說的話看得很清楚,除了我們之外,還有別人也為這件事焦急,而我應該——」

passages.original: His remarks were suddenly cut short by a loud hubbub which broke out from the stall which we had just left. Turning round we saw a little rat-faced fellow standing in the centre of the circle of yellow light which was thrown by the swinging lamp, while Breckinridge, the salesman, framed in the door of his stall, was shaking his fists fiercely at the cringing figure.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅話突然被我哋剛離開嘅嗰個攤位爆發出嘅一陣大喧鬧打斷。轉過身,我哋睇見一個長住老鼠臉嘅小個子站喺搖晃嘅燈投下嘅黃色光圈中央,而推銷員布雷肯里奇站喺佢攤位嘅門框裡,凶狠地對住嗰個畏縮嘅身影揮舞拳頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的話突然被我們剛離開的那個攤位爆發出的一陣大喧鬧打斷。轉過身,我們看見一個長著老鼠臉的小個子站在搖晃的燈投下的黃色光圈中央,而推銷員布雷肯里奇站在他攤位的門框裡,凶狠地對著那個畏縮的身影揮舞拳頭。

passages.original: “I’ve had enough of you and your geese,” he shouted. “I wish you were all at the devil together. If you come pestering me any more with your silly talk I’ll set the dog at you. You bring Mrs. Oakshott here and I’ll answer her, but what have you to do with it? Did I buy the geese off you?”
passages.vernacular: 「我受夠咗你同你嘅鵝,」佢喊道。「我希望你哋全都一起去見鬼。如果你再用你嗰愚蠢嘅話嚟糾纏我,我就放狗咬你。你把奧克肖特太太帶到呢度嚟,我嚟回答佢,但你有乜嘢關係?我係從你嗰度買嘅鵝嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我受夠了你和你的鵝,」他喊道。「我希望你們全都一起去見鬼。如果你再用你那愚蠢的話來糾纏我,我就放狗咬你。你把奧克肖特太太帶到這裡來,我來回答她,但你有什麼關係?我是從你那裡買的鵝嗎?」

passages.original: “No; but one of them was mine all the same,” whined the little man.
passages.vernacular: 「唔係;但其中有一隻定係我嘅,」小個子哀聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是;但其中有一隻還是我的,」小個子哀聲說。

passages.original: “Well, then, ask Mrs. Oakshott for it.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁,向奧克肖特太太要去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,向奧克肖特太太要去。」

passages.original: “She told me to ask you.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢叫我問你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她叫我問你。」

passages.original: “Well, you can ask the King of Proosia, for all I care. I’ve had enough of it. Get out of this!” He rushed fiercely forward, and the inquirer flitted away into the darkness.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你可以去問普魯士國王,我才不管。我受夠喇。滾開!」佢凶狠地衝上前去,嗰個詢問者閃身消失喺黑暗中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你可以去問普魯士國王,我才不管。我受夠了。滾開!」他凶狠地衝上前去,那個詢問者閃身消失在黑暗中。

passages.original: “Ha! this may save us a visit to Brixton Road,” whispered Holmes. “Come with me, and we will see what is to be made of this fellow.” Striding through the scattered knots of people who lounged round the flaring stalls, my companion speedily overtook the little man and touched him upon the shoulder. He sprang round, and I could see in the gas-light that every vestige of colour had been driven from his face.
passages.vernacular: 「哈!呢或者可以省去我哋去布里克斯頓路嘅一趟,」福爾摩斯低聲講。「跟我嚟,我哋睇睇能從呢個傢伙身上弄出乜嘢。」佢大步穿過喺火光閃爍嘅攤位周圍閒逛嘅零散人群,我嘅同伴迅速追上咗嗰個小個子,喺佢肩上拍咗一下。佢猛地轉過身,我借住煤氣燈光睇到,佢臉上所有嘅血色都消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈!這也許可以省去我們去布里克斯頓路的一趟,」福爾摩斯低聲說。「跟我來,我們看看能從這個傢伙身上弄出什麼。」他大步穿過在火光閃爍的攤位周圍閒逛的零散人群,我的同伴迅速追上了那個小個子,在他肩上拍了一下。他猛地轉過身,我借著煤氣燈光看到,他臉上所有的血色都消失了。

passages.original: “Who are you, then? What do you want?” he asked in a quavering voice.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你係邊個?你想要乜嘢?」佢用顫抖嘅聲音問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你是誰?你想要什麼?」他用顫抖的聲音問。

passages.original: “You will excuse me,” said Holmes blandly, “but I could not help overhearing the questions which you put to the salesman just now. I think that I could be of assistance to you.”
passages.vernacular: 「請原諒,」福爾摩斯溫和地講,「但我不由自主地聽到咗你頭先向推銷員提出嘅問題。我想我可以幫你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請原諒,」福爾摩斯溫和地說,「但我不由自主地聽到了你剛才向推銷員提出的問題。我想我可以幫你。」

passages.original: “You? Who are you? How could you know anything of the matter?”
passages.vernacular: 「你?你係邊個?你點可能知道呢件事?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你?你是誰?你怎麼可能知道這件事?」

passages.original: “My name is Sherlock Holmes. It is my business to know what other people don’t know.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅名字係夏洛克·福爾摩斯。我嘅職業就係知道別人唔知道嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的名字是夏洛克·福爾摩斯。我的職業就是知道別人不知道的事。」

passages.original: “But you can know nothing of this?”
passages.vernacular: 「但你唔可能知道呢件事吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你不可能知道這件事吧?」

passages.original: “Excuse me, I know everything of it. You are endeavouring to trace some geese which were sold by Mrs. Oakshott, of Brixton Road, to a salesman named Breckinridge, by him in turn to Mr. Windigate, of the Alpha, and by him to his club, of which Mr. Henry Baker is a member.”
passages.vernacular: 「對不起,我對佢無所唔知。你正在設法追蹤啲鵝,佢哋係由布里克斯頓路嘅奧克肖特太太賣畀一個叫布雷肯里奇嘅推銷員,佢又轉賣畀阿爾法旅店嘅溫迪蓋特先生,溫迪蓋特再轉畀佢嘅俱樂部,亨利·貝克先生係會員。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對不起,我對它無所不知。你正在設法追蹤一些鵝,它們是由布里克斯頓路的奧克肖特太太賣給一個叫布雷肯里奇的推銷員,他又轉賣給阿爾法旅店的溫迪蓋特先生,溫迪蓋特再轉給他的俱樂部,亨利·貝克先生是會員。」

passages.original: “Oh, sir, you are the very man whom I have longed to meet,” cried the little fellow with outstretched hands and quivering fingers. “I can hardly explain to you how interested I am in this matter.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,先生,你正是我渴望見到嘅人,」嗰小個子喊道,伸出雙手,手指顫抖。「我簡直無法向你解釋我對呢件事幾咁關切。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,先生,你正是我渴望見到的人,」那小個子喊道,伸出雙手,手指顫抖。「我簡直無法向你解釋我對這件事多麼關切。」

passages.original: Sherlock Holmes hailed a four-wheeler which was passing. “In that case we had better discuss it in a cosy room rather than in this wind-swept market-place,” said he. “But pray tell me, before we go farther, who it is that I have the pleasure of assisting.”
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯招呼咗一輛經過嘅四輪馬車。「嗰樣嘅話,我哋最好喺一個舒適嘅房間裡討論,而唔係喺呢個風吹嘅市場裡,」佢講。「但喺我哋往下走之前,請告訴我我有幸幫助嘅係邊一位。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯招呼了一輛經過的四輪馬車。「那樣的話,我們最好在一個舒適的房間裡討論,而不是在這個風吹的市場裡,」他說。「但在我們往下走之前,請告訴我我有幸幫助的是哪一位。」

passages.original: The man hesitated for an instant. “My name is John Robinson,” he answered with a sidelong glance.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人猶豫咗片刻。「我名叫約翰·羅賓遜,」佢斜瞥咗一眼回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人猶豫了片刻。「我名叫約翰·羅賓遜,」他斜瞥了一眼回答。

passages.original: “No, no; the real name,” said Holmes sweetly. “It is always awkward doing business with an alias.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,不;真名,」福爾摩斯溫和地講。「同用化名嘅人做生意總是尷尬嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不;真名,」福爾摩斯溫和地說。「同用化名的人做生意總是尷尬的。」

passages.original: A flush sprang to the white cheeks of the stranger. “Well then,” said he, “my real name is James Ryder.”
passages.vernacular: 陌生人蒼白嘅雙頰上泛起一陣紅暈。「咁,」佢講,「我嘅真名係詹姆斯·賴德。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 陌生人蒼白的雙頰上泛起一陣紅暈。「那麼,」他說,「我的真名是詹姆斯·賴德。」

passages.original: “Precisely so. Head attendant at the Hotel Cosmopolitan. Pray step into the cab, and I shall soon be able to tell you everything which you would wish to know.”
passages.vernacular: 「正是。世界主義酒店嘅首席侍者。請上馬車,我好快就能告訴你你想知道嘅一切。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「正是。世界主義酒店的首席侍者。請上馬車,我很快就能告訴你你想知道的一切。」

passages.original: The little man stood glancing from one to the other of us with half-frightened, half-hopeful eyes, as one who is not sure whether he is on the verge of a windfall or of a catastrophe. Then he stepped into the cab, and in half an hour we were back in the sitting-room at Baker Street. Nothing had been said during our drive, but the high, thin breathing of our new companion, and the claspings and unclaspings of his hands, spoke of the nervous tension within him.
passages.vernacular: 小個子站住,以半係害怕、半係希望嘅目光睇住我哋兩個,像一個不確定自己係處於意外之財定係災難邊緣嘅人。然後佢上咗馬車,半小時後我哋回到咗貝克街嘅起居室。喺我哋嘅車程中冇講過話,但我哋新同伴高而細嘅呼吸,同佢雙手嘅緊握同鬆開,講明了佢內心嘅神經緊張。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小個子站著,以半是害怕、半是希望的目光看著我們兩個,像一個不確定自己是處於意外之財還是災難邊緣的人。然後他上了馬車,半小時後我們回到了貝克街的起居室。在我們的車程中沒有說過話,但我們新同伴高而細的呼吸,和他雙手的緊握與鬆開,說明了他內心的神經緊張。

passages.original: “Here we are!” said Holmes cheerily as we filed into the room. “The fire looks very seasonable in this weather. You look cold, Mr. Ryder. Pray take the basket-chair. I will just put on my slippers before we settle this little matter of yours. Now, then! You want to know what became of those geese?”
passages.vernacular: 「到喇!」我哋魚貫走進房間時,福爾摩斯愉快地講。「呢爐火喺呢種天氣裡顯得好合時宜。賴德先生,你睇起嚟好冷。請坐嗰張藤椅。喺解決你呢件小事之前,我先穿上拖鞋。好喇!你想知道嗰啲鵝後來點樣喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「到了!」我們魚貫走進房間時,福爾摩斯愉快地說。「這爐火在這種天氣裡顯得很合時宜。賴德先生,你看起來很冷。請坐那張藤椅。在解決你這件小事之前,我先穿上拖鞋。好了!你想知道那些鵝後來怎樣了?」

passages.original: “Yes, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生。」

passages.original: “Or rather, I fancy, of that goose. It was one bird, I imagine in which you were interested—white, with a black bar across the tail.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者更確切地講,我想,係嗰隻鵝。我想你感興趣嘅係一隻——白嘅,尾巴上有一道黑條。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「或者更確切地說,我想,是那隻鵝。我想你感興趣的是一隻——白的,尾巴上有一道黑條。」

passages.original: Ryder quivered with emotion. “Oh, sir,” he cried, “can you tell me where it went to?”
passages.vernacular: 賴德激動得顫抖。「哦,先生,」佢喊道,「你能告訴我佢到邊度去咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 賴德激動得顫抖。「哦,先生,」他喊道,「你能告訴我它到哪裡去了嗎?」

passages.original: “It came here.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢嚟到呢度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它來到這裡。」

passages.original: “Here?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡?」

passages.original: “Yes, and a most remarkable bird it proved. I don’t wonder that you should take an interest in it. It laid an egg after it was dead—the bonniest, brightest little blue egg that ever was seen. I have it here in my museum.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,事實證明佢係一隻最了不起嘅鵝。你對佢感興趣,我並不奇怪。佢死後仲下咗一個蛋——係人哋見過嘅最漂亮、最明亮嘅藍色小蛋。我把佢放喺我呢度嘅博物館裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,事實證明它是一隻最了不起的鵝。你對它感興趣,我並不奇怪。它死後還下了一個蛋——是人們見過的最漂亮、最明亮的藍色小蛋。我把它放在我這裡的博物館裡。」

passages.original: Our visitor staggered to his feet and clutched the mantelpiece with his right hand. Holmes unlocked his strong-box and held up the blue carbuncle, which shone out like a star, with a cold, brilliant, many-pointed radiance. Ryder stood glaring with a drawn face, uncertain whether to claim or to disown it.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅訪客踉蹌地站起嚟,右手抓住壁爐台。福爾摩斯打開保險箱,舉起嗰塊藍寶石,佢像星星一樣閃耀,發出冷冽、輝煌、多角嘅光芒。賴德站住,表情抽搐地瞪住,不確定係該認領定係咪認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的訪客踉蹌地站起來,右手抓住壁爐台。福爾摩斯打開保險箱,舉起那塊藍寶石,它像星星一樣閃耀,發出冷冽、輝煌、多角的光芒。賴德站著,表情抽搐地瞪著,不確定是該認領還是否認。

passages.original: “The game’s up, Ryder,” said Holmes quietly. “Hold up, man, or you’ll be into the fire! Give him an arm back into his chair, Watson. He’s not got blood enough to go in for felony with impunity. Give him a dash of brandy. So! Now he looks a little more human. What a shrimp it is, to be sure!”
passages.vernacular: 「遊戲結束喇,賴德,」福爾摩斯平靜地講。「站穩,老兄,否則你要掉進火裡喇!華生,扶佢一把,讓佢回到椅子上。佢嘅血仲唔夠多,唔能夠肆無忌憚地去犯重罪。畀佢灌點白蘭地。好喇!而家佢睇起嚟更像人喇。真係個小蝦米!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「遊戲結束了,賴德,」福爾摩斯平靜地說。「站穩,老兄,否則你要掉進火裡了!華生,扶他一把,讓他回到椅子上。他的血還不夠多,不能肆無忌憚地去犯重罪。給他灌點白蘭地。好了!現在他看起來更像人了。真是個小蝦米!」

passages.original: For a moment he had staggered and nearly fallen, but the brandy brought a tinge of colour into his cheeks, and he sat staring with frightened eyes at his accuser.
passages.vernacular: 佢有一刻踉蹌住幾乎倒下,但白蘭地使佢臉頰有咗啲血色,佢坐住,用驚恐嘅眼睛瞪住指控佢嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有一刻踉蹌著幾乎倒下,但白蘭地使他臉頰有了一點血色,他坐著,用驚恐的眼睛瞪著指控他的人。

passages.original: “I have almost every link in my hands, and all the proofs which I could possibly need, so there is little which you need tell me. Still, that little may as well be cleared up to make the case complete. You had heard, Ryder, of this blue stone of the Countess of Morcar’s?”
passages.vernacular: 「我手中幾乎握有每一環,以及我可能需要嘅所有證據,所以你需要告訴我嘅好少。不過,嗰啲都不妨澄清,使案情完整。賴德,你聽講過莫卡伯爵夫人嘅呢塊藍寶石?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我手中幾乎握有每一環,以及我可能需要的所有證據,所以你需要告訴我的很少。不過,那一點也不妨澄清,使案情完整。賴德,你聽說過莫卡伯爵夫人的這塊藍寶石?」

passages.original: “It was Catherine Cusack who told me of it,” said he in a crackling voice.
passages.vernacular: 「係凱瑟琳·庫薩克告訴我嘅,」佢用嘶啞嘅聲音講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是凱瑟琳·庫薩克告訴我的,」他用嘶啞的聲音說。

passages.original: “I see—her ladyship’s waiting-maid. Well, the temptation of sudden wealth so easily acquired was too much for you, as it has been for better men before you; but you were not very scrupulous in the means you used. It seems to me, Ryder, that there is the making of a very pretty villain in you. You knew that this man Horner, the plumber, had been concerned in some such matter before, and that suspicion would rest the more readily upon him. What did you do, then? You made some small job in my lady’s room—you and your confederate Cusack—and you managed that he should be the man sent for. Then, when he had left, you rifled the jewel-case, raised the alarm, and had this unfortunate man arrested. You then—”
passages.vernacular: 「我明白喇——夫人嘅侍女。嗯,突然發財、輕易得手嘅誘惑對你來講太大喇,正如佢對你之前更好嘅人一樣;但你所用嘅手段不太謹慎。賴德,我覺得你身上有成為一個相當漂亮嘅惡棍嘅素質。你知道呢個水管工霍納以前涉及過類似嘅事,懷疑會更容易落喺佢身上。嗰你做咗乜嘢?你同你嘅同夥庫薩克,喺夫人嘅房間裡製造咗啲活兒,並設法讓佢成為被派去嘅人。然後,喺佢離開後,你洗劫咗珠寶盒,發出警報,讓呢個不幸嘅人被捕。你接住——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我明白了——夫人的侍女。嗯,突然發財、輕易得手的誘惑對你來說太大了,正如它對你之前更好的人一樣;但你所用的手段不太謹慎。賴德,我覺得你身上有成為一個相當漂亮的惡棍的素質。你知道這個水管工霍納以前涉及過類似的事,懷疑會更容易落在他身上。那你做了什麼?你和你的同夥庫薩克,在夫人的房間裡製造了一點活兒,並設法讓他成為被派去的人。然後,在他離開後,你洗劫了珠寶盒,發出警報,讓這個不幸的人被捕。你接著——」

passages.original: Ryder threw himself down suddenly upon the rug and clutched at my companion’s knees. “For God’s sake, have mercy!” he shrieked. “Think of my father! Of my mother! It would break their hearts. I never went wrong before! I never will again. I swear it. I’ll swear it on a Bible. Oh, don’t bring it into court! For Christ’s sake, don’t!”
passages.vernacular: 賴德突然撲倒喺地毯上,抓住我同伴嘅膝蓋。「睇喺上帝嘅份上,發發慈悲!」佢尖叫道。「想想我嘅父親!我嘅母親!呢會傷透佢哋嘅心。我以前從冇走過歧途!我再都唔會喇。我發誓。我會對住《聖經》發誓。哦,唔好把佢帶上法庭!睇喺基督嘅份上,唔好!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 賴德突然撲倒在地毯上,抓住我同伴的膝蓋。「看在上帝的份上,發發慈悲!」他尖叫道。「想想我的父親!我的母親!這會傷透他們的心。我以前從沒走過歧途!我再也不會了。我發誓。我會對著《聖經》發誓。哦,不要把它帶上法庭!看在基督的份上,不要!」

passages.original: “Get back into your chair!” said Holmes sternly. “It is very well to cringe and crawl now, but you thought little enough of this poor Horner in the dock for a crime of which he knew nothing.”
passages.vernacular: 「回到你嘅椅子上!」福爾摩斯嚴厲地講。「而家卑躬屈膝、爬行係好好,但你為一個佢一無所知嘅罪行,把呢個可憐嘅霍納送上被告席時,你可冇點想過佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「回到你的椅子上!」福爾摩斯嚴厲地說。「現在卑躬屈膝、爬行是很好,但你為一個他一無所知的罪行,把這個可憐的霍納送上被告席時,你可沒怎麼想過他。」

passages.original: “I will fly, Mr. Holmes. I will leave the country, sir. Then the charge against him will break down.”
passages.vernacular: 「我會逃走,福爾摩斯先生。我會離開呢個國家,先生。咁對佢嘅指控就會崩潰。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會逃走,福爾摩斯先生。我會離開這個國家,先生。那麼對他的指控就會崩潰。」

passages.original: “Hum! We will talk about that. And now let us hear a true account of the next act. How came the stone into the goose, and how came the goose into the open market? Tell us the truth, for there lies your only hope of safety.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯!我哋再談嗰個。而家讓我哋聽聽下一幕嘅真實敘述。寶石係點樣進到鵝裡面嘅,鵝又係點樣到咗公開市場上嘅?告訴我哋真相,因為嗰個係你唯一嘅安全希望。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯!我們再談那個。現在讓我們聽聽下一幕的真實敘述。寶石是怎樣進到鵝裡面的,鵝又是怎樣到了公開市場上的?告訴我們真相,因為那是你唯一的安全希望。」

passages.original: Ryder passed his tongue over his parched lips. “I will tell you it just as it happened, sir,” said he. “When Horner had been arrested, it seemed to me that it would be best for me to get away with the stone at once, for I did not know at what moment the police might not take it into their heads to search me and my room. There was no place about the hotel where it would be safe. I went out, as if on some commission, and I made for my sister’s house. She had married a man named Oakshott, and lived in Brixton Road, where she fattened fowls for the market. All the way there every man I met seemed to me to be a policeman or a detective; and, for all that it was a cold night, the sweat was pouring down my face before I came to the Brixton Road. My sister asked me what was the matter, and why I was so pale; but I told her that I had been upset by the jewel robbery at the hotel. Then I went into the back yard and smoked a pipe and wondered what it would be best to do.
passages.vernacular: 賴德用舌頭舔咗舔乾裂嘅嘴唇。「我會把佢嘅經過原原本本告訴你,先生,」佢講。「霍納被捕後,我覺得最好係即刻帶住寶石離開,因為我唔知道警察乜嘢時候會突然想到要搜查我同我嘅房間。酒店裡冇安全嘅地方。我出去,像係去辦乜嘢差事,趕往我姊姊家。佢嫁畀一個叫奧克肖特嘅人,住喺布里克斯頓路,喺嗰度佢為市場養肥家禽。一路上,我遇到嘅每個人喺我睇來都像係警察或偵探;儘管嗰個係個寒冷嘅夜晚,喺我到達布里克斯頓路之前,汗水已從我臉上流下嚟。我姊姊問我點喇,點解咁蒼白;但我告訴佢我被酒店嘅珠寶盜竊案弄得心煩意亂。然後我走進後院,抽咗一支煙斗,思考最好點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 賴德用舌頭舔了舔乾裂的嘴唇。「我會把它的經過原原本本告訴你,先生,」他說。「霍納被捕後,我覺得最好是馬上帶著寶石離開,因為我不知道警察什麼時候會突然想到要搜查我和我的房間。酒店裡沒有安全的地方。我出去,像是去辦什麼差事,趕往我姊姊家。她嫁給一個叫奧克肖特的人,住在布里克斯頓路,在那裡她為市場養肥家禽。一路上,我遇到的每個人在我看來都像是警察或偵探;儘管那是個寒冷的夜晚,在我到達布里克斯頓路之前,汗水已從我臉上流下來。我姊姊問我怎麼了,為什麼這麼蒼白;但我告訴她我被酒店的珠寶盜竊案弄得心煩意亂。然後我走進後院,抽了一支煙斗,思考最好怎麼辦。

passages.original: “I had a friend once called Maudsley, who went to the bad, and has just been serving his time in Pentonville. One day he had met me, and fell into talk about the ways of thieves, and how they could get rid of what they stole. I knew that he would be true to me, for I knew one or two things about him; so I made up my mind to go right on to Kilburn, where he lived, and take him into my confidence. He would show me how to turn the stone into money. But how to get to him in safety? I thought of the agonies I had gone through in coming from the hotel. I might at any moment be seized and searched, and there would be the stone in my waistcoat pocket. I was leaning against the wall at the time and looking at the geese which were waddling about round my feet, and suddenly an idea came into my head which showed me how I could beat the best detective that ever lived.
passages.vernacular: 「我曾有一個朋友叫莫茲利,佢走上咗歪路,啱啱喺本頓維爾服刑。有一天佢遇見咗我,談起賊嘅種種方法,以及佢哋點樣處理偷嚟嘅嘢。我知道佢會對我忠實,因為我知道佢嘅一兩件事;所以我下定決心直接去佢住嘅基爾本,把心事託付畀佢。佢會告訴我點樣把寶石變成錢。但係點樣安全地到佢嗰度?我想到我從酒店出嚟時經歷嘅痛苦。我隨時可能被抓住搜身,而寶石就喺我嘅背心口袋裡。我當時靠喺牆上,睇住喺我腳邊搖搖擺擺嘅鵝,突然我腦子裡有咗一個主意,向我展示咗我點樣能勝過有史以來最好嘅偵探。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我曾有一個朋友叫莫茲利,他走上了歪路,剛剛在本頓維爾服刑。有一天他遇見了我,談起賊的種種方法,以及他們怎樣處理偷來的東西。我知道他會對我忠實,因為我知道他的一兩件事;所以我下定決心直接去他住的基爾本,把心事託付給他。他會告訴我怎樣把寶石變成錢。但是怎樣安全地到他那裡?我想到我從酒店出來時經歷的痛苦。我隨時可能被抓住搜身,而寶石就在我的背心口袋裡。我當時靠在牆上,看著在我腳邊搖搖擺擺的鵝,突然我腦子裡有了一個主意,向我展示了我怎樣能勝過有史以來最好的偵探。

passages.original: “My sister had told me some weeks before that I might have the pick of her geese for a Christmas present, and I knew that she was always as good as her word. I would take my goose now, and in it I would carry my stone to Kilburn. There was a little shed in the yard, and behind this I drove one of the birds—a fine big one, white, with a barred tail. I caught it, and prying its bill open, I thrust the stone down its throat as far as my finger could reach. The bird gave a gulp, and I felt the stone pass along its gullet and down into its crop. But the creature flapped and struggled, and out came my sister to know what was the matter. As I turned to speak to her the brute broke loose and fluttered off among the others.
passages.vernacular: 「我姊姊幾個星期前講過,我可以喺佢嘅鵝中挑一隻當聖誕禮物,我知道佢總是講到做到。我而家就攞我嘅鵝,把寶石裝喺佢裡面帶到基爾本。院子裡有一間小棚子,我把其中一隻鵝趕到棚後面——一隻漂亮嘅大鵝,白色嘅,尾巴有條紋。我抓住佢,撬開佢嘅嘴,把寶石塞進佢嘅喉嚨,盡我手指能夠到嘅地方。鵝咕嚕一聲,我感到寶石沿住佢嘅食道滑下,進咗嗉囊。但嗰畜生拍打住翅膀掙扎,我姊姊出嚟問點回事。我轉身同佢講話時,嗰畜生掙脫喇,撲騰住混進其他鵝中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我姊姊幾個星期前說過,我可以在她的鵝中挑一隻當聖誕禮物,我知道她總是說到做到。我現在就拿我的鵝,把寶石裝在它裡面帶到基爾本。院子裡有一間小棚子,我把其中一隻鵝趕到棚後面——一隻漂亮的大鵝,白色的,尾巴有條紋。我抓住它,撬開它的嘴,把寶石塞進它的喉嚨,盡我手指能夠到的地方。鵝咕嚕一聲,我感到寶石沿著它的食道滑下,進了嗉囊。但那畜生拍打著翅膀掙扎,我姊姊出來問怎麼回事。我轉身同她說話時,那畜生掙脫了,撲騰著混進其他鵝中。

passages.original: “‘Whatever were you doing with that bird, Jem?’ says she.
passages.vernacular: 「『你到底對嗰隻鵝做乜嘢,傑姆?』佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你到底對那隻鵝做什麼,傑姆?』她說。

passages.original: “‘Well,’ said I, ‘you said you’d give me one for Christmas, and I was feeling which was the fattest.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,』我講,『你講過聖誕節畀我一隻,我喺感覺邊隻最肥。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,』我說,『你說過聖誕節給我一隻,我在感覺哪隻最肥。』

passages.original: “‘Oh,’ says she, ‘we’ve set yours aside for you—Jem’s bird, we call it. It’s the big white one over yonder. There’s twenty-six of them, which makes one for you, and one for us, and two dozen for the market.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,』佢講,『我哋已經畀你留咗一隻——我哋叫佢傑姆嘅鵝。就係嗰邊嗰隻大白鵝。共有二十六隻,一隻畀你,一隻畀我哋,兩打畀市場。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,』她說,『我們已經給你留了一隻——我們叫它傑姆的鵝。就是那邊那隻大白鵝。共有二十六隻,一隻給你,一隻給我們,兩打給市場。』

passages.original: “‘Thank you, Maggie,’ says I; ‘but if it is all the same to you, I’d rather have that one I was handling just now.’
passages.vernacular: 「『謝謝你,瑪姬,』我講;『但如果對你都一樣,我更想要我頭先摸嘅嗰隻。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『謝謝你,瑪姬,』我說;『但如果對你都一樣,我更想要我剛才摸的那隻。』

passages.original: “‘The other is a good three pound heavier,’ said she, ‘and we fattened it expressly for you.’
passages.vernacular: 「『另一隻重足足三磅,』佢講,『我哋專門為你養肥嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『另一隻重足足三磅,』她說,『我們專門為你養肥的。』

passages.original: “‘Never mind. I’ll have the other, and I’ll take it now,’ said I.
passages.vernacular: 「『冇關係。我要另一隻,而家就帶走,』我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『沒關係。我要另一隻,現在就帶走,』我說。

passages.original: “‘Oh, just as you like,’ said she, a little huffed. ‘Which is it you want, then?’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,隨你鍾意,』佢有點生氣地講。『咁你要邊一隻?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,隨你喜歡,』她有點生氣地說。『那麼你要哪一隻?』

passages.original: “‘That white one with the barred tail, right in the middle of the flock.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗰隻尾巴有條紋嘅白鵝,就喺鵝群嘅中間。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『那隻尾巴有條紋的白鵝,就在鵝群的中間。』

passages.original: “‘Oh, very well. Kill it and take it with you.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,好吧。殺咗佢帶走。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,好吧。殺了它帶走。』

passages.original: “Well, I did what she said, Mr. Holmes, and I carried the bird all the way to Kilburn. I told my pal what I had done, for he was a man that it was easy to tell a thing like that to. He laughed until he choked, and we got a knife and opened the goose. My heart turned to water, for there was no sign of the stone, and I knew that some terrible mistake had occurred. I left the bird, rushed back to my sister’s, and hurried into the back yard. There was not a bird to be seen there.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,福爾摩斯先生,我照佢講嘅做喇,把嗰隻鵝一路帶到基爾本。我告訴我嘅夥伴我做咗乜嘢,因為佢係個容易把呢種事告訴佢嘅人。佢笑得噎住喇,我哋攞咗一把刀打開嗰隻鵝。我嘅心變成咗水,因為冇寶石嘅蹤跡,我知道發生咗可怕嘅錯誤。我扔下鵝,衝回我姊姊家,匆匆趕進後院。嗰度一隻鵝都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,福爾摩斯先生,我照她說的做了,把那隻鵝一路帶到基爾本。我告訴我的夥伴我做了什麼,因為他是個容易把這種事告訴他的人。他笑得噎住了,我們拿了一把刀打開那隻鵝。我的心變成了水,因為沒有寶石的蹤跡,我知道發生了可怕的錯誤。我扔下鵝,衝回我姊姊家,匆匆趕進後院。那裡一隻鵝也沒有。

passages.original: “‘Where are they all, Maggie?’ I cried.
passages.vernacular: 「『牠哋都喺邊度,瑪姬?』我喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『牠們都在哪裡,瑪姬?』我喊道。

passages.original: “‘Gone to the dealer’s, Jem.’
passages.vernacular: 「『去批發商嗰度喇,傑姆。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『去批發商那裡了,傑姆。』

passages.original: “‘Which dealer’s?’
passages.vernacular: 「『邊個批發商?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哪個批發商?』

passages.original: “‘Breckinridge, of Covent Garden.’
passages.vernacular: 「『科文特花園嘅布雷肯里奇。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『科文特花園的布雷肯里奇。』

passages.original: “‘But was there another with a barred tail?’ I asked, ‘the same as the one I chose?’
passages.vernacular: 「『但係有冇另一隻尾巴有條紋嘅?』我問,『跟我選嘅嗰隻一樣嘅?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『但是有沒有另一隻尾巴有條紋的?』我問,『跟我選的那隻一樣的?』

passages.original: “‘Yes, Jem; there were two barred-tailed ones, and I could never tell them apart.’
passages.vernacular: 「『有,傑姆;有兩隻尾巴有條紋嘅,我從來分不清牠哋。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『有,傑姆;有兩隻尾巴有條紋的,我從來分不清牠們。』

passages.original: “Well, then, of course I saw it all, and I ran off as hard as my feet would carry me to this man Breckinridge; but he had sold the lot at once, and not one word would he tell me as to where they had gone. You heard him yourselves to-night. Well, he has always answered me like that. My sister thinks that I am going mad. Sometimes I think that I am myself. And now—and now I am myself a branded thief, without ever having touched the wealth for which I sold my character. God help me! God help me!” He burst into convulsive sobbing, with his face buried in his hands.
passages.vernacular: 「呢陣,當然,我全明白喇,我拚命跑到呢個人布雷肯里奇嗰度;但佢把嗰批鵝即刻全賣喇,關於牠哋去咗邊度,佢一個字都唔肯告訴我。你哋今晚自己都聽到喇。嗯,佢總是咁樣回答我。我姊姊以為我瘋喇。有時我自己都咁樣想。而家——而家我自己成咗一個被烙印嘅賊,卻從冇碰過我為之出賣人格嘅財富。上帝幫助我!上帝幫助我!」佢爆發出痙攣嘅啜泣,臉埋喺雙手裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這時,當然,我全明白了,我拚命跑到這個人布雷肯里奇那裡;但他把那批鵝立刻全賣了,關於牠們去了哪裡,他一個字也不肯告訴我。你們今晚自己也聽到了。嗯,他總是這樣回答我。我姊姊以為我瘋了。有時我自己也這樣想。現在——現在我自己成了一個被烙印的賊,卻從沒碰過我為之出賣人格的財富。上帝幫助我!上帝幫助我!」他爆發出痙攣的啜泣,臉埋在雙手裡。

passages.original: There was a long silence, broken only by his heavy breathing and by the measured tapping of Sherlock Holmes’ finger-tips upon the edge of the table. Then my friend rose and threw open the door.
passages.vernacular: 一陣長長嘅沉默,只被佢沉重嘅呼吸同夏洛克·福爾摩斯指尖喺桌邊有節奏嘅敲擊聲打破。然後我嘅朋友起身,把門推開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣長長的沉默,只被他沉重的呼吸和夏洛克·福爾摩斯指尖在桌邊有節奏的敲擊聲打破。然後我的朋友起身,把門推開。

passages.original: “Get out!” said he.
passages.vernacular: 「滾出去!」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「滾出去!」他說。

passages.original: “What, sir! Oh, Heaven bless you!”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢,先生!哦,上天保佑你!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼,先生!哦,上天保佑你!」

passages.original: “No more words. Get out!”
passages.vernacular: 「唔好再講喇。滾出去!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別再說了。滾出去!」

passages.original: And no more words were needed. There was a rush, a clatter upon the stairs, the bang of a door, and the crisp rattle of running footfalls from the street.
passages.vernacular: 不需要再講喇。一陣奔跑,樓梯上嘅一陣嘩啦聲,一扇門砰地關上,街上傳嚟清脆嘅奔跑嘅腳步聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不需要再說了。一陣奔跑,樓梯上的一陣嘩啦聲,一扇門砰地關上,街上傳來清脆的奔跑的腳步聲。

passages.original: “After all, Watson,” said Holmes, reaching up his hand for his clay pipe, “I am not retained by the police to supply their deficiencies. If Horner were in danger it would be another thing; but this fellow will not appear against him, and the case must collapse. I suppose that I am commuting a felony, but it is just possible that I am saving a soul. This fellow will not go wrong again; he is too terribly frightened. Send him to gaol now, and you make him a gaol-bird for life. Besides, it is the season of forgiveness. Chance has put in our way a most singular and whimsical problem, and its solution is its own reward. If you will have the goodness to touch the bell, Doctor, we will begin another investigation, in which, also a bird will be the chief feature.”
passages.vernacular: 「畢竟,華生,」福爾摩斯講,伸手去攞佢嘅陶土煙斗,「我唔係被警方雇用嚟彌補佢哋嘅缺陷嘅。如果霍納有危險,嗰個就係另一回事;但呢個傢伙唔會出庭指控佢,案子必然垮台。我想我係喺包庇重罪,但好可能我係喺拯救一個靈魂。呢個傢伙唔會再走歪路;佢嚇壞喇。而家把佢送進監獄,你就使佢成為終身嘅囚犯。此外,而家係寬恕嘅季節。機緣畀我哋送嚟咗一個最奇特而異想天開嘅問題,佢嘅解決就係佢自己嘅報酬。醫生,請你好心拉一下鈴,我哋要開始另一項調查,其中都將係以一隻鳥為主要特徵。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「畢竟,華生,」福爾摩斯說,伸手去拿他的陶土煙斗,「我不是被警方雇用來彌補他們的缺陷的。如果霍納有危險,那就是另一回事;但這個傢伙不會出庭指控他,案子必然垮台。我想我是在包庇重罪,但很可能我是在拯救一個靈魂。這個傢伙不會再走歪路;他嚇壞了。現在把他送進監獄,你就使他成為終身的囚犯。此外,現在是寬恕的季節。機緣給我們送來了一個最奇特而異想天開的問題,它的解決就是它自己的報酬。醫生,請你好心拉一下鈴,我們要開始另一項調查,其中也將是以一隻鳥為主要特徵。」

chapters.title: The Adventure of the Speckled Band 斑點帶子奇案

passages.original: On glancing over my notes of the seventy odd cases in which I have during the last eight years studied the methods of my friend Sherlock Holmes, I find many tragic, some comic, a large number merely strange, but none commonplace; for, working as he did rather for the love of his art than for the acquirement of wealth, he refused to associate himself with any investigation which did not tend towards the unusual, and even the fantastic. Of all these varied cases, however, I cannot recall any which presented more singular features than that which was associated with the well-known Surrey family of the Roylotts of Stoke Moran. The events in question occurred in the early days of my association with Holmes, when we were sharing rooms as bachelors in Baker Street. It is possible that I might have placed them upon record before, but a promise of secrecy was made at the time, from which I have only been freed during the last month by the untimely death of the lady to whom the pledge was given. It is perhaps as well that the facts should now come to light, for I have reasons to know that there are widespread rumours as to the death of Dr. Grimesby Roylott which tend to make the matter even more terrible than the truth.
passages.vernacular: 翻閱我筆記中過去八年裡研究我朋友夏洛克·福爾摩斯方法嘅七十多個案子,我發現有許多係悲劇性嘅,有些係滑稽嘅,有好多只係奇怪嘅,但冇一件係平庸嘅;因為佢工作更多係出於對自己技藝嘅熱愛,而唔係為了獲取財富,佢拒絕參與任何不趨向非凡、甚至離奇嘅調查。不過,喺所有呢啲各式各樣嘅案子中,我想不起有邊一件呈現嘅特點比同著名嘅薩里家族——斯托克莫蘭嘅羅伊洛特家有關嘅嗰件更奇特。所討論嘅事件發生喺我同福爾摩斯合作嘅初期,當時我哋作為單身漢喺貝克街合住。我本來可能早就把佢哋記錄下嚟,但當時作出咗保密嘅承諾,直到上個月,由於畀我哋承諾嘅嗰位女士嘅不幸去世,我才擺脫咗呢個承諾。而家讓事實公開或者更好,因為我有理由知道,關於格里姆斯比·羅伊洛特醫生嘅死,流傳住廣泛嘅謠言,使呢件事比真相更可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 翻閱我筆記中過去八年裡研究我朋友夏洛克·福爾摩斯方法的七十多個案子,我發現有許多是悲劇性的,有些是滑稽的,有很多只是奇怪的,但沒有一件是平庸的;因為他工作更多是出於對自己技藝的熱愛,而不是為了獲取財富,他拒絕參與任何不趨向非凡、甚至離奇的調查。不過,在所有這些各式各樣的案子中,我想不起有哪一件呈現的特點比與著名的薩里家族——斯托克莫蘭的羅伊洛特家有關的那件更奇特。所討論的事件發生在我與福爾摩斯合作的初期,當時我們作為單身漢在貝克街合住。我本來可能早就把它們記錄下來,但當時作出了保密的承諾,直到上個月,由於給我們承諾的那位女士的不幸去世,我才擺脫了這個承諾。現在讓事實公開也許更好,因為我有理由知道,關於格里姆斯比·羅伊洛特醫生的死,流傳著廣泛的謠言,使這件事比真相更可怕。

passages.original: It was early in April in the year ’83 that I woke one morning to find Sherlock Holmes standing, fully dressed, by the side of my bed. He was a late riser, as a rule, and as the clock on the mantelpiece showed me that it was only a quarter-past seven, I blinked up at him in some surprise, and perhaps just a little resentment, for I was myself regular in my habits.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係1883年4月初,一天早晨我醒嚟,發現夏洛克·福爾摩斯穿戴整齊地站喺我嘅床邊。佢通常起得晚,壁爐台上嘅鐘顯示才七點一刻,我有點驚訝,或者仲有啲點怨氣地眨眼睇住佢,因為我自己嘅習慣好規律。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是1883年4月初,一天早晨我醒來,發現夏洛克·福爾摩斯穿戴整齊地站在我的床邊。他通常起得晚,壁爐台上的鐘顯示才七點一刻,我有點驚訝,也許還有一點點怨氣地眨眼看著他,因為我自己的習慣很規律。

passages.original: “Very sorry to knock you up, Watson,” said he, “but it’s the common lot this morning. Mrs. Hudson has been knocked up, she retorted upon me, and I on you.”
passages.vernacular: 「好抱歉把你吵醒,華生,」佢講,「但今日早晨大家都一樣。哈德遜太太被吵醒喇,佢把氣出喺我身上,我又出喺你身上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很抱歉把你吵醒,華生,」他說,「但今天早晨大家都一樣。哈德遜太太被吵醒了,她把氣出在我身上,我又出在你身上。」

passages.original: “What is it, then—a fire?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢事——失火喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼事——失火了?」

passages.original: “No; a client. It seems that a young lady has arrived in a considerable state of excitement, who insists upon seeing me. She is waiting now in the sitting-room. Now, when young ladies wander about the metropolis at this hour of the morning, and knock sleepy people up out of their beds, I presume that it is something very pressing which they have to communicate. Should it prove to be an interesting case, you would, I am sure, wish to follow it from the outset. I thought, at any rate, that I should call you and give you the chance.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係;係一位委託人。似乎有一位年輕女士喺相當激動嘅狀態下嚟喇,堅持要見我。佢而家喺起居室等住。而家,當年輕女士喺呢個時間喺首都遊蕩、把瞓眼惺忪嘅人從床上吵起嚟時,我認為佢要講嘅一定係好緊迫嘅事。如果呢證明係個有趣嘅案子,我相信你會願意從頭跟進。無論如何,我想我該叫你,畀你呢個機會。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是;是一位委託人。似乎有一位年輕女士在相當激動的狀態下來了,堅持要見我。她現在在起居室等著。現在,當年輕女士在這個時間在首都遊蕩、把睡眼惺忪的人從床上吵起來時,我認為她要說的一定是非常緊迫的事。如果這證明是個有趣的案子,我相信你會願意從頭跟進。無論如何,我想我該叫你,給你這個機會。」

passages.original: “My dear fellow, I would not miss it for anything.”
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅朋友,我乜嘢都唔願意錯過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的朋友,我什麼都不願意錯過。」

passages.original: I had no keener pleasure than in following Holmes in his professional investigations, and in admiring the rapid deductions, as swift as intuitions, and yet always founded on a logical basis with which he unravelled the problems which were submitted to him. I rapidly threw on my clothes and was ready in a few minutes to accompany my friend down to the sitting-room. A lady dressed in black and heavily veiled, who had been sitting in the window, rose as we entered.
passages.vernacular: 我最大嘅樂趣莫過於跟隨福爾摩斯進行專業調查,欣賞佢嗰迅速如直覺、卻始終建立喺邏輯基礎上嘅推理,佢以此解開咗交畀佢嘅問題。我迅速穿上衣服,幾分鐘內就準備好陪我嘅朋友下到起居室。一位穿黑衣、戴住厚面紗嘅女士,一直坐喺窗邊,喺我哋進嚟時站起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最大的樂趣莫過於跟隨福爾摩斯進行專業調查,欣賞他那迅速如直覺、卻始終建立在邏輯基礎上的推理,他以此解開了交給他的問題。我迅速穿上衣服,幾分鐘內就準備好陪我的朋友下到起居室。一位穿黑衣、戴著厚面紗的女士,一直坐在窗邊,在我們進來時站起來。

passages.original: “Good-morning, madam,” said Holmes cheerily. “My name is Sherlock Holmes. This is my intimate friend and associate, Dr. Watson, before whom you can speak as freely as before myself. Ha! I am glad to see that Mrs. Hudson has had the good sense to light the fire. Pray draw up to it, and I shall order you a cup of hot coffee, for I observe that you are shivering.”
passages.vernacular: 「早安,夫人,」福爾摩斯愉快地講。「我嘅名字係夏洛克·福爾摩斯。呢個係我嘅密友同同事華生醫生,你可以喺佢面前像喺我面前一樣自由地講話。哈!我好高興睇到哈德遜太太有足夠嘅見識生咗火。請靠近佢坐,我讓人畀你端一杯熱咖啡,因為我睇你喺發抖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「早安,夫人,」福爾摩斯愉快地說。「我的名字是夏洛克·福爾摩斯。這是我的密友和同事華生醫生,你可以在他面前像在我面前一樣自由地說話。哈!我很高興看到哈德遜太太有足夠的見識生了火。請靠近它坐,我讓人給你端一杯熱咖啡,因為我看你在發抖。」

passages.original: “It is not cold which makes me shiver,” said the woman in a low voice, changing her seat as requested.
passages.vernacular: 「使我發抖嘅唔係冷,」嗰女人低聲講,按要求換咗座位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「使我發抖的不是冷,」那女人低聲說,按要求換了座位。

passages.original: “What, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼?」

passages.original: “It is fear, Mr. Holmes. It is terror.” She raised her veil as she spoke, and we could see that she was indeed in a pitiable state of agitation, her face all drawn and grey, with restless frightened eyes, like those of some hunted animal. Her features and figure were those of a woman of thirty, but her hair was shot with premature grey, and her expression was weary and haggard. Sherlock Holmes ran her over with one of his quick, all-comprehensive glances.
passages.vernacular: 「係恐懼,福爾摩斯先生。係恐怖。」佢講住掀起咗面紗,我哋睇到佢確實處於可憐嘅激動狀態,臉上緊繃而灰白,眼睛不安而驚恐,像某種被追獵嘅動物嘅眼睛。佢嘅面容同身材係一個三十歲女人嘅,但佢嘅頭髮已過早地夾雜住灰白,表情疲憊而憔悴。夏洛克·福爾摩斯以佢嗰迅速而包羅萬象嘅一瞥把佢打量咗一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是恐懼,福爾摩斯先生。是恐怖。」她說著掀起了面紗,我們看到她確實處於可憐的激動狀態,臉上緊繃而灰白,眼睛不安而驚恐,像某種被追獵的動物的眼睛。她的面容和身材是一個三十歲女人的,但她的頭髮已過早地夾雜著灰白,表情疲憊而憔悴。夏洛克·福爾摩斯以他那迅速而包羅萬象的一瞥把她打量了一遍。

passages.original: “You must not fear,” said he soothingly, bending forward and patting her forearm. “We shall soon set matters right, I have no doubt. You have come in by train this morning, I see.”
passages.vernacular: 「您唔使害怕,」佢安撫地講,俯身輕拍佢嘅前臂。「我哋好快就會把事情處理好,我毫不懷疑。我睇您今日朝早係乘火車嚟嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您不必害怕,」他安撫地說,俯身輕拍她的前臂。「我們很快就會把事情處理好,我毫不懷疑。我看您今天早上是乘火車來的。」

passages.original: “You know me, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你認識我?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你認識我?」

passages.original: “No, but I observe the second half of a return ticket in the palm of your left glove. You must have started early, and yet you had a good drive in a dog-cart, along heavy roads, before you reached the station.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,但我注意到您左手手套掌心有半張回程票。您一定出發得好早,但喺到達車站之前,您仲乘坐雙輪輕馬車喺泥濘嘅路上走咗好長一段路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,但我注意到您左手手套掌心有半張回程票。您一定出發得很早,但在到達車站之前,您還乘坐雙輪輕馬車在泥濘的路上走了很長一段路。」

passages.original: The lady gave a violent start and stared in bewilderment at my companion.
passages.vernacular: 嗰位女士猛然一驚,困惑地盯住我嘅同伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位女士猛然一驚,困惑地盯著我的同伴。

passages.original: “There is no mystery, my dear madam,” said he, smiling. “The left arm of your jacket is spattered with mud in no less than seven places. The marks are perfectly fresh. There is no vehicle save a dog-cart which throws up mud in that way, and then only when you sit on the left-hand side of the driver.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇乜嘢神秘,親愛嘅夫人,」佢微笑住講。「您外套嘅左臂上有不少於七處泥濺。痕跡完全係新鮮嘅。除咗雙輪輕馬車,冇其他車輛會咁樣濺起泥,而且只有當您坐喺車夫嘅左邊時才會。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有什麼神秘,親愛的夫人,」他微笑著說。「您外套的左臂上有不少於七處泥濺。痕跡完全是新鮮的。除了雙輪輕馬車,沒有其他車輛會這樣濺起泥,而且只有當您坐在車夫的左邊時才會。」

passages.original: “Whatever your reasons may be, you are perfectly correct,” said she. “I started from home before six, reached Leatherhead at twenty past, and came in by the first train to Waterloo. Sir, I can stand this strain no longer; I shall go mad if it continues. I have no one to turn to—none, save only one, who cares for me, and he, poor fellow, can be of little aid. I have heard of you, Mr. Holmes; I have heard of you from Mrs. Farintosh, whom you helped in the hour of her sore need. It was from her that I had your address. Oh, sir, do you not think that you could help me, too, and at least throw a little light through the dense darkness which surrounds me? At present it is out of my power to reward you for your services, but in a month or six weeks I shall be married, with the control of my own income, and then at least you shall not find me ungrateful.”
passages.vernacular: 「無論你嘅理由係乜嘢,你完全正確,」佢講。「我六點以前從家裡出發,二好到達利瑟黑德,乘第一班火車到滑鐵盧。先生,我再都受不了呢種緊張喇;如果佢繼續下去,我會發瘋嘅。我冇人可以求助——除咗一個人,佢關心我,而佢,可憐嘅人,幫不上乜嘢忙。我聽講過你,福爾摩斯先生;我從法林托什太太嗰度聽講你,佢喺最痛苦需要嘅時刻,你幫助過佢。係從佢嗰度我得到咗你嘅地址。哦,先生,你不認為你都能幫助我,至少讓啲光穿透包圍住我嘅濃重黑暗嗎?目前我無力酬謝你嘅服務,但一個月或六個星期後,我就要結婚喇,可以掌管自己嘅收入,嗰時至少你唔會發現我係忘恩負義嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「無論你的理由是什麼,你完全正確,」她說。「我六點以前從家裡出發,二十分到達利瑟黑德,乘第一班火車到滑鐵盧。先生,我再也受不了這種緊張了;如果它繼續下去,我會發瘋的。我沒有人可以求助——除了一個人,他關心我,而他,可憐的人,幫不上什麼忙。我聽說過你,福爾摩斯先生;我從法林托什太太那裡聽說你,她在最痛苦需要的時刻,你幫助過她。是從她那裡我得到了你的地址。哦,先生,你不認為你也能幫助我,至少讓一點光穿透包圍著我的濃重黑暗嗎?目前我無力酬謝你的服務,但一個月或六個星期後,我就要結婚了,可以掌管自己的收入,那時至少你不會發現我是忘恩負義的。」

passages.original: Holmes turned to his desk and, unlocking it, drew out a small case-book, which he consulted.
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯轉向佢嘅書桌,打開鎖,攞出一本小案卷簿,翻閱起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯轉向他的書桌,打開鎖,拿出一本小案卷簿,翻閱起來。

passages.original: “Farintosh,” said he. “Ah yes, I recall the case; it was concerned with an opal tiara. I think it was before your time, Watson. I can only say, madam, that I shall be happy to devote the same care to your case as I did to that of your friend. As to reward, my profession is its own reward; but you are at liberty to defray whatever expenses I may be put to, at the time which suits you best. And now I beg that you will lay before us everything that may help us in forming an opinion upon the matter.”
passages.vernacular: 「法林托什,」佢講。「啊,係嘅,我記得呢個案子;佢涉及一頂蛋白石冠冕。我想嗰個係喺你之前嘅事,華生。夫人,我只能講,我將樂意把同對您朋友嘅案子同樣嘅關注,投入您嘅案子。至於報酬,我嘅職業就係自己嘅報酬;但您可以喺最適合您嘅時候,自由支付我可能產生嘅任何費用。而家,請把一切可能幫助我哋對此事形成意見嘅嘢擺喺我哋面前。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「法林托什,」他說。「啊,是的,我記得這個案子;它涉及一頂蛋白石冠冕。我想那是在你之前的事,華生。夫人,我只能說,我將樂意把與對您朋友的案子同樣的關注,投入您的案子。至於報酬,我的職業就是自己的報酬;但您可以在最適合您的時候,自由支付我可能產生的任何費用。現在,請把一切可能幫助我們對此事形成意見的東西擺在我們面前。」

passages.original: “Alas!” replied our visitor, “the very horror of my situation lies in the fact that my fears are so vague, and my suspicions depend so entirely upon small points, which might seem trivial to another, that even he to whom of all others I have a right to look for help and advice looks upon all that I tell him about it as the fancies of a nervous woman. He does not say so, but I can read it from his soothing answers and averted eyes. But I have heard, Mr. Holmes, that you can see deeply into the manifold wickedness of the human heart. You may advise me how to walk amid the dangers which encompass me.”
passages.vernacular: 「唉!」我哋嘅訪客回答,「我處境嘅恐怖正在於,我嘅恐懼係咁模糊,我嘅疑心完全依賴於啲喺別人睇來可能微不足道嘅小點,以致連我最有權向佢求助同建議嘅嗰個人,都把我告訴佢嘅一切睇作神經質女人嘅幻想。佢冇咁講,但我能從佢安慰嘅回答同避開嘅眼睛睇出嚟。但我聽講,福爾摩斯先生,你能深入洞察人心嘅種種邪惡。你可以告訴我點樣喺圍繞我嘅危險中行走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「唉!」我們的訪客回答,「我處境的恐怖正在於,我的恐懼是那麼模糊,我的疑心完全依賴於一些在別人看來可能微不足道的小點,以致連我最有權向他求助和建議的那個人,都把我告訴他的一切看作神經質女人的幻想。他沒有這麼說,但我能從他安慰的回答和避開的眼睛看出來。但我聽說,福爾摩斯先生,你能深入洞察人心的種種邪惡。你可以告訴我怎樣在圍繞我的危險中行走。」

passages.original: “I am all attention, madam.”
passages.vernacular: 「我全神貫注,夫人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我全神貫注,夫人。」

passages.original: “My name is Helen Stoner, and I am living with my stepfather, who is the last survivor of one of the oldest Saxon families in England, the Roylotts of Stoke Moran, on the western border of Surrey.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅名字係海倫·斯托納,我同我嘅繼父住喺一起,佢係英格蘭最古老嘅撒克遜家族之一嘅最後倖存者,薩里西部邊界上斯托克莫蘭嘅羅伊洛特家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的名字是海倫·斯托納,我同我的繼父住在一起,他是英格蘭最古老的撒克遜家族之一的最後倖存者,薩里西部邊界上斯托克莫蘭的羅伊洛特家。」

passages.original: Holmes nodded his head. “The name is familiar to me,” said he.
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯點咗點頭。「呢個名字我好熟悉,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯點了點頭。「這個名字我很熟悉,」他說。

passages.original: “The family was at one time among the richest in England, and the estates extended over the borders into Berkshire in the north, and Hampshire in the west. In the last century, however, four successive heirs were of a dissolute and wasteful disposition, and the family ruin was eventually completed by a gambler in the days of the Regency. Nothing was left save a few acres of ground, and the two-hundred-year-old house, which is itself crushed under a heavy mortgage. The last squire dragged out his existence there, living the horrible life of an aristocratic pauper; but his only son, my stepfather, seeing that he must adapt himself to the new conditions, obtained an advance from a relative, which enabled him to take a medical degree and went out to Calcutta, where, by his professional skill and his force of character, he established a large practice. In a fit of anger, however, caused by some robberies which had been perpetrated in the house, he beat his native butler to death and narrowly escaped a capital sentence. As it was, he suffered a long term of imprisonment and afterwards returned to England a morose and disappointed man.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個家族一度係英格蘭最富有嘅家族之一,地產向北延伸到伯克郡邊界,向西到漢普郡。然而喺上個世紀,連續四代繼承人都係放蕩浪費嘅性格,攝政時期嘅一個賭徒最終完成咗家族嘅毀滅。除咗幾英畝地同嗰座兩百年歷史嘅房子之外,乜嘢都冇留下,而呢座房子本身都被沉重嘅抵押壓垮喇。最後一位鄉紳喺嗰度苟延殘喘,過住貴族貧民嘅可怕生活;但佢唯一嘅兒子,我嘅繼父,睇到自己必須適應新嘅條件,從一個親戚嗰度得到一筆預支,使佢能獲得醫學學位,前往加爾各答,喺嗰度憑藉佢嘅專業技能同性格力量,建立咗一個大診所。然而,喺家中發生啲盜竊案所引起嘅一次怒氣發作中,佢把佢嘅本地管家打死喇,險些被判死刑。實際上,佢受到長期監禁,後來作為一個陰沉失意嘅人回到英國。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個家族一度是英格蘭最富有的家族之一,地產向北延伸到伯克郡邊界,向西到漢普郡。然而在上個世紀,連續四代繼承人都是放蕩浪費的性格,攝政時期的一個賭徒最終完成了家族的毀滅。除了幾英畝地和那座兩百年歷史的房子之外,什麼也沒留下,而這座房子本身也被沉重的抵押壓垮了。最後一位鄉紳在那裡苟延殘喘,過著貴族貧民的可怕生活;但他唯一的兒子,我的繼父,看到自己必須適應新的條件,從一個親戚那裡得到一筆預支,使他能獲得醫學學位,前往加爾各答,在那裡憑藉他的專業技能和性格力量,建立了一個大診所。然而,在家中發生一些盜竊案所引起的一次怒氣發作中,他把他的本地管家打死了,險些被判死刑。實際上,他受到長期監禁,後來作為一個陰沉失意的人回到英國。

passages.original: “When Dr. Roylott was in India he married my mother, Mrs. Stoner, the young widow of Major-General Stoner, of the Bengal Artillery. My sister Julia and I were twins, and we were only two years old at the time of my mother’s re-marriage. She had a considerable sum of money—not less than £ 1000 a year—and this she bequeathed to Dr. Roylott entirely while we resided with him, with a provision that a certain annual sum should be allowed to each of us in the event of our marriage. Shortly after our return to England my mother died—she was killed eight years ago in a railway accident near Crewe. Dr. Roylott then abandoned his attempts to establish himself in practice in London and took us to live with him in the old ancestral house at Stoke Moran. The money which my mother had left was enough for all our wants, and there seemed to be no obstacle to our happiness.
passages.vernacular: 「羅伊洛特醫生喺印度時,娶咗我母親,斯托納太太,孟加拉炮兵團斯托納少將嘅年輕寡婦。我姊姊朱莉婭同我係雙胞胎,我母親再婚時我哋只有兩歲。佢有一筆相當可觀嘅錢——每年不少於一千鎊——佢把呢筆錢全部遺贈畀咗羅伊洛特醫生,條件係我哋同佢住喺一起時,如果結婚,每人可以得到一筆年金。我哋回到英國後不久,我母親去世喇——八年前,喺克魯附近嘅一次鐵路事故中遇難。羅伊洛特醫生隨後放棄咗喺倫敦開業嘅嘗試,帶我哋到斯托克莫蘭嘅古老祖屋同佢住喺一起。我母親留下嘅錢足以應付我哋所有嘅需要,似乎我哋嘅幸福冇乜嘢障礙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「羅伊洛特醫生在印度時,娶了我母親,斯托納太太,孟加拉炮兵團斯托納少將的年輕寡婦。我姊姊朱莉婭和我是雙胞胎,我母親再婚時我們只有兩歲。她有一筆相當可觀的錢——每年不少於一千鎊——她把這筆錢全部遺贈給了羅伊洛特醫生,條件是我們同他住在一起時,如果結婚,每人可以得到一筆年金。我們回到英國後不久,我母親去世了——八年前,在克魯附近的一次鐵路事故中遇難。羅伊洛特醫生隨後放棄了在倫敦開業的嘗試,帶我們到斯托克莫蘭的古老祖屋同他住在一起。我母親留下的錢足以應付我們所有的需要,似乎我們的幸福沒有什麼障礙。

passages.original: “But a terrible change came over our stepfather about this time. Instead of making friends and exchanging visits with our neighbours, who had at first been overjoyed to see a Roylott of Stoke Moran back in the old family seat, he shut himself up in his house and seldom came out save to indulge in ferocious quarrels with whoever might cross his path. Violence of temper approaching to mania has been hereditary in the men of the family, and in my stepfather’s case it had, I believe, been intensified by his long residence in the tropics. A series of disgraceful brawls took place, two of which ended in the police-court, until at last he became the terror of the village, and the folks would fly at his approach, for he is a man of immense strength, and absolutely uncontrollable in his anger.
passages.vernacular: 「但大約喺呢陣,我哋嘅繼父發生咗可怕嘅變化。佢冇同鄰居交朋友、互相拜訪,而鄰居哋起初睇到斯托克莫蘭嘅羅伊洛特回到老家宅,係好高興嘅,佢卻把自己關喺屋裡,好少出嚟,除非係同可能擋佢路嘅人進行凶猛嘅爭吵。近乎瘋狂嘅暴脾氣係家族男子遺傳嘅,我相信喺我繼父身上,因為佢長期喺熱帶居住而加劇喇。發生咗一連串可恥嘅鬥毆,其中兩次以警察法庭告終,最終佢成咗村裡嘅恐怖人物,人哋睇到佢走近就逃跑,因為佢體力巨大,發怒時完全無法控制。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但大約在這時,我們的繼父發生了可怕的變化。他沒有與鄰居交朋友、互相拜訪,而鄰居們起初看到斯托克莫蘭的羅伊洛特回到老家宅,是非常高興的,他卻把自己關在屋裡,很少出來,除非是同可能擋他路的人進行凶猛的爭吵。近乎瘋狂的暴脾氣是家族男子遺傳的,我相信在我繼父身上,因為他長期在熱帶居住而加劇了。發生了一連串可恥的鬥毆,其中兩次以警察法庭告終,最終他成了村裡的恐怖人物,人們看到他走近就逃跑,因為他體力巨大,發怒時完全無法控制。

passages.original: “Last week he hurled the local blacksmith over a parapet into a stream, and it was only by paying over all the money which I could gather together that I was able to avert another public exposure. He had no friends at all save the wandering gipsies, and he would give these vagabonds leave to encamp upon the few acres of bramble-covered land which represent the family estate, and would accept in return the hospitality of their tents, wandering away with them sometimes for weeks on end. He has a passion also for Indian animals, which are sent over to him by a correspondent, and he has at this moment a cheetah and a baboon, which wander freely over his grounds and are feared by the villagers almost as much as their master.
passages.vernacular: 「上星期,佢把本地嘅鐵匠扔過護牆,摔進一條小溪,我只能通過付出我能湊到嘅所有錢,才避免咗又一次公開曝光。佢除咗流浪嘅吉普賽人之外,完全冇朋友,佢允許呢啲流浪者喺代表家族地產嘅嗰幾英畝長滿荊棘嘅土地上露營,並作為回報接受佢哋帳篷嘅款待,有時隨佢哋流浪一連幾個星期。佢仲特別喜愛印度動物,係一位通信者寄畀佢嘅,此刻佢有一隻獵豹同一隻狒狒,喺佢嘅園地上自由遊蕩,村民哋對牠哋嘅懼怕幾乎不亞於對牠哋主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「上星期,他把本地的鐵匠扔過護牆,摔進一條小溪,我只能通過付出我能湊到的所有錢,才避免了又一次公開曝光。他除了流浪的吉普賽人之外,完全沒有朋友,他允許這些流浪者在代表家族地產的那幾英畝長滿荊棘的土地上露營,並作為回報接受他們帳篷的款待,有時隨他們流浪一連幾個星期。他還特別喜愛印度動物,是一位通信者寄給他的,此刻他有一隻獵豹和一隻狒狒,在他的園地上自由遊蕩,村民們對牠們的懼怕幾乎不亞於對牠們主人。

passages.original: “You can imagine from what I say that my poor sister Julia and I had no great pleasure in our lives. No servant would stay with us, and for a long time we did all the work of the house. She was but thirty at the time of her death, and yet her hair had already begun to whiten, even as mine has.”
passages.vernacular: 「從我所講嘅,你可以想像,我可憐嘅姊姊朱莉婭同我生活中冇多少快樂。冇僕人肯留喺我哋呢度,長時間以來我哋做所有嘅家務。佢去世時才三十歲,但佢嘅頭髮已經開始變白,像我嘅一樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從我所說的,你可以想像,我可憐的姊姊朱莉婭和我生活中沒有多少快樂。沒有僕人肯留在我們這裡,長時間以來我們做所有的家務。她去世時才三十歲,但她的頭髮已經開始變白,像我的一樣。」

passages.original: “Your sister is dead, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅姊姊死咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的姊姊死了嗎?」

passages.original: “She died just two years ago, and it is of her death that I wish to speak to you. You can understand that, living the life which I have described, we were little likely to see anyone of our own age and position. We had, however, an aunt, my mother’s maiden sister, Miss Honoria Westphail, who lives near Harrow, and we were occasionally allowed to pay short visits at this lady’s house. Julia went there at Christmas two years ago, and met there a half-pay major of marines, to whom she became engaged. My stepfather learned of the engagement when my sister returned and offered no objection to the marriage; but within a fortnight of the day which had been fixed for the wedding, the terrible event occurred which has deprived me of my only companion.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢剛好兩年前去世,我想同你談嘅正是佢嘅死。你可以理解,過住我所描述嘅生活,我哋不太可能見到任何同我哋年齡同地位相當嘅人。不過,我哋有一個姨媽,我母親嘅未婚妹妹,霍諾里亞·韋斯特菲爾小姐,住喺哈羅附近,我哋偶爾被允許去呢位女士家做短暫嘅拜訪。朱莉婭兩年前聖誕節去嗰度,喺嗰度遇到一位領半薪嘅海軍陸戰隊少校,同佢訂咗婚。我姊姊回嚟時,我繼父得知咗訂婚嘅事,並冇反對呢門婚事;但喺定好嘅婚期前兩個星期內,發生咗嗰件可怕嘅事,奪去咗我唯一嘅伴侶。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她剛好兩年前去世,我想同你談的正是她的死。你可以理解,過著我所描述的生活,我們不太可能見到任何與我們年齡和地位相當的人。不過,我們有一個姨媽,我母親的未婚妹妹,霍諾里亞·韋斯特菲爾小姐,住在哈羅附近,我們偶爾被允許去這位女士家做短暫的拜訪。朱莉婭兩年前聖誕節去那裡,在那裡遇到一位領半薪的海軍陸戰隊少校,同他訂了婚。我姊姊回來時,我繼父得知了訂婚的事,並沒有反對這門婚事;但在定好的婚期前兩個星期內,發生了那件可怕的事,奪去了我唯一的伴侶。」

passages.original: Sherlock Holmes had been leaning back in his chair with his eyes closed and his head sunk in a cushion, but he half opened his lids now and glanced across at his visitor.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯一直靠喺椅背上,眼睛閉住,頭埋喺墊子裡,但而家佢半睜開眼瞼,瞥向佢嘅訪客。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯一直靠在椅背上,眼睛閉著,頭埋在墊子裡,但現在他半睜開眼瞼,瞥向他的訪客。

passages.original: “Pray be precise as to details,” said he.
passages.vernacular: 「請喺細節上準確,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請在細節上準確,」他說。

passages.original: “It is easy for me to be so, for every event of that dreadful time is seared into my memory. The manor-house is, as I have already said, very old, and only one wing is now inhabited. The bedrooms in this wing are on the ground floor, the sitting-rooms being in the central block of the buildings. Of these bedrooms the first is Dr. Roylott’s, the second my sister’s, and the third my own. There is no communication between them, but they all open out into the same corridor. Do I make myself plain?”
passages.vernacular: 「對我來講呢個好容易,因為嗰段可怕時間嘅每件事都烙印喺我嘅記憶裡。莊園住宅,如我已講過嘅,好古老,而家只有一翼有人居住。呢一翼嘅臥室喺底層,起居室喺建築嘅中央部分。喺呢啲臥室中,第一間係羅伊洛特醫生嘅,第二間係我姊姊嘅,第三間係我自己嘅。佢哋之間冇通道,但都通向同一條走廊。我講清楚咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對我來說這很容易,因為那段可怕時間的每件事都烙印在我的記憶裡。莊園住宅,如我已說過的,非常古老,現在只有一翼有人居住。這一翼的臥室在底層,起居室在建築的中央部分。在這些臥室中,第一間是羅伊洛特醫生的,第二間是我姊姊的,第三間是我自己的。它們之間沒有通道,但都通向同一條走廊。我說清楚了嗎?」

passages.original: “Perfectly so.”
passages.vernacular: 「好清楚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「非常清楚。」

passages.original: “The windows of the three rooms open out upon the lawn. That fatal night Dr. Roylott had gone to his room early, though we knew that he had not retired to rest, for my sister was troubled by the smell of the strong Indian cigars which it was his custom to smoke. She left her room, therefore, and came into mine, where she sat for some time, chatting about her approaching wedding. At eleven o’clock she rose to leave me, but she paused at the door and looked back.
passages.vernacular: 「三個房間嘅窗子都朝向草坪。嗰個致命嘅夜晚,羅伊洛特醫生好早就進咗佢嘅房間,雖然我哋知道佢仲冇就寢,因為我姊姊被佢習慣抽嘅濃烈印度雪茄嘅氣味所困擾。因此佢離開咗佢嘅房間,嚟到我嘅房間,喺嗰度坐咗一會兒,聊住佢即將到來嘅婚禮。十啲鐘,佢起身要離開我,但佢喺門口停下,回頭睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「三個房間的窗子都朝向草坪。那個致命的夜晚,羅伊洛特醫生很早就進了他的房間,雖然我們知道他還沒有就寢,因為我姊姊被他習慣抽的濃烈印度雪茄的氣味所困擾。因此她離開了她的房間,來到我的房間,在那裡坐了一會兒,聊著她即將到來的婚禮。十一點鐘,她起身要離開我,但她在門口停下,回頭看。

passages.original: “‘Tell me, Helen,’ said she, ‘have you ever heard anyone whistle in the dead of the night?’
passages.vernacular: 「『告訴我,海倫,』佢講,『你有冇喺深夜聽見過有人吹口哨?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『告訴我,海倫,』她說,『你有沒有在深夜聽見過有人吹口哨?』

passages.original: “‘Never,’ said I.
passages.vernacular: 「『從來冇,』我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『從來沒有,』我說。

passages.original: “‘I suppose that you could not possibly whistle, yourself, in your sleep?’
passages.vernacular: 「『我想你唔可能喺瞓夢中自己吹口哨吧?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我想你不可能在睡夢中自己吹口哨吧?』

passages.original: “‘Certainly not. But why?’
passages.vernacular: 「『當然唔會。但點解問?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『當然不會。但為什麼問?』

passages.original: “‘Because during the last few nights I have always, about three in the morning, heard a low, clear whistle. I am a light sleeper, and it has awakened me. I cannot tell where it came from—perhaps from the next room, perhaps from the lawn. I thought that I would just ask you whether you had heard it.’
passages.vernacular: 「『因為最近幾夜,大約凌晨三點,我總是聽到一聲低沉、清晰嘅口哨聲。我瞓得淺,佢把我吵醒喇。我講不出佢來自邊度——或者來自隔壁房間,或者來自草坪。我想問問你有冇聽到。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『因為最近幾夜,大約凌晨三點,我總是聽到一聲低沉、清晰的口哨聲。我睡得淺,它把我吵醒了。我說不出它來自哪裡——也許來自隔壁房間,也許來自草坪。我想問問你有沒有聽到。』

passages.original: “‘No, I have not. It must be those wretched gipsies in the plantation.’
passages.vernacular: 「『冇,我冇。一定係嗰啲種植園裡可惡嘅吉普賽人。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『沒有,我沒有。一定是那些種植園裡可惡的吉普賽人。』

passages.original: “‘Very likely. And yet if it were on the lawn, I wonder that you did not hear it also.’
passages.vernacular: 「『好可能。不過如果係喺草坪上,我奇怪你點都冇聽到。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『很可能。可是如果是在草坪上,我奇怪你怎麼也沒聽到。』

passages.original: “‘Ah, but I sleep more heavily than you.’
passages.vernacular: 「『啊,但我瞓得比你沉。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『啊,但我睡得比你沉。』

passages.original: “‘Well, it is of no great consequence, at any rate.’ She smiled back at me, closed my door, and a few moments later I heard her key turn in the lock.”
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,無論如何,呢個冇乜嘢大不咗嘅。』佢對我微笑,關上我嘅門,片刻後我聽到佢嘅鑰匙喺鎖裡轉動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,無論如何,這沒什麼大不了的。』她對我微笑,關上我的門,片刻後我聽到她的鑰匙在鎖裡轉動。」

passages.original: “Indeed,” said Holmes. “Was it your custom always to lock yourselves in at night?”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅,」福爾摩斯講。「你哋晚上總是習慣鎖上門嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的,」福爾摩斯說。「你們晚上總是習慣鎖上門嗎?」

passages.original: “Always.”
passages.vernacular: 「總是。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「總是。」

passages.original: “And why?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼?」

passages.original: “I think that I mentioned to you that the Doctor kept a cheetah and a baboon. We had no feeling of security unless our doors were locked.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想我對你提過醫生養咗一隻獵豹同一隻狒狒。不鎖門,我哋就冇安全感。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我對你提過醫生養了一隻獵豹和一隻狒狒。不鎖門,我們就沒有安全感。」

passages.original: “Quite so. Pray proceed with your statement.”
passages.vernacular: 「完全明白。請繼續你嘅陳述。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「完全明白。請繼續你的陳述。」

passages.original: “I could not sleep that night. A vague feeling of impending misfortune impressed me. My sister and I, you will recollect, were twins, and you know how subtle are the links which bind two souls which are so closely allied. It was a wild night. The wind was howling outside, and the rain was beating and splashing against the windows. Suddenly, amid all the hubbub of the gale, there burst forth the wild scream of a terrified woman. I knew that it was my sister’s voice. I sprang from my bed, wrapped a shawl round me, and rushed into the corridor. As I opened my door I seemed to hear a low whistle, such as my sister described, and a few moments later a clanging sound, as if a mass of metal had fallen. As I ran down the passage, my sister’s door was unlocked, and revolved slowly upon its hinges. I stared at it horror-stricken, not knowing what was about to issue from it. By the light of the corridor-lamp I saw my sister appear at the opening, her face blanched with terror, her hands groping for help, her whole figure swaying to and fro like that of a drunkard. I ran to her and threw my arms round her, but at that moment her knees seemed to give way and she fell to the ground. She writhed as one who is in terrible pain, and her limbs were dreadfully convulsed. At first I thought that she had not recognised me, but as I bent over her she suddenly shrieked out in a voice which I shall never forget, ‘Oh, my God! Helen! It was the band! The speckled band!’ There was something else which she would fain have said, and she stabbed with her finger into the air in the direction of the Doctor’s room, but a fresh convulsion seized her and choked her words. I rushed out, calling loudly for my stepfather, and I met him hastening from his room in his dressing-gown. When he reached my sister’s side she was unconscious, and though he poured brandy down her throat and sent for medical aid from the village, all efforts were in vain, for she slowly sank and died without having recovered her consciousness. Such was the dreadful end of my beloved sister.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰天晚上我瞓不住。一種模糊嘅、即將有不幸嘅感覺壓喺我心上。你會記得,我同我姊姊係雙胞胎,你知道把兩個如此緊密相連嘅靈魂結合喺一起嘅聯繫係幾咁微妙。嗰個係個狂風暴雨嘅夜晚。外面風喺呼嘯,雨敲打並濺喺窗子上。突然,喺狂風嘅喧囂中,爆發出一個驚恐女人嘅狂叫。我知道嗰個係我姊姊嘅聲音。我從床上跳起,披上披肩,衝進走廊。我打開門時,似乎聽到一聲低沉嘅口哨,像我姊姊所描述嘅,片刻後係一聲叮噹嘅響聲,好像一團金屬掉落。我沿住走廊跑去,我姊姊嘅門被打開喇,喺門軸上緩緩轉動。我驚恐地盯住佢,唔知道會有乜嘢從裡面出嚟。借住走廊燈嘅光,我睇見我姊姊出而家門口,臉因恐懼而發白,雙手摸索住求助,整個身體像醉漢一樣搖嚟晃去。我跑到佢身邊,張開雙臂抱住佢,但就喺嗰一刻,佢嘅膝蓋似乎軟喇,倒喺地上。佢像一個忍受劇痛嘅人一樣扭動,四肢可怕地抽搐。起初我以為佢冇認出我,但當我俯身睇佢時,佢突然用一種我永遠唔會忘記嘅聲音尖叫:『哦,我嘅上帝!海倫!係嗰條帶子!斑點帶子!』仲有別嘅乜嘢佢好想講,佢用手指向空中朝醫生房間嘅方向刺咗一下,但新一陣抽搐抓住咗佢,堵住咗佢嘅話。我衝出去,大聲呼喚我嘅繼父,我遇見佢穿住瞓袍從房間匆匆趕嚟。佢走到我姊姊身邊時,佢已不省人事,儘管佢把白蘭地灌進佢嘅喉嚨,派人到村裡請醫生,一切努力都係徒勞嘅,因為佢慢慢沉下去,冇恢復知覺就死喇。呢個就係我心愛姊姊嘅可怕結局。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那天晚上我睡不著。一種模糊的、即將有不幸的感覺壓在我心上。你會記得,我和我姊姊是雙胞胎,你知道把兩個如此緊密相連的靈魂結合在一起的聯繫是多麼微妙。那是個狂風暴雨的夜晚。外面風在呼嘯,雨敲打並濺在窗子上。突然,在狂風的喧囂中,爆發出一個驚恐女人的狂叫。我知道那是我姊姊的聲音。我從床上跳起,披上披肩,衝進走廊。我打開門時,似乎聽到一聲低沉的口哨,像我姊姊所描述的,片刻後是一聲叮噹的響聲,好像一團金屬掉落。我沿著走廊跑去,我姊姊的門被打開了,在門軸上緩緩轉動。我驚恐地盯著它,不知道會有什麼從裡面出來。借著走廊燈的光,我看見我姊姊出現在門口,臉因恐懼而發白,雙手摸索著求助,整個身體像醉漢一樣搖來晃去。我跑到她身邊,張開雙臂抱住她,但就在那一刻,她的膝蓋似乎軟了,倒在地上。她像一個忍受劇痛的人一樣扭動,四肢可怕地抽搐。起初我以為她沒有認出我,但當我俯身看她時,她突然用一種我永遠不會忘記的聲音尖叫:『哦,我的上帝!海倫!是那條帶子!斑點帶子!』還有別的什麼她很想說,她用手指向空中朝醫生房間的方向刺了一下,但新一陣抽搐抓住了她,堵住了她的話。我衝出去,大聲呼喚我的繼父,我遇見他穿著睡袍從房間匆匆趕來。他走到我姊姊身邊時,她已不省人事,儘管他把白蘭地灌進她的喉嚨,派人到村裡請醫生,一切努力都是徒勞的,因為她慢慢沉下去,沒有恢復知覺就死了。這就是我心愛姊姊的可怕結局。」

passages.original: “One moment,” said Holmes, “are you sure about this whistle and metallic sound? Could you swear to it?”
passages.vernacular: 「請稍等,」福爾摩斯講,「你確定呢個口哨聲同金屬聲嗎?你能發誓嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請稍等,」福爾摩斯說,「你確定這個口哨聲和金屬聲嗎?你能發誓嗎?」

passages.original: “That was what the county coroner asked me at the inquiry. It is my strong impression that I heard it, and yet, among the crash of the gale and the creaking of an old house, I may possibly have been deceived.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係郡驗屍官喺調查中問我嘅問題。我有強烈嘅印象我聽到喇,然而,喺狂風嘅轟鳴同老房子嘅吱嘎聲中,我都可能被騙喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是郡驗屍官在調查中問我的問題。我有強烈的印象我聽到了,然而,在狂風的轟鳴和老房子的吱嘎聲中,我也可能被騙了。」

passages.original: “Was your sister dressed?”
passages.vernacular: 「你姊姊穿住衣服嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你姊姊穿著衣服嗎?」

passages.original: “No, she was in her night-dress. In her right hand was found the charred stump of a match, and in her left a match-box.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,佢穿住瞓衣。佢右手裡發現咗一根燒焦嘅火柴梗,左手裡有一個火柴盒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,她穿著睡衣。她右手裡發現了一根燒焦的火柴梗,左手裡有一個火柴盒。」

passages.original: “Showing that she had struck a light and looked about her when the alarm took place. That is important. And what conclusions did the coroner come to?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢表明警報發生時,佢劃咗火柴,環顧四周。嗰好重要。驗屍官得出咗乜嘢結論?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這表明警報發生時,她劃了火柴,環顧四周。那很重要。驗屍官得出了什麼結論?」

passages.original: “He investigated the case with great care, for Dr. Roylott’s conduct had long been notorious in the county, but he was unable to find any satisfactory cause of death. My evidence showed that the door had been fastened upon the inner side, and the windows were blocked by old-fashioned shutters with broad iron bars, which were secured every night. The walls were carefully sounded, and were shown to be quite solid all round, and the flooring was also thoroughly examined, with the same result. The chimney is wide, but is barred up by four large staples. It is certain, therefore, that my sister was quite alone when she met her end. Besides, there were no marks of any violence upon her.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢好仔細地調查咗案子,因為羅伊洛特醫生嘅行為喺郡裡早就聲名狼藉,但佢找唔到令人滿意嘅死因。我嘅證詞表明,門從裡面閂上喇,窗子被帶寬鐵條嘅老式百葉窗擋住,每晚都鎖上。牆壁被仔細敲擊過,證明四周完全堅實,地板都被徹底檢查,結果相同。煙囪好寬,但用四個大釘環封住喇。因此可以肯定,我姊姊遇到結局時完全係獨自一人。此外,佢身上冇任何暴力嘅痕跡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他非常仔細地調查了案子,因為羅伊洛特醫生的行為在郡裡早就聲名狼藉,但他找不到令人滿意的死因。我的證詞表明,門從裡面閂上了,窗子被帶寬鐵條的老式百葉窗擋住,每晚都鎖上。牆壁被仔細敲擊過,證明四周完全堅實,地板也被徹底檢查,結果相同。煙囪很寬,但用四個大釘環封住了。因此可以肯定,我姊姊遇到結局時完全是獨自一人。此外,她身上沒有任何暴力的痕跡。」

passages.original: “How about poison?”
passages.vernacular: 「中毒呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「中毒呢?」

passages.original: “The doctors examined her for it, but without success.”
passages.vernacular: 「醫生哋檢查過,但冇結果。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「醫生們檢查過,但沒有結果。」

passages.original: “What do you think that this unfortunate lady died of, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁你認為呢位不幸嘅女士係死於乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼你認為這位不幸的女士是死於什麼?」

passages.original: “It is my belief that she died of pure fear and nervous shock, though what it was that frightened her I cannot imagine.”
passages.vernacular: 「我相信佢死於純粹嘅恐懼同神經休克,雖然係乜嘢嚇到佢,我想像不出。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我相信她死於純粹的恐懼和神經休克,雖然是什麼嚇到她,我想像不出。」

passages.original: “Were there gipsies in the plantation at the time?”
passages.vernacular: 「當時種植園裡有吉普賽人嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當時種植園裡有吉普賽人嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, there are nearly always some there.”
passages.vernacular: 「有,嗰度幾乎總有啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有,那裡幾乎總有一些。」

passages.original: “Ah, and what did you gather from this allusion to a band—a speckled band?”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,你從呢個提到一條帶子——斑點帶子——嘅暗示中得出咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,你從這個提到一條帶子——斑點帶子——的暗示中得出了什麼?」

passages.original: “Sometimes I have thought that it was merely the wild talk of delirium, sometimes that it may have referred to some band of people, perhaps to these very gipsies in the plantation. I do not know whether the spotted handkerchiefs which so many of them wear over their heads might have suggested the strange adjective which she used.”
passages.vernacular: 「有時我想嗰不過係譫妄嘅胡話,有時我想佢可能指某一夥人,或者指嘅就係種植園裡嘅嗰啲吉普賽人。我唔知道佢哋許多人戴喺頭上嘅嗰啲有斑點嘅頭巾,係咪可能畀佢使用嘅嗰個奇怪嘅形容詞提供咗暗示。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有時我想那不過是譫妄的胡話,有時我想它可能指某一夥人,也許指的就是種植園裡的那些吉普賽人。我不知道他們許多人戴在頭上的那些有斑點的頭巾,是否可能給她使用的那個奇怪的形容詞提供了暗示。」

passages.original: Holmes shook his head like a man who is far from being satisfied.
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯搖頭,像一個遠冇滿意嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯搖頭,像一個遠沒有滿意的人。

passages.original: “These are very deep waters,” said he; “pray go on with your narrative.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢啲水好深,」佢講;「請繼續你嘅敘述。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這些水很深,」他說;「請繼續你的敘述。」

passages.original: “Two years have passed since then, and my life has been until lately lonelier than ever. A month ago, however, a dear friend, whom I have known for many years, has done me the honour to ask my hand in marriage. His name is Armitage—Percy Armitage—the second son of Mr. Armitage, of Crane Water, near Reading. My stepfather has offered no opposition to the match, and we are to be married in the course of the spring. Two days ago some repairs were started in the west wing of the building, and my bedroom wall has been pierced, so that I have had to move into the chamber in which my sister died, and to sleep in the very bed in which she slept. Imagine, then, my thrill of terror when last night, as I lay awake, thinking over her terrible fate, I suddenly heard in the silence of the night the low whistle which had been the herald of her own death. I sprang up and lit the lamp, but nothing was to be seen in the room. I was too shaken to go to bed again, however, so I dressed, and as soon as it was daylight I slipped down, got a dog-cart at the Crown Inn, which is opposite, and drove to Leatherhead, from whence I have come on this morning with the one object of seeing you and asking your advice.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰以後兩年過去喇,我嘅生活直到最近比以前更孤獨。不過,一個月前,一位我認識多年嘅親愛朋友賞臉向我求婚。佢嘅名字係阿米蒂奇——珀西·阿米蒂奇——係雷丁附近克蘭水嘅阿米蒂奇先生嘅次子。我繼父對呢門親事冇反對,我哋將喺春季結婚。兩天前,建築物嘅西翼開始咗啲修理,我嘅臥室牆被鑿穿喇,所以我唔得不搬到我姊姊死去嘅嗰個房間,瞓喺佢瞓過嘅嗰張床上。咁想像一下,尋日夜裡,我醒住躺喺床上,想住佢嘅可怕命運,突然喺夜晚嘅寂靜中聽到佢自己死亡前嘅預兆——嗰聲低沉嘅口哨,我嘅恐怖震顫。我跳起嚟點亮燈,但房間裡乜嘢都睇唔見。然而,我太震動喇,無法再上床,所以我穿上衣服,天一亮我就溜下嚟,喺對面嘅王冠旅店雇咗一輛雙輪輕馬車,駛到利瑟黑德,從嗰度今日朝早嚟,唯一嘅目的就係見你,請教你嘅意見。」
