passages.vernacular: 「哦,我聽講過嗰個人,」我嘅訪客回答,「如果佢肯接手呢件事,我會好高興,雖然當然我都必須利用官方警察。您能畀我介紹一下佢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我聽說過那個人,」我的訪客回答,「如果他肯接手這件事,我會非常高興,雖然當然我也必須利用官方警察。您能給我介紹一下他嗎?」

passages.original: “I’ll do better. I’ll take you round to him myself.”
passages.vernacular: 「我會做得更好。我親自帶您去見佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會做得更好。我親自帶您去見他。」

passages.original: “I should be immensely obliged to you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我將好感激您。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我將非常感激您。」

passages.original: “We’ll call a cab and go together. We shall just be in time to have a little breakfast with him. Do you feel equal to it?”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋叫輛馬車一起去。我哋剛好趕上同佢一起食點早餐。您覺得自己受得咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們叫輛馬車一起去。我們剛好趕上和他一起吃點早餐。您覺得自己受得了嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes; I shall not feel easy until I have told my story.”
passages.vernacular: 「受得喇;不把我嘅故事講完,我心裡唔會安寧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「受得了;不把我的故事講完,我心裡不會安寧。」

passages.original: “Then my servant will call a cab, and I shall be with you in an instant.” I rushed upstairs, explained the matter shortly to my wife, and in five minutes was inside a hansom, driving with my new acquaintance to Baker Street.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我嘅僕人會叫馬車,我即刻就同您一起去。」我衝上樓,向我妻子簡短地解釋咗事情,五分鐘後坐進一輛雙輪馬車,同我嘅新相識駛往貝克街。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我的僕人會叫馬車,我馬上就和您一起去。」我衝上樓,向我妻子簡短地解釋了事情,五分鐘後坐進一輛雙輪馬車,同我的新相識駛往貝克街。

passages.original: Sherlock Holmes was, as I expected, lounging about his sitting-room in his dressing-gown, reading the agony column of The Times and smoking his before-breakfast pipe, which was composed of all the plugs and dottles left from his smokes of the day before, all carefully dried and collected on the corner of the mantelpiece. He received us in his quietly genial fashion, ordered fresh rashers and eggs, and joined us in a hearty meal. When it was concluded he settled our new acquaintance upon the sofa, placed a pillow beneath his head, and laid a glass of brandy and water within his reach.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯正如我預料嘅,穿住晨衣喺起居室裡閒逛,讀住《泰晤士報》嘅尋人啟事欄,抽住佢早餐前嘅煙斗,煙斗裡裝嘅係前一天抽剩下嘅所有煙頭同殘渣,全都仔細地曬乾,收集喺壁爐台一角。佢以安靜而親切嘅方式接待咗我哋,吩咐煮新鮮嘅培根片同雞蛋,同我哋一起痛快地食咗一頓。飯後,佢讓我哋嘅新相識躺喺沙發上,喺佢頭下放咗一個枕頭,把一杯白蘭地兌水放喺佢伸手可及嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯正如我預料的,穿著晨衣在起居室裡閒逛,讀著《泰晤士報》的尋人啟事欄,抽著他早餐前的煙斗,煙斗裡裝的是前一天抽剩下的所有煙頭和殘渣,全都仔細地曬乾,收集在壁爐台一角。他以安靜而親切的方式接待了我們,吩咐煮新鮮的培根片和雞蛋,同我們一起痛快地吃了一頓。飯後,他讓我們的新相識躺在沙發上,在他頭下放了一個枕頭,把一杯白蘭地兌水放在他伸手可及的地方。

passages.original: “It is easy to see that your experience has been no common one, Mr. Hatherley,” said he. “Pray, lie down there and make yourself absolutely at home. Tell us what you can, but stop when you are tired and keep up your strength with a little stimulant.”
passages.vernacular: 「好容易睇出,哈瑟利先生,您嘅經歷唔係尋常嘅,」佢講。「請躺喺嗰度,完全當自己喺家。盡您所能告訴我哋,但累咗就停下,飲點興奮劑保持體力。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很容易看出,哈瑟利先生,您的經歷不是尋常的,」他說。「請躺在那裡,完全當自己在家。盡您所能告訴我們,但累了就停下,喝點興奮劑保持體力。」

passages.original: “Thank you,” said my patient, “but I have felt another man since the doctor bandaged me, and I think that your breakfast has completed the cure. I shall take up as little of your valuable time as possible, so I shall start at once upon my peculiar experiences.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝,」我嘅病人講,「但自從醫生畀我包紮之後,我覺得像換咗一個人,我想您嘅早餐完成咗治療。我會盡可能少佔用您寶貴嘅時間,所以我即刻開始講我嘅奇特經歷。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝,」我的病人說,「但自從醫生給我包紮之後,我覺得像換了一個人,我想您的早餐完成了治療。我會盡可能少佔用您寶貴的時間,所以我馬上開始講我的奇特經歷。」

passages.original: Holmes sat in his big armchair with the weary, heavy-lidded expression which veiled his keen and eager nature, while I sat opposite to him, and we listened in silence to the strange story which our visitor detailed to us.
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯坐喺佢嘅大扶手椅上,帶住疲倦、眼皮沉重嘅表情,嗰掩蓋咗佢敏銳而急切嘅天性,而我坐喺佢對面,我哋默默地聽住我哋嘅訪客向我哋詳述嘅奇特故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯坐在他的大扶手椅上,帶著疲倦、眼皮沉重的表情,那掩蓋了他敏銳而急切的天性,而我坐在他對面,我們默默地聽著我們的訪客向我們詳述的奇特故事。

passages.original: “You must know,” said he, “that I am an orphan and a bachelor, residing alone in lodgings in London. By profession I am a hydraulic engineer, and I have had considerable experience of my work during the seven years that I was apprenticed to Venner & Matheson, the well-known firm, of Greenwich. Two years ago, having served my time, and having also come into a fair sum of money through my poor father’s death, I determined to start in business for myself and took professional chambers in Victoria Street.
passages.vernacular: 「您必須知道,」佢講,「我係個孤兒同單身漢,獨自住喺倫敦嘅出租房裡。我嘅職業係水力工程師,喺格林尼治著名嘅韋納同馬西森公司當學徒嘅七年間,我對我嘅工作有咗相當多嘅經驗。兩年前,學徒期滿,又因可憐嘅父親去世而得到一筆可觀嘅錢,我決定自己創業,喺維多利亞街租咗專業辦公室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您必須知道,」他說,「我是個孤兒和單身漢,獨自住在倫敦的出租房裡。我的職業是水力工程師,在格林尼治著名的韋納與馬西森公司當學徒的七年間,我對我的工作有了相當多的經驗。兩年前,學徒期滿,又因可憐的父親去世而得到一筆可觀的錢,我決定自己創業,在維多利亞街租了專業辦公室。

passages.original: “I suppose that everyone finds his first independent start in business a dreary experience. To me it has been exceptionally so. During two years I have had three consultations and one small job, and that is absolutely all that my profession has brought me. My gross takings amount to £ 27 10s. Every day, from nine in the morning until four in the afternoon, I waited in my little den, until at last my heart began to sink, and I came to believe that I should never have any practice at all.
passages.vernacular: 「我想每個人都會覺得佢第一次獨立創業係一次淒涼嘅經歷。對我來講尤其如此。兩年嚟,我只有三次諮詢同一份小工作,呢完全係我嘅職業畀我帶嚟嘅全部。我嘅總收入係二十七鎊十先令。每天,從朝早九點到下午四點,我喺我嘅小窩裡等待,直到最後我嘅心開始下沉,我開始相信我永遠唔會有任何業務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想每個人都會覺得他第一次獨立創業是一次淒涼的經歷。對我來說尤其如此。兩年來,我只有三次諮詢和一份小工作,這完全是我的職業給我帶來的全部。我的總收入是二十七鎊十先令。每天,從早上九點到下午四點,我在我的小窩裡等待,直到最後我的心開始下沉,我開始相信我永遠不會有任何業務。

passages.original: “Yesterday, however, just as I was thinking of leaving the office, my clerk entered to say there was a gentleman waiting who wished to see me upon business. He brought up a card, too, with the name of ‘Colonel Lysander Stark’ engraved upon it. Close at his heels came the colonel himself, a man rather over the middle size, but of an exceeding thinness. I do not think that I have ever seen so thin a man. His whole face sharpened away into nose and chin, and the skin of his cheeks was drawn quite tense over his outstanding bones. Yet this emaciation seemed to be his natural habit, and due to no disease, for his eye was bright, his step brisk, and his bearing assured. He was plainly but neatly dressed, and his age, I should judge, would be nearer forty than thirty.
passages.vernacular: 「然而,尋日,就喺我想離開辦公室嘅時候,我嘅職員進來講,有一位先生等住要見我談事務。佢仲攞上嚟一張名片,上面刻住『萊桑德·斯塔克上校』嘅名字。緊跟住佢嘅係上校本人,一個身高略高於中等、但極其瘦嘅人。我想我從未見過咁瘦嘅人。佢整張臉都尖削成鼻子同下巴,臉頰嘅皮膚緊緊繃喺突出嘅骨頭上。然而呢種消瘦似乎係佢嘅天然習慣,唔係由於任何疾病,因為佢嘅眼睛明亮,步伐輕快,舉止自信。佢穿得樸素但整潔,佢嘅年紀,我判斷,更接近四十而唔係三十。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然而,昨天,就在我想離開辦公室的時候,我的職員進來說,有一位先生等著要見我談事務。他還拿上來一張名片,上面刻著『萊桑德·斯塔克上校』的名字。緊跟著他的是上校本人,一個身高略高於中等、但極其瘦的人。我想我從未見過這麼瘦的人。他整張臉都尖削成鼻子和下巴,臉頰的皮膚緊緊繃在突出的骨頭上。然而這種消瘦似乎是他的天然習慣,不是由於任何疾病,因為他的眼睛明亮,步伐輕快,舉止自信。他穿得樸素但整潔,他的年紀,我判斷,更接近四十而不是三十。

passages.original: “‘Mr. Hatherley?’ said he, with something of a German accent. ‘You have been recommended to me, Mr. Hatherley, as being a man who is not only proficient in his profession but is also discreet and capable of preserving a secret.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哈瑟利先生?』佢講,帶有啲德國口音。『哈瑟利先生,有人向我推薦您,講您不僅喺專業上精通,而且謹慎,能夠保守秘密。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哈瑟利先生?』他說,帶有一點德國口音。『哈瑟利先生,有人向我推薦您,說您不僅在專業上精通,而且謹慎,能夠保守秘密。』

passages.original: “I bowed, feeling as flattered as any young man would at such an address. ‘May I ask who it was who gave me so good a character?’
passages.vernacular: 「我鞠咗一躬,感到像任何年輕人聽到呢種稱呼嗰樣受寵若驚。『我可以問問係邊個畀咗我咁好嘅評價嗎?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我鞠了一躬,感到像任何年輕人聽到這種稱呼那樣受寵若驚。『我可以問問是誰給了我這麼好的評價嗎?』

passages.original: “‘Well, perhaps it is better that I should not tell you that just at this moment. I have it from the same source that you are both an orphan and a bachelor and are residing alone in London.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,或者我最好此刻唔好告訴您。我從同一來源得知,您既係孤兒又係單身漢,獨自住喺倫敦。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,也許我最好此刻不要告訴您。我從同一來源得知,您既是孤兒又是單身漢,獨自住在倫敦。』

passages.original: “‘That is quite correct,’ I answered; ‘but you will excuse me if I say that I cannot see how all this bears upon my professional qualifications. I understand that it was on a professional matter that you wished to speak to me?’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗰完全正確,』我回答;『但請原諒我講,我睇不出呢一切同我嘅專業資格有何關係。我理解您想同我談嘅係一件專業嘅事?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『那完全正確,』我回答;『但請原諒我說,我看不出這一切與我的專業資格有何關係。我理解您想同我談的是一件專業的事?』

passages.original: “‘Undoubtedly so. But you will find that all I say is really to the point. I have a professional commission for you, but absolute secrecy is quite essential—absolute secrecy, you understand, and of course we may expect that more from a man who is alone than from one who lives in the bosom of his family.’
passages.vernacular: 「『確實如此。但您會發現我講嘅一切真嘅都係切題嘅。我有一項專業委託畀您,但絕對保密係必要嘅——絕對保密,您明白,而且當然,我哋可以預期獨居嘅人比生活喺家庭懷抱中嘅人更能做到呢啲。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『確實如此。但您會發現我說的一切真的都是切題的。我有一項專業委託給您,但絕對保密是必要的——絕對保密,您明白,而且當然,我們可以預期獨居的人比生活在家庭懷抱中的人更能做到這一點。』

passages.original: “‘If I promise to keep a secret,’ said I, ‘you may absolutely depend upon my doing so.’
passages.vernacular: 「『如果我答應保守秘密,』我講,『您可以完全相信我會做到。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『如果我答應保守秘密,』我說,『您可以完全相信我會做到。』

passages.original: “He looked very hard at me as I spoke, and it seemed to me that I had never seen so suspicious and questioning an eye.
passages.vernacular: 「我講呢話時,佢好用力地睇住我,喺我睇來,我從冇見過咁多疑同探詢嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說這話時,他非常用力地看著我,在我看來,我從沒見過這麼多疑和探詢的眼睛。

passages.original: “‘Do you promise, then?’ said he at last.
passages.vernacular: 「『嗰您答應喇?』佢最後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『那您答應了?』他最後說。

passages.original: “‘Yes, I promise.’
passages.vernacular: 「『係嘅,我答應。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『是的,我答應。』

passages.original: “‘Absolute and complete silence before, during, and after? No reference to the matter at all, either in word or writing?’
passages.vernacular: 「『事前、事中、事後都絕對同完全嘅沉默?完全不提呢件事,無論口頭定係書面?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『事前、事中、事後都絕對和完全的沉默?完全不提這件事,無論口頭還是書面?』

passages.original: “‘I have already given you my word.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我已經向您保證喇。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我已經向您保證了。』

passages.original: “‘Very good.’ He suddenly sprang up, and darting like lightning across the room he flung open the door. The passage outside was empty.
passages.vernacular: 「『好好。』佢突然跳起嚟,像閃電一樣穿過房間,猛地打開門。外面嘅走廊係空嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『很好。』他突然跳起來,像閃電一樣穿過房間,猛地打開門。外面的走廊是空的。

passages.original: “‘That’s all right,’ said he, coming back. ‘I know that clerks are sometimes curious as to their master’s affairs. Now we can talk in safety.’ He drew up his chair very close to mine and began to stare at me again with the same questioning and thoughtful look.
passages.vernacular: 「『冇問題,』佢講,走回嚟。『我知道職員有時會好奇佢哋主人嘅事務。而家我哋可以安全地談話喇。』佢把椅子拉得離我嘅好近,又開始以同樣探詢同沉思嘅目光盯住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『沒問題,』他說,走回來。『我知道職員有時會好奇他們主人的事務。現在我們可以安全地談話了。』他把椅子拉得離我的非常近,又開始以同樣探詢和沉思的目光盯著我。

passages.original: “A feeling of repulsion, and of something akin to fear had begun to rise within me at the strange antics of this fleshless man. Even my dread of losing a client could not restrain me from showing my impatience.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個冇血肉嘅人嘅奇怪舉動,開始喺我心中升起一種排斥感,同某種近似恐懼嘅嘢。甚至我對失去客戶嘅擔心,都無法阻止我表現出不耐煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個沒有血肉的人的奇怪舉動,開始在我心中升起一種排斥感,和某種近似恐懼的東西。甚至我對失去客戶的擔心,也無法阻止我表現出不耐煩。

passages.original: “‘I beg that you will state your business, sir,’ said I; ‘my time is of value.’ Heaven forgive me for that last sentence, but the words came to my lips.
passages.vernacular: 「『先生,請講明您嘅事務,』我講;『我嘅時間係有價值嘅。』願上天原諒我最後嗰句話,但嗰啲話就到咗我嘅嘴邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『先生,請說明您的事務,』我說;『我的時間是有價值的。』願上天原諒我最後那句話,但那些話就到了我的嘴邊。

passages.original: “‘How would fifty guineas for a night’s work suit you?’ he asked.
passages.vernacular: 「『一個晚上嘅工作畀五十畿尼,您覺得如何?』佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『一個晚上的工作給五十畿尼,您覺得如何?』他問。

passages.original: “‘Most admirably.’
passages.vernacular: 「『好合適。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『非常合適。』

passages.original: “‘I say a night’s work, but an hour’s would be nearer the mark. I simply want your opinion about a hydraulic stamping machine which has got out of gear. If you show us what is wrong we shall soon set it right ourselves. What do you think of such a commission as that?’
passages.vernacular: 「『我講一個晚上嘅工作,但一個小時更接近實際。我只係想聽聽您對一台失靈嘅水力沖壓機嘅意見。如果您指出毛病喺邊度,我哋好快就能自己修好。您覺得咁樣嘅委託如何?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我說一個晚上的工作,但一個小時更接近實際。我只是想聽聽您對一台失靈的水力沖壓機的意見。如果您指出毛病在哪裡,我們很快就能自己修好。您覺得這樣的委託如何?』

passages.original: “‘The work appears to be light and the pay munificent.’
passages.vernacular: 「『工作似乎輕鬆,報酬豐厚。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『工作似乎輕鬆,報酬豐厚。』

passages.original: “‘Precisely so. We shall want you to come to-night by the last train.’
passages.vernacular: 「『正是咁樣。我哋要您今晚乘最後一班火車嚟。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『正是這樣。我們要您今晚乘最後一班火車來。』

passages.original: “‘Where to?’
passages.vernacular: 「『去邊度?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『去哪裡?』

passages.original: “‘To Eyford, in Berkshire. It is a little place near the borders of Oxfordshire, and within seven miles of Reading. There is a train from Paddington which would bring you there at about 11:15.’
passages.vernacular: 「『去伯克郡嘅艾福德。嗰個係個靠近牛津郡邊界嘅小地方,離雷丁唔到七英里。從帕丁頓有一班火車,大約十啲十五分把您帶到嗰度。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『去伯克郡的艾福德。那是個靠近牛津郡邊界的小地方,離雷丁不到七英里。從帕丁頓有一班火車,大約十一點十五分把您帶到那裡。』

passages.original: “‘Very good.’
“‘I shall come down in a carriage to meet you.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我會駕車下去接您。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我會駕車下去接您。』

passages.original: “‘There is a drive, then?’
passages.vernacular: 「『咁要乘車?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『那麼要乘車?』

passages.original: “‘Yes, our little place is quite out in the country. It is a good seven miles from Eyford Station.’
passages.vernacular: 「『係嘅,我哋嘅小地方完全喺鄉下。離艾福德車站足有七英里。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『是的,我們的小地方完全在鄉下。離艾福德車站足有七英里。』

passages.original: “‘Then we can hardly get there before midnight. I suppose there would be no chance of a train back. I should be compelled to stop the night.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗰我哋幾乎唔能夠喺午夜前到嗰度。我想唔會有回程嘅火車。我將被迫過夜。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『那我們幾乎不能在午夜前到那裡。我想不會有回程的火車。我將被迫過夜。』

passages.original: “‘Yes, we could easily give you a shake-down.’
passages.vernacular: 「『係嘅,我哋可以輕易畀您一個臨時鋪位。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『是的,我們可以輕易給您一個臨時鋪位。』

passages.original: “‘That is very awkward. Could I not come at some more convenient hour?’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗰好不方便。我唔能夠喺更方便嘅時間去嗎?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『那非常不方便。我不能在更方便的時間去嗎?』

passages.original: “‘We have judged it best that you should come late. It is to recompense you for any inconvenience that we are paying to you, a young and unknown man, a fee which would buy an opinion from the very heads of your profession. Still, of course, if you would like to draw out of the business, there is plenty of time to do so.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我哋判斷最好讓您晚點嚟。正是為了補償您嘅任何不便,我哋才付畀您咁樣一個年輕無名嘅人一筆足以買嚟你哋專業首腦意見嘅酬金。不過,當然,如果您想退出呢件事,有足夠嘅時間咁樣做。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我們判斷最好讓您晚點來。正是為了補償您的任何不便,我們才付給您這樣一個年輕無名的人一筆足以買來你們專業首腦意見的酬金。不過,當然,如果您想退出這件事,有足夠的時間這樣做。』

passages.original: “I thought of the fifty guineas, and of how very useful they would be to me. ‘Not at all,’ said I, ‘I shall be very happy to accommodate myself to your wishes. I should like, however, to understand a little more clearly what it is that you wish me to do.’
passages.vernacular: 「我想到咗嗰五十畿尼,同佢哋對我會幾咁有用。『啲都不,』我講,『我會好高興遷就您嘅願望。不過,我想更清楚地了解啲,您希望我做乜嘢。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想到了那五十畿尼,和它們對我會多麼有用。『一點也不,』我說,『我會很高興遷就您的願望。不過,我想更清楚地了解一點,您希望我做什麼。』

passages.original: “‘Quite so. It is very natural that the pledge of secrecy which we have exacted from you should have aroused your curiosity. I have no wish to commit you to anything without your having it all laid before you. I suppose that we are absolutely safe from eavesdroppers?’
passages.vernacular: 「『完全可以。我哋向您要求嘅保密誓言引起您嘅好奇係好自然嘅。我唔想喺您冇睇到全部情況之前就讓您承擔任何事。我想我哋絕對唔會被偷聽吧?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『完全可以。我們向您要求的保密誓言引起您的好奇是很自然的。我不想在您沒有看到全部情況之前就讓您承擔任何事。我想我們絕對不會被偷聽吧?』

passages.original: “‘Entirely.’
passages.vernacular: 「『完全唔會。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『完全不會。』

passages.original: “‘Then the matter stands thus. You are probably aware that fuller’s-earth is a valuable product, and that it is only found in one or two places in England?’
passages.vernacular: 「『咁事情係咁樣嘅。您大概知道,漂白土係一種有價值嘅產品,喺英國只喺一兩個地方才能找到?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『那麼事情是這樣的。您大概知道,漂白土是一種有價值的產品,在英國只在一兩個地方才能找到?』

passages.original: “‘I have heard so.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我聽講過。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我聽說過。』

passages.original: “‘Some little time ago I bought a small place—a very small place—within ten miles of Reading. I was fortunate enough to discover that there was a deposit of fuller’s-earth in one of my fields. On examining it, however, I found that this deposit was a comparatively small one, and that it formed a link between two very much larger ones upon the right and left—both of them, however, in the grounds of my neighbours. These good people were absolutely ignorant that their land contained that which was quite as valuable as a gold-mine. Naturally, it was to my interest to buy their land before they discovered its true value, but unfortunately I had no capital by which I could do this. I took a few of my friends into the secret, however, and they suggested that we should quietly and secretly work our own little deposit and that in this way we should earn the money which would enable us to buy the neighbouring fields. This we have now been doing for some time, and in order to help us in our operations we erected a hydraulic press. This press, as I have already explained, has got out of order, and we wish your advice upon the subject. We guard our secret very jealously, however, and if it once became known that we had hydraulic engineers coming to our little house, it would soon rouse inquiry, and then, if the facts came out, it would be good-bye to any chance of getting these fields and carrying out our plans. That is why I have made you promise me that you will not tell a human being that you are going to Eyford to-night. I hope that I make it all plain?’
passages.vernacular: 「『不久前,我買咗一小塊地——好小嘅一塊地——離雷丁唔到十英里。我幸運地發現我嘅一塊田裡有漂白土礦床。然而,檢查之後,我發現呢個礦床相對較小,佢係左右兩個更大得多嘅礦床之間嘅一個連結——但嗰兩個都喺我鄰居嘅地上。呢啲好人完全唔知道佢哋嘅土地含有價值不亞於金礦嘅嘢。自然,喺佢哋發現其真正價值之前買下佢哋嘅地對我有利,但不幸嘅係我冇資本去做呢件事。不過,我把呢個秘密告訴咗幾個朋友,佢哋建議我哋靜悄悄秘密地開採我哋自己嘅小礦床,咁樣我哋就能賺到使我哋能夠買下鄰近田地嘅錢。我哋而家已經咁樣做咗一段時間,為了幫助我哋嘅作業,我哋安裝咗一台水力壓機。呢台壓機,正如我已講明嘅,壞喇,我哋希望得到您喺呢個問題上嘅建議。不過,我哋好嚴密地守護住我哋嘅秘密,如果一旦知道有水力工程師到我哋嘅小房子嚟,好快就會引起詢問,然後,如果事實傳出去,嗰就別想有機會得到呢啲田地、實施我哋嘅計畫喇。呢個就係點解我讓您答應我,唔好告訴任何人您今晚要去艾福德。我希望我講清楚喇?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『不久前,我買了一小塊地——非常小的一塊地——離雷丁不到十英里。我幸運地發現我的一塊田裡有漂白土礦床。然而,檢查之後,我發現這個礦床相對較小,它是左右兩個更大得多的礦床之間的一個連結——但那兩個都在我鄰居的地上。這些好人完全不知道他們的土地含有價值不亞於金礦的東西。自然,在他們發現其真正價值之前買下他們的地對我有利,但不幸的是我沒有資本去做這件事。不過,我把這個秘密告訴了幾個朋友,他們建議我們靜悄悄秘密地開採我們自己的小礦床,這樣我們就能賺到使我們能夠買下鄰近田地的錢。我們現在已經這樣做了一段時間,為了幫助我們的作業,我們安裝了一台水力壓機。這台壓機,正如我已說明的,壞了,我們希望得到您在這個問題上的建議。不過,我們非常嚴密地守護著我們的秘密,如果一旦知道有水力工程師到我們的小房子來,很快就會引起詢問,然後,如果事實傳出去,那就別想有機會得到這些田地、實施我們的計畫了。這就是為什麼我讓您答應我,不要告訴任何人您今晚要去艾福德。我希望我說清楚了?』

passages.original: “‘I quite follow you,’ said I. ‘The only point which I could not quite understand was what use you could make of a hydraulic press in excavating fuller’s-earth, which, as I understand, is dug out like gravel from a pit.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我完全明白,』我講。『我唯一不太明白嘅啲係,您喺挖掘漂白土中能用水力壓機做乜嘢,據我了解,佢係像從礦坑裡挖礫石一樣挖出嚟嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我完全明白,』我說。『我唯一不太明白的一點是,您在挖掘漂白土中能用水力壓機做什麼,據我了解,它是像從礦坑裡挖礫石一樣挖出來的。』

passages.original: “‘Ah!’ said he carelessly, ‘we have our own process. We compress the earth into bricks, so as to remove them without revealing what they are. But that is a mere detail. I have taken you fully into my confidence now, Mr. Hatherley, and I have shown you how I trust you.’ He rose as he spoke. ‘I shall expect you, then, at Eyford at 11:15.’
passages.vernacular: 「『啊!』佢漫不經心地講,『我哋有我哋自己嘅工序。我哋把土壓成磚,咁樣搬走佢哋時就唔會暴露佢哋係乜嘢。但嗰只係細節。哈瑟利先生,我而家已經完全信任您喇,我都讓您睇到咗我係點樣信任您嘅。』佢講住站起嚟。『咁我期待您十啲十五分喺艾福德。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『啊!』他漫不經心地說,『我們有我們自己的工序。我們把土壓成磚,這樣搬走它們時就不會暴露它們是什麼。但那只是細節。哈瑟利先生,我現在已經完全信任您了,我也讓您看到了我是怎樣信任您的。』他說著站起來。『那麼我期待您十一點十五分在艾福德。』

passages.original: “‘I shall certainly be there.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我一定到。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我一定到。』

passages.original: “‘And not a word to a soul.’ He looked at me with a last long, questioning gaze, and then, pressing my hand in a cold, dank grasp, he hurried from the room.
passages.vernacular: 「『唔好對任何人講一個字。』佢最後以一個長長嘅、探詢嘅目光睇住我,然後用冰冷濕冷嘅握力握咗握我嘅手,匆匆離開咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『不要對任何人說一個字。』他最後以一個長長的、探詢的目光看著我,然後用冰冷濕冷的握力握了握我的手,匆匆離開了房間。

passages.original: “Well, when I came to think it all over in cool blood I was very much astonished, as you may both think, at this sudden commission which had been intrusted to me. On the one hand, of course, I was glad, for the fee was at least tenfold what I should have asked had I set a price upon my own services, and it was possible that this order might lead to other ones. On the other hand, the face and manner of my patron had made an unpleasant impression upon me, and I could not think that his explanation of the fuller’s-earth was sufficient to explain the necessity for my coming at midnight, and his extreme anxiety lest I should tell anyone of my errand. However, I threw all fears to the winds, ate a hearty supper, drove to Paddington, and started off, having obeyed to the letter the injunction as to holding my tongue.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,當我冷靜下嚟把呢一切重新想一遍時,你哋兩位或者會想到,我對託付畀我嘅呢項突如其嚟嘅委託好驚訝。一方面,我當然好高興,因為呢筆酬金至少係我自己畀自己嘅服務定價時所要求嘅十倍,而且呢個訂單可能帶嚟其他訂單。另一方面,我嘅資助人嘅臉同態度畀我留下咗不愉快嘅印象,我不認為佢對漂白土嘅解釋足以講明我必須午夜前嚟嘅必要性,以及佢極度擔心我把我嘅差事告訴任何人。不過,我把所有嘅恐懼拋到九霄雲外,痛快地食咗一頓晚餐,駕車到帕丁頓,出發喇,一字不差地遵守咗關於守口如瓶嘅告誡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,當我冷靜下來把這一切重新想一遍時,你們兩位也許會想到,我對託付給我的這項突如其來的委託非常驚訝。一方面,我當然很高興,因為這筆酬金至少是我自己給自己的服務定價時所要求的十倍,而且這個訂單可能帶來其他訂單。另一方面,我的資助人的臉和態度給我留下了不愉快的印象,我不認為他對漂白土的解釋足以說明我必須午夜前來的必要性,以及他極度擔心我把我的差事告訴任何人。不過,我把所有的恐懼拋到九霄雲外,痛快地吃了一頓晚餐,駕車到帕丁頓,出發了,一字不差地遵守了關於守口如瓶的告誡。

passages.original: “At Reading I had to change not only my carriage but my station. However, I was in time for the last train to Eyford, and I reached the little dim-lit station after eleven o’clock. I was the only passenger who got out there, and there was no one upon the platform save a single sleepy porter with a lantern. As I passed out through the wicket gate, however, I found my acquaintance of the morning waiting in the shadow upon the other side. Without a word he grasped my arm and hurried me into a carriage, the door of which was standing open. He drew up the windows on either side, tapped on the wood-work, and away we went as fast as the horse could go.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺雷丁,我不僅要換車廂,仲要換車站。不過,我趕上咗去艾福德嘅最後一班火車,十啲多到達嗰個燈光昏暗嘅小站。我係唯一喺嗰度下車嘅乘客,月台上除咗一個提住燈、瞓眼惺忪嘅搬運工之外,冇別人。然而,當我穿過小門出去時,我發現早晨嘅相識者喺另一邊嘅陰影裡等住。佢一言不發地抓住我嘅手臂,匆匆把我領進一輛車廂,車門係開住嘅。佢拉起兩側嘅窗子,敲咗敲木板,我哋就以馬能跑嘅最快速度出發喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在雷丁,我不僅要換車廂,還要換車站。不過,我趕上了去艾福德的最後一班火車,十一點多到達那個燈光昏暗的小站。我是唯一在那裡下車的乘客,月台上除了一個提著燈、睡眼惺忪的搬運工之外,沒有別人。然而,當我穿過小門出去時,我發現早晨的相識者在另一邊的陰影裡等著。他一言不發地抓住我的手臂,匆匆把我領進一輛車廂,車門是開著的。他拉起兩側的窗子,敲了敲木板,我們就以馬能跑的最快速度出發了。」

passages.original: “One horse?” interjected Holmes.
passages.vernacular: 「一匹馬?」福爾摩斯插話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一匹馬?」福爾摩斯插話。

passages.original: “Yes, only one.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,只有一匹。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,只有一匹。」

passages.original: “Did you observe the colour?”
passages.vernacular: 「你有冇注意到顏色?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有沒有注意到顏色?」

passages.original: “Yes, I saw it by the side-lights when I was stepping into the carriage. It was a chestnut.”
passages.vernacular: 「有,我上車時借住側燈睇到喇。係栗色嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有,我上車時借著側燈看到了。是栗色的。」

passages.original: “Tired-looking or fresh?”
passages.vernacular: 「睇起嚟疲倦定係精神?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看起來疲倦還是精神?」

passages.original: “Oh, fresh and glossy.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,精神而有光澤。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,精神而有光澤。」

passages.original: “Thank you. I am sorry to have interrupted you. Pray continue your most interesting statement.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝。好抱歉打斷你。請繼續你呢個最有趣嘅陳述。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝。很抱歉打斷你。請繼續你這最有趣的陳述。」

passages.original: “Away we went then, and we drove for at least an hour. Colonel Lysander Stark had said that it was only seven miles, but I should think, from the rate that we seemed to go, and from the time that we took, that it must have been nearer twelve. He sat at my side in silence all the time, and I was aware, more than once when I glanced in his direction, that he was looking at me with great intensity. The country roads seem to be not very good in that part of the world, for we lurched and jolted terribly. I tried to look out of the windows to see something of where we were, but they were made of frosted glass, and I could make out nothing save the occasional bright blur of a passing light. Now and then I hazarded some remark to break the monotony of the journey, but the colonel answered only in monosyllables, and the conversation soon flagged. At last, however, the bumping of the road was exchanged for the crisp smoothness of a gravel-drive, and the carriage came to a stand. Colonel Lysander Stark sprang out, and, as I followed after him, pulled me swiftly into a porch which gaped in front of us. We stepped, as it were, right out of the carriage and into the hall, so that I failed to catch the most fleeting glance of the front of the house. The instant that I had crossed the threshold the door slammed heavily behind us, and I heard faintly the rattle of the wheels as the carriage drove away.
passages.vernacular: 「於是我哋出發喇,駕咗至少一個小時嘅車。萊桑德·斯塔克上校講過只有七英里,但根據我哋似乎行駛嘅速度,同我哋花嘅時間,我想一定更接近十二英里。佢一直沉默地坐喺我旁邊,我不止一次瞥向佢時,意識到佢喺極其專注地睇住我。嗰個地方嘅鄉間道路似乎不太好,因為我哋顛簸得好厲害。我試圖從窗子往外睇,睇睇我哋喺邊度,但窗子係磨砂玻璃做嘅,除咗偶爾經過嘅燈光明亮模糊嘅一片之外,我乜嘢都睇不出。我不時冒昧地講一句話嚟打破旅途嘅單調,但上校只用單音節詞回答,談話好快就冷咗場。不過,最後,路面嘅顛簸換成咗碎石車道嘅清脆平滑,馬車停下喇。萊桑德·斯塔克上校跳出去,我跟喺佢後面時,佢迅速把我拉進我哋面前敞開嘅門廊。我哋可以講係直接從馬車走進咗門廳,所以我冇能捕捉到房子正面嘅邊怕最短暫嘅一瞥。我剛跨過門檻,門就喺我哋身後沉重地砰地關上,我隱約聽到馬車駛離時輪子嘅嘎嘎聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「於是我們出發了,駕了至少一個小時的車。萊桑德·斯塔克上校說過只有七英里,但根據我們似乎行駛的速度,和我們花的時間,我想一定更接近十二英里。他一直沉默地坐在我旁邊,我不止一次瞥向他時,意識到他在極其專注地看著我。那個地方的鄉間道路似乎不太好,因為我們顛簸得很厲害。我試圖從窗子往外看,看看我們在哪裡,但窗子是磨砂玻璃做的,除了偶爾經過的燈光明亮模糊的一片之外,我什麼也看不出。我不時冒昧地說一句話來打破旅途的單調,但上校只用單音節詞回答,談話很快就冷了場。不過,最後,路面的顛簸換成了碎石車道的清脆平滑,馬車停下了。萊桑德·斯塔克上校跳出去,我跟在他後面時,他迅速把我拉進我們面前敞開的門廊。我們可以說是直接從馬車走進了門廳,所以我沒能捕捉到房子正面的哪怕最短暫的一瞥。我剛跨過門檻,門就在我們身後沉重地砰地關上,我隱約聽到馬車駛離時輪子的嘎嘎聲。

passages.original: “It was pitch dark inside the house, and the colonel fumbled about looking for matches and muttering under his breath. Suddenly a door opened at the other end of the passage, and a long, golden bar of light shot out in our direction. It grew broader, and a woman appeared with a lamp in her hand, which she held above her head, pushing her face forward and peering at us. I could see that she was pretty, and from the gloss with which the light shone upon her dark dress I knew that it was a rich material. She spoke a few words in a foreign tongue in a tone as though asking a question, and when my companion answered in a gruff monosyllable she gave such a start that the lamp nearly fell from her hand. Colonel Stark went up to her, whispered something in her ear, and then, pushing her back into the room from whence she had come, he walked towards me again with the lamp in his hand.
passages.vernacular: 「房子裡面一片漆黑,上校摸索住找火柴,低聲嘟囔。突然,走廊另一端嘅一扇門打開,一道長長嘅金色光帶朝我哋射嚟。佢變寬喇,一個女人出現,手裡攞住燈,舉過頭頂,把臉向前探,凝視住我哋。我睇出佢好漂亮,從光照喺佢深色衣服上嘅光澤,我知道嗰個係上等料子。佢用外國語講咗幾個字,語氣像喺問一個問題,當我嘅同伴用粗聲嘅單音節回答時,佢驚得嗰樣厲害,燈幾乎從佢手中掉下嚟。斯塔克上校走到佢身邊,喺佢耳邊低聲講咗些乜嘢,然後把佢推回佢出嚟嘅房間,佢手裡攞住燈再次朝我走嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「房子裡面一片漆黑,上校摸索著找火柴,低聲嘟囔。突然,走廊另一端的一扇門打開,一道長長的金色光帶朝我們射來。它變寬了,一個女人出現,手裡拿著燈,舉過頭頂,把臉向前探,凝視著我們。我看出她很漂亮,從光照在她深色衣服上的光澤,我知道那是上等料子。她用外國語說了幾個字,語氣像在問一個問題,當我的同伴用粗聲的單音節回答時,她驚得那樣厲害,燈幾乎從她手中掉下來。斯塔克上校走到她身邊,在她耳邊低聲說了些什麼,然後把她推回她出來的房間,他手裡拿著燈再次朝我走來。

passages.original: “‘Perhaps you will have the kindness to wait in this room for a few minutes,’ said he, throwing open another door. It was a quiet, little, plainly furnished room, with a round table in the centre, on which several German books were scattered. Colonel Stark laid down the lamp on the top of a harmonium beside the door. ‘I shall not keep you waiting an instant,’ said he, and vanished into the darkness.
passages.vernacular: 「『或者您能好心喺呢個房間裡等幾分鐘,』佢講,猛地打開另一扇門。嗰個係個安靜嘅小房間,陳設簡單,中央有一張圓桌,上面散放住幾本德文書。斯塔克上校把燈放喺門旁一台簧風琴嘅頂上。『我唔會讓您等一刻,』佢講,消失喺黑暗中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『也許您能好心在這個房間裡等幾分鐘,』他說,猛地打開另一扇門。那是個安靜的小房間,陳設簡單,中央有一張圓桌,上面散放著幾本德文書。斯塔克上校把燈放在門旁一台簧風琴的頂上。『我不會讓您等一刻,』他說,消失在黑暗中。

passages.original: “I glanced at the books upon the table, and in spite of my ignorance of German I could see that two of them were treatises on science, the others being volumes of poetry. Then I walked across to the window, hoping that I might catch some glimpse of the country-side, but an oak shutter, heavily barred, was folded across it. It was a wonderfully silent house. There was an old clock ticking loudly somewhere in the passage, but otherwise everything was deadly still. A vague feeling of uneasiness began to steal over me. Who were these German people, and what were they doing living in this strange, out-of-the-way place? And where was the place? I was ten miles or so from Eyford, that was all I knew, but whether north, south, east, or west I had no idea. For that matter, Reading, and possibly other large towns, were within that radius, so the place might not be so secluded, after all. Yet it was quite certain, from the absolute stillness, that we were in the country. I paced up and down the room, humming a tune under my breath to keep up my spirits and feeling that I was thoroughly earning my fifty-guinea fee.
passages.vernacular: 「我瞥咗一眼桌上嘅書,儘管我不懂德語,我睇得出其中兩本係科學論文,其他係詩集。然後我走到窗子旁,希望能瞥見啲鄉村景色,但一扇橡木百葉窗,上咗粗重嘅橫栓,折疊住擋喺上面。呢個係一所異常安靜嘅房子。走廊裡某處有一個老鐘響亮地滴答作響,但除此之外一切都死一般靜。一種模糊嘅不安感開始悄悄爬上我嘅心。呢啲德國人係邊個,佢哋喺呢個奇怪、偏僻嘅地方做乜嘢?呢個地方又喺邊度?我離艾福德大約十英里,呢個就係我所知道嘅一切,但係北、南、東定係西,我毫無概念。就此而言,雷丁,以及可能其他大城鎮,都喺嗰個半徑之內,所以呢個地方或者畢竟唔係咁隱蔽。然而從絕對嘅寂靜可以完全確定,我哋係喺鄉下。我喺房間裡嚟回踱步,低聲哼住一支曲子嚟維持精神,覺得我確實在掙我嘅五十畿尼酬金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我瞥了一眼桌上的書,儘管我不懂德語,我看得出其中兩本是科學論文,其他是詩集。然後我走到窗子旁,希望能瞥見一點鄉村景色,但一扇橡木百葉窗,上了粗重的橫栓,折疊著擋在上面。這是一所異常安靜的房子。走廊裡某處有一個老鐘響亮地滴答作響,但除此之外一切都死一般靜。一種模糊的不安感開始悄悄爬上我的心。這些德國人是誰,他們在這個奇怪、偏僻的地方做什麼?這個地方又在哪裡?我離艾福德大約十英里,這就是我所知道的一切,但是北、南、東還是西,我毫無概念。就此而言,雷丁,以及可能其他大城鎮,都在那個半徑之內,所以這個地方也許畢竟不是那麼隱蔽。然而從絕對的寂靜可以完全確定,我們是在鄉下。我在房間裡來回踱步,低聲哼著一支曲子來維持精神,覺得我確實在掙我的五十畿尼酬金。

passages.original: “Suddenly, without any preliminary sound in the midst of the utter stillness, the door of my room swung slowly open. The woman was standing in the aperture, the darkness of the hall behind her, the yellow light from my lamp beating upon her eager and beautiful face. I could see at a glance that she was sick with fear, and the sight sent a chill to my own heart. She held up one shaking finger to warn me to be silent, and she shot a few whispered words of broken English at me, her eyes glancing back, like those of a frightened horse, into the gloom behind her.
passages.vernacular: 「突然,喺徹底嘅寂靜中,冇任何預先嘅聲音,我房間嘅門慢慢地打開喇。嗰個女人站喺門口,身後係門廳嘅黑暗,我嘅燈嘅黃色光芒照喺佢急切而美麗嘅臉上。我一眼就睇出佢怕得要命,呢個景象使我自己嘅心都發冷。佢舉起一根顫抖嘅手指警告我保持安靜,並向我迸出幾句斷續嘅英語耳語,佢嘅眼睛像受驚嘅馬一樣,回頭望住身後嘅昏暗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「突然,在徹底的寂靜中,沒有任何預先的聲音,我房間的門慢慢地打開了。那個女人站在門口,身後是門廳的黑暗,我的燈的黃色光芒照在她急切而美麗的臉上。我一眼就看出她怕得要命,這個景象使我自己的心也發冷。她舉起一根顫抖的手指警告我保持安靜,並向我迸出幾句斷續的英語耳語,她的眼睛像受驚的馬一樣,回頭望著身後的昏暗。

passages.original: “‘I would go,’ said she, trying hard, as it seemed to me, to speak calmly; ‘I would go. I should not stay here. There is no good for you to do.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我會走,』佢講,喺我睇來,佢喺拚命努力平靜地講話;『我會走。我唔應該該留喺呢度。你喺呢度做不咗乜嘢好事。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我會走,』她說,在我看來,她在拚命努力平靜地說話;『我會走。我不應該留在這裡。你在這裡做不了什麼好事。』

passages.original: “‘But, madam,’ said I, ‘I have not yet done what I came for. I cannot possibly leave until I have seen the machine.’
passages.vernacular: 「『但係,夫人,』我講,『我仲冇做我嚟做嘅事。喺見到嗰台機器之前,我絕唔可能離開。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『但是,夫人,』我說,『我還沒有做我來做的事。在見到那台機器之前,我絕不可能離開。』

passages.original: “‘It is not worth your while to wait,’ she went on. ‘You can pass through the door; no one hinders.’ And then, seeing that I smiled and shook my head, she suddenly threw aside her constraint and made a step forward, with her hands wrung together. ‘For the love of Heaven!’ she whispered, ‘get away from here before it is too late!’
passages.vernacular: 「『等待不值得,』佢繼續講。『你可以走出呢扇門;冇人阻攔。』然後,睇到我微笑並搖頭,佢突然拋開咗自制,向前邁咗一步,雙手絞喺一起。『睇喺上天嘅份上!』佢低聲講,『趁仲嚟得及,離開呢度!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『等待不值得,』她繼續說。『你可以走出這扇門;沒有人阻攔。』然後,看到我微笑並搖頭,她突然拋開了自制,向前邁了一步,雙手絞在一起。『看在上天的份上!』她低聲說,『趁還來得及,離開這裡!』

passages.original: “But I am somewhat headstrong by nature, and the more ready to engage in an affair when there is some obstacle in the way. I thought of my fifty-guinea fee, of my wearisome journey, and of the unpleasant night which seemed to be before me. Was it all to go for nothing? Why should I slink away without having carried out my commission, and without the payment which was my due? This woman might, for all I knew, be a monomaniac. With a stout bearing, therefore, though her manner had shaken me more than I cared to confess, I still shook my head and declared my intention of remaining where I was. She was about to renew her entreaties when a door slammed overhead, and the sound of several footsteps was heard upon the stairs. She listened for an instant, threw up her hands with a despairing gesture, and vanished as suddenly and as noiselessly as she had come.
passages.vernacular: 「但我天性有些固執,遇到障礙時更願意投入一件事。我想到我嘅五十畿尼酬金,我疲勞嘅旅程,以及似乎擺喺我面前嘅不愉快嘅夜晚。呢一切就都白費咗嗎?我點解要喺冇完成我嘅委託、冇得到我應得嘅酬金嘅情況下悄悄溜走?就我所知,呢個女人可能係個偏執狂。於是,我帶住堅定嘅神態,雖然佢嘅態度對我嘅震動比我願意承認嘅更大,我定係搖咗搖頭,宣布我打算留喺原地。佢正要重新懇求,呢陣頭頂上一扇門砰地關上,樓梯上傳嚟幾個人嘅腳步聲。佢聽咗片刻,以絕望嘅手勢舉起雙手,像嚟時一樣突然、無聲地消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我天性有些固執,遇到障礙時更願意投入一件事。我想到我的五十畿尼酬金,我疲勞的旅程,以及似乎擺在我面前的不愉快的夜晚。這一切就都白費了嗎?我為什麼要在沒有完成我的委託、沒有得到我應得的酬金的情況下悄悄溜走?就我所知,這個女人可能是個偏執狂。於是,我帶著堅定的神態,雖然她的態度對我的震動比我願意承認的更大,我還是搖了搖頭,宣布我打算留在原地。她正要重新懇求,這時頭頂上一扇門砰地關上,樓梯上傳來幾個人的腳步聲。她聽了片刻,以絕望的手勢舉起雙手,像來時一樣突然、無聲地消失了。

passages.original: “The newcomers were Colonel Lysander Stark and a short thick man with a chinchilla beard growing out of the creases of his double chin, who was introduced to me as Mr. Ferguson.
passages.vernacular: 「新嚟嘅係萊桑德·斯塔克上校同一個矮胖嘅男人,佢嘅雙下巴摺縫中長出一部絨鼠色嘅鬍子,向我介紹講係弗格森先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「新來的是萊桑德·斯塔克上校和一個矮胖的男人,他的雙下巴摺縫中長出一部絨鼠色的鬍子,向我介紹說是弗格森先生。

passages.original: “‘This is my secretary and manager,’ said the colonel. ‘By the way, I was under the impression that I left this door shut just now. I fear that you have felt the draught.’
passages.vernacular: 「『呢個係我嘅秘書同經理,』上校講。『順便講,我頭先有印象,我把呢扇門關上喇。我怕您感覺到咗穿堂風。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『這是我的秘書和經理,』上校說。『順便說,我剛才有印象,我把這扇門關上了。我怕您感覺到了穿堂風。』

passages.original: “‘On the contrary,’ said I, ‘I opened the door myself because I felt the room to be a little close.’
passages.vernacular: 「『相反,』我講,『係我自己開嘅門,因為我覺得房間有點悶。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『相反,』我說,『是我自己開的門,因為我覺得房間有點悶。』

passages.original: “He shot one of his suspicious looks at me. ‘Perhaps we had better proceed to business, then,’ said he. ‘Mr. Ferguson and I will take you up to see the machine.’
passages.vernacular: 「佢向我投嚟一個多疑嘅眼光。『咁或者我哋最好進入正題,』佢講。『弗格森先生同我帶您上去睇機器。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他向我投來一個多疑的眼光。『那麼也許我們最好進入正題,』他說。『弗格森先生和我帶您上去看機器。』

passages.original: “‘I had better put my hat on, I suppose.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我想我最好戴上帽子。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我想我最好戴上帽子。』

passages.original: “‘Oh, no, it is in the house.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,不,佢喺屋裡。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,不,它在屋裡。』

passages.original: “‘What, you dig fuller’s-earth in the house?’
passages.vernacular: 「『乜嘢,你哋喺屋裡挖漂白土?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『什麼,你們在屋裡挖漂白土?』

passages.original: “‘No, no. This is only where we compress it. But never mind that. All we wish you to do is to examine the machine and to let us know what is wrong with it.’
passages.vernacular: 「『不,不。呢只係我哋壓縮佢嘅地方。但唔好管呢個。我哋希望您做嘅只係檢查機器,讓我哋知道佢有乜嘢毛病。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『不,不。這只是我們壓縮它的地方。但不要管這個。我們希望您做的只是檢查機器,讓我們知道它有什麼毛病。』

passages.original: “We went upstairs together, the colonel first with the lamp, the fat manager and I behind him. It was a labyrinth of an old house, with corridors, passages, narrow winding staircases, and little low doors, the thresholds of which were hollowed out by the generations who had crossed them. There were no carpets and no signs of any furniture above the ground floor, while the plaster was peeling off the walls, and the damp was breaking through in green, unhealthy blotches. I tried to put on as unconcerned an air as possible, but I had not forgotten the warnings of the lady, even though I disregarded them, and I kept a keen eye upon my two companions. Ferguson appeared to be a morose and silent man, but I could see from the little that he said that he was at least a fellow-countryman.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋一起上樓,上校舉住燈喺最前面,胖經理同我跟喺佢後面。嗰個係一所迷宮般嘅老房子,有走廊、通道、狹窄嘅盤旋樓梯同低矮嘅小門,門檻被穿過佢哋嘅世世代代磨出咗凹陷。底層以上冇地毯,都冇任何家具嘅跡象,牆上嘅灰泥正在剝落,潮濕以綠色嘅、不健康嘅斑塊滲出。我試住盡可能裝出漠不關心嘅樣子,但我冇忘記嗰位女士嘅警告,儘管我不理會佢哋,我密切地注視住我嘅兩個同伴。弗格森似乎係個陰鬱沉默嘅人,但從佢所講嘅少數幾句話中,我睇出佢至少係我嘅同胞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們一起上樓,上校舉著燈在最前面,胖經理和我跟在他後面。那是一所迷宮般的老房子,有走廊、通道、狹窄的盤旋樓梯和低矮的小門,門檻被穿過它們的世世代代磨出了凹陷。底層以上沒有地毯,也沒有任何家具的跡象,牆上的灰泥正在剝落,潮濕以綠色的、不健康的斑塊滲出。我試著盡可能裝出漠不關心的樣子,但我沒有忘記那位女士的警告,儘管我不理會它們,我密切地注視著我的兩個同伴。弗格森似乎是個陰鬱沉默的人,但從他所說的少數幾句話中,我看出他至少是我的同胞。

passages.original: “Colonel Lysander Stark stopped at last before a low door, which he unlocked. Within was a small, square room, in which the three of us could hardly get at one time. Ferguson remained outside, and the colonel ushered me in.
passages.vernacular: 「萊桑德·斯塔克上校最後喺一扇矮門前停下,佢打開咗鎖。裡面係一個小嘅方形房間,我哋三個人同時進去幾乎擠不下。弗格森留喺外面,上校領我進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「萊桑德·斯塔克上校最後在一扇矮門前停下,他打開了鎖。裡面是一個小的方形房間,我們三個人同時進去幾乎擠不下。弗格森留在外面,上校領我進去。

passages.original: “‘We are now,’ said he, ‘actually within the hydraulic press, and it would be a particularly unpleasant thing for us if anyone were to turn it on. The ceiling of this small chamber is really the end of the descending piston, and it comes down with the force of many tons upon this metal floor. There are small lateral columns of water outside which receive the force, and which transmit and multiply it in the manner which is familiar to you. The machine goes readily enough, but there is some stiffness in the working of it, and it has lost a little of its force. Perhaps you will have the goodness to look it over and to show us how we can set it right.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我哋而家,』佢講,『實際上係喺水力壓機之內,如果有人把佢開動,對我哋將係特別不愉快嘅事。呢個小房間嘅天花板其實係下降活塞嘅末端,佢以許多噸嘅力量落喺呢個金屬地板上。外面有小嘅側向水柱接受呢種力量,並以您熟悉嘅方式傳遞同放大佢。機器運轉得夠順暢,但佢嘅操作有些僵硬,力量損失咗啲。或者您能好心檢查一下,告訴我哋點樣把佢修好。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我們現在,』他說,『實際上是在水力壓機之內,如果有人把它開動,對我們將是特別不愉快的事。這個小房間的天花板其實是下降活塞的末端,它以許多噸的力量落在這個金屬地板上。外面有小的側向水柱接受這種力量,並以您熟悉的方式傳遞和放大它。機器運轉得夠順暢,但它的操作有些僵硬,力量損失了一點。也許您能好心檢查一下,告訴我們怎樣把它修好。』

passages.original: “I took the lamp from him, and I examined the machine very thoroughly. It was indeed a gigantic one, and capable of exercising enormous pressure. When I passed outside, however, and pressed down the levers which controlled it, I knew at once by the whishing sound that there was a slight leakage, which allowed a regurgitation of water through one of the side cylinders. An examination showed that one of the india-rubber bands which was round the head of a driving-rod had shrunk so as not quite to fill the socket along which it worked. This was clearly the cause of the loss of power, and I pointed it out to my companions, who followed my remarks very carefully and asked several practical questions as to how they should proceed to set it right. When I had made it clear to them, I returned to the main chamber of the machine and took a good look at it to satisfy my own curiosity. It was obvious at a glance that the story of the fuller’s-earth was the merest fabrication, for it would be absurd to suppose that so powerful an engine could be designed for so inadequate a purpose. The walls were of wood, but the floor consisted of a large iron trough, and when I came to examine it I could see a crust of metallic deposit all over it. I had stooped and was scraping at this to see exactly what it was when I heard a muttered exclamation in German and saw the cadaverous face of the colonel looking down at me.
passages.vernacular: 「我從佢手裡接過燈,好徹底地檢查咗呢台機器。佢確實係一台龐然大物,能產生巨大嘅壓力。然而,當我走到外面,按下控制佢嘅操縱杆時,我即刻從嘶嘶聲得知有輕微嘅洩漏,使水從側面一個氣缸回流。檢查顯示,繞喺驅動桿頭上嘅一個橡皮圈收縮喇,冇完全填滿佢運作嘅槽孔。呢顯然係動力損失嘅原因,我向我嘅同伴指出,佢哋好仔細地聽住我嘅話,並就如何著手修好佢問咗幾個實際嘅問題。當我向佢哋講明白後,我回到機器嘅主室,仔細睇咗一遍,以滿足我自己嘅好奇心。一眼就可以睇出,漂白土嘅故事純屬捏造,因為假設咁強大嘅機器係為了咁不相稱嘅目的設計嘅,係荒謬嘅。牆壁係木頭嘅,但地板係一個大鐵槽,當我去檢查佢時,我睇到上面有一層金屬沉積物嘅硬殼。我彎下腰刮佢,想睇睇究竟係乜嘢,呢陣我聽到一聲用德語低聲嘟囔嘅驚呼,睇見上校嗰張屍體般嘅臉喺向下睇住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從他手裡接過燈,非常徹底地檢查了這台機器。它確實是一台龐然大物,能產生巨大的壓力。然而,當我走到外面,按下控制它的操縱杆時,我立刻從嘶嘶聲得知有輕微的洩漏,使水從側面一個氣缸回流。檢查顯示,繞在驅動桿頭上的一個橡皮圈收縮了,沒有完全填滿它運作的槽孔。這顯然是動力損失的原因,我向我的同伴指出,他們非常仔細地聽著我的話,並就如何著手修好它問了幾個實際的問題。當我向他們說明白後,我回到機器的主室,仔細看了一遍,以滿足我自己的好奇心。一眼就可以看出,漂白土的故事純屬捏造,因為假設這麼強大的機器是為了這麼不相稱的目的設計的,是荒謬的。牆壁是木頭的,但地板是一個大鐵槽,當我去檢查它時,我看到上面有一層金屬沉積物的硬殼。我彎下腰刮它,想看看究竟是什麼,這時我聽到一聲用德語低聲嘟囔的驚呼,看見上校那張屍體般的臉在向下看著我。

passages.original: “‘What are you doing there?’ he asked.
passages.vernacular: 「『你喺嗰度做乜嘢?』佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你在那裡做什麼?』他問。

passages.original: “I felt angry at having been tricked by so elaborate a story as that which he had told me. ‘I was admiring your fuller’s-earth,’ said I; ‘I think that I should be better able to advise you as to your machine if I knew what the exact purpose was for which it was used.’
passages.vernacular: 「我為被佢告訴我嘅咁精心設計嘅故事所欺騙而感到憤怒。『我喺欣賞您嘅漂白土,』我講;『我想如果我知道佢被使用的確切目的,我就能更好地就您嘅機器提出建議。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我為被他告訴我的那麼精心設計的故事所欺騙而感到憤怒。『我在欣賞您的漂白土,』我說;『我想如果我知道它被使用的確切目的,我就能更好地就您的機器提出建議。』

passages.original: “The instant that I uttered the words I regretted the rashness of my speech. His face set hard, and a baleful light sprang up in his grey eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「我講出呢啲話嘅嗰一刻,就後悔我言語嘅輕率。佢嘅臉僵硬喇,一道不祥嘅光從佢嘅灰眼睛中跳出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說出這些話的那一刻,就後悔我言語的輕率。他的臉僵硬了,一道不祥的光從他的灰眼睛中跳出來。

passages.original: “‘Very well,’ said he, ‘you shall know all about the machine.’ He took a step backward, slammed the little door, and turned the key in the lock. I rushed towards it and pulled at the handle, but it was quite secure, and did not give in the least to my kicks and shoves. ‘Hullo!’ I yelled. ‘Hullo! Colonel! Let me out!’
passages.vernacular: 「『好好,』佢講,『您將知道呢台機器嘅一切。』佢往後退咗一步,砰地關上小門,喺鎖中轉動鑰匙。我衝向佢,拉門把手,但佢好牢固,對我嘅踢同推絲毫不動。『喂!』我大喊。『喂!上校!放我出去!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『很好,』他說,『您將知道這台機器的一切。』他往後退了一步,砰地關上小門,在鎖中轉動鑰匙。我衝向它,拉門把手,但它非常牢固,對我的踢和推絲毫不動。『喂!』我大喊。『喂!上校!放我出去!』

passages.original: “And then suddenly in the silence I heard a sound which sent my heart into my mouth. It was the clank of the levers and the swish of the leaking cylinder. He had set the engine at work. The lamp still stood upon the floor where I had placed it when examining the trough. By its light I saw that the black ceiling was coming down upon me, slowly, jerkily, but, as none knew better than myself, with a force which must within a minute grind me to a shapeless pulp. I threw myself, screaming, against the door, and dragged with my nails at the lock. I implored the colonel to let me out, but the remorseless clanking of the levers drowned my cries. The ceiling was only a foot or two above my head, and with my hand upraised I could feel its hard, rough surface. Then it flashed through my mind that the pain of my death would depend very much upon the position in which I met it. If I lay on my face the weight would come upon my spine, and I shuddered to think of that dreadful snap. Easier the other way, perhaps; and yet, had I the nerve to lie and look up at that deadly black shadow wavering down upon me? Already I was unable to stand erect, when my eye caught something which brought a gush of hope back to my heart.
passages.vernacular: 「然後突然喺寂靜中我聽到一個聲音,使我嘅心跳到咗嗓子眼。嗰個係操縱杆嘅鏗鏘聲同洩漏嘅氣缸嘅嘶嘶聲。佢開動咗機器。燈仍然放喺地板上,我檢查鐵槽時把佢放喺嗰度。借住佢嘅光,我睇見黑色嘅天花板正向我壓下嚟,緩慢地、一頓一頓地,但,冇人比我自己更清楚,帶住一種力量,必定喺一分鐘內把我碾成冇形狀嘅肉泥。我尖叫住撲向門,用指甲拉扯鎖。我懇求上校放我出去,但操縱杆無情嘅鏗鏘聲淹沒咗我嘅叫喊。天花板離我頭頂只有一兩英尺,我舉起手就能感到佢堅硬粗糙嘅表面。然後我腦子裡閃過一個念頭:我死亡嘅痛苦將好大程度上取決於我遇上佢嘅姿勢。如果我臉朝下躺住,重量會壓喺我嘅脊椎上,我想到嗰可怕嘅折斷聲就發抖。或者另一種方式容易些;不過,我有冇膽量躺住睇住嗰個搖搖晃晃向我壓下嘅致命黑影?我已經無法站直,呢陣我嘅眼睛捕捉到一樣嘢,使一股希望湧回我心中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後突然在寂靜中我聽到一個聲音,使我的心跳到了嗓子眼。那是操縱杆的鏗鏘聲和洩漏的氣缸的嘶嘶聲。他開動了機器。燈仍然放在地板上,我檢查鐵槽時把它放在那裡。借著它的光,我看見黑色的天花板正向我壓下來,緩慢地、一頓一頓地,但,沒有人比我自己更清楚,帶著一種力量,必定在一分鐘內把我碾成沒有形狀的肉泥。我尖叫著撲向門,用指甲拉扯鎖。我懇求上校放我出去,但操縱杆無情的鏗鏘聲淹沒了我的叫喊。天花板離我頭頂只有一兩英尺,我舉起手就能感到它堅硬粗糙的表面。然後我腦子裡閃過一個念頭:我死亡的痛苦將很大程度上取決於我遇上它的姿勢。如果我臉朝下躺著,重量會壓在我的脊椎上,我想到那可怕的折斷聲就發抖。也許另一種方式容易些;可是,我有沒有膽量躺著看著那個搖搖晃晃向我壓下的致命黑影?我已經無法站直,這時我的眼睛捕捉到一樣東西,使一股希望湧回我心中。

passages.original: “I have said that though the floor and ceiling were of iron, the walls were of wood. As I gave a last hurried glance around, I saw a thin line of yellow light between two of the boards, which broadened and broadened as a small panel was pushed backward. For an instant I could hardly believe that here was indeed a door which led away from death. The next instant I threw myself through, and lay half-fainting upon the other side. The panel had closed again behind me, but the crash of the lamp, and a few moments afterwards the clang of the two slabs of metal, told me how narrow had been my escape.
passages.vernacular: 「我講過,雖然地板同天花板係鐵嘅,牆壁係木頭嘅。我最後匆忙環顧四周時,睇到兩塊板之間有一道細細嘅黃色光線,隨住一塊小嵌板被向後推開,佢越嚟越寬。有一刻我幾乎唔能夠相信呢度真嘅有一扇通往逃離死亡嘅門。下一刻我撲咗過去,半昏半醒地躺喺另一邊。嵌板喺我身後又關上喇,但燈嘅碎裂聲,以及片刻後兩塊金屬板嘅鏗鏘聲,告訴我我逃得幾咁險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說過,雖然地板和天花板是鐵的,牆壁是木頭的。我最後匆忙環顧四周時,看到兩塊板之間有一道細細的黃色光線,隨著一塊小嵌板被向後推開,它越來越寬。有一刻我幾乎不能相信這裡真的有一扇通往逃離死亡的門。下一刻我撲了過去,半昏半醒地躺在另一邊。嵌板在我身後又關上了,但燈的碎裂聲,以及片刻後兩塊金屬板的鏗鏘聲,告訴我我逃得多麼險。

passages.original: “I was recalled to myself by a frantic plucking at my wrist, and I found myself lying upon the stone floor of a narrow corridor, while a woman bent over me and tugged at me with her left hand, while she held a candle in her right. It was the same good friend whose warning I had so foolishly rejected.
passages.vernacular: 「一陣瘋狂嘅拉扯我手腕嘅動作使我清醒過嚟,我發現自己躺喺一條窄走廊嘅石頭地板上,一個女人俯身喺我上方,用左手拉住我,右手攞住一支蠟燭。係同一位好朋友,我曾嗰樣愚蠢地拒絕佢嘅警告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一陣瘋狂的拉扯我手腕的動作使我清醒過來,我發現自己躺在一條窄走廊的石頭地板上,一個女人俯身在我上方,用左手拉著我,右手拿著一支蠟燭。是同一位好朋友,我曾那樣愚蠢地拒絕她的警告。

passages.original: “‘Come! come!’ she cried breathlessly. ‘They will be here in a moment. They will see that you are not there. Oh, do not waste the so-precious time, but come!’
passages.vernacular: 「『嚟!嚟!』佢喘住氣喊道。『佢哋即刻就到呢度喇。佢哋會睇到你不喺嗰度。哦,唔好浪費咁寶貴嘅時間,快嚟!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『來!來!』她喘著氣喊道。『他們馬上就到這裡了。他們會看到你不在那裡。哦,不要浪費這麼寶貴的時間,快來!』

passages.original: “This time, at least, I did not scorn her advice. I staggered to my feet and ran with her along the corridor and down a winding stair. The latter led to another broad passage, and just as we reached it we heard the sound of running feet and the shouting of two voices, one answering the other from the floor on which we were and from the one beneath. My guide stopped and looked about her like one who is at her wit’s end. Then she threw open a door which led into a bedroom, through the window of which the moon was shining brightly.
passages.vernacular: 「呢一次,至少,我冇輕視佢嘅建議。我踉蹌地站起嚟,同佢沿住走廊跑,走下一道盤旋樓梯。樓梯通向另一條寬走廊,我哋剛到嗰度,就聽到奔跑嘅腳步聲同兩個人嘅叫喊聲,一個回答另一個,從我哋所在嘅樓層同下面一層傳嚟。我嘅嚮導停下,環顧四周,像一個走投無路嘅人。然後佢猛地打開一扇通往臥室嘅門,窗子裡月光明亮地照進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這一次,至少,我沒有輕視她的建議。我踉蹌地站起來,同她沿著走廊跑,走下一道盤旋樓梯。樓梯通向另一條寬走廊,我們剛到那裡,就聽到奔跑的腳步聲和兩個人的叫喊聲,一個回答另一個,從我們所在的樓層和下面一層傳來。我的嚮導停下,環顧四周,像一個走投無路的人。然後她猛地打開一扇通往臥室的門,窗子裡月光明亮地照進來。

passages.original: “‘It is your only chance,’ said she. ‘It is high, but it may be that you can jump it.’
passages.vernacular: 「『呢個係你唯一嘅機會,』佢講。『好高,但或者你能跳下去。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『這是你唯一的機會,』她說。『很高,但也許你能跳下去。』

passages.original: “As she spoke a light sprang into view at the further end of the passage, and I saw the lean figure of Colonel Lysander Stark rushing forward with a lantern in one hand and a weapon like a butcher’s cleaver in the other. I rushed across the bedroom, flung open the window, and looked out. How quiet and sweet and wholesome the garden looked in the moonlight, and it could not be more than thirty feet down. I clambered out upon the sill, but I hesitated to jump until I should have heard what passed between my saviour and the ruffian who pursued me. If she were ill-used, then at any risks I was determined to go back to her assistance. The thought had hardly flashed through my mind before he was at the door, pushing his way past her; but she threw her arms round him and tried to hold him back.
passages.vernacular: 「佢講話時,通道遠端有一道光出現,我睇見萊桑德·斯塔克上校瘦削嘅身影衝上前嚟,一隻手攞住燈籠,另一隻手攞住像屠夫切肉刀一樣嘅武器。我衝過臥室,推開窗子往外睇。花園喺月光下顯得幾咁安靜、甜美同健康,而且下去唔會超過三十英尺。我爬到窗台上,但猶豫住不跳,想聽聽我嘅救星同追我嘅惡棍之間講乜嘢。如果佢受到虐待,嗰我決心不惜任何風險回去幫助佢。呢個念頭剛閃過我嘅腦海,佢就到咗門口,從佢身邊擠過去;但佢用雙臂摟住佢,試圖拉住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她說話時,通道遠端有一道光出現,我看見萊桑德·斯塔克上校瘦削的身影衝上前來,一隻手拿著燈籠,另一隻手拿著像屠夫切肉刀一樣的武器。我衝過臥室,推開窗子往外看。花園在月光下顯得多麼安靜、甜美和健康,而且下去不會超過三十英尺。我爬到窗台上,但猶豫著不跳,想聽聽我的救星和追我的惡棍之間說什麼。如果她受到虐待,那我決心不惜任何風險回去幫助她。這個念頭剛閃過我的腦海,他就到了門口,從她身邊擠過去;但她用雙臂摟住他,試圖拉住他。

passages.original: “‘Fritz! Fritz!’ she cried in English, ‘remember your promise after the last time. You said it should not be again. He will be silent! Oh, he will be silent!’
passages.vernacular: 「『弗里茨!弗里茨!』佢用英語喊道,『記住你上次之後嘅承諾。你講過唔會再有喇。佢會保持沉默嘅!哦,佢會保持沉默嘅!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『弗里茨!弗里茨!』她用英語喊道,『記住你上次之後的承諾。你說過不會再有了。他會保持沉默的!哦,他會保持沉默的!』

passages.original: “‘You are mad, Elise!’ he shouted, struggling to break away from her. ‘You will be the ruin of us. He has seen too much. Let me pass, I say!’ He dashed her to one side, and, rushing to the window, cut at me with his heavy weapon. I had let myself go, and was hanging by the hands to the sill, when his blow fell. I was conscious of a dull pain, my grip loosened, and I fell into the garden below.
passages.vernacular: 「『你瘋喇,艾莉絲!』佢喊道,拚命想掙脫佢。『你會毀咗我哋。佢睇到嘅太多喇。讓我過去,我講!』佢把佢猛推到一邊,衝到窗邊,用佢沉重嘅武器向我砍嚟。我已鬆手,正用雙手吊喺窗台上,呢陣佢嘅一擊落下喇。我感到一陣鈍痛,抓握鬆開,掉進咗下面嘅花園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你瘋了,艾莉絲!』他喊道,拚命想掙脫她。『你會毀了我們。他看到的太多了。讓我過去,我說!』他把她猛推到一邊,衝到窗邊,用他沉重的武器向我砍來。我已鬆手,正用雙手吊在窗台上,這時他的一擊落下了。我感到一陣鈍痛,抓握鬆開,掉進了下面的花園。

passages.original: “I was shaken but not hurt by the fall; so I picked myself up and rushed off among the bushes as hard as I could run, for I understood that I was far from being out of danger yet. Suddenly, however, as I ran, a deadly dizziness and sickness came over me. I glanced down at my hand, which was throbbing painfully, and then, for the first time, saw that my thumb had been cut off and that the blood was pouring from my wound. I endeavoured to tie my handkerchief round it, but there came a sudden buzzing in my ears, and next moment I fell in a dead faint among the rose-bushes.
passages.vernacular: 「我被摔得震動,但冇受傷;所以我爬起嚟,盡我所能地跑進灌木叢,因為我明白我仲遠冇脫離危險。然而,我跑住嘅時候,突然一陣致命嘅眩暈同噁心襲嚟。我低頭睇我嘅手,佢痛苦地跳動,然後,第一次睇到我嘅拇指被砍掉喇,血從我嘅傷口湧出。我努力用手帕紮住佢,但我嘅耳朵裡突然傳嚟嗡嗡聲,下一刻我就昏死過去,倒喺玫瑰叢中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我被摔得震動,但沒有受傷;所以我爬起來,盡我所能地跑進灌木叢,因為我明白我還遠沒有脫離危險。然而,我跑著的時候,突然一陣致命的眩暈和噁心襲來。我低頭看我的手,它痛苦地跳動,然後,第一次看到我的拇指被砍掉了,血從我的傷口湧出。我努力用手帕紮住它,但我的耳朵裡突然傳來嗡嗡聲,下一刻我就昏死過去,倒在玫瑰叢中。

passages.original: “How long I remained unconscious I cannot tell. It must have been a very long time, for the moon had sunk, and a bright morning was breaking when I came to myself. My clothes were all sodden with dew, and my coat-sleeve was drenched with blood from my wounded thumb. The smarting of it recalled in an instant all the particulars of my night’s adventure, and I sprang to my feet with the feeling that I might hardly yet be safe from my pursuers. But to my astonishment, when I came to look round me, neither house nor garden were to be seen. I had been lying in an angle of the hedge close by the high road, and just a little lower down was a long building, which proved, upon my approaching it, to be the very station at which I had arrived upon the previous night. Were it not for the ugly wound upon my hand, all that had passed during those dreadful hours might have been an evil dream.
passages.vernacular: 「我昏迷咗多久,我講不出。一定係好長嘅時間,因為月亮已經下沉,我醒嚟時明亮嘅早晨正在破曉。我嘅衣服全被露水浸透,我嘅外套袖子被我受傷拇指嘅血浸濕。傷口嘅刺痛即刻喚回咗我夜間冒險嘅所有細節,我跳起嚟,覺得我仲幾乎唔能夠脫離追趕者嘅危險。但令我食驚嘅係,當我環顧四周時,睇唔到房子,都睇唔到花園。我一直躺喺靠近大路嘅一個樹籬角落裡,稍微往下啲係一幢長長嘅建築,我走近一睇,證明佢就係我前一晚到達嘅嗰個車站。若唔係我手上嗰個難睇嘅傷口,喺嗰啲可怕嘅時辰裡所發生嘅一切,可能只係一場惡夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我昏迷了多久,我說不出。一定是很長的時間,因為月亮已經下沉,我醒來時明亮的早晨正在破曉。我的衣服全被露水浸透,我的外套袖子被我受傷拇指的血浸濕。傷口的刺痛立刻喚回了我夜間冒險的所有細節,我跳起來,覺得我還幾乎不能脫離追趕者的危險。但令我吃驚的是,當我環顧四周時,看不到房子,也看不到花園。我一直躺在靠近大路的一個樹籬角落裡,稍微往下一點是一幢長長的建築,我走近一看,證明它就是我前一晚到達的那個車站。若不是我手上那個難看的傷口,在那些可怕的時辰裡所發生的一切,可能只是一場惡夢。

passages.original: “Half dazed, I went into the station and asked about the morning train. There would be one to Reading in less than an hour. The same porter was on duty, I found, as had been there when I arrived. I inquired of him whether he had ever heard of Colonel Lysander Stark. The name was strange to him. Had he observed a carriage the night before waiting for me? No, he had not. Was there a police-station anywhere near? There was one about three miles off.
passages.vernacular: 「半昏半醒地,我走進車站,詢問早晨嘅火車。唔到一小時就有一班去雷丁嘅。我發現,當值嘅係我到達時喺嗰度嘅同一個搬運工。我問佢有冇聽講過萊桑德·斯塔克上校。呢個名字對佢好陌生。佢有冇注意到前一晚有一輛馬車喺等我?冇,佢冇。附近有警察局嗎?大約三英里外有一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「半昏半醒地,我走進車站,詢問早晨的火車。不到一小時就有一班去雷丁的。我發現,當值的是我到達時在那裡的同一個搬運工。我問他有沒有聽說過萊桑德·斯塔克上校。這個名字對他很陌生。他有沒有注意到前一晚有一輛馬車在等我?沒有,他沒有。附近有警察局嗎?大約三英里外有一個。

passages.original: “It was too far for me to go, weak and ill as I was. I determined to wait until I got back to town before telling my story to the police. It was a little past six when I arrived, so I went first to have my wound dressed, and then the doctor was kind enough to bring me along here. I put the case into your hands and shall do exactly what you advise.”
passages.vernacular: 「對於我咁樣虛弱病痛嘅人來講,太遠喇。我決定等回到城裡再向警察講述我嘅故事。我到達時剛過六點,所以我先去處理傷口,然後醫生好心把我帶到呢度。我把呢個案子交到你手中,將完全照你嘅建議去做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對於我這樣虛弱病痛的人來說,太遠了。我決定等回到城裡再向警察講述我的故事。我到達時剛過六點,所以我先去處理傷口,然後醫生好心把我帶到這裡。我把這個案子交到你手中,將完全照你的建議去做。」

passages.original: We both sat in silence for some little time after listening to this extraordinary narrative. Then Sherlock Holmes pulled down from the shelf one of the ponderous commonplace books in which he placed his cuttings.
passages.vernacular: 聽完呢個非凡嘅敘述之後,我哋兩人默默地坐咗好一會兒。然後夏洛克·福爾摩斯從架子上抽下一本佢用嚟貼剪報嘅笨重嘅備忘簿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽完這個非凡的敘述之後,我們兩人默默地坐了好一會兒。然後夏洛克·福爾摩斯從架子上抽下一本他用來貼剪報的笨重的備忘簿。

passages.original: “Here is an advertisement which will interest you,” said he. “It appeared in all the papers about a year ago. Listen to this: ‘Lost, on the 9th inst., Mr. Jeremiah Hayling, aged twenty-six, a hydraulic engineer. Left his lodgings at ten o’clock at night, and has not been heard of since. Was dressed in,’ etc., etc. Ha! That represents the last time that the colonel needed to have his machine overhauled, I fancy.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢度有一則你會感興趣嘅廣告,」佢講。「大約一年前佢登喺所有報紙上。聽呢個:『本月9日失蹤,傑里邁亞·海林先生,二十六歲,水力工程師。晚上十點離開寓所,從此音訊全無。所穿衣服為,』等等,等等。哈!我想,呢代表咗上校最後一次需要檢修佢嘅機器。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡有一則你會感興趣的廣告,」他說。「大約一年前它登在所有報紙上。聽這個:『本月9日失蹤,傑里邁亞·海林先生,二十六歲,水力工程師。晚上十點離開寓所,從此音訊全無。所穿衣服為,』等等,等等。哈!我想,這代表了上校最後一次需要檢修他的機器。」

passages.original: “Good heavens!” cried my patient. “Then that explains what the girl said.”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!」我嘅病人喊道。「咁呢解釋咗嗰位姑娘講嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!」我的病人喊道。「那麼這解釋了那位姑娘說的話。」

passages.original: “Undoubtedly. It is quite clear that the colonel was a cool and desperate man, who was absolutely determined that nothing should stand in the way of his little game, like those out-and-out pirates who will leave no survivor from a captured ship. Well, every moment now is precious, so if you feel equal to it we shall go down to Scotland Yard at once as a preliminary to starting for Eyford.”
passages.vernacular: 「無疑如此。好明顯,上校係個冷靜而亡命嘅人,佢絕對下決心不讓任何嘢妨礙佢嘅小遊戲,像嗰啲徹頭徹尾嘅海盜,不讓被俘船隻上留下任何倖存者。好,而家每一刻都寶貴,所以如果你覺得食得消,我哋即刻去蘇格蘭場,作為前往艾福德嘅前期準備。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「無疑如此。很明顯,上校是個冷靜而亡命的人,他絕對下決心不讓任何東西妨礙他的小遊戲,像那些徹頭徹尾的海盜,不讓被俘船隻上留下任何倖存者。好,現在每一刻都寶貴,所以如果你覺得吃得消,我們立刻去蘇格蘭場,作為前往艾福德的前期準備。」

passages.original: Some three hours or so afterwards we were all in the train together, bound from Reading to the little Berkshire village. There were Sherlock Holmes, the hydraulic engineer, Inspector Bradstreet, of Scotland Yard, a plain-clothes man, and myself. Bradstreet had spread an ordnance map of the county out upon the seat and was busy with his compasses drawing a circle with Eyford for its centre.
passages.vernacular: 大約三個小時後,我哋都喺火車上,從雷丁前往嗰個伯克郡小村。有夏洛克·福爾摩斯、嗰位水力工程師、蘇格蘭場嘅布拉德斯特里特督察、一名便衣,同我。布拉德斯特里特把郡嘅地形測量地圖鋪在座位上,忙住用圓規畫一個以艾福德為圓心嘅圓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約三個小時後,我們都在火車上,從雷丁前往那個伯克郡小村。有夏洛克·福爾摩斯、那位水力工程師、蘇格蘭場的布拉德斯特里特督察、一名便衣,和我。布拉德斯特里特把郡的地形測量地圖鋪在座位上,忙著用圓規畫一個以艾福德為圓心的圓。

passages.original: “There you are,” said he. “That circle is drawn at a radius of ten miles from the village. The place we want must be somewhere near that line. You said ten miles, I think, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺嗰度,」佢講。「嗰個圓係以離村子十英里為半徑畫嘅。我哋要找嘅地方一定喺嗰條線附近嘅某處。我想您講嘅係十英里,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在那裡,」他說。「那個圓是以離村子十英里為半徑畫的。我們要找的地方一定在那條線附近的某處。我想您說的是十英里,先生。」

passages.original: “It was an hour’s good drive.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係一個小時嘅順暢車程。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是一個小時的順暢車程。」

passages.original: “And you think that they brought you back all that way when you were unconscious?”
passages.vernacular: 「您認為佢哋喺您昏迷時又把您帶回咗咁遠?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您認為他們在您昏迷時又把您帶回了那麼遠?」

passages.original: “They must have done so. I have a confused memory, too, of having been lifted and conveyed somewhere.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋一定係咁樣做嘅。我都有模糊嘅記憶,被抬起嚟送到某個地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們一定是這樣做的。我也有模糊的記憶,被抬起來送到某個地方。」

passages.original: “What I cannot understand,” said I, “is why they should have spared you when they found you lying fainting in the garden. Perhaps the villain was softened by the woman’s entreaties.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白嘅係,」我講,「佢哋發現你昏倒喺花園裡時,點解會放過你。或者嗰惡棍被嗰個女人嘅懇求軟化喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白的是,」我說,「他們發現你昏倒在花園裡時,為什麼會放過你。也許那惡棍被那個女人的懇求軟化了。」

passages.original: “I hardly think that likely. I never saw a more inexorable face in my life.”
passages.vernacular: 「我幾乎不認為可能。我一生中從冇見過更無情嘅臉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我幾乎不認為可能。我一生中從沒見過更無情的臉。」

passages.original: “Oh, we shall soon clear up all that,” said Bradstreet. “Well, I have drawn my circle, and I only wish I knew at what point upon it the folk that we are in search of are to be found.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我哋好快就會弄清呢一切,」布拉德斯特里特講。「好,我已畫咗我嘅圓,我只希望知道我哋要找嘅人喺佢上面嘅邊啲能找到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我們很快就會弄清這一切,」布拉德斯特里特說。「好,我已畫了我的圓,我只希望知道我們要找的人在它上面的哪一點能找到。」

passages.original: “I think I could lay my finger on it,” said Holmes quietly.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我可以指出嚟,」福爾摩斯平靜地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我可以指出來,」福爾摩斯平靜地說。

passages.original: “Really, now!” cried the inspector, “you have formed your opinion! Come, now, we shall see who agrees with you. I say it is south, for the country is more deserted there.”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅嗎!」督察喊道,「你形成咗你嘅睇法!嚟吧,我哋睇睇邊個同意你。我講喺南邊,因為嗰度嘅鄉村更荒涼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的嗎!」督察喊道,「你形成了你的看法!來吧,我們看看誰同意你。我說在南邊,因為那裡的鄉村更荒涼。」

passages.original: “And I say east,” said my patient.
passages.vernacular: 「我講喺東邊,」我嘅病人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說在東邊,」我的病人說。

passages.original: “I am for west,” remarked the plain-clothes man. “There are several quiet little villages up there.”
passages.vernacular: 「我贊成西邊,」便衣講。「嗰邊有幾個安靜嘅小村。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我贊成西邊,」便衣說。「那邊有幾個安靜的小村。」

passages.original: “And I am for north,” said I, “because there are no hills there, and our friend says that he did not notice the carriage go up any.”
passages.vernacular: 「我贊成北邊,」我講,「因為嗰度冇山,而我哋呢位朋友講佢冇注意到馬車上過任何坡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我贊成北邊,」我說,「因為那裡沒有山,而我們這位朋友說他沒注意到馬車上過任何坡。」

passages.original: “Come,” cried the inspector, laughing; “it’s a very pretty diversity of opinion. We have boxed the compass among us. Who do you give your casting vote to?”
passages.vernacular: 「得喇,」督察笑住喊道;「真係個好漂亮嘅意見分歧。我哋把羅盤嘅方位都包喇。你把決定票投畀邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「得了,」督察笑著喊道;「真是個很漂亮的意見分歧。我們把羅盤的方位都包了。你把決定票投給誰?」

passages.original: “You are all wrong.”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋都錯喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們都錯了。」

passages.original: “But we can’t all be.”
passages.vernacular: 「但我哋唔可能都錯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我們不可能都錯。」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, you can. This is my point.” He placed his finger in the centre of the circle. “This is where we shall find them.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,你哋可以。呢個係我嘅點。」佢把手指放喺圓嘅中心。「我哋將喺呢度找到佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,你們可以。這是我的點。」他把手指放在圓的中心。「我們將在這裡找到他們。」

passages.original: “But the twelve-mile drive?” gasped Hatherley.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰十二英里嘅車程呢?」哈瑟利喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那十二英里的車程呢?」哈瑟利喘著氣說。

passages.original: “Six out and six back. Nothing simpler. You say yourself that the horse was fresh and glossy when you got in. How could it be that if it had gone twelve miles over heavy roads?”
passages.vernacular: 「去六英里,回六英里。再簡單不過。您自己講過,您上車時馬係精神而有光澤嘅。如果牠喺崎嶇嘅路上跑咗十二英里,點可能咁樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去六英里,回六英里。再簡單不過。您自己說過,您上車時馬是精神而有光澤的。如果牠在崎嶇的路上跑了十二英里,怎麼可能這樣?」

passages.original: “Indeed, it is a likely ruse enough,” observed Bradstreet thoughtfully. “Of course there can be no doubt as to the nature of this gang.”
passages.vernacular: 「確實,呢個係一個好可能嘅詭計,」布拉德斯特里特若有所思地講。「當然,毫無疑問呢夥人嘅性質係乜嘢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「確實,這是一個很可能的詭計,」布拉德斯特里特若有所思地說。「當然,毫無疑問這夥人的性質是什麼了。」

passages.original: “None at all,” said Holmes. “They are coiners on a large scale, and have used the machine to form the amalgam which has taken the place of silver.”
passages.vernacular: 「毫無疑問,」福爾摩斯講。「佢哋係大規模嘅偽幣製造者,用呢台機器製造代替銀嘅合金。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「毫無疑問,」福爾摩斯說。「他們是大規模的偽幣製造者,用這台機器製造代替銀的合金。」

passages.original: “We have known for some time that a clever gang was at work,” said the inspector. “They have been turning out half-crowns by the thousand. We even traced them as far as Reading, but could get no farther, for they had covered their traces in a way that showed that they were very old hands. But now, thanks to this lucky chance, I think that we have got them right enough.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋知道有一夥聰明嘅團夥喺活動已經有一段時間喇,」督察講。「佢哋一直喺成千上萬地製造半克朗硬幣。我哋甚至追蹤到雷丁,但無法再往前,因為佢哋以一種顯示佢哋係好老手嘅方式掩蓋咗蹤跡。但而家,多虧呢個幸運嘅機會,我想我哋肯定能抓住佢哋喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們知道有一夥聰明的團夥在活動已經有一段時間了,」督察說。「他們一直在成千上萬地製造半克朗硬幣。我們甚至追蹤到雷丁,但無法再往前,因為他們以一種顯示他們是非常老手的方式掩蓋了蹤跡。但現在,多虧這個幸運的機會,我想我們肯定能抓住他們了。」

passages.original: But the inspector was mistaken, for those criminals were not destined to fall into the hands of justice. As we rolled into Eyford Station we saw a gigantic column of smoke which streamed up from behind a small clump of trees in the neighbourhood and hung like an immense ostrich feather over the landscape.
passages.vernacular: 但督察錯喇,因為嗰啲罪犯註定唔會落入法網。我哋嘅火車駛入艾福德車站時,我哋睇到一股巨大嘅煙柱,從附近一小叢樹後面冒出,像一根巨大嘅鴕鳥羽毛一樣懸喺風景上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但督察錯了,因為那些罪犯註定不會落入法網。我們的火車駛入艾福德車站時,我們看到一股巨大的煙柱,從附近一小叢樹後面冒出,像一根巨大的鴕鳥羽毛一樣懸在風景上。

passages.original: “A house on fire?” asked Bradstreet as the train steamed off again on its way.
passages.vernacular: 「一幢房子住火喇?」火車再次噴住汽離開時,布拉德斯特里特問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一幢房子著火了?」火車再次噴著汽離開時,布拉德斯特里特問。

passages.original: “Yes, sir!” said the station-master.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生!」站長講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生!」站長說。

passages.original: “When did it break out?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢時候燒起嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼時候燒起來的?」

passages.original: “I hear that it was during the night, sir, but it has got worse, and the whole place is in a blaze.”
passages.vernacular: 「我聽講係喺夜裡,先生,但越嚟越嚴重,整個地方都喺燃燒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我聽說是在夜裡,先生,但越來越嚴重,整個地方都在燃燒。」

passages.original: “Whose house is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「係邊個嘅房子?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是誰的房子?」

passages.original: “Dr. Becher’s.”
passages.vernacular: 「貝徹醫生嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「貝徹醫生的。」

passages.original: “Tell me,” broke in the engineer, “is Dr. Becher a German, very thin, with a long, sharp nose?”
passages.vernacular: 「告訴我,」工程師插嘴講,「貝徹醫生係德國人嗎,好瘦,有一個又長又尖嘅鼻子?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「告訴我,」工程師插嘴說,「貝徹醫生是德國人嗎,非常瘦,有一個又長又尖的鼻子?」

passages.original: The station-master laughed heartily. “No, sir, Dr. Becher is an Englishman, and there isn’t a man in the parish who has a better-lined waistcoat. But he has a gentleman staying with him, a patient, as I understand, who is a foreigner, and he looks as if a little good Berkshire beef would do him no harm.”
passages.vernacular: 站長痛快地笑喇。「不,先生,貝徹醫生係英國人,呢個教區冇一個人嘅背心襯得比佢更滿。但佢有一位先生住喺佢嗰度,據我了解係個病人,係個外國人,佢睇起嚟好像食點好嘅伯克郡牛肉對佢冇壞處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站長痛快地笑了。「不,先生,貝徹醫生是英國人,這個教區沒有一個人的背心襯得比他更滿。但他有一位先生住在他那裡,據我了解是個病人,是個外國人,他看起來好像吃點好的伯克郡牛肉對他沒有壞處。」

passages.original: The station-master had not finished his speech before we were all hastening in the direction of the fire. The road topped a low hill, and there was a great widespread whitewashed building in front of us, spouting fire at every chink and window, while in the garden in front three fire-engines were vainly striving to keep the flames under.
passages.vernacular: 站長嘅話仲冇講完,我哋就都匆匆朝住起火嘅方向趕去。道路越過一座矮丘,我哋面前係一幢廣闊嘅白色建築,每道縫隙同每扇窗子都喺噴火,花園裡三輛消防車徒勞地試圖壓住火焰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站長的話還沒說完,我們就都匆匆朝著起火的方向趕去。道路越過一座矮丘,我們面前是一幢廣闊的白色建築,每道縫隙和每扇窗子都在噴火,花園裡三輛消防車徒勞地試圖壓住火焰。

passages.original: “That’s it!” cried Hatherley, in intense excitement. “There is the gravel-drive, and there are the rose-bushes where I lay. That second window is the one that I jumped from.”
passages.vernacular: 「就係嗰度!」哈瑟利極其興奮地喊道。「嗰個係碎石車道,嗰個係我躺過嘅玫瑰叢。嗰第二扇窗子就係我跳下嚟嘅嗰一扇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是那裡!」哈瑟利極其興奮地喊道。「那是碎石車道,那是我躺過的玫瑰叢。那第二扇窗子就是我跳下來的那一扇。」

passages.original: “Well, at least,” said Holmes, “you have had your revenge upon them. There can be no question that it was your oil-lamp which, when it was crushed in the press, set fire to the wooden walls, though no doubt they were too excited in the chase after you to observe it at the time. Now keep your eyes open in this crowd for your friends of last night, though I very much fear that they are a good hundred miles off by now.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,至少,」福爾摩斯講,「你已經向佢哋報咗仇。毫無疑問,係你嘅油燈喺壓機中被壓碎,點燃咗木牆,雖然無疑佢哋當時追趕你太興奮,冇注意到。而家,喺呢群人裡留心睇睇你琴晚嘅朋友哋,雖然我好擔心佢哋而家已喺一百英里之外喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,至少,」福爾摩斯說,「你已經向他們報了仇。毫無疑問,是你的油燈在壓機中被壓碎,點燃了木牆,雖然無疑他們當時追趕你太興奮,沒有注意到。現在,在這群人裡留心看看你昨晚的朋友們,雖然我非常擔心他們現在已在一百英里之外了。」

passages.original: And Holmes’ fears came to be realised, for from that day to this no word has ever been heard either of the beautiful woman, the sinister German, or the morose Englishman. Early that morning a peasant had met a cart containing several people and some very bulky boxes driving rapidly in the direction of Reading, but there all traces of the fugitives disappeared, and even Holmes’ ingenuity failed ever to discover the least clue as to their whereabouts.
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯嘅擔心變成咗現實,因為從嗰天到而家,從未聽到過嗰位美麗女人、嗰個陰險嘅德國人、或嗰個陰鬱嘅英國人嘅任何消息。嗰天清早,一個農民遇到一輛載住幾個人同幾個好大嘅箱子嘅馬車,向雷丁嘅方向疾駛,但喺嗰度逃亡者嘅一切痕跡都消失喇,連福爾摩斯嘅聰明才智都始終未能發現佢哋下落嘅最小線索。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯的擔心變成了現實,因為從那天到現在,從未聽到過那位美麗女人、那個陰險的德國人、或那個陰鬱的英國人的任何消息。那天清早,一個農民遇到一輛載著幾個人和幾個很大的箱子的馬車,向雷丁的方向疾駛,但在那裡逃亡者的一切痕跡都消失了,連福爾摩斯的聰明才智也始終未能發現他們下落的最小線索。

passages.original: The firemen had been much perturbed at the strange arrangements which they had found within, and still more so by discovering a newly severed human thumb upon a window-sill of the second floor. About sunset, however, their efforts were at last successful, and they subdued the flames, but not before the roof had fallen in, and the whole place been reduced to such absolute ruin that, save some twisted cylinders and iron piping, not a trace remained of the machinery which had cost our unfortunate acquaintance so dearly. Large masses of nickel and of tin were discovered stored in an out-house, but no coins were to be found, which may have explained the presence of those bulky boxes which have been already referred to.
passages.vernacular: 消防員對佢哋喺裡面發現嘅奇怪裝置好不安,更不安嘅係喺二樓一個窗台上發現一根新近被砍下嘅人嘅拇指。然而,大約日落時,佢哋嘅努力終於成功,控制咗火勢,但屋頂已經塌下,整個地方被毀成咁樣徹底嘅廢墟,除咗啲扭曲嘅氣缸同鐵管之外,嗰台使我哋不幸嘅相識付出如此慘重代價嘅機器已不留一絲痕跡。喺一間外屋裡發現咗大量嘅鎳同錫存放住,但冇找到硬幣,呢或者解釋咗嗰啲已經提到嘅大箱子嘅存在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 消防員對他們在裡面發現的奇怪裝置非常不安,更不安的是在二樓一個窗台上發現一根新近被砍下的人的拇指。然而,大約日落時,他們的努力終於成功,控制了火勢,但屋頂已經塌下,整個地方被毀成這樣徹底的廢墟,除了一些扭曲的氣缸和鐵管之外,那台使我們不幸的相識付出如此慘重代價的機器已不留一絲痕跡。在一間外屋裡發現了大量的鎳和錫存放著,但沒有找到硬幣,這也許解釋了那些已經提到的大箱子的存在。

passages.original: How our hydraulic engineer had been conveyed from the garden to the spot where he recovered his senses might have remained forever a mystery were it not for the soft mould, which told us a very plain tale. He had evidently been carried down by two persons, one of whom had remarkably small feet and the other unusually large ones. On the whole, it was most probable that the silent Englishman, being less bold or less murderous than his companion, had assisted the woman to bear the unconscious man out of the way of danger.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅水力工程師係點樣從花園被送到佢恢復知覺嘅地方嘅,可能永遠係個謎,若唔係柔軟嘅泥土向我哋講述咗一個好清楚嘅故事。顯然佢係被兩個人抬下去嘅,其中一個腳異常小,另一個異常大。總嘅來講,最可能嘅係嗰個沉默嘅英國人,不如佢嘅同伴大膽或不如佢嗜殺,協助嗰個女人把不省人事嘅人抬離危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的水力工程師是怎樣從花園被送到他恢復知覺的地方的,可能永遠是個謎,若不是柔軟的泥土向我們講述了一個非常清楚的故事。顯然他是被兩個人抬下去的,其中一個腳異常小,另一個異常大。總的來說,最可能的是那個沉默的英國人,不如他的同伴大膽或不如他嗜殺,協助那個女人把不省人事的人抬離危險。

passages.original: “Well,” said our engineer ruefully as we took our seats to return once more to London, “it has been a pretty business for me! I have lost my thumb and I have lost a fifty-guinea fee, and what have I gained?”
passages.vernacular: 「唉,」我哋嘅工程師沮喪地講,我哋坐下嚟再次返回倫敦,「對我來講呢真係一樁漂亮嘅事!我失去咗拇指,失去咗五十畿尼酬金,而我得到咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「唉,」我們的工程師沮喪地說,我們坐下來再次返回倫敦,「對我來說這真是一樁漂亮的事!我失去了拇指,失去了五十畿尼酬金,而我得到了什麼?」

passages.original: “Experience,” said Holmes, laughing. “Indirectly it may be of value, you know; you have only to put it into words to gain the reputation of being excellent company for the remainder of your existence.”
passages.vernacular: 「經驗,」福爾摩斯笑住講。「你知道,間接地佢可能有價值;你只需把佢講出嚟,就可以喺你餘生中贏得出色談伴嘅名聲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「經驗,」福爾摩斯笑著說。「你知道,間接地它可能有價值;你只需把它說出來,就可以在你餘生中贏得出色談伴的名聲。」

chapters.title: The Adventure of the Noble Bachelor 貴族單身漢

passages.original: The Lord St. Simon marriage, and its curious termination, have long ceased to be a subject of interest in those exalted circles in which the unfortunate bridegroom moves. Fresh scandals have eclipsed it, and their more piquant details have drawn the gossips away from this four-year-old drama. As I have reason to believe, however, that the full facts have never been revealed to the general public, and as my friend Sherlock Holmes had a considerable share in clearing the matter up, I feel that no memoir of him would be complete without some little sketch of this remarkable episode.
passages.vernacular: 聖西蒙勳爵嘅婚姻及其奇特嘅結局,早已唔再係嗰個不幸新郎所處嘅上流圈子裡感興趣嘅話題。新嘅醜聞已將佢蓋過,其更辛辣嘅細節已把閒話者從呢齣四年前嘅戲劇引開。然而,既然我有理由相信,全部事實從未向公眾透露,而且我嘅朋友夏洛克·福爾摩斯喺澄清此事中起咗相當大嘅作用,我覺得,若不稍微描述一下呢段非凡嘅插曲,關於佢嘅回憶錄就不完整。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖西蒙勳爵的婚姻及其奇特的結局,早已不再是那個不幸新郎所處的上流圈子裡感興趣的話題。新的醜聞已將它蓋過,其更辛辣的細節已把閒話者從這齣四年前的戲劇引開。然而,既然我有理由相信,全部事實從未向公眾透露,而且我的朋友夏洛克·福爾摩斯在澄清此事中起了相當大的作用,我覺得,若不稍微描述一下這段非凡的插曲,關於他的回憶錄就不完整。

passages.original: It was a few weeks before my own marriage, during the days when I was still sharing rooms with Holmes in Baker Street, that he came home from an afternoon stroll to find a letter on the table waiting for him. I had remained indoors all day, for the weather had taken a sudden turn to rain, with high autumnal winds, and the jezail bullet which I had brought back in one of my limbs as a relic of my Afghan campaign throbbed with dull persistence. With my body in one easy-chair and my legs upon another, I had surrounded myself with a cloud of newspapers until at last, saturated with the news of the day, I tossed them all aside and lay listless, watching the huge crest and monogram upon the envelope upon the table and wondering lazily who my friend’s noble correspondent could be.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係喺我自己結婚前幾個星期,當時我仲同福爾摩斯喺貝克街合住,佢下午散步回嚟,發現桌上有一封等住佢嘅信。我整天待喺室內,因為天氣突然轉雨,秋風猛烈,而我從阿富汗戰役中帶回嘅、留喺我一條肢體裡作為紀念嘅賈扎伊爾槍彈,正鈍痛而持續地跳動住。我嘅身體躺喺一把安樂椅上,雙腿放喺另一把上,身邊圍咗一圈報紙,直到最後,被當天嘅新聞浸透,我把佢哋全扔到一邊,無精打采地躺住,睇住桌上信封上巨大嘅徽章同花押字,懶洋洋地猜我朋友嘅呢位貴族通信者可能係邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是在我自己結婚前幾個星期,當時我還同福爾摩斯在貝克街合住,他下午散步回來,發現桌上有一封等著他的信。我整天待在室內,因為天氣突然轉雨,秋風猛烈,而我從阿富汗戰役中帶回的、留在我一條肢體裡作為紀念的賈扎伊爾槍彈,正鈍痛而持續地跳動著。我的身體躺在一把安樂椅上,雙腿放在另一把上,身邊圍了一圈報紙,直到最後,被當天的新聞浸透,我把它們全扔到一邊,無精打采地躺著,看著桌上信封上巨大的徽章和花押字,懶洋洋地猜我朋友的這位貴族通信者可能是誰。

passages.original: “Here is a very fashionable epistle,” I remarked as he entered. “Your morning letters, if I remember right, were from a fish-monger and a tide-waiter.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係一封好時髦嘅信,」佢進嚟時我講。「如果我冇記錯,你朝早嘅信係一個魚販同一個海關稽查員寄嚟嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是一封非常時髦的信,」他進來時我說。「如果我沒記錯,你早上的信是一個魚販和一個海關稽查員寄來的。」

passages.original: “Yes, my correspondence has certainly the charm of variety,” he answered, smiling, “and the humbler are usually the more interesting. This looks like one of those unwelcome social summonses which call upon a man either to be bored or to lie.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我嘅通信確實有多樣性嘅魅力,」佢微笑住回答,「而越卑微嘅通常越有趣。呢個睇起嚟像係嗰種不受歡迎嘅社交邀請,要求人要麼感到無聊,要麼撒謊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我的通信確實有多樣性的魅力,」他微笑著回答,「而越卑微的通常越有趣。這看起來像是那種不受歡迎的社交邀請,要求人要麼感到無聊,要麼撒謊。」

passages.original: He broke the seal and glanced over the contents.
passages.vernacular: 佢拆開封印,瀏覽咗內容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拆開封印,瀏覽了內容。

passages.original: “Oh, come, it may prove to be something of interest, after all.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,得喇,畢竟佢可能係有趣嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,得了,畢竟它可能是有趣的事。」

passages.original: “Not social, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰唔係社交嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那不是社交的?」

passages.original: “No, distinctly professional.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係,明顯係專業嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是,明顯是專業的。」

passages.original: “And from a noble client?”
passages.vernacular: 「來自貴族委託人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來自貴族委託人?」

passages.original: “One of the highest in England.”
passages.vernacular: 「英格蘭最高貴族之一。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「英格蘭最高貴族之一。」

passages.original: “My dear fellow, I congratulate you.”
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅朋友,我祝賀你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的朋友,我祝賀你。」

passages.original: “I assure you, Watson, without affectation, that the status of my client is a matter of less moment to me than the interest of his case. It is just possible, however, that that also may not be wanting in this new investigation. You have been reading the papers diligently of late, have you not?”
passages.vernacular: 「華生,我向你保證,毫不做作,委託人嘅地位對我來講比佢案子嘅趣味更不重要。不過,呢次新嘅調查中,趣味都好可能不缺。你最近一直喺勤奮地讀報,對吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「華生,我向你保證,毫不做作,委託人的地位對我來說比他案子的趣味更不重要。不過,這次新的調查中,趣味也很可能不缺。你最近一直在勤奮地讀報,對吧?」

passages.original: “It looks like it,” said I ruefully, pointing to a huge bundle in the corner. “I have had nothing else to do.”
passages.vernacular: 「睇起嚟係咁樣,」我沮喪地講,指住角落裡一大捆報紙。「我冇別嘅事可做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看起來是這樣,」我沮喪地說,指著角落裡一大捆報紙。「我沒有別的事可做。」

passages.original: “It is fortunate, for you will perhaps be able to post me up. I read nothing except the criminal news and the agony column. The latter is always instructive. But if you have followed recent events so closely you must have read about Lord St. Simon and his wedding?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個好幸運,因為你或者能向我提供最新消息。我除咗犯罪新聞同尋人啟事欄,乜嘢都不讀。後者總是有教益嘅。但如果你咁樣密切地跟蹤咗最近嘅事件,你一定讀到過聖西蒙勳爵同佢嘅婚禮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這很幸運,因為你也許能向我提供最新消息。我除了犯罪新聞和尋人啟事欄,什麼也不讀。後者總是有教益的。但如果你這樣密切地跟蹤了最近的事件,你一定讀到過聖西蒙勳爵和他的婚禮?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, with the deepest interest.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,極感興趣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,極感興趣。」

passages.original: “That is well. The letter which I hold in my hand is from Lord St. Simon. I will read it to you, and in return you must turn over these papers and let me have whatever bears upon the matter. This is what he says:
passages.vernacular: 「嗰好好。我手中嘅信係聖西蒙勳爵寫嘅。我讀畀你聽,作為回報,你必須翻翻呢啲報紙,把同此事有關嘅任何嘢畀我。佢係咁樣講嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那很好。我手中的信是聖西蒙勳爵寫的。我讀給你聽,作為回報,你必須翻翻這些報紙,把與此事有關的任何東西給我。他是這樣說的:

passages.original: “‘MY DEAR MR. SHERLOCK HOLMES,—Lord Backwater tells me that I may place implicit reliance upon your judgment and discretion. I have determined, therefore, to call upon you and to consult you in reference to the very painful event which has occurred in connection with my wedding. Mr. Lestrade, of Scotland Yard, is acting already in the matter, but he assures me that he sees no objection to your co-operation, and that he even thinks that it might be of some assistance. I will call at four o’clock in the afternoon, and, should you have any other engagement at that time, I hope that you will postpone it, as this matter is of paramount importance. Yours faithfully,
passages.vernacular: 「『親愛嘅夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生:巴克沃特勳爵告訴我,我可以完全信賴您嘅判斷力同謹慎。因此,我決定拜訪您,就同我嘅婚禮有關發生嘅嗰件好痛苦嘅事向您請教。蘇格蘭場嘅雷斯垂德先生已經喺處理呢件事,但佢向我保證,佢不反對您嘅合作,甚至認為呢可能有些幫助。我將喺下午四點鐘拜訪,如果您嗰時有任何其他約會,我希望您將佢推遲,因為此事至關重要。您忠實嘅,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『親愛的夏洛克·福爾摩斯先生:巴克沃特勳爵告訴我,我可以完全信賴您的判斷力和謹慎。因此,我決定拜訪您,就與我的婚禮有關發生的那件非常痛苦的事向您請教。蘇格蘭場的雷斯垂德先生已經在處理這件事,但他向我保證,他不反對您的合作,甚至認為這可能有些幫助。我將在下午四點鐘拜訪,如果您那時有任何其他約會,我希望您將它推遲,因為此事至關重要。您忠實的,

passages.original: “‘ROBERT ST. SIMON.’
passages.vernacular: 「『羅伯特·聖西蒙。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『羅伯特·聖西蒙。』

passages.original: “It is dated from Grosvenor Mansions, written with a quill pen, and the noble lord has had the misfortune to get a smear of ink upon the outer side of his right little finger,” remarked Holmes as he folded up the epistle.
passages.vernacular: 「信係從格羅夫納公寓寄出嘅,係用羽毛筆寫嘅,而呢位貴族勳爵不幸喺右手小指外側弄咗啲墨漬,」福爾摩斯把信折起嚟時講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「信是從格羅夫納公寓寄出的,是用羽毛筆寫的,而這位貴族勳爵不幸在右手小指外側弄了一點墨漬,」福爾摩斯把信折起來時說。

passages.original: “He says four o’clock. It is three now. He will be here in an hour.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢講四點鐘。而家係三點。佢一小時後會到呢度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他說四點鐘。現在是三點。他一小時後會到這裡。」

passages.original: “Then I have just time, with your assistance, to get clear upon the subject. Turn over those papers and arrange the extracts in their order of time, while I take a glance as to who our client is.” He picked a red-covered volume from a line of books of reference beside the mantelpiece. “Here he is,” said he, sitting down and flattening it out upon his knee. “‘Lord Robert Walsingham de Vere St. Simon, second son of the Duke of Balmoral.’ Hum! ‘Arms: Azure, three caltrops in chief over a fess sable. Born in 1846.’ He’s forty-one years of age, which is mature for marriage. Was Under-Secretary for the colonies in a late administration. The Duke, his father, was at one time Secretary for Foreign Affairs. They inherit Plantagenet blood by direct descent, and Tudor on the distaff side. Ha! Well, there is nothing very instructive in all this. I think that I must turn to you Watson, for something more solid.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我有時間,喺你嘅協助下,弄清呢個主題。翻翻嗰啲報紙,把摘錄按時間順序排好,我睇睇我哋嘅委託人係邊個。」佢從壁爐台旁一排參考書中抽出一本紅封面嘅書。「佢喺呢度,」佢講,坐下嚟把佢攤喺膝上。「『羅伯特·沃爾辛厄姆·德維爾·聖西蒙勳爵,巴爾莫勒公爵之次子。』嗯!『紋章:藍底,上有三個蒺藜,下有一道黑橫條。生於1846年。』佢四十一歲,對結婚來講算係成熟喇。喺前一屆政府中曾任殖民地事務次官。公爵,佢嘅父親,曾一度擔任外交大臣。佢哋直系繼承金雀花王朝嘅血統,母系繼承都鐸王朝嘅血統。哈!嗯,呢啲冇乜嘢好有教益嘅。我想我必須轉向你,華生,求取啲更實在嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我有時間,在你的協助下,弄清這個主題。翻翻那些報紙,把摘錄按時間順序排好,我看看我們的委託人是誰。」他從壁爐台旁一排參考書中抽出一本紅封面的書。「他在這裡,」他說,坐下來把它攤在膝上。「『羅伯特·沃爾辛厄姆·德維爾·聖西蒙勳爵,巴爾莫勒公爵之次子。』嗯!『紋章:藍底,上有三個蒺藜,下有一道黑橫條。生於1846年。』他四十一歲,對結婚來說算是成熟了。在前一屆政府中曾任殖民地事務次官。公爵,他的父親,曾一度擔任外交大臣。他們直系繼承金雀花王朝的血統,母系繼承都鐸王朝的血統。哈!嗯,這些沒有什麼很有教益的。我想我必須轉向你,華生,求取一些更實在的東西。」

passages.original: “I have very little difficulty in finding what I want,” said I, “for the facts are quite recent, and the matter struck me as remarkable. I feared to refer them to you, however, as I knew that you had an inquiry on hand and that you disliked the intrusion of other matters.”
passages.vernacular: 「我好容易找到我想要嘅,」我講,「因為事實好新,呢件事畀我嘅印象係好非凡嘅。不過,我怕攞嚟畀你,因為我知道你手上有一項調查,而且你不鍾意其他事情嘅打擾。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很容易找到我想要的,」我說,「因為事實很新,這件事給我的印象是很非凡的。不過,我怕拿來給你,因為我知道你手上有一項調查,而且你不喜歡其他事情的打擾。」

passages.original: “Oh, you mean the little problem of the Grosvenor Square furniture van. That is quite cleared up now—though, indeed, it was obvious from the first. Pray give me the results of your newspaper selections.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你指嘅係格羅夫納廣場家具搬運車嘅小問題。而家已經完全解決喇——雖然,確實,從一開始就好明顯。請把你報紙選段嘅結果畀我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你指的是格羅夫納廣場家具搬運車的小問題。現在已經完全解決了——雖然,確實,從一開始就很明顯。請把你報紙選段的結果給我。」

passages.original: “Here is the first notice which I can find. It is in the personal column of the Morning Post, and dates, as you see, some weeks back: ‘A marriage has been arranged,’ it says, ‘and will, if rumour is correct, very shortly take place, between Lord Robert St. Simon, second son of the Duke of Balmoral, and Miss Hatty Doran, the only daughter of Aloysius Doran. Esq., of San Francisco, Cal., U.S.A.’ That is all.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我能找到嘅第一則通告。「『已安排一門婚事,』上面講,『如果傳聞屬實,好快將喺巴爾莫勒公爵次子羅伯特·聖西蒙勳爵,同哈蒂·多蘭小姐,阿洛伊修斯·多蘭嘅獨生女之間舉行。先生,美國加利福尼亞州舊金山人。』就呢啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我能找到的第一則通告。「『已安排一門婚事,』上面說,『如果傳聞屬實,很快將在巴爾莫勒公爵次子羅伯特·聖西蒙勳爵,與哈蒂·多蘭小姐,阿洛伊修斯·多蘭的獨生女之間舉行。先生,美國加利福尼亞州舊金山人。』就這些。」
