passages.original: “Terse and to the point,” remarked Holmes, stretching his long, thin legs towards the fire.
passages.vernacular: 「簡潔而切題,」福爾摩斯講,把佢又長又細嘅雙腿伸向爐火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「簡潔而切題,」福爾摩斯說,把他又長又細的雙腿伸向爐火。

passages.original: “There was a paragraph amplifying this in one of the society papers of the same week. Ah, here it is: ‘There will soon be a call for protection in the marriage market, for the present free-trade principle appears to tell heavily against our home product. One by one the management of the noble houses of Great Britain is passing into the hands of our fair cousins from across the Atlantic. An important addition has been made during the last week to the list of the prizes which have been borne away by these charming invaders. Lord St. Simon, who has shown himself for over twenty years proof against the little god’s arrows, has now definitely announced his approaching marriage with Miss Hatty Doran, the fascinating daughter of a California millionaire. Miss Doran, whose graceful figure and striking face attracted much attention at the Westbury House festivities, is an only child, and it is currently reported that her dowry will run to considerably over the six figures, with expectancies for the future. As it is an open secret that the Duke of Balmoral has been compelled to sell his pictures within the last few years, and as Lord St. Simon has no property of his own save the small estate of Birchmoor, it is obvious that the Californian heiress is not the only gainer by an alliance which will enable her to make the easy and common transition from a Republican lady to a British peeress.’”
passages.vernacular: 「同一個星期嘅一份社交報紙上,有一段對此作咗擴充。啊,喺呢度:『婚姻市場上好快就需要保護喇,因為目前嘅自由貿易原則似乎對我哋嘅本國產品好不利。大不列顛貴族家庭嘅管理權,一個接一個地落入我哋來自大西洋彼岸嘅美麗表親手中。上個星期,呢啲迷人嘅入侵者帶走嘅戰利品名單上,又增添咗一項重要嘅條目。聖西蒙勳爵,二十多年嚟一直證明自己不受小神箭矢所傷,而家已明確宣布佢即將同加利福尼亞百萬富翁嘅迷人女兒哈蒂·多蘭小姐結婚。多蘭小姐嘅優雅身姿同引人注目的容貌,喺韋斯特伯里府嘅慶典上引起好多注意,佢係獨生女,據目前傳言,佢嘅嫁妝將遠遠超過六位數,將來仲有繼承嘅期望。既然巴爾莫勒公爵近幾年被迫出售佢嘅畫作係公開嘅秘密,而聖西蒙勳爵除咗小小嘅伯奇穆爾莊園之外冇自己嘅財產,顯然,從共和國嘅女士輕易而普遍地轉變為英國貴族夫人嘅呢門親事,並非只使呢位加利福尼亞繼承人獲益。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同一個星期的一份社交報紙上,有一段對此作了擴充。啊,在這裡:『婚姻市場上很快就需要保護了,因為目前的自由貿易原則似乎對我們的本國產品非常不利。大不列顛貴族家庭的管理權,一個接一個地落入我們來自大西洋彼岸的美麗表親手中。上個星期,這些迷人的入侵者帶走的戰利品名單上,又增添了一項重要的條目。聖西蒙勳爵,二十多年來一直證明自己不受小神箭矢所傷,現在已明確宣布他即將與加利福尼亞百萬富翁的迷人女兒哈蒂·多蘭小姐結婚。多蘭小姐的優雅身姿和引人注目的容貌,在韋斯特伯里府的慶典上引起很多注意,她是獨生女,據目前傳言,她的嫁妝將遠遠超過六位數,將來還有繼承的期望。既然巴爾莫勒公爵近幾年被迫出售他的畫作是公開的秘密,而聖西蒙勳爵除了小小的伯奇穆爾莊園之外沒有自己的財產,顯然,從共和國的女士輕易而普遍地轉變為英國貴族夫人的這門親事,並非只使這位加利福尼亞繼承人獲益。』」

passages.original: “Anything else?” asked Holmes, yawning.
passages.vernacular: 「仲有別嘅嗎?」福爾摩斯打住呵欠問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還有別的嗎?」福爾摩斯打著呵欠問。

passages.original: “Oh, yes; plenty. Then there is another note in the Morning Post to say that the marriage would be an absolutely quiet one, that it would be at St. George’s, Hanover Square, that only half a dozen intimate friends would be invited, and that the party would return to the furnished house at Lancaster Gate which has been taken by Mr. Aloysius Doran. Two days later—that is, on Wednesday last—there is a curt announcement that the wedding had taken place, and that the honeymoon would be passed at Lord Backwater’s place, near Petersfield. Those are all the notices which appeared before the disappearance of the bride.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,有嘅;好多。然後《晨郵報》上又有一則啟事,講婚禮將係絕對安靜嘅,將喺漢諾威廣場嘅聖喬治教堂舉行,只邀請半打密友,隨後婚禮隊伍將返回阿洛伊修斯·多蘭先生租下嘅蘭開斯特門嘅帶家具嘅房子。兩天後——都就係上星期三——有一則簡短嘅通告,講婚禮已經舉行,蜜月將喺彼得斯菲爾德附近巴克沃特勳爵嘅地方度過。呢個係新娘失蹤之前出現嘅所有通告。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,有的;很多。然後《晨郵報》上又有一則啟事,說婚禮將是絕對安靜的,將在漢諾威廣場的聖喬治教堂舉行,只邀請半打密友,隨後婚禮隊伍將返回阿洛伊修斯·多蘭先生租下的蘭開斯特門的帶家具的房子。兩天後——也就是上星期三——有一則簡短的通告,說婚禮已經舉行,蜜月將在彼得斯菲爾德附近巴克沃特勳爵的地方度過。這是新娘失蹤之前出現的所有通告。」

passages.original: “Before the what?” asked Holmes with a start.
passages.vernacular: 「新娘乜嘢之前?」福爾摩斯食咗一驚問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「新娘什麼之前?」福爾摩斯吃了一驚問。

passages.original: “The vanishing of the lady.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰位女士嘅消失。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那位女士的消失。」

passages.original: “When did she vanish, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰佢係乜嘢時候消失嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那她是什麼時候消失的?」

passages.original: “At the wedding breakfast.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺婚宴上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在婚宴上。」

passages.original: “Indeed. This is more interesting than it promised to be; quite dramatic, in fact.”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅。呢比佢預示嘅更有趣;事實上相當戲劇性。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的。這比它預示的更有趣;事實上相當戲劇性。」

passages.original: “Yes; it struck me as being a little out of the common.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅;佢畀我嘅印象有點不同尋常。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的;它給我的印象有點不同尋常。」

passages.original: “They often vanish before the ceremony, and occasionally during the honeymoon; but I cannot call to mind anything quite so prompt as this. Pray let me have the details.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋常喺儀式之前消失,偶爾喺蜜月期間;但我想不起有乜嘢像咁樣迅速嘅。請把細節畀我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她們常在儀式之前消失,偶爾在蜜月期間;但我想不起有什麼像這樣迅速的。請把細節給我。」

passages.original: “I warn you that they are very incomplete.”
passages.vernacular: 「我警告你,佢哋好不完整。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我警告你,它們非常不完整。」

passages.original: “Perhaps we may make them less so.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者我哋可以使佢哋不咁不完整。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許我們可以使它們不那麼不完整。」

passages.original: “Such as they are, they are set forth in a single article of a morning paper of yesterday, which I will read to you. It is headed, ‘Singular Occurrence at a Fashionable Wedding’:
passages.vernacular: 「就呢啲喇,佢哋載於尋日一份晨報嘅一篇文章中,我讀畀你聽。標題係『時髦婚禮上嘅離奇事件』:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就這些了,它們載於昨天一份晨報的一篇文章中,我讀給你聽。標題是『時髦婚禮上的離奇事件』:

passages.original: “‘The family of Lord Robert St. Simon has been thrown into the greatest consternation by the strange and painful episodes which have taken place in connection with his wedding. The ceremony, as shortly announced in the papers of yesterday, occurred on the previous morning; but it is only now that it has been possible to confirm the strange rumours which have been so persistently floating about. In spite of the attempts of the friends to hush the matter up, so much public attention has now been drawn to it that no good purpose can be served by affecting to disregard what is a common subject for conversation.
passages.vernacular: 「『羅伯特·聖西蒙勳爵嘅家人,因同佢嘅婚禮有關而發生嘅奇怪而痛苦嘅插曲,陷入咗極大嘅驚慌。儀式,如昨日報紙簡短宣布嘅,係喺前一天早晨舉行嘅;但直到而家才有可能證實一直喺持續流傳嘅奇怪傳言。儘管朋友哋試圖把呢件事壓下去,而家公眾已經好關注,假裝無視一個普遍談論嘅話題係冇用嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『羅伯特·聖西蒙勳爵的家人,因與他的婚禮有關而發生的奇怪而痛苦的插曲,陷入了極大的驚慌。儀式,如昨日報紙簡短宣布的,是在前一天早晨舉行的;但直到現在才有可能證實一直在持續流傳的奇怪傳言。儘管朋友們試圖把這件事壓下去,現在公眾已經非常關注,假裝無視一個普遍談論的話題是沒有用的。

passages.original: “‘The ceremony, which was performed at St. George’s, Hanover Square, was a very quiet one, no one being present save the father of the bride, Mr. Aloysius Doran, the Duchess of Balmoral, Lord Backwater, Lord Eustace and Lady Clara St. Simon (the younger brother and sister of the bridegroom), and Lady Alicia Whittington. The whole party proceeded afterwards to the house of Mr. Aloysius Doran, at Lancaster Gate, where breakfast had been prepared. It appears that some little trouble was caused by a woman, whose name has not been ascertained, who endeavoured to force her way into the house after the bridal party, alleging that she had some claim upon Lord St. Simon. It was only after a painful and prolonged scene that she was ejected by the butler and the footman. The bride, who had fortunately entered the house before this unpleasant interruption, had sat down to breakfast with the rest, when she complained of a sudden indisposition and retired to her room. Her prolonged absence having caused some comment, her father followed her, but learned from her maid that she had only come up to her chamber for an instant, caught up an ulster and bonnet, and hurried down to the passage. One of the footmen declared that he had seen a lady leave the house thus apparelled, but had refused to credit that it was his mistress, believing her to be with the company. On ascertaining that his daughter had disappeared, Mr. Aloysius Doran, in conjunction with the bridegroom, instantly put themselves in communication with the police, and very energetic inquiries are being made, which will probably result in a speedy clearing up of this very singular business. Up to a late hour last night, however, nothing had transpired as to the whereabouts of the missing lady. There are rumours of foul play in the matter, and it is said that the police have caused the arrest of the woman who had caused the original disturbance, in the belief that, from jealousy or some other motive, she may have been concerned in the strange disappearance of the bride.’”
passages.vernacular: 「『儀式喺漢諾威廣場嘅聖喬治教堂舉行,好安靜,在場嘅只有新娘嘅父親阿洛伊修斯·多蘭先生、巴爾莫勒公爵夫人、巴克沃特勳爵、尤斯塔斯勳爵同克拉拉·聖西蒙夫人(新郎嘅弟弟同妹妹),以及艾麗西亞·惠廷頓夫人。全體隨後前往阿洛伊修斯·多蘭先生喺蘭開斯特門嘅房子,嗰度已準備好早餐。似乎有一個姓名未能確定嘅女人引起咗啲麻煩,佢喺婚禮隊伍之後試圖強行闖入房子,聲稱佢對聖西蒙勳爵有某種要求。經過一場痛苦而漫長嘅場面,佢才被管家同男僕趕出去。新娘幸運地喺呢令人不快嘅打斷之前已進咗屋,同其他人一起坐下嚟食早餐,呢陣佢訴講突然不舒服,回房去喇。佢長時間不喺引起咗啲議論,佢父親跟住佢去,但從佢嘅女傭嗰度得知,佢只係上樓到佢房間一會兒,攞起一件長大衣同一頂軟帽,匆匆下到走廊。一名男僕聲稱佢睇到一位女士咁樣打扮離開房子,但拒絕相信嗰個係佢嘅女主人,以為佢同賓客喺一起。喺確定女兒失蹤後,阿洛伊修斯·多蘭先生同新郎即刻同警方聯繫,正在進行好有力嘅調查,好可能導致呢件好離奇嘅事迅速澄清。然而,直到昨夜好晚,關於失蹤女士嘅下落,冇任何消息透露。有謠言講呢件事涉及不法行為,據講警方已逮捕咗嗰個引起最初騷亂嘅女人,相信佢由於嫉妒或其他動機,可能同新娘嘅離奇失蹤有關。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『儀式在漢諾威廣場的聖喬治教堂舉行,非常安靜,在場的只有新娘的父親阿洛伊修斯·多蘭先生、巴爾莫勒公爵夫人、巴克沃特勳爵、尤斯塔斯勳爵和克拉拉·聖西蒙夫人(新郎的弟弟和妹妹),以及艾麗西亞·惠廷頓夫人。全體隨後前往阿洛伊修斯·多蘭先生在蘭開斯特門的房子,那裡已準備好早餐。似乎有一個姓名未能確定的女人引起了一點麻煩,她在婚禮隊伍之後試圖強行闖入房子,聲稱她對聖西蒙勳爵有某種要求。經過一場痛苦而漫長的場面,她才被管家和男僕趕出去。新娘幸運地在這令人不快的打斷之前已進了屋,同其他人一起坐下來吃早餐,這時她訴說突然不舒服,回房去了。她長時間不在引起了一些議論,她父親跟著她去,但從她的女傭那裡得知,她只是上樓到她房間一會兒,拿起一件長大衣和一頂軟帽,匆匆下到走廊。一名男僕聲稱他看到一位女士這樣打扮離開房子,但拒絕相信那是他的女主人,以為她和賓客在一起。在確定女兒失蹤後,阿洛伊修斯·多蘭先生同新郎立刻與警方聯繫,正在進行非常有力的調查,很可能導致這件非常離奇的事迅速澄清。然而,直到昨夜很晚,關於失蹤女士的下落,沒有任何消息透露。有謠言說這件事涉及不法行為,據說警方已逮捕了那個引起最初騷亂的女人,相信她由於嫉妒或其他動機,可能與新娘的離奇失蹤有關。』」

passages.original: “And is that all?”
passages.vernacular: 「就呢啲嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就這些嗎?」

passages.original: “Only one little item in another of the morning papers, but it is a suggestive one.”
passages.vernacular: 「只有另一份晨報上有一條小新聞,但佢係有啟發性嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只有另一份晨報上有一條小新聞,但它是有啟發性的。」

passages.original: “And it is—”

“That Miss Flora Millar, the lady who had caused the disturbance, has actually been arrested. It appears that she was formerly a danseuse at the Allegro, and that she has known the bridegroom for some years. There are no further particulars, and the whole case is in your hands now—so far as it has been set forth in the public press.”
passages.vernacular: 「引起騷亂嘅嗰位女士弗洛拉·米勒小姐確實被捕喇。似乎佢以前係快板劇院嘅舞女,認識新郎已有幾年。冇更多嘅細節,整個案子而家喺你手裡喇——就公共報刊上所提供嘅而言。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「引起騷亂的那位女士弗洛拉·米勒小姐確實被捕了。似乎她以前是快板劇院的舞女,認識新郎已有幾年。沒有更多的細節,整個案子現在在你手裡了——就公共報刊上所提供的而言。」

passages.original: “And an exceedingly interesting case it appears to be. I would not have missed it for worlds. But there is a ring at the bell, Watson, and as the clock makes it a few minutes after four, I have no doubt that this will prove to be our noble client. Do not dream of going, Watson, for I very much prefer having a witness, if only as a check to my own memory.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢似乎係個極其有趣嘅案子。我無論如何唔願錯過佢。但門鈴響喇,華生,鐘上係四點過幾分,我毫不懷疑呢將係我哋嘅貴族委託人。別想住走,華生,因為我好希望有一個證人,即使只係為了核對我自己嘅記憶。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這似乎是個極其有趣的案子。我無論如何不願錯過它。但門鈴響了,華生,鐘上是四點過幾分,我毫不懷疑這將是我們的貴族委託人。別想著走,華生,因為我很希望有一個證人,即使只是為了核對我自己的記憶。」

passages.original: “Lord Robert St. Simon,” announced our page-boy, throwing open the door. A gentleman entered, with a pleasant, cultured face, high-nosed and pale, with something perhaps of petulance about the mouth, and with the steady, well-opened eye of a man whose pleasant lot it had ever been to command and to be obeyed. His manner was brisk, and yet his general appearance gave an undue impression of age, for he had a slight forward stoop and a little bend of the knees as he walked. His hair, too, as he swept off his very curly-brimmed hat, was grizzled round the edges and thin upon the top. As to his dress, it was careful to the verge of foppishness, with high collar, black frock-coat, white waistcoat, yellow gloves, patent-leather shoes, and light-coloured gaiters. He advanced slowly into the room, turning his head from left to right, and swinging in his right hand the cord which held his golden eyeglasses.
passages.vernacular: 「羅伯特·聖西蒙勳爵到,」我哋嘅小廝通報,猛地推開門。一位紳士走進嚟,有一張愉快、文雅嘅臉,高鼻子,蒼白,嘴巴周圍或者有些任性,眼睛沉穩而睜得好大,係一個享受命令別人同被服從嘅愉快命運嘅人。佢嘅態度輕快,但佢嘅總體外表畀人過分年老嘅印象,因為佢走路時微微前傾,膝蓋有啲彎曲。當佢脫下嗰頂邊緣好捲曲嘅帽子時,佢嘅頭髮邊緣花白,頭頂稀疏。至於佢嘅穿住,講究到近乎花俏,高領,黑色長禮服外套,白背心,黃手套,漆皮鞋,淺色綁腿。佢慢慢走進房間,頭從左轉向右,右手搖晃住繫住金邊眼鏡嘅繩子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「羅伯特·聖西蒙勳爵到,」我們的小廝通報,猛地推開門。一位紳士走進來,有一張愉快、文雅的臉,高鼻子,蒼白,嘴巴周圍也許有些任性,眼睛沉穩而睜得很大,是一個享受命令別人和被服從的愉快命運的人。他的態度輕快,但他的總體外表給人過分年老的印象,因為他走路時微微前傾,膝蓋有一點彎曲。當他脫下那頂邊緣非常捲曲的帽子時,他的頭髮邊緣花白,頭頂稀疏。至於他的穿著,講究到近乎花俏,高領,黑色長禮服外套,白背心,黃手套,漆皮鞋,淺色綁腿。他慢慢走進房間,頭從左轉向右,右手搖晃著繫著金邊眼鏡的繩子。

passages.original: “Good-day, Lord St. Simon,” said Holmes, rising and bowing. “Pray take the basket-chair. This is my friend and colleague, Dr. Watson. Draw up a little to the fire, and we will talk this matter over.”
passages.vernacular: 「日安,聖西蒙勳爵,」福爾摩斯講,站起嚟鞠躬。「請坐藤椅。呢個係我嘅朋友同同事華生醫生。請靠近火邊啲,我哋嚟談談呢件事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「日安,聖西蒙勳爵,」福爾摩斯說,站起來鞠躬。「請坐藤椅。這是我的朋友和同事華生醫生。請靠近火邊一些,我們來談談這件事。」

passages.original: “A most painful matter to me, as you can most readily imagine, Mr. Holmes. I have been cut to the quick. I understand that you have already managed several delicate cases of this sort, sir, though I presume that they were hardly from the same class of society.”
passages.vernacular: 「對我來講係件好痛苦嘅事,福爾摩斯先生,你好容易想像。我受到咗深深嘅傷害。我了解您已經處理過幾件呢類嘅微妙案子,先生,雖然我想佢哋幾乎唔係來自同一社會階層。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對我來說是件非常痛苦的事,福爾摩斯先生,你很容易想像。我受到了深深的傷害。我了解您已經處理過幾件這類的微妙案子,先生,雖然我想它們幾乎不是來自同一社會階層。」

passages.original: “No, I am descending.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,我喺降格。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我在降格。」

passages.original: “I beg pardon.”
passages.vernacular: 「請原諒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請原諒?」

passages.original: “My last client of the sort was a king.”
passages.vernacular: 「我最近呢類嘅委託人係一位國王。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我最近這類的委託人是一位國王。」

passages.original: “Oh, really! I had no idea. And which king?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,真嘅!我唔知道。係邊位國王?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,真的!我不知道。是哪位國王?」

passages.original: “The King of Scandinavia.”
passages.vernacular: 「斯堪嘅納維亞國王。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「斯堪的納維亞國王。」

passages.original: “What! Had he lost his wife?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢!佢失去咗妻子?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼!他失去了妻子?」

passages.original: “You can understand,” said Holmes suavely, “that I extend to the affairs of my other clients the same secrecy which I promise to you in yours.”
passages.vernacular: 「你可以理解,」福爾摩斯溫和地講,「我對我其他委託人嘅事務,畀予同我向您承諾嘅您嘅事務同樣嘅保密。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你可以理解,」福爾摩斯溫和地說,「我對我其他委託人的事務,給予與我向您承諾的您的事務同樣的保密。」

passages.original: “Of course! Very right! very right! I’m sure I beg pardon. As to my own case, I am ready to give you any information which may assist you in forming an opinion.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然!好對!好對!我確實請求原諒。至於我自己嘅案子,我準備畀您任何可能幫助您形成意見嘅資料。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然!很對!很對!我確實請求原諒。至於我自己的案子,我準備給您任何可能幫助您形成意見的資料。」

passages.original: “Thank you. I have already learned all that is in the public prints, nothing more. I presume that I may take it as correct—this article, for example, as to the disappearance of the bride.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝。我已經了解咗公共報刊上嘅一切,冇更多。我想我可以認為佢係正確嘅——比如呢篇關於新娘失蹤嘅文章。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝。我已經了解了公共報刊上的一切,沒有更多。我想我可以認為它是正確的——比如這篇關於新娘失蹤的文章。」

passages.original: Lord St. Simon glanced over it. “Yes, it is correct, as far as it goes.”
passages.vernacular: 聖西蒙勳爵瞥咗一眼。「係嘅,就佢所述範圍而言,係正確嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖西蒙勳爵瞥了一眼。「是的,就它所述範圍而言,是正確的。」

passages.original: “But it needs a great deal of supplementing before anyone could offer an opinion. I think that I may arrive at my facts most directly by questioning you.”
passages.vernacular: 「但喺任何人提出意見之前,需要大量補充。我想我可以通過詢問您最直接地得出我嘅事實。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但在任何人提出意見之前,需要大量補充。我想我可以通過詢問您最直接地得出我的事實。」

passages.original: “Pray do so.”
passages.vernacular: 「請問。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請問。」

passages.original: “When did you first meet Miss Hatty Doran?”
passages.vernacular: 「您乜嘢時候第一次遇到哈蒂·多蘭小姐?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您什麼時候第一次遇到哈蒂·多蘭小姐?」

passages.original: “In San Francisco, a year ago.”
passages.vernacular: 「一年前,喺舊金山。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一年前,在舊金山。」

passages.original: “You were travelling in the States?”
passages.vernacular: 「您當時喺美國旅行?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您當時在美國旅行?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。」

passages.original: “Did you become engaged then?”
passages.vernacular: 「您嗰時訂婚喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您那時訂婚了?」

passages.original: “No.”
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有。」

passages.original: “But you were on a friendly footing?”
passages.vernacular: 「但您哋關係友好?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但您們關係友好?」

passages.original: “I was amused by her society, and she could see that I was amused.”
passages.vernacular: 「我鍾意佢嘅陪伴,佢都睇得出我鍾意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我喜歡她的陪伴,她也看得出我喜歡。」

passages.original: “Her father is very rich?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢嘅父親好富有?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她的父親很富有?」

passages.original: “He is said to be the richest man on the Pacific slope.”
passages.vernacular: 「據講佢係太平洋沿岸最富有嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「據說他是太平洋沿岸最富有的人。」

passages.original: “And how did he make his money?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係點賺到錢嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是怎麼賺到錢的?」

passages.original: “In mining. He had nothing a few years ago. Then he struck gold, invested it, and came up by leaps and bounds.”
passages.vernacular: 「採礦。幾年前佢一無所有。然後佢發現咗金礦,投資,飛躍式地崛起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「採礦。幾年前他一無所有。然後他發現了金礦,投資,飛躍式地崛起。」

passages.original: “Now, what is your own impression as to the young lady’s—your wife’s character?”
passages.vernacular: 「而家,您自己對呢位年輕女士——您嘅妻子——嘅性格有乜嘢印象?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,您自己對這位年輕女士——您的妻子——的性格有什麼印象?」

passages.original: The nobleman swung his glasses a little faster and stared down into the fire. “You see, Mr. Holmes,” said he, “my wife was twenty before her father became a rich man. During that time she ran free in a mining camp and wandered through woods or mountains, so that her education has come from Nature rather than from the schoolmaster. She is what we call in England a tomboy, with a strong nature, wild and free, unfettered by any sort of traditions. She is impetuous—volcanic, I was about to say. She is swift in making up her mind and fearless in carrying out her resolutions. On the other hand, I would not have given her the name which I have the honour to bear”—he gave a little stately cough—“had I not thought her to be at bottom a noble woman. I believe that she is capable of heroic self-sacrifice and that anything dishonourable would be repugnant to her.”
passages.vernacular: 貴族稍微加快搖晃佢嘅眼鏡,俯視住火。「你睇,福爾摩斯先生,」佢講,「我妻子喺佢父親成為富人之前已經二十歲喇。喺嗰段時間裡,佢喺一個礦營裡自由奔跑,喺樹林或山間遊蕩,所以佢嘅教育來自大自然而唔係教師。佢就係我哋喺英國所講嘅野丫頭,性格強烈,狂野自由,不受任何傳統嘅束縛。佢衝動——我差點講火山般嘅。佢下決心好快,執行佢嘅決定毫無畏懼。另一方面,如果我不認為佢本質上係個高貴嘅女子,我係唔會把我有幸擁有嘅姓畀佢嘅——佢略帶莊重地輕咳咗一聲。我相信佢能夠作出英雄式嘅自我犧牲,任何不名譽嘅事對佢都係厭惡嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貴族稍微加快搖晃他的眼鏡,俯視著火。「你看,福爾摩斯先生,」他說,「我妻子在她父親成為富人之前已經二十歲了。在那段時間裡,她在一個礦營裡自由奔跑,在樹林或山間遊蕩,所以她的教育來自大自然而不是教師。她就是我們在英國所說的野丫頭,性格強烈,狂野自由,不受任何傳統的束縛。她衝動——我差點說火山般的。她下決心很快,執行她的決定毫無畏懼。另一方面,如果我不認為她本質上是個高貴的女子,我是不會把我有幸擁有的姓給她的——他略帶莊重地輕咳了一聲。我相信她能夠作出英雄式的自我犧牲,任何不名譽的事對她都是厭惡的。」

passages.original: “Have you her photograph?”
passages.vernacular: 「您有佢嘅照片嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您有她的照片嗎?」

passages.original: “I brought this with me.” He opened a locket and showed us the full face of a very lovely woman. It was not a photograph but an ivory miniature, and the artist had brought out the full effect of the lustrous black hair, the large dark eyes, and the exquisite mouth. Holmes gazed long and earnestly at it. Then he closed the locket and handed it back to Lord St. Simon.
passages.vernacular: 「我帶嚟咗呢個。」佢打開一個小盒墜,畀我哋睇一個好可愛嘅女人嘅正面。嗰唔係照片,而係象牙微型畫像,畫家把嗰烏黑發亮嘅頭髮、大而黑嘅眼睛同精緻嘅嘴巴嘅全部效果都表現咗出嚟。福爾摩斯長時間、認真地注視住佢。然後佢合上盒墜,遞還畀聖西蒙勳爵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我帶來了這個。」他打開一個小盒墜,給我們看一個非常可愛的女人的正面。那不是照片,而是象牙微型畫像,畫家把那烏黑發亮的頭髮、大而黑的眼睛和精緻的嘴巴的全部效果都表現了出來。福爾摩斯長時間、認真地注視著它。然後他合上盒墜,遞還給聖西蒙勳爵。

passages.original: “The young lady came to London, then, and you renewed your acquaintance?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁呢位年輕女士嚟到倫敦,您哋重新結識?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼這位年輕女士來到倫敦,您們重新結識?」

passages.original: “Yes, her father brought her over for this last London season. I met her several times, became engaged to her, and have now married her.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,佢父親帶佢嚟過最近呢個倫敦社交季。我見咗佢幾次,同佢訂咗婚,而家已娶咗佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,她父親帶她來過最近這個倫敦社交季。我見了她幾次,同她訂了婚,現在已娶了她。」

passages.original: “She brought, I understand, a considerable dowry?”
passages.vernacular: 「據我了解,佢帶嚟一筆可觀嘅嫁妝?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「據我了解,她帶來一筆可觀的嫁妝?」

passages.original: “A fair dowry. Not more than is usual in my family.”
passages.vernacular: 「一筆相當嘅嫁妝。不超過我哋家族通常嘅數目。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一筆相當的嫁妝。不超過我們家族通常的數目。」

passages.original: “And this, of course, remains to you, since the marriage is a fait accompli?”
passages.vernacular: 「既然婚姻係既成事實,呢當然仍歸您所有?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「既然婚姻是既成事實,這當然仍歸您所有?」

passages.original: “I really have made no inquiries on the subject.”
passages.vernacular: 「我確實冇就呢個題目做過詢問。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確實沒有就這個題目做過詢問。」

passages.original: “Very naturally not. Did you see Miss Doran on the day before the wedding?”
passages.vernacular: 「好自然唔會。您喺婚禮前一天見過多蘭小姐嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很自然不會。您在婚禮前一天見過多蘭小姐嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 「見過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「見過。」

passages.original: “Was she in good spirits?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢情緒好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她情緒好嗎?」

passages.original: “Never better. She kept talking of what we should do in our future lives.”
passages.vernacular: 「從未咁好。佢一直喺談我哋未來嘅生活要做乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從未這麼好。她一直在談我們未來的生活要做什麼。」

passages.original: “Indeed! That is very interesting. And on the morning of the wedding?”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅!呢個好有趣。嗰婚禮當天早晨呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的!這非常有趣。那婚禮當天早晨呢?」

passages.original: “She was as bright as possible—at least until after the ceremony.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢盡可能地開朗——至少直到儀式之後。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她盡可能地開朗——至少直到儀式之後。」

passages.original: “And did you observe any change in her then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰時您有冇觀察到佢有乜嘢變化?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那時您有沒有觀察到她有什麼變化?」

passages.original: “Well, to tell the truth, I saw then the first signs that I had ever seen that her temper was just a little sharp. The incident however, was too trivial to relate and can have no possible bearing upon the case.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,講實話,嗰時我第一次睇到佢嘅脾氣有啲尖銳嘅跡象。不過呢件事太瑣碎,不值得敘述,唔可能同案子有任何關係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,說實話,那時我第一次看到她的脾氣有一點尖銳的跡象。不過這件事太瑣碎,不值得敘述,不可能與案子有任何關係。」

passages.original: “Pray let us have it, for all that.”
passages.vernacular: 「無論如何,請讓我哋聽聽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「無論如何,請讓我們聽聽。」

passages.original: “Oh, it is childish. She dropped her bouquet as we went towards the vestry. She was passing the front pew at the time, and it fell over into the pew. There was a moment’s delay, but the gentleman in the pew handed it up to her again, and it did not appear to be the worse for the fall. Yet when I spoke to her of the matter, she answered me abruptly; and in the carriage, on our way home, she seemed absurdly agitated over this trifling cause.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,呢個好幼稚。我哋走向聖器室時,佢掉咗佢嘅花束。佢當時正經過前排長椅,花束掉進咗長椅。耽擱咗一會兒,但坐喺長椅裡嘅嗰位先生把佢遞還畀佢,佢似乎並冇因為掉落而變糟。然而,我同佢講起呢件事時,佢突然地回答我;而喺回家嘅路上,喺馬車裡,佢似乎為呢件瑣事荒唐地激動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,這很幼稚。我們走向聖器室時,她掉了她的花束。她當時正經過前排長椅,花束掉進了長椅。耽擱了一會兒,但坐在長椅裡的那位先生把它遞還給她,它似乎並沒有因為掉落而變糟。然而,我同她說起這件事時,她突然地回答我;而在回家的路上,在馬車裡,她似乎為這件瑣事荒唐地激動。」

passages.original: “Indeed! You say that there was a gentleman in the pew. Some of the general public were present, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅!您講長椅裡有一位先生。咁有啲普通公眾在場?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的!您說長椅裡有一位先生。那麼有一些普通公眾在場?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes. It is impossible to exclude them when the church is open.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅。教堂開放時,唔可能把佢哋排除喺外。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的。教堂開放時,不可能把他們排除在外。」

passages.original: “This gentleman was not one of your wife’s friends?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢位先生唔係您妻子嘅朋友之一?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這位先生不是您妻子的朋友之一?」

passages.original: “No, no; I call him a gentleman by courtesy, but he was quite a common-looking person. I hardly noticed his appearance. But really I think that we are wandering rather far from the point.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,不;我出於禮貌稱佢為先生,但佢係個相當普通模樣嘅人。我幾乎冇注意佢嘅外貌。但講真嘅,我想我哋已經離題相當遠喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不;我出於禮貌稱他為先生,但他是個相當普通模樣的人。我幾乎沒有注意他的外貌。但說真的,我想我們已經離題相當遠了。」

passages.original: “Lady St. Simon, then, returned from the wedding in a less cheerful frame of mind than she had gone to it. What did she do on re-entering her father’s house?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁,聖西蒙夫人從婚禮回嚟時,心情不如去時愉快。佢回到佢父親嘅房子時做咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,聖西蒙夫人從婚禮回來時,心情不如去時愉快。她回到她父親的房子時做了什麼?」

passages.original: “I saw her in conversation with her maid.”
passages.vernacular: 「我睇見佢同佢嘅女傭交談。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看見她同她的女傭交談。」

passages.original: “And who is her maid?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢嘅女傭係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她的女傭是誰?」

passages.original: “Alice is her name. She is an American and came from California with her.”
passages.vernacular: 「叫艾麗絲。佢係個美國人,同佢一起從加利福尼亞嚟嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「叫艾麗絲。她是個美國人,同她一起從加利福尼亞來的。」

passages.original: “A confidential servant?”
passages.vernacular: 「一個心腹僕人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個心腹僕人?」

passages.original: “A little too much so. It seemed to me that her mistress allowed her to take great liberties. Still, of course, in America they look upon these things in a different way.”
passages.vernacular: 「有點過頭喇。喺我睇來,佢嘅女主人允許佢太隨便。不過,當然,喺美國佢哋睇待呢啲事嘅方式不同。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有點過頭了。在我看來,她的女主人允許她太隨便。不過,當然,在美國他們看待這些事的方式不同。」

passages.original: “How long did she speak to this Alice?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢同呢個艾麗絲講咗多久?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她同這個艾麗絲說了多久?」

passages.original: “Oh, a few minutes. I had something else to think of.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,幾分鐘。我仲有別嘅事要想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,幾分鐘。我還有別的事要想。」

passages.original: “You did not overhear what they said?”
passages.vernacular: 「您冇偷聽到佢哋講乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您沒有偷聽到她們說什麼?」

passages.original: “Lady St. Simon said something about ‘jumping a claim.’ She was accustomed to use slang of the kind. I have no idea what she meant.”
passages.vernacular: 「聖西蒙夫人講咗啲關於『侵佔礦權』嘅話。佢習慣用嗰類俚語。我唔知道佢係乜嘢意思。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聖西蒙夫人說了一些關於『侵佔礦權』的話。她習慣用那類俚語。我不知道她是什麼意思。」

passages.original: “American slang is very expressive sometimes. And what did your wife do when she finished speaking to her maid?”
passages.vernacular: 「美國俚語有時好有表現力。您妻子同佢女傭講完話後做咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「美國俚語有時非常有表現力。您妻子同她女傭說完話後做了什麼?」

passages.original: “She walked into the breakfast-room.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢走進早餐室。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她走進早餐室。」

passages.original: “On your arm?”
passages.vernacular: 「挽住您嘅手臂?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「挽著您的手臂?」

passages.original: “No, alone. She was very independent in little matters like that. Then, after we had sat down for ten minutes or so, she rose hurriedly, muttered some words of apology, and left the room. She never came back.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,獨自一人。喺呢類小事上,佢好獨立。然後,我哋坐下大約好鐘後,佢匆忙起身,咕噥咗幾句道歉嘅話,離開咗房間。佢再都冇回嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,獨自一人。在這類小事上,她很獨立。然後,我們坐下大約十分鐘後,她匆忙起身,咕噥了幾句道歉的話,離開了房間。她再也沒有回來。」

passages.original: “But this maid, Alice, as I understand, deposes that she went to her room, covered her bride’s dress with a long ulster, put on a bonnet, and went out.”
passages.vernacular: 「但呢個女傭艾麗絲,據我了解,作證講佢回到自己嘅房間,把新娘禮服用一件長大衣罩住,戴上軟帽,出去喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但這個女傭艾麗絲,據我了解,作證說她回到自己的房間,把新娘禮服用一件長大衣罩住,戴上軟帽,出去了。」

passages.original: “Quite so. And she was afterwards seen walking into Hyde Park in company with Flora Millar, a woman who is now in custody, and who had already made a disturbance at Mr. Doran’s house that morning.”
passages.vernacular: 「完全正確。後來有人睇見佢同弗洛拉·米勒一起走進海德公園,嗰個女人而家被拘留,而且嗰天朝早已喺多蘭先生家引起過騷亂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「完全正確。後來有人看見她同弗洛拉·米勒一起走進海德公園,那個女人現在被拘留,而且那天早上已在多蘭先生家引起過騷亂。」

passages.original: “Ah, yes. I should like a few particulars as to this young lady, and your relations to her.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,係嘅。我想了解啲關於呢位年輕女士嘅細節,以及您同佢嘅關係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,是的。我想了解一些關於這位年輕女士的細節,以及您同她的關係。」

passages.original: Lord St. Simon shrugged his shoulders and raised his eyebrows. “We have been on a friendly footing for some years—I may say on a very friendly footing. She used to be at the Allegro. I have not treated her ungenerously, and she had no just cause of complaint against me, but you know what women are, Mr. Holmes. Flora was a dear little thing, but exceedingly hot-headed and devotedly attached to me. She wrote me dreadful letters when she heard that I was about to be married, and, to tell the truth, the reason why I had the marriage celebrated so quietly was that I feared lest there might be a scandal in the church. She came to Mr. Doran’s door just after we returned, and she endeavoured to push her way in, uttering very abusive expressions towards my wife, and even threatening her, but I had foreseen the possibility of something of the sort, and I had two police fellows there in private clothes, who soon pushed her out again. She was quiet when she saw that there was no good in making a row.”
passages.vernacular: 聖西蒙勳爵聳咗聳肩,揚起眉毛。「我哋有關係友好已有幾年——我可以講好友好。佢以前喺快板劇院。我對佢並不吝嗇,佢對我冇正當嘅抱怨理由,但您知道女人係乜嘢樣嘅,福爾摩斯先生。弗洛拉係個可愛嘅小嘢,但極其急躁,死心塌地依戀我。佢聽講我要結婚時,畀我寫咗可怕嘅信,講實話,我之所以讓婚禮舉行得咁安靜,係因為我怕教堂裡可能發生醜聞。我哋剛回嚟,佢就嚟到多蘭先生嘅門口,試圖強行擠進去,對我妻子講咗好辱罵嘅話,甚至威脅佢,但我已預見到可能發生呢類事,喺嗰度安排咗兩個穿便服嘅警察,佢哋好快又把佢推咗出去。佢睇到鬧事冇好處,就安靜喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖西蒙勳爵聳了聳肩,揚起眉毛。「我們有關係友好已有幾年——我可以說非常友好。她以前在快板劇院。我對她並不吝嗇,她對我沒有正當的抱怨理由,但您知道女人是什麼樣的,福爾摩斯先生。弗洛拉是個可愛的小東西,但極其急躁,死心塌地依戀我。她聽說我要結婚時,給我寫了可怕的信,說實話,我之所以讓婚禮舉行得這麼安靜,是因為我怕教堂裡可能發生醜聞。我們剛回來,她就來到多蘭先生的門口,試圖強行擠進去,對我妻子說了非常辱罵的話,甚至威脅她,但我已預見到可能發生這類事,在那裡安排了兩個穿便服的警察,他們很快又把她推了出去。她看到鬧事沒有好處,就安靜了。」

passages.original: “Did your wife hear all this?”
passages.vernacular: 「您妻子聽到呢一切咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您妻子聽到這一切了嗎?」

passages.original: “No, thank goodness, she did not.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,謝天謝地,佢冇聽到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,謝天謝地,她沒聽到。」

passages.original: “And she was seen walking with this very woman afterwards?”
passages.vernacular: 「而後來有人睇見佢同呢個女人一起走?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而後來有人看見她和這個女人一起走?」

passages.original: “Yes. That is what Mr. Lestrade, of Scotland Yard, looks upon as so serious. It is thought that Flora decoyed my wife out and laid some terrible trap for her.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。呢個就係蘇格蘭場嘅雷斯垂德先生認為咁嚴重嘅。大家認為係弗洛拉把我妻子誘騙出去,為佢設下咗某種可怕嘅陷阱。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。這就是蘇格蘭場的雷斯垂德先生認為那麼嚴重的。大家認為是弗洛拉把我妻子誘騙出去,為她設下了某種可怕的陷阱。」

passages.original: “Well, it is a possible supposition.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個係一個可能嘅假設。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這是一個可能的假設。」

passages.original: “You think so, too?”
passages.vernacular: 「您都咁樣認為?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您也這樣認為?」

passages.original: “I did not say a probable one. But you do not yourself look upon this as likely?”
passages.vernacular: 「我冇講係一個好可能嘅。但您自己不認為呢個好可能嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒說是一個很可能的。但您自己不認為這很可能嗎?」

passages.original: “I do not think Flora would hurt a fly.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不認為弗洛拉連一隻蒼蠅都會傷害。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不認為弗洛拉連一隻蒼蠅都會傷害。」

passages.original: “Still, jealousy is a strange transformer of characters. Pray what is your own theory as to what took place?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過,嫉妒係性格嘅一個奇特嘅改變者。請問您自己對所發生嘅事有乜嘢理論?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過,嫉妒是性格的一個奇特的改變者。請問您自己對所發生的事有什麼理論?」

passages.original: “Well, really, I came to seek a theory, not to propound one. I have given you all the facts. Since you ask me, however, I may say that it has occurred to me as possible that the excitement of this affair, the consciousness that she had made so immense a social stride, had the effect of causing some little nervous disturbance in my wife.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,講真嘅,我係嚟尋求理論嘅,唔係嚟提出理論嘅。我已把所有事實都畀咗您。不過,既然您問我,我可以講,我曾想到呢種可能:呢件事嘅興奮,佢意識到自己已邁出咗咁巨大嘅社會一步,可能使我妻子出現咗啲小小嘅神經失常。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,說真的,我是來尋求理論的,不是來提出理論的。我已把所有事實都給了您。不過,既然您問我,我可以說,我曾想到這種可能:這件事的興奮,她意識到自己已邁出了那麼巨大的社會一步,可能使我妻子出現了一些小小的神經失常。」

passages.original: “In short, that she had become suddenly deranged?”
passages.vernacular: 「簡言之,佢突然精神錯亂喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「簡言之,她突然精神錯亂了?」

passages.original: “Well, really, when I consider that she has turned her back—I will not say upon me, but upon so much that many have aspired to without success—I can hardly explain it in any other fashion.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,講真嘅,當我考慮到佢背棄喇——我不講係我,而係許多人曾追求而唔得嘅咁多嘢——我幾乎無法用任何其他方式解釋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,說真的,當我考慮到她背棄了——我不說是我,而是許多人曾追求而不得的那麼多東西——我幾乎無法用任何其他方式解釋。」

passages.original: “Well, certainly that is also a conceivable hypothesis,” said Holmes, smiling. “And now, Lord St. Simon, I think that I have nearly all my data. May I ask whether you were seated at the breakfast-table so that you could see out of the window?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢肯定都係一個可以想像嘅假講,」福爾摩斯微笑住講。「而家,聖西蒙勳爵,我想我已經幾乎掌握咗我所有嘅資料。我可以問一下,您喺早餐桌旁係咪坐喺可以睇到窗外嘅位置嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這肯定也是一個可以想像的假說,」福爾摩斯微笑著說。「現在,聖西蒙勳爵,我想我已經幾乎掌握了我所有的資料。我可以問一下,您在早餐桌旁是否坐在可以看到窗外的位置嗎?」

passages.original: “We could see the other side of the road and the Park.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋可以睇到馬路嘅另一邊同公園。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們可以看到馬路的另一邊和公園。」

passages.original: “Quite so. Then I do not think that I need to detain you longer. I shall communicate with you.”
passages.vernacular: 「完全正確。咁我想我不需要再耽擱您喇。我會同您聯繫。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「完全正確。那麼我想我不需要再耽擱您了。我會與您聯繫。」

passages.original: “Should you be fortunate enough to solve this problem,” said our client, rising.
passages.vernacular: 「如果您有幸解決呢個問題,」我哋嘅委託人講,站起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果您有幸解決這個問題,」我們的委託人說,站起來。

passages.original: “I have solved it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我已經解決喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我已經解決了。」

passages.original: “Eh? What was that?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯?嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯?那是什麼?」

passages.original: “I say that I have solved it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我講我已經解決喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說我已經解決了。」

passages.original: “Where, then, is my wife?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁我妻子喺邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼我妻子在哪裡?」

passages.original: “That is a detail which I shall speedily supply.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係一個我會好快提供嘅細節。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是一個我會很快提供的細節。」

passages.original: Lord St. Simon shook his head. “I am afraid that it will take wiser heads than yours or mine,” he remarked, and bowing in a stately, old-fashioned manner he departed.
passages.vernacular: 聖西蒙勳爵搖咗搖頭。「我怕呢需要比您或我更聰明嘅頭腦,」佢講,以莊重嘅、老式嘅方式鞠躬後離去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖西蒙勳爵搖了搖頭。「我怕這需要比您或我更聰明的頭腦,」他說,以莊重的、老式的方式鞠躬後離去。

passages.original: “It is very good of Lord St. Simon to honour my head by putting it on a level with his own,” said Sherlock Holmes, laughing. “I think that I shall have a whisky and soda and a cigar after all this cross-questioning. I had formed my conclusions as to the case before our client came into the room.”
passages.vernacular: 「聖西蒙勳爵真好,把我嘅腦袋同佢自己嘅放喺同一水平上,賜予榮譽,」夏洛克·福爾摩斯笑住講。「經過呢一番盤問,我想我畢竟要飲一杯威士忌蘇打,抽一支雪茄。喺我哋嘅委託人進房間之前,我已經對呢個案子形成了結論。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聖西蒙勳爵真好,把我的腦袋同他自己的放在同一水平上,賜予榮譽,」夏洛克·福爾摩斯笑著說。「經過這一番盤問,我想我畢竟要喝一杯威士忌蘇打,抽一支雪茄。在我們的委託人進房間之前,我已經對這個案子形成了結論。」

passages.original: “My dear Holmes!”
passages.vernacular: 「我親愛嘅福爾摩斯!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我親愛的福爾摩斯!」

passages.original: “I have notes of several similar cases, though none, as I remarked before, which were quite as prompt. My whole examination served to turn my conjecture into a certainty. Circumstantial evidence is occasionally very convincing, as when you find a trout in the milk, to quote Thoreau’s example.”
passages.vernacular: 「我有幾個類似案子嘅筆記,雖然,如我之前所講,冇一個係咁迅速嘅。我整個詢問嘅作用,係把我嘅猜想變為確定。間接證據有時好有講服力,比如你喺牛奶裡發現一條鱒魚,借用梭羅嘅例子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有幾個類似案子的筆記,雖然,如我之前所說,沒有一個是這麼迅速的。我整個詢問的作用,是把我的猜想變為確定。間接證據有時非常有說服力,比如你在牛奶裡發現一條鱒魚,借用梭羅的例子。」

passages.original: “But I have heard all that you have heard.”
passages.vernacular: 「但我聽到嘅同你聽到嘅一切相同。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我聽到的與你聽到的一切相同。」

passages.original: “Without, however, the knowledge of pre-existing cases which serves me so well. There was a parallel instance in Aberdeen some years back, and something on very much the same lines at Munich the year after the Franco-Prussian War. It is one of these cases—but, hullo, here is Lestrade! Good-afternoon, Lestrade! You will find an extra tumbler upon the sideboard, and there are cigars in the box.”
passages.vernacular: 「但冇我對早先案例嘅了解,嗰對我好有用。幾年前喺阿伯丁有一個類似嘅例子,喺普法戰爭後第二年嘅慕尼黑都有大致相同性質嘅事。呢個係呢類案子之一——但係,喂,雷斯垂德嚟喇!下午好,雷斯垂德!你會喺餐具櫃上找到一個備用嘅玻璃杯,盒子裡有雪茄。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但沒有我對早先案例的了解,那對我非常有用。幾年前在阿伯丁有一個類似的例子,在普法戰爭後第二年的慕尼黑也有大致相同性質的事。這是這類案子之一——但是,喂,雷斯垂德來了!下午好,雷斯垂德!你會在餐具櫃上找到一個備用的玻璃杯,盒子裡有雪茄。」

passages.original: The official detective was attired in a pea-jacket and cravat, which gave him a decidedly nautical appearance, and he carried a black canvas bag in his hand. With a short greeting he seated himself and lit the cigar which had been offered to him.
passages.vernacular: 呢位官方偵探穿住粗呢短外套,打住領巾,使佢顯得明顯像水手,手裡攞住一個黑色帆布袋。佢簡短地打咗個招呼,坐下嚟,點燃咗遞畀佢嘅雪茄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這位官方偵探穿著粗呢短外套,打著領巾,使他顯得明顯像水手,手裡拿著一個黑色帆布袋。他簡短地打了個招呼,坐下來,點燃了遞給他的雪茄。

passages.original: “What’s up, then?” asked Holmes with a twinkle in his eye. “You look dissatisfied.”
passages.vernacular: 「點喇?」福爾摩斯眼睛閃住光問。「你睇起嚟不滿意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了?」福爾摩斯眼睛閃著光問。「你看起來不滿意。」

passages.original: “And I feel dissatisfied. It is this infernal St. Simon marriage case. I can make neither head nor tail of the business.”
passages.vernacular: 「我確實不滿意。都係呢個該死嘅聖西蒙婚姻案。我對呢件事摸不住頭腦。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確實不滿意。都是這個該死的聖西蒙婚姻案。我對這件事摸不著頭腦。」

passages.original: “Really! You surprise me.”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅!你使我驚訝。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的!你使我驚訝。」

passages.original: “Who ever heard of such a mixed affair? Every clue seems to slip through my fingers. I have been at work upon it all day.”
passages.vernacular: 「邊個聽講過咁混亂嘅事?每一條線索似乎都從我手指間溜走。我一整天都喺處理佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰聽說過這麼混亂的事?每一條線索似乎都從我手指間溜走。我一整天都在處理它。」

passages.original: “And very wet it seems to have made you,” said Holmes laying his hand upon the arm of the pea-jacket.
passages.vernacular: 「而且佢似乎把你弄得好濕,」福爾摩斯講,把手放喺嗰件粗呢短外套嘅袖子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且它似乎把你弄得很濕,」福爾摩斯說,把手放在那件粗呢短外套的袖子上。

passages.original: “Yes, I have been dragging the Serpentine.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我一直喺拖撈蛇形湖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我一直在拖撈蛇形湖。」

passages.original: “In Heaven’s name, what for?”
passages.vernacular: 「睇喺老天份上,點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看在老天份上,為什麼?」

passages.original: “In search of the body of Lady St. Simon.”
passages.vernacular: 「為了尋找聖西蒙夫人嘅屍體。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為了尋找聖西蒙夫人的屍體。」

passages.original: Sherlock Holmes leaned back in his chair and laughed heartily.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯往後靠喺椅子上,放聲大笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯往後靠在椅子上,放聲大笑。

passages.original: “Have you dragged the basin of Trafalgar Square fountain?” he asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你有冇拖撈特拉法加廣場噴泉嘅水池?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有沒有拖撈特拉法加廣場噴泉的水池?」他問。

passages.original: “Why? What do you mean?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解?你係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼?你是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “Because you have just as good a chance of finding this lady in the one as in the other.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為你喺一個裡面找到呢位女士嘅機會,同喺另一個裡面一樣好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為你在一個裡面找到這位女士的機會,和在另一個裡面一樣好。」

passages.original: Lestrade shot an angry glance at my companion. “I suppose you know all about it,” he snarled.
passages.vernacular: 雷斯垂德向我嘅同伴投去憤怒嘅一瞥。「我猜你對此事無所唔知,」佢咆哮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷斯垂德向我的同伴投去憤怒的一瞥。「我猜你對此事無所不知,」他咆哮。

passages.original: “Well, I have only just heard the facts, but my mind is made up.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我啱啱聽到事實,但我已攞定主意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我剛剛聽到事實,但我已拿定主意。」

passages.original: “Oh, indeed! Then you think that the Serpentine plays no part in the matter?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,真嘅!咁你認為蛇形湖喺呢件事中不起作用?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,真的!那麼你認為蛇形湖在這件事中不起作用?」

passages.original: “I think it very unlikely.”
passages.vernacular: 「我認為好唔可能。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我認為非常不可能。」

passages.original: “Then perhaps you will kindly explain how it is that we found this in it?” He opened his bag as he spoke, and tumbled onto the floor a wedding-dress of watered silk, a pair of white satin shoes and a bride’s wreath and veil, all discoloured and soaked in water. “There,” said he, putting a new wedding-ring upon the top of the pile. “There is a little nut for you to crack, Master Holmes.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁或者你能好心解釋一下,我哋點會喺裡面發現呢個?」佢講住打開佢嘅袋子,把一件水紋絲綢嘅婚紗、一雙白緞鞋,同一頂新娘花環同面紗倒喺地板上,全都褪色並浸透咗水。「瞧,」佢講,把一枚新嘅結婚戒指放喺嗰堆嘢頂上。「呢個係畀你嘅一個小硬核桃,福爾摩斯大師。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼也許你能好心解釋一下,我們怎麼會在裡面發現這個?」他說著打開他的袋子,把一件水紋絲綢的婚紗、一雙白緞鞋,和一頂新娘花環與面紗倒在地板上,全都褪色並浸透了水。「瞧,」他說,把一枚新的結婚戒指放在那堆東西頂上。「這是給你的一個小硬核桃,福爾摩斯大師。」

passages.original: “Oh, indeed!” said my friend, blowing blue rings into the air. “You dragged them from the Serpentine?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,真嘅!」我嘅朋友講,向空中吹出藍色煙圈。「你從蛇形湖拖出嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,真的!」我的朋友說,向空中吹出藍色煙圈。「你從蛇形湖拖出來的?」

passages.original: “No. They were found floating near the margin by a park-keeper. They have been identified as her clothes, and it seemed to me that if the clothes were there the body would not be far off.”
passages.vernacular: 「不。係一個公園管理員發現佢哋漂喺岸邊附近嘅。佢哋被認出係佢嘅衣服,喺我睇來,如果衣服喺嗰度,屍體就唔會遠喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不。是一個公園管理員發現它們漂在岸邊附近的。它們被認出是她的衣服,在我看來,如果衣服在那裡,屍體就不會遠了。」

passages.original: “By the same brilliant reasoning, every man’s body is to be found in the neighbourhood of his wardrobe. And pray what did you hope to arrive at through this?”
passages.vernacular: 「根據同樣精彩嘅推理,每個人嘅屍體都該喺佢衣櫥嘅附近找到。請問你希望通過呢個得出乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「根據同樣精彩的推理,每個人的屍體都該在他衣櫥的附近找到。請問你希望通過這個得出什麼?」

passages.original: “At some evidence implicating Flora Millar in the disappearance.”
passages.vernacular: 「得出啲牽涉弗洛拉·米勒小姐失蹤嘅證據。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「得出一些牽涉弗洛拉·米勒小姐失蹤的證據。」

passages.original: “I am afraid that you will find it difficult.”
passages.vernacular: 「恐怕你會發現呢個好困難。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「恐怕你會發現這很困難。」

passages.original: “Are you, indeed, now?” cried Lestrade with some bitterness. “I am afraid, Holmes, that you are not very practical with your deductions and your inferences. You have made two blunders in as many minutes. This dress does implicate Miss Flora Millar.”
passages.vernacular: 「你真嘅恐怕嗎?」雷斯垂德有些苦澀地喊道。「福爾摩斯,恐怕你嘅演繹同推理不太實際。你喺兩分鐘內犯咗兩個錯誤。呢件衣服確實牽涉弗洛拉·米勒小姐。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真的恐怕嗎?」雷斯垂德有些苦澀地喊道。「福爾摩斯,恐怕你的演繹和推理不太實際。你在兩分鐘內犯了兩個錯誤。這件衣服確實牽涉弗洛拉·米勒小姐。」

passages.original: “And how?”
passages.vernacular: 「點牽涉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼牽涉?」

passages.original: “In the dress is a pocket. In the pocket is a card-case. In the card-case is a note. And here is the very note.” He slapped it down upon the table in front of him. “Listen to this: ‘You will see me when all is ready. Come at once. F. H. M.’ Now my theory all along has been that Lady St. Simon was decoyed away by Flora Millar, and that she, with confederates, no doubt, was responsible for her disappearance. Here, signed with her initials, is the very note which was no doubt quietly slipped into her hand at the door and which lured her within their reach.”
passages.vernacular: 「衣服裡有一個口袋。口袋裡有一個名片夾。名片夾裡有一張便條。呢個就係嗰張便條。」佢把佢啪地拍喺面前嘅桌子上。「聽呢個:『一切準備好時你會見到我。即刻嚟。F. H. M.』而家我嘅理論一直係,聖西蒙夫人被弗洛拉·米勒誘騙,佢同同夥,無疑要對佢嘅失蹤負責。呢度,有佢姓名嘅首字母簽名,就係嗰張無疑係喺門口悄悄塞進佢手裡、把佢誘入佢哋掌控嘅便條。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「衣服裡有一個口袋。口袋裡有一個名片夾。名片夾裡有一張便條。這就是那張便條。」他把它啪地拍在面前的桌子上。「聽這個:『一切準備好時你會見到我。立刻來。F. H. M.』現在我的理論一直是,聖西蒙夫人被弗洛拉·米勒誘騙,她和同夥,無疑要對她的失蹤負責。這裡,有她姓名的首字母簽名,就是那張無疑是在門口悄悄塞進她手裡、把她誘入他們掌控的便條。」

passages.original: “Very good, Lestrade,” said Holmes, laughing. “You really are very fine indeed. Let me see it.” He took up the paper in a listless way, but his attention instantly became riveted, and he gave a little cry of satisfaction. “This is indeed important,” said he.
passages.vernacular: 「好好,雷斯垂德,」福爾摩斯笑住講。「你真嘅好高明。讓我睇睇。」佢以漫不經心嘅方式攞起嗰張紙,但佢嘅注意力即刻被吸住,佢發出一聲滿意嘅小叫。「呢確實重要,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好,雷斯垂德,」福爾摩斯笑著說。「你真的非常高明。讓我看看。」他以漫不經心的方式拿起那張紙,但他的注意力立刻被吸住,他發出一聲滿意的小叫。「這確實重要,」他說。

passages.original: “Ha! you find it so?”
passages.vernacular: 「哈!你覺得係咁樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈!你覺得是這樣?」

passages.original: “Extremely so. I congratulate you warmly.”
passages.vernacular: 「極其重要。我熱烈地祝賀你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「極其重要。我熱烈地祝賀你。」

passages.original: Lestrade rose in his triumph and bent his head to look. “Why,” he shrieked, “you’re looking at the wrong side!”
passages.vernacular: 雷斯垂德得意洋洋地站起嚟,低頭睇。「哎呀,」佢尖叫,「你睇嘅係反面!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷斯垂德得意洋洋地站起來,低頭看。「哎呀,」他尖叫,「你看的是反面!」

passages.original: “On the contrary, this is the right side.”
passages.vernacular: 「相反,呢個係正面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「相反,這是正面。」

passages.original: “The right side? You’re mad! Here is the note written in pencil over here.”
passages.vernacular: 「正面?你瘋喇!便條係用鉛筆寫喺呢一面嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「正面?你瘋了!便條是用鉛筆寫在這一面的。」

passages.original: “And over here is what appears to be the fragment of a hotel bill, which interests me deeply.”
passages.vernacular: 「而呢一面係一張似乎係酒店賬單嘅殘片,對此我深感興趣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而這一面是一張似乎是酒店賬單的殘片,對此我深感興趣。」

passages.original: “There’s nothing in it. I looked at it before,” said Lestrade. “‘Oct. 4th, rooms 8s., breakfast 2s. 6d., cocktail 1s., lunch 2s. 6d., glass sherry, 8d.’ I see nothing in that.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰上面乜嘢都冇。我以前睇過,」雷斯垂德講。「『10月4日,房間八先令,早餐兩先令六便士,雞尾酒一先令,午餐兩先令六便士,一杯雪利酒八便士。』我睇不出嗰有乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那上面什麼都沒有。我以前看過,」雷斯垂德說。「『10月4日,房間八先令,早餐兩先令六便士,雞尾酒一先令,午餐兩先令六便士,一杯雪利酒八便士。』我看不出那有什麼。」

passages.original: “Very likely not. It is most important, all the same. As to the note, it is important also, or at least the initials are, so I congratulate you again.”
passages.vernacular: 「好可能睇不出。佢仍係最重要嘅。至於便條,都好重要,或至少嗰啲首字母係,所以我再次祝賀你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很可能看不出。它仍是最重要的。至於便條,也很重要,或至少那些首字母是,所以我再次祝賀你。」

passages.original: “I’ve wasted time enough,” said Lestrade, rising. “I believe in hard work and not in sitting by the fire spinning fine theories. Good-day, Mr. Holmes, and we shall see which gets to the bottom of the matter first.” He gathered up the garments, thrust them into the bag, and made for the door.
passages.vernacular: 「我浪費嘅時間夠多喇,」雷斯垂德講,站起嚟。「我相信努力工作,而唔係坐喺火邊編織精妙嘅理論。再見,福爾摩斯先生,我哋睇睇邊個先查出事情嘅底細。」佢把衣服收起嚟,塞進袋裡,朝門口走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我浪費的時間夠多了,」雷斯垂德說,站起來。「我相信努力工作,而不是坐在火邊編織精妙的理論。再見,福爾摩斯先生,我們看看誰先查出事情的底細。」他把衣服收起來,塞進袋裡,朝門口走去。

passages.original: “Just one hint to you, Lestrade,” drawled Holmes before his rival vanished; “I will tell you the true solution of the matter. Lady St. Simon is a myth. There is not, and there never has been, any such person.”
passages.vernacular: 「只畀你一個提示,雷斯垂德,」福爾摩斯喺佢嘅對手消失前拖長聲調講;「我告訴你呢件事嘅真正答案。聖西蒙夫人係個神話。冇、都從來冇過咁樣嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只給你一個提示,雷斯垂德,」福爾摩斯在他的對手消失前拖長聲調說;「我告訴你這件事的真正答案。聖西蒙夫人是個神話。沒有、也從來沒有過這樣的人。」

passages.original: Lestrade looked sadly at my companion. Then he turned to me, tapped his forehead three times, shook his head solemnly, and hurried away.
passages.vernacular: 雷斯垂德悲哀地睇住我嘅同伴。然後佢轉向我,敲咗三下佢嘅額頭,莊重地搖咗搖頭,匆匆離去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷斯垂德悲哀地看著我的同伴。然後他轉向我,敲了三下他的額頭,莊重地搖了搖頭,匆匆離去。

passages.original: He had hardly shut the door behind him when Holmes rose to put on his overcoat. “There is something in what the fellow says about outdoor work,” he remarked, “so I think, Watson, that I must leave you to your papers for a little.”
passages.vernacular: 佢剛喺身後關上門,福爾摩斯就起身去穿佢嘅大衣。「呢傢伙關於戶外工作所講嘅有些道理,」佢講,「所以我想,華生,我得把你留畀你嘅報紙一會兒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他剛在身後關上門,福爾摩斯就起身去穿他的大衣。「這傢伙關於戶外工作所說的有些道理,」他說,「所以我想,華生,我得把你留給你的報紙一會兒。」

passages.original: It was after five o’clock when Sherlock Holmes left me, but I had no time to be lonely, for within an hour there arrived a confectioner’s man with a very large flat box. This he unpacked with the help of a youth whom he had brought with him, and presently, to my very great astonishment, a quite epicurean little cold supper began to be laid out upon our humble lodging-house mahogany. There were a couple of brace of cold woodcock, a pheasant, a pâté de foie gras pie with a group of ancient and cobwebby bottles. Having laid out all these luxuries, my two visitors vanished away, like the genii of the Arabian Nights, with no explanation save that the things had been paid for and were ordered to this address.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯離開我時已過五點,但我冇時間孤單,因為一小時內嚟咗一個糖果店嘅人,帶嚟一個好大嘅扁平箱子。佢喺隨佢嚟嘅一個小夥子嘅幫助下把佢打開,不久,令我好驚訝嘅係,一頓相當講究嘅小型冷餐開始擺喺我哋簡陋寓所嘅桃花心木桌上。有兩對冷山鷸、一隻雉雞、一個鵝肝醬餡餅,同一群古老蒙塵嘅瓶子。擺好呢啲奢侈品後,我嘅兩位訪客像《天方夜譚》裡嘅精靈一樣消失喇,冇別嘅解釋,只講嘢已付款,並已吩咐送到呢個地址。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克·福爾摩斯離開我時已過五點,但我沒有時間孤單,因為一小時內來了一個糖果店的人,帶來一個很大的扁平箱子。他在隨他來的一個小夥子的幫助下把它打開,不久,令我非常驚訝的是,一頓相當講究的小型冷餐開始擺在我們簡陋寓所的桃花心木桌上。有兩對冷山鷸、一隻雉雞、一個鵝肝醬餡餅,和一群古老蒙塵的瓶子。擺好這些奢侈品後,我的兩位訪客像《天方夜譚》裡的精靈一樣消失了,沒有別的解釋,只說東西已付款,並已吩咐送到這個地址。

passages.original: Just before nine o’clock Sherlock Holmes stepped briskly into the room. His features were gravely set, but there was a light in his eye which made me think that he had not been disappointed in his conclusions.
passages.vernacular: 九點差啲,夏洛克·福爾摩斯輕快地走進房間。佢嘅面容嚴肅地繃住,但眼睛裡有一道光,使我想到佢嘅結論冇讓佢失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 九點差一點,夏洛克·福爾摩斯輕快地走進房間。他的面容嚴肅地繃著,但眼睛裡有一道光,使我想到他的結論沒有讓他失望。

passages.original: “They have laid the supper, then,” he said, rubbing his hands.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋把晚餐擺好喇,」佢講,搓著手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們把晚餐擺好了,」他說,搓著手。

passages.original: “You seem to expect company. They have laid for five.”
passages.vernacular: 「你似乎喺期待客人。佢哋擺咗五個人嘅位子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你似乎在期待客人。他們擺了五個人的位子。」

passages.original: “Yes, I fancy we may have some company dropping in,” said he. “I am surprised that Lord St. Simon has not already arrived. Ha! I fancy that I hear his step now upon the stairs.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我想可能會有啲客人嚟訪,」佢講。「我驚訝聖西蒙勳爵仲冇到。哈!我想我而家聽到佢喺樓梯上嘅腳步聲喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我想可能會有一些客人來訪,」他說。「我驚訝聖西蒙勳爵還沒有到。哈!我想我現在聽到他在樓梯上的腳步聲了。」

passages.original: It was indeed our visitor of the afternoon who came bustling in, dangling his glasses more vigorously than ever, and with a very perturbed expression upon his aristocratic features.
passages.vernacular: 果然係我哋下午嘅訪客急匆匆地進嚟,比以往更用力地搖晃住佢嘅眼鏡,貴族嘅臉上帶住好不安嘅表情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 果然是我們下午的訪客急匆匆地進來,比以往更用力地搖晃著他的眼鏡,貴族的臉上帶著非常不安的表情。

passages.original: “My messenger reached you, then?” asked Holmes.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅信使到咗您嗰度?」福爾摩斯問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的信使到了您那裡?」福爾摩斯問。

passages.original: “Yes, and I confess that the contents startled me beyond measure. Have you good authority for what you say?”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我承認內容使我食驚得無以復加。您對所講嘅有可靠嘅根據嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我承認內容使我吃驚得無以復加。您對所說的有可靠的根據嗎?」

passages.original: “The best possible.”
passages.vernacular: 「最可靠嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最可靠的。」

passages.original: Lord St. Simon sank into a chair and passed his hand over his forehead.
passages.vernacular: 聖西蒙勳爵沉入椅子,用手抹過前額。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖西蒙勳爵沉入椅子,用手抹過前額。

passages.original: “What will the Duke say,” he murmured, “when he hears that one of the family has been subjected to such humiliation?”
passages.vernacular: 「公爵會點講,」佢喃喃道,「當佢聽到家族中嘅一員遭受咁樣嘅羞辱?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「公爵會怎麼說,」他喃喃道,「當他聽到家族中的一員遭受這樣的羞辱?」

passages.original: “It is the purest accident. I cannot allow that there is any humiliation.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢純屬意外。我唔能夠承認有任何羞辱。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這純屬意外。我不能承認有任何羞辱。」

passages.original: “Ah, you look on these things from another standpoint.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,您係從另一個立場睇呢啲事嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,您是從另一個立場看這些事的。」

passages.original: “I fail to see that anyone is to blame. I can hardly see how the lady could have acted otherwise, though her abrupt method of doing it was undoubtedly to be regretted. Having no mother, she had no one to advise her at such a crisis.”
passages.vernacular: 「我睇不出任何人該受責備。我幾乎睇不出嗰位女士怎能有別嘅做法,雖然佢嗰種突然嘅方式無疑係令人遺憾嘅。佢冇母親,喺咁樣嘅危機中冇人可以畀佢建議。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看不出任何人該受責備。我幾乎看不出那位女士怎能有別的做法,雖然她那種突然的方式無疑是令人遺憾的。她沒有母親,在這樣的危機中沒有人可以給她建議。」

passages.original: “It was a slight, sir, a public slight,” said Lord St. Simon, tapping his fingers upon the table.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係個輕視,先生,一個公開嘅輕視,」聖西蒙勳爵講,手指敲住桌子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是個輕視,先生,一個公開的輕視,」聖西蒙勳爵說,手指敲著桌子。

passages.original: “You must make allowance for this poor girl, placed in so unprecedented a position.”
passages.vernacular: 「您必須體諒呢位處喺如此史無前例處境嘅可憐女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您必須體諒這位處在如此史無前例處境的可憐女孩。」

passages.original: “I will make no allowance. I am very angry indeed, and I have been shamefully used.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔會體諒。我確實好生氣,我受到咗可恥嘅對待。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不會體諒。我確實非常生氣,我受到了可恥的對待。」

passages.original: “I think that I heard a ring,” said Holmes. “Yes, there are steps on the landing. If I cannot persuade you to take a lenient view of the matter, Lord St. Simon, I have brought an advocate here who may be more successful.” He opened the door and ushered in a lady and gentleman. “Lord St. Simon,” said he “allow me to introduce you to Mr. and Mrs. Francis Hay Moulton. The lady, I think, you have already met.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想我聽到咗門鈴聲,」福爾摩斯講。「係嘅,樓梯口有腳步聲。如果我唔能夠講服您對呢件事採取寬容嘅睇法,聖西蒙勳爵,我帶嚟咗一位或者更成功嘅辯護人。」佢打開門,領進一位女士同一位先生。「聖西蒙勳爵,」佢講,「請允許我向您介紹弗朗西斯·海·莫爾頓先生同夫人。呢位女士,我想,您已經見過喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我聽到了門鈴聲,」福爾摩斯說。「是的,樓梯口有腳步聲。如果我不能說服您對這件事採取寬容的看法,聖西蒙勳爵,我帶來了一位也許更成功的辯護人。」他打開門,領進一位女士和一位先生。「聖西蒙勳爵,」他說,「請允許我向您介紹弗朗西斯·海·莫爾頓先生和夫人。這位女士,我想,您已經見過了。」

passages.original: At the sight of these newcomers our client had sprung from his seat and stood very erect, with his eyes cast down and his hand thrust into the breast of his frock-coat, a picture of offended dignity. The lady had taken a quick step forward and had held out her hand to him, but he still refused to raise his eyes. It was as well for his resolution, perhaps, for her pleading face was one which it was hard to resist.
passages.vernacular: 睇到呢啲新嚟者,我哋嘅委託人從座位上跳起嚟,站得筆直,眼睛垂下,手插進長禮服外套嘅胸前,係一幅受辱尊嚴嘅畫像。嗰位女士迅速上前一步,向佢伸出手,但佢仍拒絕抬起眼睛。呢或者對佢嘅決心係好事,因為佢懇求嘅臉係好難抗拒嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到這些新來者,我們的委託人從座位上跳起來,站得筆直,眼睛垂下,手插進長禮服外套的胸前,是一幅受辱尊嚴的畫像。那位女士迅速上前一步,向他伸出手,但他仍拒絕抬起眼睛。這也許對他的決心是好事,因為她懇求的臉是很難抗拒的。

passages.original: “You’re angry, Robert,” said she. “Well, I guess you have every cause to be.”
passages.vernacular: 「你生氣喇,羅伯特,」佢講。「嗯,我想你有一切理由生氣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你生氣了,羅伯特,」她說。「嗯,我想你有一切理由生氣。」

passages.original: “Pray make no apology to me,” said Lord St. Simon bitterly.
passages.vernacular: 「請唔好向我道歉,」聖西蒙勳爵苦澀地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請不要向我道歉,」聖西蒙勳爵苦澀地說。

passages.original: “Oh, yes, I know that I have treated you real bad and that I should have spoken to you before I went; but I was kind of rattled, and from the time when I saw Frank here again I just didn’t know what I was doing or saying. I only wonder I didn’t fall down and do a faint right there before the altar.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,我知道我對你好不好,我本該喺走之前同你講;但我有點慌亂,從我再次睇到呢位弗蘭克嘅嗰一刻起,我完全唔知道自己喺做乜嘢、講乜嘢。我只係奇怪我冇就喺祭壇前倒下昏過去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,我知道我對你很不好,我本該在走之前同你說;但我有點慌亂,從我再次看到這位弗蘭克的那一刻起,我完全不知道自己在做什麼、說什麼。我只是奇怪我沒有就在祭壇前倒下昏過去。」

passages.original: “Perhaps, Mrs. Moulton, you would like my friend and me to leave the room while you explain this matter?”
passages.vernacular: 「或者,莫爾頓夫人,您願意讓我嘅朋友同我喺您解釋此事時離開房間?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許,莫爾頓夫人,您願意讓我的朋友和我在您解釋此事時離開房間?」

passages.original: “If I may give an opinion,” remarked the strange gentleman, “we’ve had just a little too much secrecy over this business already. For my part, I should like all Europe and America to hear the rights of it.” He was a small, wiry, sunburnt man, clean-shaven, with a sharp face and alert manner.
passages.vernacular: 「如果我可以發表意見,」嗰位陌生紳士講,「我哋喺呢件事上已經有太多啲點嘅秘密喇。就我而言,我希望全歐洲同美洲都聽到佢嘅真相。」佢係個矮小、精瘦、曬黑嘅人,臉刮得乾淨,臉尖,態度機警。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我可以發表意見,」那位陌生紳士說,「我們在這件事上已經有太多一點點的秘密了。就我而言,我希望全歐洲和美洲都聽到它的真相。」他是個矮小、精瘦、曬黑的人,臉刮得乾淨,臉尖,態度機警。

passages.original: “Then I’ll tell our story right away,” said the lady. “Frank here and I met in ’84, in McQuire’s camp, near the Rockies, where Pa was working a claim. We were engaged to each other, Frank and I; but then one day father struck a rich pocket and made a pile, while poor Frank here had a claim that petered out and came to nothing. The richer Pa grew the poorer was Frank; so at last Pa wouldn’t hear of our engagement lasting any longer, and he took me away to ’Frisco. Frank wouldn’t throw up his hand, though; so he followed me there, and he saw me without Pa knowing anything about it. It would only have made him mad to know, so we just fixed it all up for ourselves. Frank said that he would go and make his pile, too, and never come back to claim me until he had as much as Pa. So then I promised to wait for him to the end of time and pledged myself not to marry anyone else while he lived. ‘Why shouldn’t we be married right away, then,’ said he, ‘and then I will feel sure of you; and I won’t claim to be your husband until I come back?’ Well, we talked it over, and he had fixed it all up so nicely, with a clergyman all ready in waiting, that we just did it right there; and then Frank went off to seek his fortune, and I went back to Pa.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我即刻講我哋嘅故事,」嗰位女士講。「呢位弗蘭克同我係1884年喺落基山脈附近嘅麥奎爾營地認識嘅,爸爸當時喺嗰度開礦區。我哋訂咗婚,弗蘭克同我;但後來有一天,父親挖到咗一個富礦囊,發咗大財,而可憐嘅弗蘭克嘅礦區卻枯竭喇,乜嘢都冇。爸爸越富,弗蘭克越窮;所以最後爸爸唔願意我哋嘅婚約再繼續,把我帶到咗舊金山。不過,弗蘭克唔肯認輸;所以佢跟到嗰度,喺爸爸唔知道嘅情況下見我。讓佢知道只會讓佢發瘋,所以我哋就自己安排好咗一切。弗蘭克講佢都要去發財,喺佢有像爸爸咁多嘅錢之前,永遠不回嚟要我。於是我答應等佢到時間嘅盡頭,並發誓只要佢活住,就不嫁畀別嘅任何人。『咁點解我哋不即刻結婚,』佢講,『嗰樣我就確信你屬於我喇;我回嚟之前,我唔好求做你嘅丈夫?』嗯,我哋商量喇,佢把一切安排得咁好,有一位牧師隨時準備好等住,我哋就喺嗰兒辦喇;然後弗蘭克出去尋找佢嘅運氣,我回到爸爸嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我馬上講我們的故事,」那位女士說。「這位弗蘭克和我是1884年在落基山脈附近的麥奎爾營地認識的,爸爸當時在那裡開礦區。我們訂了婚,弗蘭克和我;但後來有一天,父親挖到了一個富礦囊,發了大財,而可憐的弗蘭克的礦區卻枯竭了,什麼也沒有。爸爸越富,弗蘭克越窮;所以最後爸爸不願意我們的婚約再繼續,把我帶到了舊金山。不過,弗蘭克不肯認輸;所以他跟到那裡,在爸爸不知道的情況下見我。讓他知道只會讓他發瘋,所以我們就自己安排好了一切。弗蘭克說他也要去發財,在他有像爸爸那麼多的錢之前,永遠不回來要我。於是我答應等他到時間的盡頭,並發誓只要他活著,就不嫁給別的任何人。『那麼為什麼我們不立刻結婚,』他說,『那樣我就確信你屬於我了;我回來之前,我不要求做你的丈夫?』嗯,我們商量了,他把一切安排得那麼好,有一位牧師隨時準備好等著,我們就在那兒辦了;然後弗蘭克出去尋找他的運氣,我回到爸爸那裡。

passages.original: “The next I heard of Frank was that he was in Montana, and then he went prospecting in Arizona, and then I heard of him from New Mexico. After that came a long newspaper story about how a miners’ camp had been attacked by Apache Indians, and there was my Frank’s name among the killed. I fainted dead away, and I was very sick for months after. Pa thought I had a decline and took me to half the doctors in ’Frisco. Not a word of news came for a year and more, so that I never doubted that Frank was really dead. Then Lord St. Simon came to ’Frisco, and we came to London, and a marriage was arranged, and Pa was very pleased, but I felt all the time that no man on this earth would ever take the place in my heart that had been given to my poor Frank.
passages.vernacular: 「我聽到弗蘭克嘅下一個消息係佢喺蒙大攞,然後佢去亞利桑嗰找礦,然後我從新墨西哥聽講佢。之後來咗一篇長長嘅報紙報導,講一個礦工營地如何被阿帕奇印第安人襲擊,我嘅弗蘭克嘅名字就喺被殺者之中。我當場昏咗過去,之後病咗好幾個月。爸爸以為我得咗肺病,帶我去睇咗舊金山一半嘅醫生。一年多冇一個字嘅消息,所以我從不懷疑弗蘭克確實死喇。然後聖西蒙勳爵嚟到舊金山,我哋嚟到倫敦,安排咗婚事,爸爸好高興,但我一直覺得,世上冇任何男人能取代我心裡畀咗我可憐嘅弗蘭克嘅位置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我聽到弗蘭克的下一個消息是他在蒙大拿,然後他去亞利桑那找礦,然後我從新墨西哥聽說他。之後來了一篇長長的報紙報導,講一個礦工營地如何被阿帕奇印第安人襲擊,我的弗蘭克的名字就在被殺者之中。我當場昏了過去,之後病了好幾個月。爸爸以為我得了肺病,帶我去看了舊金山一半的醫生。一年多沒有一個字的消息,所以我從不懷疑弗蘭克確實死了。然後聖西蒙勳爵來到舊金山,我們來到倫敦,安排了婚事,爸爸非常高興,但我一直覺得,世上沒有任何男人能取代我心裡給了我可憐的弗蘭克的位置。

passages.original: “Still, if I had married Lord St. Simon, of course I’d have done my duty by him. We can’t command our love, but we can our actions. I went to the altar with him with the intention to make him just as good a wife as it was in me to be. But you may imagine what I felt when, just as I came to the altar rails, I glanced back and saw Frank standing and looking at me out of the first pew. I thought it was his ghost at first; but when I looked again there he was still, with a kind of question in his eyes, as if to ask me whether I were glad or sorry to see him. I wonder I didn’t drop. I know that everything was turning round, and the words of the clergyman were just like the buzz of a bee in my ear. I didn’t know what to do. Should I stop the service and make a scene in the church? I glanced at him again, and he seemed to know what I was thinking, for he raised his finger to his lips to tell me to be still. Then I saw him scribble on a piece of paper, and I knew that he was writing me a note. As I passed his pew on the way out I dropped my bouquet over to him, and he slipped the note into my hand when he returned me the flowers. It was only a line asking me to join him when he made the sign to me to do so. Of course I never doubted for a moment that my first duty was now to him, and I determined to do just whatever he might direct.
passages.vernacular: 「然而,如果我嫁畀咗聖西蒙勳爵,當然我會對佢盡到我嘅責任。我哋唔能夠命令我哋嘅愛,但我哋可以命令我哋嘅行動。我同佢走向祭壇時,打算盡我所能做佢一個同樣好嘅妻子。但你可以想像我嘅感受,當我剛到祭壇欄杆旁,回頭一瞥,睇見弗蘭克站喺第一排長椅裡睇住我。起初我以為嗰個係佢嘅鬼魂;但我再睇時,佢仍喺嗰兒,眼睛裡帶住某種疑問,好像喺問我見到佢係高興定係難過。我奇怪我竟冇倒下。我知道一切都喺旋轉,牧師嘅話就像蜜蜂喺我耳邊嘅嗡嗡聲。我唔知道該點算。我應該停止儀式,喺教堂裡鬧一場嗎?我又瞥咗佢一眼,佢似乎知道我喺想乜嘢,因為佢把手指舉到嘴唇上,告訴我保持安靜。然後我睇見佢喺一張紙上潦草地寫字,我知道佢喺畀我寫便條。我出去經過佢嘅長椅時,把花束掉畀佢,佢仲我花時把便條塞進咗我嘅手裡。只係一行字,要求我等佢向我做出記號時去找佢。當然,我從冇一刻懷疑,我而家嘅首要責任係對佢,我決定佢吩咐乜嘢我就做乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然而,如果我嫁給了聖西蒙勳爵,當然我會對他盡到我的責任。我們不能命令我們的愛,但我們可以命令我們的行動。我同他走向祭壇時,打算盡我所能做他一個同樣好的妻子。但你可以想像我的感受,當我剛到祭壇欄杆旁,回頭一瞥,看見弗蘭克站在第一排長椅裡看著我。起初我以為那是他的鬼魂;但我再看時,他仍在那兒,眼睛裡帶著某種疑問,好像在問我見到他是高興還是難過。我奇怪我竟沒有倒下。我知道一切都在旋轉,牧師的話就像蜜蜂在我耳邊的嗡嗡聲。我不知道該怎麼辦。我應該停止儀式,在教堂裡鬧一場嗎?我又瞥了他一眼,他似乎知道我在想什麼,因為他把手指舉到嘴唇上,告訴我保持安靜。然後我看見他在一張紙上潦草地寫字,我知道他在給我寫便條。我出去經過他的長椅時,把花束掉給他,他還我花時把便條塞進了我的手裡。只是一行字,要求我等他向我做出記號時去找他。當然,我從沒有一刻懷疑,我現在的首要責任是對他,我決定他吩咐什麼我就做什麼。

passages.original: “When I got back I told my maid, who had known him in California, and had always been his friend. I ordered her to say nothing, but to get a few things packed and my ulster ready. I know I ought to have spoken to Lord St. Simon, but it was dreadful hard before his mother and all those great people. I just made up my mind to run away and explain afterwards. I hadn’t been at the table ten minutes before I saw Frank out of the window at the other side of the road. He beckoned to me and then began walking into the Park. I slipped out, put on my things, and followed him. Some woman came talking something or other about Lord St. Simon to me—seemed to me from the little I heard as if he had a little secret of his own before marriage also—but I managed to get away from her and soon overtook Frank. We got into a cab together, and away we drove to some lodgings he had taken in Gordon Square, and that was my true wedding after all those years of waiting. Frank had been a prisoner among the Apaches, had escaped, came on to ’Frisco, found that I had given him up for dead and had gone to England, followed me there, and had come upon me at last on the very morning of my second wedding.”
passages.vernacular: 「我回去後告訴咗我嘅女傭,佢喺加利福尼亞就認識佢,一直係佢嘅朋友。我命令佢乜嘢都唔好講,而係收拾啲嘢,把我嘅長大衣準備好。我知道我本該對聖西蒙勳爵講,但喺佢母親同所有嗰啲大人物面前,實在太難喇。我只係下定決心先逃走,以後再解釋。我喺桌邊坐咗唔到好鐘,就從窗子睇見弗蘭克喺馬路另一邊。佢向我招手,然後開始走進公園。我悄悄溜出去,穿上衣服,跟住佢。有個女人過嚟跟我講乜嘢關於聖西蒙勳爵嘅事——從我聽到嘅啲嚟睇,似乎佢婚前都有一個小秘密——但我設法擺脫咗佢,好快追上咗弗蘭克。我哋一起上咗一輛馬車,駛去佢喺戈登廣場租嘅住處,呢才係我喺等咗咁多年之後真正嘅婚禮。弗蘭克曾係阿帕奇人嘅俘虜,逃咗出嚟,到咗舊金山,發現我已當佢死咗、去咗英國,佢追到嗰度,終於喺我第二次婚禮嘅嗰天早晨碰上咗我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我回去後告訴了我的女傭,她在加利福尼亞就認識他,一直是他的朋友。我命令她什麼也不要說,而是收拾一些東西,把我的長大衣準備好。我知道我本該對聖西蒙勳爵說,但在他母親和所有那些大人物面前,實在太難了。我只是下定決心先逃走,以後再解釋。我在桌邊坐了不到十分鐘,就從窗子看見弗蘭克在馬路另一邊。他向我招手,然後開始走進公園。我悄悄溜出去,穿上衣服,跟著他。有個女人過來跟我說什麼關於聖西蒙勳爵的事——從我聽到的一點來看,似乎他婚前也有一個小秘密——但我設法擺脫了她,很快追上了弗蘭克。我們一起上了一輛馬車,駛去他在戈登廣場租的住處,這才是我在等了那麼多年之後真正的婚禮。弗蘭克曾是阿帕奇人的俘虜,逃了出來,到了舊金山,發現我已當他死了、去了英國,他追到那裡,終於在我第二次婚禮的那天早晨碰上了我。」

passages.original: “I saw it in a paper,” explained the American. “It gave the name and the church but not where the lady lived.”
passages.vernacular: 「我喺報紙上睇到嘅,」嗰個美國人解釋。「上面有名字同教堂,但冇嗰位女士住嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在報紙上看到的,」那個美國人解釋。「上面有名字和教堂,但沒有那位女士住的地方。」

passages.original: “Then we had a talk as to what we should do, and Frank was all for openness, but I was so ashamed of it all that I felt as if I should like to vanish away and never see any of them again—just sending a line to Pa, perhaps, to show him that I was alive. It was awful to me to think of all those lords and ladies sitting round that breakfast-table and waiting for me to come back. So Frank took my wedding-clothes and things and made a bundle of them, so that I should not be traced, and dropped them away somewhere where no one could find them. It is likely that we should have gone on to Paris to-morrow, only that this good gentleman, Mr. Holmes, came round to us this evening, though how he found us is more than I can think, and he showed us very clearly and kindly that I was wrong and that Frank was right, and that we should be putting ourselves in the wrong if we were so secret. Then he offered to give us a chance of talking to Lord St. Simon alone, and so we came right away round to his rooms at once. Now, Robert, you have heard it all, and I am very sorry if I have given you pain, and I hope that you do not think very meanly of me.”
passages.vernacular: 「然後我哋商量該點算,弗蘭克全力主張公開,但我對呢一切咁羞愧,我覺得我想消失,再都唔見佢哋任何一個——或者只畀爸爸寫一行字,讓佢知道我仲活住。想到所有嗰啲勳爵同夫人坐喺嗰張早餐桌旁等我回嚟,對我來講太可怕喇。所以弗蘭克攞咗我嘅婚紗同嘢,打成一包,使我不被追蹤,把佢哋丟到冇人能找到嘅地方。我哋好可能聽日就去巴黎喇,只係呢位好先生,福爾摩斯先生,今晚嚟到我哋呢度,雖然佢點樣找到我哋我想不出,佢好清楚而善意地向我哋講明了我錯喇,弗蘭克係對嘅,如果我哋咁秘密,我哋就係把自己放喺錯誤嘅一邊。然後佢提出畀我哋一個機會同聖西蒙勳爵單獨談話,所以我哋就即刻嚟到咗佢嘅房間。而家,羅伯特,你聽到咗一切,如果我讓你痛苦,我好抱歉,我希望你唔好把我睇得太卑鄙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後我們商量該怎麼辦,弗蘭克全力主張公開,但我對這一切那麼羞愧,我覺得我想消失,再也不見他們任何一個——也許只給爸爸寫一行字,讓他知道我還活著。想到所有那些勳爵和夫人坐在那張早餐桌旁等我回來,對我來說太可怕了。所以弗蘭克拿了我的婚紗和東西,打成一包,使我不被追蹤,把它們丟到沒人能找到的地方。我們很可能明天就去巴黎了,只是這位好先生,福爾摩斯先生,今晚來到我們這裡,雖然他怎樣找到我們我想不出,他非常清楚而善意地向我們說明了我錯了,弗蘭克是對的,如果我們那麼秘密,我們就是把自己放在錯誤的一邊。然後他提出給我們一個機會與聖西蒙勳爵單獨談話,所以我們就立刻來到了他的房間。現在,羅伯特,你聽到了一切,如果我讓你痛苦,我很抱歉,我希望你不要把我看得太卑鄙。」

passages.original: Lord St. Simon had by no means relaxed his rigid attitude, but had listened with a frowning brow and a compressed lip to this long narrative.
passages.vernacular: 聖西蒙勳爵絕冇放鬆佢僵硬嘅姿態,而係皺住眉頭、緊抿住嘴唇聽完咗呢個長長嘅敘述。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖西蒙勳爵絕沒有放鬆他僵硬的姿態,而是皺著眉頭、緊抿著嘴唇聽完了這個長長的敘述。

passages.original: “Excuse me,” he said, “but it is not my custom to discuss my most intimate personal affairs in this public manner.”
passages.vernacular: 「對不起,」佢講,「但我習慣不以呢種公開嘅方式討論我最私人嘅事務。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對不起,」他說,「但我習慣不以這種公開的方式討論我最私人的事務。」

passages.original: “Then you won’t forgive me? You won’t shake hands before I go?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你不原諒我?你喺我走之前不握握手嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你不原諒我?你在我走之前不握握手嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, certainly, if it would give you any pleasure.” He put out his hand and coldly grasped that which she extended to him.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,當然,如果呢能畀你乜嘢快樂嘅話。」佢伸出手,冷淡地握咗握佢向佢伸出嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,當然,如果這能給你什麼快樂的話。」他伸出手,冷淡地握了握她向他伸出的手。

passages.original: “I had hoped,” suggested Holmes, “that you would have joined us in a friendly supper.”
passages.vernacular: 「我本希望,」福爾摩斯提議,「您會同我哋一起友好地食頓晚飯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我本希望,」福爾摩斯提議,「您會和我們一起友好地吃頓晚飯。」

passages.original: “I think that there you ask a little too much,” responded his Lordship. “I may be forced to acquiesce in these recent developments, but I can hardly be expected to make merry over them. I think that with your permission I will now wish you all a very good-night.” He included us all in a sweeping bow and stalked out of the room.
passages.vernacular: 「我想您喺呢度要求得有點多喇,」勳爵回答。「我可能被迫默認呢啲最近嘅發展,但我好難被期望對佢哋尋歡作樂。我想,經您允許,我而家祝你哋大家晚安。」佢向我哋大家鞠咗一個大躬,大步走出房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想您在這裡要求得有點多了,」勳爵回答。「我可能被迫默認這些最近的發展,但我很難被期望對它們尋歡作樂。我想,經您允許,我現在祝你們大家晚安。」他向我們大家鞠了一個大躬,大步走出房間。

passages.original: “Then I trust that you at least will honour me with your company,” said Sherlock Holmes. “It is always a joy to meet an American, Mr. Moulton, for I am one of those who believe that the folly of a monarch and the blundering of a minister in far-gone years will not prevent our children from being some day citizens of the same world-wide country under a flag which shall be a quartering of the Union Jack with the Stars and Stripes.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁我相信您至少會賞光同我作伴,」夏洛克·福爾摩斯講。「見到一個美國人總是一種樂趣,莫爾頓先生,因為我係咁樣嘅人之一:我相信,往昔一位君主嘅愚蠢同一位大臣嘅失誤,唔會妨礙我哋嘅子孫有一天成為同一個世界性國家嘅公民,喺一面把米字旗同星條旗四分合成嘅旗幟之下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼我相信您至少會賞光與我作伴,」夏洛克·福爾摩斯說。「見到一個美國人總是一種樂趣,莫爾頓先生,因為我是這樣的人之一:我相信,往昔一位君主的愚蠢和一位大臣的失誤,不會妨礙我們的子孫有一天成為同一個世界性國家的公民,在一面把米字旗與星條旗四分合成的旗幟之下。」

passages.original: “The case has been an interesting one,” remarked Holmes when our visitors had left us, “because it serves to show very clearly how simple the explanation may be of an affair which at first sight seems to be almost inexplicable. Nothing could be more natural than the sequence of events as narrated by this lady, and nothing stranger than the result when viewed, for instance, by Mr. Lestrade of Scotland Yard.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢案子好有趣,」我哋嘅訪客離開後,福爾摩斯講,「因為佢好清楚地表明,一件乍睇幾乎無法解釋嘅事,其解釋可以幾咁簡單。冇乜嘢比呢位女士所敘述嘅事件順序更自然,都冇乜嘢比結果,例如當蘇格蘭場嘅雷斯垂德先生睇來,更奇怪嘅喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這案子很有趣,」我們的訪客離開後,福爾摩斯說,「因為它很清楚地表明,一件乍看幾乎無法解釋的事,其解釋可以多麼簡單。沒有什麼比這位女士所敘述的事件順序更自然,也沒有什麼比結果,例如當蘇格蘭場的雷斯垂德先生看來,更奇怪的了。」

passages.original: “You were not yourself at fault at all, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁你自己完全冇出錯?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼你自己完全沒有出錯?」

passages.original: “From the first, two facts were very obvious to me, the one that the lady had been quite willing to undergo the wedding ceremony, the other that she had repented of it within a few minutes of returning home. Obviously something had occurred during the morning, then, to cause her to change her mind. What could that something be? She could not have spoken to anyone when she was out, for she had been in the company of the bridegroom. Had she seen someone, then? If she had, it must be someone from America because she had spent so short a time in this country that she could hardly have allowed anyone to acquire so deep an influence over her that the mere sight of him would induce her to change her plans so completely. You see we have already arrived, by a process of exclusion, at the idea that she might have seen an American. Then who could this American be, and why should he possess so much influence over her? It might be a lover; it might be a husband. Her young womanhood had, I knew, been spent in rough scenes and under strange conditions. So far I had got before I ever heard Lord St. Simon’s narrative. When he told us of a man in a pew, of the change in the bride’s manner, of so transparent a device for obtaining a note as the dropping of a bouquet, of her resort to her confidential maid, and of her very significant allusion to claim-jumping—which in miners’ parlance means taking possession of that which another person has a prior claim to—the whole situation became absolutely clear. She had gone off with a man, and the man was either a lover or was a previous husband—the chances being in favour of the latter.”
passages.vernacular: 「從一開始,兩個事實對我就好明顯,一個係嗰位女士完全願意經歷婚禮儀式,另一個係佢喺回家後幾分鐘內就後悔喇。顯然,嗰天早晨發生咗乜嘢事,使佢改變咗主意。嗰件事可能係乜嘢?佢外出時唔可能同任何人講過話,因為佢一直同新郎喺一起。咁,係佢見到咗乜嘢人嗎?如果係,嗰一定係來自美國嘅人,因為佢喺呢個國家待嘅時間咁短,佢不太可能讓任何人對佢產生如此深嘅影響,以致僅僅睇到佢就會使佢咁樣徹底改變計畫。你睇,我哋已通過排除嘅過程,得出佢可能睇見咗一個美國人嘅想法。咁呢個美國人可能係邊個,點解佢對佢有咁大影響?可能係情人;可能係丈夫。我知道,佢嘅少女時代係喺粗獷嘅場景同奇特嘅條件下度過嘅。喺我聽到聖西蒙勳爵嘅敘述之前,我已想到呢度。當佢告訴我哋長椅裡有個人,新娘態度嘅變化,用掉落花束咁樣透明嘅手段取得便條,佢求助於佢嘅心腹女傭,以及佢嗰極有意味嘅、提到侵佔礦權——用礦工嘅行話,意思係佔有另一個人先有權利嘅嘢——嘅話,整個局勢變得絕對清楚。佢同一個男人走喇,呢個男人要麼係情人,要麼係以前嘅丈夫——後者嘅可能性較大。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從一開始,兩個事實對我就很明顯,一個是那位女士完全願意經歷婚禮儀式,另一個是她在回家後幾分鐘內就後悔了。顯然,那天早晨發生了什麼事,使她改變了主意。那件事可能是什麼?她外出時不可能同任何人說過話,因為她一直同新郎在一起。那麼,是她見到了什麼人嗎?如果是,那一定是來自美國的人,因為她在這個國家待的時間那麼短,她不太可能讓任何人對她產生如此深的影響,以致僅僅看到他就會使她這樣徹底改變計畫。你看,我們已通過排除的過程,得出她可能看見了一個美國人的想法。那麼這個美國人可能是誰,為什麼他對她有這麼大影響?可能是情人;可能是丈夫。我知道,她的少女時代是在粗獷的場景和奇特的條件下度過的。在我聽到聖西蒙勳爵的敘述之前,我已想到這裡。當他告訴我們長椅裡有個人,新娘態度的變化,用掉落花束這樣透明的手段取得便條,她求助於她的心腹女傭,以及她那極有意味的、提到侵佔礦權——用礦工的行話,意思是佔有另一個人先有權利的東西——的話,整個局勢變得絕對清楚。她同一個男人走了,這個男人要麼是情人,要麼是以前的丈夫——後者的可能性較大。」

passages.original: “And how in the world did you find them?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你到底係點找到佢哋嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你到底是怎麼找到他們的?」

passages.original: “It might have been difficult, but friend Lestrade held information in his hands the value of which he did not himself know. The initials were, of course, of the highest importance, but more valuable still was it to know that within a week he had settled his bill at one of the most select London hotels.”
passages.vernacular: 「本來可能好難,但我嘅朋友雷斯垂德手中握有信息,佢自己並唔知道其價值。首字母當然係最重要嘅,但更有價值嘅係知道一個星期之內佢喺倫敦最高檔嘅酒店之一結咗賬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「本來可能很難,但我的朋友雷斯垂德手中握有信息,他自己並不知道其價值。首字母當然是最重要的,但更有價值的是知道一個星期之內他在倫敦最高檔的酒店之一結了賬。」

passages.original: “How did you deduce the select?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點推論出係高檔嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼推論出是高檔的?」

passages.original: “By the select prices. Eight shillings for a bed and eightpence for a glass of sherry pointed to one of the most expensive hotels. There are not many in London which charge at that rate. In the second one which I visited in Northumberland Avenue, I learned by an inspection of the book that Francis H. Moulton, an American gentleman, had left only the day before, and on looking over the entries against him, I came upon the very items which I had seen in the duplicate bill. His letters were to be forwarded to 226 Gordon Square; so thither I travelled, and being fortunate enough to find the loving couple at home, I ventured to give them some paternal advice and to point out to them that it would be better in every way that they should make their position a little clearer both to the general public and to Lord St. Simon in particular. I invited them to meet him here, and, as you see, I made him keep the appointment.”
passages.vernacular: 「從高檔嘅價格。一張床八先令,一杯雪利酒八便士,講明係最昂貴嘅酒店之一。倫敦收呢種價格嘅不多。喺我拜訪嘅第二家,北安伯蘭大道上嘅酒店,通過查睇登記簿,我得知美國紳士弗朗西斯·H·莫爾頓前一天剛離開,查睇對佢嘅記錄時,我碰上咗喺重複賬單上見過嘅嗰啲項目。佢嘅信件要轉寄到戈登廣場226號;所以我去咗嗰度,幸運地發現呢對戀人喺家,我冒昧地畀咗佢哋啲父親般嘅建議,指出佢哋最好喺各方面把自己嘅處境,對公眾,尤其係對聖西蒙勳爵,弄清楚啲。我邀請佢哋喺呢度同佢見面,而且,如你所見,我讓佢赴咗約。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從高檔的價格。一張床八先令,一杯雪利酒八便士,說明是最昂貴的酒店之一。倫敦收這種價格的不多。在我拜訪的第二家,北安伯蘭大道上的酒店,通過查看登記簿,我得知美國紳士弗朗西斯·H·莫爾頓前一天剛離開,查看對他的記錄時,我碰上了在重複賬單上見過的那些項目。他的信件要轉寄到戈登廣場226號;所以我去了那裡,幸運地發現這對戀人在家,我冒昧地給了他們一些父親般的建議,指出他們最好在各方面把自己的處境,對公眾,尤其是對聖西蒙勳爵,弄清楚一點。我邀請他們在這裡與他見面,而且,如你所見,我讓他赴了約。」

passages.original: “But with no very good result,” I remarked. “His conduct was certainly not very gracious.”
passages.vernacular: 「但結果並不好好,」我講。「佢嘅行為肯定不太親切。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但結果並不很好,」我說。「他的行為肯定不太親切。」

passages.original: “Ah, Watson,” said Holmes, smiling, “perhaps you would not be very gracious either, if, after all the trouble of wooing and wedding, you found yourself deprived in an instant of wife and of fortune. I think that we may judge Lord St. Simon very mercifully and thank our stars that we are never likely to find ourselves in the same position. Draw your chair up and hand me my violin, for the only problem we have still to solve is how to while away these bleak autumnal evenings.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,華生,」福爾摩斯微笑住講,「或者你都唔會好親切,如果喺經歷咗求愛同結婚嘅所有麻煩之後,你發現自己轉眼被剝奪咗妻子同財產。我想我哋可以好寬容地評判聖西蒙勳爵,並感謝我哋嘅幸運星,我哋不太可能發現自己處於同樣嘅處境。把你嘅椅子拉近,把我嘅小提琴遞畀我,因為我哋仲要解決嘅唯一問題,就係如何打發呢啲凄涼嘅秋夜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,華生,」福爾摩斯微笑著說,「也許你也不會很親切,如果在經歷了求愛和結婚的所有麻煩之後,你發現自己轉眼被剝奪了妻子和財產。我想我們可以非常寬容地評判聖西蒙勳爵,並感謝我們的幸運星,我們不太可能發現自己處於同樣的處境。把你的椅子拉近,把我的小提琴遞給我,因為我們還要解決的唯一問題,就是如何打發這些凄涼的秋夜。」

chapters.title: The Adventure of the Beryl Coronet 綠玉冠冕

passages.original: “Holmes,” said I as I stood one morning in our bow-window looking down the street, “here is a madman coming along. It seems rather sad that his relatives should allow him to come out alone.”
passages.vernacular: 「福爾摩斯,」一天早晨我站喺我哋嘅凸窗旁向街上望去,講,「呢度嚟咗一個瘋子。佢嘅親戚讓佢獨自出嚟,似乎相當可悲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「福爾摩斯,」一天早晨我站在我們的凸窗旁向街上望去,說,「這裡來了一個瘋子。他的親戚讓他獨自出來,似乎相當可悲。」

passages.original: My friend rose lazily from his armchair and stood with his hands in the pockets of his dressing-gown, looking over my shoulder. It was a bright, crisp February morning, and the snow of the day before still lay deep upon the ground, shimmering brightly in the wintry sun. Down the centre of Baker Street it had been ploughed into a brown crumbly band by the traffic, but at either side and on the heaped-up edges of the footpaths it still lay as white as when it fell. The grey pavement had been cleaned and scraped, but was still dangerously slippery, so that there were fewer passengers than usual. Indeed, from the direction of the Metropolitan Station no one was coming save the single gentleman whose eccentric conduct had drawn my attention.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅朋友懶洋洋地從扶手椅上起身,雙手插喺晨衣口袋裡站住,越過我嘅肩膀睇。嗰個係個明亮清爽嘅二月早晨,前一天嘅雪仍深深地蓋喺地上,喺冬日嘅陽光下閃閃發亮。貝克街中央被車輛碾成一條棕色鬆脆嘅帶子,但喺兩側同堆積嘅人行道邊緣,佢仍像落下時一樣白。灰色嘅人行道已被清掃同刮過,但仍危險地濕滑,所以行人比平時少。確實,從大都會車站嘅方向,除咗嗰位行為古怪、吸引咗我注意嘅先生之外,冇人過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的朋友懶洋洋地從扶手椅上起身,雙手插在晨衣口袋裡站著,越過我的肩膀看。那是個明亮清爽的二月早晨,前一天的雪仍深深地蓋在地上,在冬日的陽光下閃閃發亮。貝克街中央被車輛碾成一條棕色鬆脆的帶子,但在兩側和堆積的人行道邊緣,它仍像落下時一樣白。灰色的人行道已被清掃和刮過,但仍危險地濕滑,所以行人比平時少。確實,從大都會車站的方向,除了那位行為古怪、吸引了我注意的先生之外,沒有人過來。

passages.original: He was a man of about fifty, tall, portly, and imposing, with a massive, strongly marked face and a commanding figure. He was dressed in a sombre yet rich style, in black frock-coat, shining hat, neat brown gaiters, and well-cut pearl-grey trousers. Yet his actions were in absurd contrast to the dignity of his dress and features, for he was running hard, with occasional little springs, such as a weary man gives who is little accustomed to set any tax upon his legs. As he ran he jerked his hands up and down, waggled his head, and writhed his face into the most extraordinary contortions.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個五十歲左右嘅人,高大、肥胖、有威嚴,有一張粗獷、棱角鮮明嘅臉同一副有氣勢嘅身材。佢穿住陰沉而富麗嘅風格,黑色長禮服外套,發亮嘅帽子,整潔嘅棕色綁腿,同剪裁良好嘅珍珠灰長褲。然而佢嘅行為同佢衣住同相貌嘅尊嚴形成荒唐嘅對比,因為佢喺拚命跑,不時小小地躍起,就像一個好少讓雙腿承受負擔嘅疲倦人嗰樣。佢跑住時,雙手上下猛甩,腦袋搖晃,臉扭曲成最非同尋常嘅怪相。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個五十歲左右的人,高大、肥胖、有威嚴,有一張粗獷、棱角鮮明的臉和一副有氣勢的身材。他穿著陰沉而富麗的風格,黑色長禮服外套,發亮的帽子,整潔的棕色綁腿,和剪裁良好的珍珠灰長褲。然而他的行為與他衣著和相貌的尊嚴形成荒唐的對比,因為他在拚命跑,不時小小地躍起,就像一個很少讓雙腿承受負擔的疲倦人那樣。他跑著時,雙手上下猛甩,腦袋搖晃,臉扭曲成最非同尋常的怪相。

passages.original: “What on earth can be the matter with him?” I asked. “He is looking up at the numbers of the houses.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢到底出咗乜嘢事?」我問。「佢喺抬頭睇房子嘅號碼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他到底出了什麼事?」我問。「他在抬頭看房子的號碼。」

passages.original: “I believe that he is coming here,” said Holmes, rubbing his hands.
passages.vernacular: 「我相信佢係嚟呢度嘅,」福爾摩斯搓著手講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我相信他是來這裡的,」福爾摩斯搓著手說。

passages.original: “Here?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡?」

passages.original: “Yes; I rather think he is coming to consult me professionally. I think that I recognise the symptoms. Ha! did I not tell you?” As he spoke, the man, puffing and blowing, rushed at our door and pulled at our bell until the whole house resounded with the clanging.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅;我倒係認為佢係嚟專業地向我諮詢嘅。我想我認出咗呢啲症狀。哈!我冇告訴你嗎?」佢講話時,嗰人氣喘吁吁地衝到我哋門前,拉我哋嘅門鈴,直到整幢房子都響住鈴聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的;我倒是認為他是來專業地向我諮詢的。我想我認出了這些症狀。哈!我沒告訴你嗎?」他說話時,那人氣喘吁吁地衝到我們門前,拉我們的門鈴,直到整幢房子都響著鈴聲。

passages.original: A few moments later he was in our room, still puffing, still gesticulating, but with so fixed a look of grief and despair in his eyes that our smiles were turned in an instant to horror and pity. For a while he could not get his words out, but swayed his body and plucked at his hair like one who has been driven to the extreme limits of his reason. Then, suddenly springing to his feet, he beat his head against the wall with such force that we both rushed upon him and tore him away to the centre of the room. Sherlock Holmes pushed him down into the easy-chair and, sitting beside him, patted his hand and chatted with him in the easy, soothing tones which he knew so well how to employ.
passages.vernacular: 片刻後,佢進咗我哋嘅房間,仍喺喘氣,仍喺比劃,但眼裡咁固定嘅悲傷同絕望嘅神情,使我哋嘅微笑頓時變成咗恐懼同憐憫。有一會兒佢講不出話嚟,只係搖晃住身體,拔住頭髮,像一個被逼到理智極限嘅人。然後,佢突然跳起嚟,用力把頭撞向牆壁,我哋兩人都衝上去,把佢拉到房間中央。夏洛克·福爾摩斯把佢按進扶手椅,坐喺佢旁邊,拍住佢嘅手,以佢好擅長使用嘅嗰種輕鬆、安撫嘅語調同佢交談。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 片刻後,他進了我們的房間,仍在喘氣,仍在比劃,但眼裡那麼固定的悲傷和絕望的神情,使我們的微笑頓時變成了恐懼和憐憫。有一會兒他說不出話來,只是搖晃著身體,拔著頭髮,像一個被逼到理智極限的人。然後,他突然跳起來,用力把頭撞向牆壁,我們兩人都衝上去,把他拉到房間中央。夏洛克·福爾摩斯把他按進扶手椅,坐在他旁邊,拍著他的手,以他很擅長使用的那種輕鬆、安撫的語調同他交談。
