It was not mere curiosity, though I have my share of that. It was more a feeling of duty—a feeling that some good might come from my penetrating to this place. They talk of woman’s instinct; perhaps it was woman’s instinct which gave me that feeling. At any rate, it was there, and I was keenly on the lookout for any chance to pass the forbidden door.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,福爾摩斯先生,從我明白嗰套房間有乜嘢我不該知道嘅嘢嘅嗰一刻起,我渴望去參觀佢哋。呢不僅係好奇,雖然我有我嗰份好奇。呢更多係一種責任感——一種我進入呢個地方可能會帶嚟啲好處嘅感覺。人哋講女人嘅直覺;或者係女人嘅直覺畀咗我嗰種感覺。無論如何,佢喺嗰度,我敏銳地留意住任何走過嗰扇禁門嘅機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,福爾摩斯先生,從我明白那套房間有什麼我不該知道的東西的那一刻起,我渴望去參觀它們。這不僅是好奇,雖然我有我那份好奇。這更多是一種責任感——一種我進入這個地方可能會帶來一些好處的感覺。人們說女人的直覺;也許是女人的直覺給了我那種感覺。無論如何,它在那裡,我敏銳地留意著任何走過那扇禁門的機會。

passages.original: “It was only yesterday that the chance came. I may tell you that, besides Mr. Rucastle, both Toller and his wife find something to do in these deserted rooms, and I once saw him carrying a large black linen bag with him through the door. Recently he has been drinking hard, and yesterday evening he was very drunk; and when I came upstairs there was the key in the door. I have no doubt at all that he had left it there. Mr. and Mrs. Rucastle were both downstairs, and the child was with them, so that I had an admirable opportunity. I turned the key gently in the lock, opened the door, and slipped through.
passages.vernacular: 「機會係尋日才嚟嘅。我可以告訴你哋,除咗魯卡斯爾先生,托勒同佢嘅妻子都喺呢啲廢棄嘅房間裡有事可做,我曾睇到佢帶住一個大黑亞麻布袋穿過嗰扇門。最近佢一直喺狂飲,琴晚佢飲得爛醉;我上樓時,鑰匙就喺門上。我毫不懷疑,佢把佢留喺嗰度喇。魯卡斯爾夫婦都喺樓下,細路都同佢哋喺一起,所以我有咗極好嘅機會。我輕輕轉動鎖裡嘅鑰匙,打開門,溜咗進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「機會是昨天才來的。我可以告訴你們,除了魯卡斯爾先生,托勒和他的妻子都在這些廢棄的房間裡有事可做,我曾看到他帶著一個大黑亞麻布袋穿過那扇門。最近他一直在狂飲,昨晚他喝得爛醉;我上樓時,鑰匙就在門上。我毫不懷疑,他把它留在那裡了。魯卡斯爾夫婦都在樓下,孩子也和他們在一起,所以我有了極好的機會。我輕輕轉動鎖裡的鑰匙,打開門,溜了進去。

passages.original: “There was a little passage in front of me, unpapered and uncarpeted, which turned at a right angle at the farther end. Round this corner were three doors in a line, the first and third of which were open. They each led into an empty room, dusty and cheerless, with two windows in the one and one in the other, so thick with dirt that the evening light glimmered dimly through them. The centre door was closed, and across the outside of it had been fastened one of the broad bars of an iron bed, padlocked at one end to a ring in the wall, and fastened at the other with stout cord. The door itself was locked as well, and the key was not there. This barricaded door corresponded clearly with the shuttered window outside, and yet I could see by the glimmer from beneath it that the room was not in darkness. Evidently there was a skylight which let in light from above. As I stood in the passage gazing at the sinister door and wondering what secret it might veil, I suddenly heard the sound of steps within the room and saw a shadow pass backward and forward against the little slit of dim light which shone out from under the door. A mad, unreasoning terror rose up in me at the sight, Mr. Holmes. My overstrung nerves failed me suddenly, and I turned and ran—ran as though some dreadful hand were behind me clutching at the skirt of my dress. I rushed down the passage, through the door, and straight into the arms of Mr. Rucastle, who was waiting outside.
passages.vernacular: 「我面前有一條小走廊,冇糊壁紙,都冇鋪地毯,喺遠端成直角轉彎。轉過呢個拐角,有三扇門排成一排,第一扇同第三扇係開住嘅。佢哋各通向一個空房間,滿係灰塵,陰冷冇生氣,一個有兩扇窗,另一個有一扇,窗子髒得好厚,傍晚嘅光只能微弱地透過。中間嗰扇門關住,門外釘住一根鐵床嘅寬橫條,一端用掛鎖鎖喺牆上嘅環上,另一端用粗繩綁住。門本身都鎖住,鑰匙不喺嗰度。呢扇設咗路障嘅門顯然對應外面關咗百葉窗嘅窗子,然而我從門下嘅微光可以睇出,房間並唔係黑暗嘅。顯然有一扇天窗從上面透光。我站喺走廊裡盯住呢扇不祥嘅門,想知道佢可能遮蓋住乜嘢秘密,呢陣我突然聽到房間裡有腳步聲,睇見一個影子喺從門下透出嘅嗰一小道昏暗嘅光縫上嚟回移動。福爾摩斯先生,睇到呢情景,我心裡升起瘋狂、毫無道理嘅恐懼。我繃得過緊嘅神經突然垮喇,我轉身跑——跑得好像有一隻可怕嘅手喺我身後抓住我裙子嘅下擺。我衝過走廊,穿過門,直接撞進咗喺外面等住嘅魯卡斯爾先生嘅懷抱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我面前有一條小走廊,沒有糊壁紙,也沒鋪地毯,在遠端成直角轉彎。轉過這個拐角,有三扇門排成一排,第一扇和第三扇是開著的。它們各通向一個空房間,滿是灰塵,陰冷沒有生氣,一個有兩扇窗,另一個有一扇,窗子髒得很厚,傍晚的光只能微弱地透過。中間那扇門關著,門外釘著一根鐵床的寬橫條,一端用掛鎖鎖在牆上的環上,另一端用粗繩綁住。門本身也鎖著,鑰匙不在那裡。這扇設了路障的門顯然對應外面關了百葉窗的窗子,然而我從門下的微光可以看出,房間並不是黑暗的。顯然有一扇天窗從上面透光。我站在走廊裡盯著這扇不祥的門,想知道它可能遮蓋著什麼秘密,這時我突然聽到房間裡有腳步聲,看見一個影子在從門下透出的那一小道昏暗的光縫上來回移動。福爾摩斯先生,看到這情景,我心裡升起瘋狂、毫無道理的恐懼。我繃得過緊的神經突然垮了,我轉身跑——跑得好像有一隻可怕的手在我身後抓住我裙子的下擺。我衝過走廊,穿過門,直接撞進了在外面等著的魯卡斯爾先生的懷抱。

passages.original: “‘So,’ said he, smiling, ‘it was you, then. I thought that it must be when I saw the door open.’
passages.vernacular: 「『咁講,』佢微笑住講,『原來係您。我睇到門開住時就想一定係。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『這麼說,』他微笑著說,『原來是您。我看到門開著時就想一定是。』

passages.original: “‘Oh, I am so frightened!’ I panted.
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,我嚇壞喇!』我喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,我嚇壞了!』我喘著氣說。

passages.original: “‘My dear young lady! my dear young lady!’—you cannot think how caressing and soothing his manner was—‘and what has frightened you, my dear young lady?’
passages.vernacular: 「『我親愛嘅年輕小姐!我親愛嘅年輕小姐!』——你想像唔到佢嘅態度幾咁愛撫同安撫——『乜嘢嚇到咗您,我親愛嘅年輕小姐?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我親愛的年輕小姐!我親愛的年輕小姐!』——你想像不到他的態度多麼愛撫和安撫——『什麼嚇到了您,我親愛的年輕小姐?』

passages.original: “But his voice was just a little too coaxing. He overdid it. I was keenly on my guard against him.
passages.vernacular: 「但佢嘅聲音只係稍微太哄人咗啲。佢做得過頭喇。我對佢保持住高度警惕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但他的聲音只是稍微太哄人了一點。他做得過頭了。我對他保持著高度警惕。

passages.original: “‘I was foolish enough to go into the empty wing,’ I answered. ‘But it is so lonely and eerie in this dim light that I was frightened and ran out again. Oh, it is so dreadfully still in there!’
passages.vernacular: 「『我愚蠢地走進咗嗰個空嘅翼,』我回答。『但喺呢昏暗嘅光線下,嗰度咁孤寂可怕,我害怕喇,又跑出嚟。哦,嗰度面可怕地寂靜!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我愚蠢地走進了那個空的翼,』我回答。『但在這昏暗的光線下,那裡那麼孤寂可怕,我害怕了,又跑出來。哦,那裡面可怕地寂靜!』

passages.original: “‘Only that?’ said he, looking at me keenly.
passages.vernacular: 「『只係咁樣?』佢講,銳利地睇住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『只是這樣?』他說,銳利地看著我。

passages.original: “‘Why, what did you think?’ I asked.
passages.vernacular: 「『哎呀,您以為係乜嘢?』我問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哎呀,您以為是什麼?』我問。

passages.original: “‘Why do you think that I lock this door?’
passages.vernacular: 「『您以為我點解鎖呢扇門?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『您以為我為什麼鎖這扇門?』

passages.original: “‘I am sure that I do not know.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我確實唔知道。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我確實不知道。』

passages.original: “‘It is to keep people out who have no business there. Do you see?’ He was still smiling in the most amiable manner.
passages.vernacular: 「『係為了把嗰啲喺嗰度冇事嘅人擋喺外面。您明白嗎?』佢仍以最和藹嘅方式微笑住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『是為了把那些在那裡沒有事的人擋在外面。您明白嗎?』他仍以最和藹的方式微笑著。

passages.original: “‘I am sure if I had known—’
passages.vernacular: 「『我確信如果我知道——』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我確信如果我知道——』

passages.original: “‘Well, then, you know now. And if you ever put your foot over that threshold again’—here in an instant the smile hardened into a grin of rage, and he glared down at me with the face of a demon—‘I’ll throw you to the mastiff.’
passages.vernacular: 「『好吧,咁您而家知道喇。如果您再踏過嗰個門檻一步』——呢陣佢嘅微笑頃刻硬成咗憤怒嘅獰笑,佢以惡魔嘅面孔怒視住我——『我就把您扔畀嗰條獒犬。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『好吧,那麼您現在知道了。如果您再踏過那個門檻一步』——這時他的微笑頃刻硬成了憤怒的獰笑,他以惡魔的面孔怒視著我——『我就把您扔給那條獒犬。』

passages.original: “I was so terrified that I do not know what I did. I suppose that I must have rushed past him into my room. I remember nothing until I found myself lying on my bed trembling all over. Then I thought of you, Mr. Holmes. I could not live there longer without some advice. I was frightened of the house, of the man, of the woman, of the servants, even of the child. They were all horrible to me. If I could only bring you down all would be well. Of course I might have fled from the house, but my curiosity was almost as strong as my fears. My mind was soon made up. I would send you a wire. I put on my hat and cloak, went down to the office, which is about half a mile from the house, and then returned, feeling very much easier. A horrible doubt came into my mind as I approached the door lest the dog might be loose, but I remembered that Toller had drunk himself into a state of insensibility that evening, and I knew that he was the only one in the household who had any influence with the savage creature, or who would venture to set him free. I slipped in in safety and lay awake half the night in my joy at the thought of seeing you. I had no difficulty in getting leave to come into Winchester this morning, but I must be back before three o’clock, for Mr. and Mrs. Rucastle are going on a visit, and will be away all the evening, so that I must look after the child. Now I have told you all my adventures, Mr. Holmes, and I should be very glad if you could tell me what it all means, and, above all, what I should do.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嚇壞喇,唔知道自己做咗乜嘢。我想我一定係從佢身邊衝進咗我嘅房間。我乜嘢都不記得,直到發現自己躺喺床上,全身發抖。然後我想到咗您,福爾摩斯先生。冇啲建議,我再都無法喺嗰度生活。我害怕嗰座房子,害怕嗰個男人、嗰個女人、僕人哋,甚至細路。佢哋對我都係可怕嘅。如果我能請您下嚟,一切都會好。當然我本可以逃離房子,但我嘅好奇心幾乎同我嘅恐懼一樣強。我好快下咗決心。我要畀您發電報。我戴上帽子,穿上斗篷,下到離房子約半英里嘅電報局,然後回嚟,覺得輕鬆得多。我走近門時,一個可怕嘅疑慮進入我嘅腦海,怕狗已被放出嚟,但我記起托勒嗰天晚上已飲得不省人事,而我知道佢係家裡唯一對嗰兇猛嘅畜生有任何影響,或敢於放牠出嚟嘅人。我安全地溜進去,想到會見到您,高興得半夜冇瞓。我毫不費力就得到咗今日早晨嚟溫徹斯特嘅許可,但我必須喺三點前回去,因為魯卡斯爾夫婦要去拜訪人,整個晚上不喺,所以我必須照睇細路。而家我已把我所有嘅冒險告訴您喇,福爾摩斯先生,如果您能告訴我呢一切意味住乜嘢,而且最重要嘅係我應該點做,我會好高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我嚇壞了,不知道自己做了什麼。我想我一定是從他身邊衝進了我的房間。我什麼也不記得,直到發現自己躺在床上,全身發抖。然後我想到了您,福爾摩斯先生。沒有一些建議,我再也無法在那裡生活。我害怕那座房子,害怕那個男人、那個女人、僕人們,甚至孩子。他們對我都是可怕的。如果我能請您下來,一切都會好。當然我本可以逃離房子,但我的好奇心幾乎和我的恐懼一樣強。我很快下了決心。我要給您發電報。我戴上帽子,穿上斗篷,下到離房子約半英里的電報局,然後回來,覺得輕鬆得多。我走近門時,一個可怕的疑慮進入我的腦海,怕狗已被放出來,但我記起托勒那天晚上已喝得不省人事,而我知道他是家裡唯一對那兇猛的畜生有任何影響,或敢於放牠出來的人。我安全地溜進去,想到會見到您,高興得半夜沒睡。我毫不費力就得到了今天早晨來溫徹斯特的許可,但我必須在三點前回去,因為魯卡斯爾夫婦要去拜訪人,整個晚上不在,所以我必須照看孩子。現在我已把我所有的冒險告訴您了,福爾摩斯先生,如果您能告訴我這一切意味著什麼,而且最重要的是我應該怎麼做,我會非常高興。」

passages.original: Holmes and I had listened spellbound to this extraordinary story. My friend rose now and paced up and down the room, his hands in his pockets, and an expression of the most profound gravity upon his face.
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯同我如痴如醉地聽完咗呢個非凡嘅故事。我嘅朋友而家起身,喺房間裡走嚟走去,雙手插喺口袋裡,臉上帶住最深沉嘅嚴肅表情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯和我如痴如醉地聽完了這個非凡的故事。我的朋友現在起身,在房間裡走來走去,雙手插在口袋裡,臉上帶著最深沉的嚴肅表情。

passages.original: “Is Toller still drunk?” he asked.
passages.vernacular: 「托勒仲醉住嗎?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「托勒還醉著嗎?」他問。

passages.original: “Yes. I heard his wife tell Mrs. Rucastle that she could do nothing with him.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。我聽到佢妻子對魯卡斯爾太太講佢攞佢冇辦法。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。我聽到他妻子對魯卡斯爾太太說她拿他沒辦法。」

passages.original: “That is well. And the Rucastles go out to-night?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰好好。魯卡斯爾夫婦今晚出去嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那很好。魯卡斯爾夫婦今晚出去嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。」

passages.original: “Is there a cellar with a good strong lock?”
passages.vernacular: 「有冇一個鎖好結實嘅地窖?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有沒有一個鎖很結實的地窖?」

passages.original: “Yes, the wine-cellar.”
passages.vernacular: 「有,酒窖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有,酒窖。」

passages.original: “You seem to me to have acted all through this matter like a very brave and sensible girl, Miss Hunter. Do you think that you could perform one more feat? I should not ask it of you if I did not think you a quite exceptional woman.”
passages.vernacular: 「亨特小姐,喺整件事中您嘅行為喺我睇來像一個好勇敢而明智嘅女孩。您認為您仲能再做一件事嗎?如果我不認為您係一位相當非凡嘅女性,我唔會向您提出。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「亨特小姐,在整件事中您的行為在我看來像一個非常勇敢而明智的女孩。您認為您還能再做一件事嗎?如果我不認為您是一位相當非凡的女性,我不會向您提出。」

passages.original: “I will try. What is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「我會試試。係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會試試。是什麼?」

passages.original: “We shall be at the Copper Beeches by seven o’clock, my friend and I. The Rucastles will be gone by that time, and Toller will, we hope, be incapable. There only remains Mrs. Toller, who might give the alarm. If you could send her into the cellar on some errand, and then turn the key upon her, you would facilitate matters immensely.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅朋友同我七點鐘會到銅山毛櫸莊。魯卡斯爾夫婦到嗰時會走喇,而托勒,我哋希望,會失去行動能力。只剩下托勒太太,佢可能會發警報。如果您能找個差事把佢送進地窖,然後喺佢身上轉動鑰匙,您會大大便利事情。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的朋友和我七點鐘會到銅山毛櫸莊。魯卡斯爾夫婦到那時會走了,而托勒,我們希望,會失去行動能力。只剩下托勒太太,她可能會發警報。如果您能找個差事把她送進地窖,然後在她身上轉動鑰匙,您會大大便利事情。」

passages.original: “I will do it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我會做嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會做的。」

passages.original: “Excellent! We shall then look thoroughly into the affair. Of course there is only one feasible explanation. You have been brought there to personate someone, and the real person is imprisoned in this chamber. That is obvious. As to who this prisoner is, I have no doubt that it is the daughter, Miss Alice Rucastle, if I remember right, who was said to have gone to America. You were chosen, doubtless, as resembling her in height, figure, and the colour of your hair. Hers had been cut off, very possibly in some illness through which she has passed, and so, of course, yours had to be sacrificed also. By a curious chance you came upon her tresses. The man in the road was undoubtedly some friend of hers—possibly her fiancé—and no doubt, as you wore the girl’s dress and were so like her, he was convinced from your laughter, whenever he saw you, and afterwards from your gesture, that Miss Rucastle was perfectly happy, and that she no longer desired his attentions. The dog is let loose at night to prevent him from endeavouring to communicate with her. So much is fairly clear. The most serious point in the case is the disposition of the child.”
passages.vernacular: 「好極喇!然後我哋將徹底調查呢件事。當然,只有一種可行嘅解釋。您被帶到嗰度去冒充某人,而真正嘅人被關喺呢個房間裡。呢個係顯而易見嘅。至於呢個囚犯係邊個,我毫不懷疑係女兒,如果我冇記錯,愛麗絲·魯卡斯爾小姐,據講去咗美國嘅嗰個。無疑,選您係因為您喺身高、身材同頭髮顏色上像佢。佢嘅頭髮被剪掉喇,好可能係喺佢經歷嘅某場病中,所以,當然,您嘅都必須犧牲。出於一個奇特嘅巧合,您碰上咗佢嘅髮辮。路上嘅嗰個人無疑係佢嘅某位朋友——可能係佢嘅未婚夫——無疑,因為您穿住嗰姑娘嘅衣服,又咁像佢,每當佢睇到您,從您嘅笑聲,以及後來從您嘅手勢,佢確信魯卡斯爾小姐完全幸福,唔再希望佢嘅殷勤。夜裡放狗,係為了防止佢設法同佢聯繫。呢啲相當清楚。呢個案子最嚴重嘅啲係嗰個細路嘅性格。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好極了!然後我們將徹底調查這件事。當然,只有一種可行的解釋。您被帶到那裡去冒充某人,而真正的人被關在這個房間裡。這是顯而易見的。至於這個囚犯是誰,我毫不懷疑是女兒,如果我沒記錯,愛麗絲·魯卡斯爾小姐,據說去了美國的那個。無疑,選您是因為您在身高、身材和頭髮顏色上像她。她的頭髮被剪掉了,很可能是在她經歷的某場病中,所以,當然,您的也必須犧牲。出於一個奇特的巧合,您碰上了她的髮辮。路上的那個人無疑是她的某位朋友——可能是她的未婚夫——無疑,因為您穿著那姑娘的衣服,又那麼像她,每當他看到您,從您的笑聲,以及後來從您的手勢,他確信魯卡斯爾小姐完全幸福,不再希望他的殷勤。夜裡放狗,是為了防止他設法與她聯繫。這些相當清楚。這個案子最嚴重的一點是那個孩子的性格。」

passages.original: “What on earth has that to do with it?” I ejaculated.
passages.vernacular: 「呢到底同佢有乜嘢關係?」我脫口而出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這到底和它有什麼關係?」我脫口而出。

passages.original: “My dear Watson, you as a medical man are continually gaining light as to the tendencies of a child by the study of the parents. Don’t you see that the converse is equally valid. I have frequently gained my first real insight into the character of parents by studying their children. This child’s disposition is abnormally cruel, merely for cruelty’s sake, and whether he derives this from his smiling father, as I should suspect, or from his mother, it bodes evil for the poor girl who is in their power.”
passages.vernacular: 「我親愛嘅華生,你作為醫生,通過研究父母不斷獲得對細路傾向嘅啟發。難道你冇睇到,反過嚟都同樣有效嗎。我常常通過研究細路,第一次真正洞察到父母嘅性格。呢個細路嘅性情異常殘忍,純粹為了殘忍而殘忍,不管佢係從佢嗰微笑嘅父親嗰度得嚟嘅,如我所懷疑嘅,定係從母親嗰度,對落喺佢哋手中嘅可憐女孩都係不祥之兆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我親愛的華生,你作為醫生,通過研究父母不斷獲得對孩子傾向的啟發。難道你沒看到,反過來也同樣有效嗎。我常常通過研究孩子,第一次真正洞察到父母的性格。這個孩子的性情異常殘忍,純粹為了殘忍而殘忍,不管他是從他那微笑的父親那裡得來的,如我所懷疑的,還是從母親那裡,對落在他們手中的可憐女孩都是不祥之兆。」

passages.original: “I am sure that you are right, Mr. Holmes,” cried our client. “A thousand things come back to me which make me certain that you have hit it. Oh, let us lose not an instant in bringing help to this poor creature.”
passages.vernacular: 「福爾摩斯先生,我確信您係對嘅,」我哋嘅客戶喊道。「上千件事回到我腦海,使我確定您講中喇。哦,我哋一刻都唔好耽擱,去幫助呢個可憐嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「福爾摩斯先生,我確信您是對的,」我們的客戶喊道。「上千件事回到我腦海,使我確定您說中了。哦,我們一刻也不要耽擱,去幫助這個可憐的人。」

passages.original: “We must be circumspect, for we are dealing with a very cunning man. We can do nothing until seven o’clock. At that hour we shall be with you, and it will not be long before we solve the mystery.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋必須謹慎,因為我哋喺對付一個好狡猾嘅人。七點以前我哋乜嘢都做不喇。嗰個時刻我哋會同您喺一起,不久就會解開呢個謎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們必須謹慎,因為我們在對付一個非常狡猾的人。七點以前我們什麼也做不了。那個時刻我們會與您在一起,不久就會解開這個謎。」

passages.original: We were as good as our word, for it was just seven when we reached the Copper Beeches, having put up our trap at a wayside public-house. The group of trees, with their dark leaves shining like burnished metal in the light of the setting sun, were sufficient to mark the house even had Miss Hunter not been standing smiling on the door-step.
passages.vernacular: 我哋講到做到,因為我哋到達銅山毛櫸莊時剛好七點,把我哋嘅馬車停喺路邊一家酒館。嗰叢樹,黑色嘅葉子喺夕陽嘅光中閃耀住像擦亮嘅金屬,即使亨特小姐冇微笑住站喺門階上,都足以標示房子嘅位置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們說到做到,因為我們到達銅山毛櫸莊時剛好七點,把我們的馬車停在路邊一家酒館。那叢樹,黑色的葉子在夕陽的光中閃耀著像擦亮的金屬,即使亨特小姐沒有微笑著站在門階上,也足以標示房子的位置。

passages.original: “Have you managed it?” asked Holmes.
passages.vernacular: 「您做到咗嗎?」福爾摩斯問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您做到了嗎?」福爾摩斯問。

passages.original: A loud thudding noise came from somewhere downstairs. “That is Mrs. Toller in the cellar,” said she. “Her husband lies snoring on the kitchen rug. Here are his keys, which are the duplicates of Mr. Rucastle’s.”
passages.vernacular: 樓下某處傳嚟響亮嘅砰砰聲。「嗰個係托勒太太喺地窖裡,」佢講。「佢丈夫躺喺廚房地毯上打鼾。呢個係佢嘅鑰匙,係魯卡斯爾先生嘅複製品。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樓下某處傳來響亮的砰砰聲。「那是托勒太太在地窖裡,」她說。「她丈夫躺在廚房地毯上打鼾。這是他的鑰匙,是魯卡斯爾先生的複製品。」

passages.original: “You have done well indeed!” cried Holmes with enthusiasm. “Now lead the way, and we shall soon see the end of this black business.”
passages.vernacular: 「您確實做得好!」福爾摩斯熱情地喊道。「而家帶路,我哋好快就會睇到呢黑暗事件嘅結局。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您確實做得好!」福爾摩斯熱情地喊道。「現在帶路,我們很快就會看到這黑暗事件的結局。」

passages.original: We passed up the stair, unlocked the door, followed on down a passage, and found ourselves in front of the barricade which Miss Hunter had described. Holmes cut the cord and removed the transverse bar. Then he tried the various keys in the lock, but without success. No sound came from within, and at the silence Holmes’ face clouded over.
passages.vernacular: 我哋上咗樓梯,打開門,沿住走廊走,發現自己站喺亨特小姐描述嘅路障前。福爾摩斯割斷繩子,移開橫條。然後佢試咗鎖裡嘅各種鑰匙,但冇成功。裡面冇聲音,聽到呢寂靜,福爾摩斯嘅臉色陰沉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們上了樓梯,打開門,沿著走廊走,發現自己站在亨特小姐描述的路障前。福爾摩斯割斷繩子,移開橫條。然後他試了鎖裡的各種鑰匙,但沒有成功。裡面沒有聲音,聽到這寂靜,福爾摩斯的臉色陰沉了。

passages.original: “I trust that we are not too late,” said he. “I think, Miss Hunter, that we had better go in without you. Now, Watson, put your shoulder to it, and we shall see whether we cannot make our way in.”
passages.vernacular: 「我希望我哋冇太遲,」佢講。「亨特小姐,我想我哋最好不帶您進去。而家,華生,用你嘅肩膀頂佢,我哋睇睇能唔能夠撞進去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望我們沒有太遲,」他說。「亨特小姐,我想我們最好不帶您進去。現在,華生,用你的肩膀頂它,我們看看能不能撞進去。」

passages.original: It was an old rickety door and gave at once before our united strength. Together we rushed into the room. It was empty. There was no furniture save a little pallet bed, a small table, and a basketful of linen. The skylight above was open, and the prisoner gone.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一扇搖搖晃晃嘅舊門,喺我哋合力之下即刻讓開喇。我哋一起衝進房間。佢係空嘅。除咗一張小草墊床、一張小桌子同一籃亞麻布之外,冇家具。上面嘅天窗開住,囚犯唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一扇搖搖晃晃的舊門,在我們合力之下立刻讓開了。我們一起衝進房間。它是空的。除了一張小草墊床、一張小桌子和一籃亞麻布之外,沒有家具。上面的天窗開著,囚犯不見了。

passages.original: “There has been some villainy here,” said Holmes; “this beauty has guessed Miss Hunter’s intentions and has carried his victim off.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢度發生咗惡行,」福爾摩斯講;「呢個美人猜到咗亨特小姐嘅意圖,把佢嘅受害者帶走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡發生了惡行,」福爾摩斯說;「這個美人猜到了亨特小姐的意圖,把他的受害者帶走了。」

passages.original: “But how?”
passages.vernacular: 「但點?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但怎麼?」

passages.original: “Through the skylight. We shall soon see how he managed it.” He swung himself up onto the roof. “Ah, yes,” he cried, “here’s the end of a long light ladder against the eaves. That is how he did it.”
passages.vernacular: 「通過天窗。我哋好快就會睇到佢係點做到嘅。」佢一躍而上屋頂。「啊,係嘅,」佢喊道,「呢度有一架輕便長梯嘅末端靠喺屋簷上。佢就係咁樣做嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「通過天窗。我們很快就會看到他是怎麼做到的。」他一躍而上屋頂。「啊,是的,」他喊道,「這裡有一架輕便長梯的末端靠在屋簷上。他就是這樣做的。」

passages.original: “But it is impossible,” said Miss Hunter; “the ladder was not there when the Rucastles went away.”
passages.vernacular: 「但呢唔可能,」亨特小姐講;「魯卡斯爾夫婦離開時梯子不喺嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但這不可能,」亨特小姐說;「魯卡斯爾夫婦離開時梯子不在那裡。」

passages.original: “He has come back and done it. I tell you that he is a clever and dangerous man. I should not be very much surprised if this were he whose step I hear now upon the stair. I think, Watson, that it would be as well for you to have your pistol ready.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢回嚟做嘅。我告訴你,佢係個聰明而危險嘅人。如果我而家聽到喺樓梯上嘅腳步聲就係佢,我唔會太驚訝。華生,我想你最好準備好你嘅手槍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他回來做的。我告訴你,他是個聰明而危險的人。如果我現在聽到在樓梯上的腳步聲就是他,我不會太驚訝。華生,我想你最好準備好你的手槍。」

passages.original: The words were hardly out of his mouth before a man appeared at the door of the room, a very fat and burly man, with a heavy stick in his hand. Miss Hunter screamed and shrunk against the wall at the sight of him, but Sherlock Holmes sprang forward and confronted him.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅話剛講出口,房間門口就出現咗一個人,一個好肥胖魁梧嘅人,手裡攞住一根粗棍。亨特小姐睇到佢尖叫一聲,縮到牆邊,但夏洛克·福爾摩斯跳上前去面對佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的話剛說出口,房間門口就出現了一個人,一個非常肥胖魁梧的人,手裡拿著一根粗棍。亨特小姐看到他尖叫一聲,縮到牆邊,但夏洛克·福爾摩斯跳上前去面對他。

passages.original: “You villain!” said he, “where’s your daughter?”
passages.vernacular: 「你呢惡棍!」佢講,「你嘅女兒喺邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你這惡棍!」他說,「你的女兒在哪裡?」

passages.original: The fat man cast his eyes round, and then up at the open skylight.
passages.vernacular: 胖子環顧四周,然後抬頭睇開住嘅天窗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 胖子環顧四周,然後抬頭看開著的天窗。

passages.original: “It is for me to ask you that,” he shrieked, “you thieves! Spies and thieves! I have caught you, have I? You are in my power. I’ll serve you!” He turned and clattered down the stairs as hard as he could go.
passages.vernacular: 「該我問你呢個,」佢尖叫,「你哋呢啲賊!間諜同賊!我抓住你哋喇,係唔係?你哋喺我掌握之中。我要收拾你哋!」佢轉身,盡佢所能快地嘩啦啦地衝下樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「該我問你這個,」他尖叫,「你們這些賊!間諜和賊!我抓住你們了,是不是?你們在我掌握之中。我要收拾你們!」他轉身,盡他所能快地嘩啦啦地衝下樓。

passages.original: “He’s gone for the dog!” cried Miss Hunter.
passages.vernacular: 「佢去放狗喇!」亨特小姐喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他去放狗了!」亨特小姐喊道。

passages.original: “I have my revolver,” said I.
passages.vernacular: 「我有我嘅左輪手槍,」我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有我的左輪手槍,」我說。

passages.original: “Better close the front door,” cried Holmes, and we all rushed down the stairs together. We had hardly reached the hall when we heard the baying of a hound, and then a scream of agony, with a horrible worrying sound which it was dreadful to listen to. An elderly man with a red face and shaking limbs came staggering out at a side door.
passages.vernacular: 「最好關上前門,」福爾摩斯喊道,我哋一起衝下樓梯。我哋剛到門廳,就聽到獵犬嘅吠叫聲,然後係一聲痛苦嘅尖叫,伴隨住可怕嘅撕咬聲,聽住令人毛骨悚然。一個紅臉、四肢顫抖嘅老年男子,從側門蹣跚而出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最好關上前門,」福爾摩斯喊道,我們一起衝下樓梯。我們剛到門廳,就聽到獵犬的吠叫聲,然後是一聲痛苦的尖叫,伴隨著可怕的撕咬聲,聽著令人毛骨悚然。一個紅臉、四肢顫抖的老年男子,從側門蹣跚而出。

passages.original: “My God!” he cried. “Someone has loosed the dog. It’s not been fed for two days. Quick, quick, or it’ll be too late!”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅上帝!」佢喊道。「有人放咗狗。牠兩天冇餵喇。快,快,否則太遲喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的上帝!」他喊道。「有人放了狗。牠兩天沒餵了。快,快,否則太遲了!」

passages.original: Holmes and I rushed out and round the angle of the house, with Toller hurrying behind us. There was the huge famished brute, its black muzzle buried in Rucastle’s throat, while he writhed and screamed upon the ground. Running up, I blew its brains out, and it fell over with its keen white teeth still meeting in the great creases of his neck. With much labour we separated them and carried him, living but horribly mangled, into the house. We laid him upon the drawing-room sofa, and having dispatched the sobered Toller to bear the news to his wife, I did what I could to relieve his pain. We were all assembled round him when the door opened, and a tall, gaunt woman entered the room.
passages.vernacular: 福爾摩斯同我衝出去,繞過房子嘅拐角,托勒急忙跟喺我哋後面。嗰頭巨大嘅飢餓野獸喺嗰度,黑色嘅口鼻埋喺魯卡斯爾嘅喉嚨上,佢喺地上扭動、尖叫。我跑上去,打爆咗牠嘅腦袋,牠倒下去,銳利嘅白牙仍然喺佢脖子嘅大褶皺中咬合住。費咗好大力氣,我哋把佢哋分開,把佢抬進房子裡,佢仲活住,但被撕咬得可怕。我哋把佢放喺客廳嘅沙發上,派清醒過嚟嘅托勒把消息帶畀佢嘅妻子後,我盡我所能減輕佢嘅疼痛。我哋都聚集喺佢周圍,呢陣門開喇,一個又高又瘦嘅女人走進房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福爾摩斯和我衝出去,繞過房子的拐角,托勒急忙跟在我們後面。那頭巨大的飢餓野獸在那裡,黑色的口鼻埋在魯卡斯爾的喉嚨上,他在地上扭動、尖叫。我跑上去,打爆了牠的腦袋,牠倒下去,銳利的白牙仍然在他脖子的大褶皺中咬合著。費了很大力氣,我們把他們分開,把他抬進房子裡,他還活著,但被撕咬得可怕。我們把他放在客廳的沙發上,派清醒過來的托勒把消息帶給他的妻子後,我盡我所能減輕他的疼痛。我們都聚集在他周圍,這時門開了,一個又高又瘦的女人走進房間。

passages.original: “Mrs. Toller!” cried Miss Hunter.
passages.vernacular: 「托勒太太!」亨特小姐喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「托勒太太!」亨特小姐喊道。

passages.original: “Yes, miss. Mr. Rucastle let me out when he came back before he went up to you. Ah, miss, it is a pity you didn’t let me know what you were planning, for I would have told you that your pains were wasted.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,小姐。魯卡斯爾先生喺佢上去找你哋之前回嚟時,把我放出嚟喇。啊,小姐,可惜你冇讓我知道你嘅計畫,因為我會告訴你你白費咗力氣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,小姐。魯卡斯爾先生在他上去找你們之前回來時,把我放出來了。啊,小姐,可惜你沒有讓我知道你的計畫,因為我會告訴你你白費了力氣。」

passages.original: “Ha!” said Holmes, looking keenly at her. “It is clear that Mrs. Toller knows more about this matter than anyone else.”
passages.vernacular: 「哈!」福爾摩斯講,銳利地睇住佢。「好顯然,托勒太太比任何人都更了解呢件事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈!」福爾摩斯說,銳利地看著她。「很顯然,托勒太太比任何人都更了解這件事。」

passages.original: “Yes, sir, I do, and I am ready enough to tell what I know.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生,我了解,我好樂意講我知道嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生,我了解,我很樂意講我知道的。」

passages.original: “Then, pray, sit down, and let us hear it for there are several points on which I must confess that I am still in the dark.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁請坐下,讓我哋聽聽,因為有幾點我必須承認我仍然摸不住頭腦。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼請坐下,讓我們聽聽,因為有幾點我必須承認我仍然摸不著頭腦。」

passages.original: “I will soon make it clear to you,” said she; “and I’d have done so before now if I could ha’ got out from the cellar. If there’s police-court business over this, you’ll remember that I was the one that stood your friend, and that I was Miss Alice’s friend too.
passages.vernacular: 「我好快會向你哋講清楚,」佢講;「如果我能從地窖出嚟,我早就講喇。如果呢事有警察法庭嘅事,你哋會記得我係站喺你哋朋友呢一邊嘅人,而且我都係愛麗絲小姐嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很快會向你們說清楚,」她說;「如果我能從地窖出來,我早就說了。如果這事有警察法庭的事,你們會記得我是站在你們朋友這一邊的人,而且我也是愛麗絲小姐的朋友。

passages.original: “She was never happy at home, Miss Alice wasn’t, from the time that her father married again. She was slighted like and had no say in anything, but it never really became bad for her until after she met Mr. Fowler at a friend’s house. As well as I could learn, Miss Alice had rights of her own by will, but she was so quiet and patient, she was, that she never said a word about them but just left everything in Mr. Rucastle’s hands. He knew he was safe with her; but when there was a chance of a husband coming forward, who would ask for all that the law would give him, then her father thought it time to put a stop on it. He wanted her to sign a paper, so that whether she married or not, he could use her money. When she wouldn’t do it, he kept on worrying her until she got brain-fever, and for six weeks was at death’s door. Then she got better at last, all worn to a shadow, and with her beautiful hair cut off; but that didn’t make no change in her young man, and he stuck to her as true as man could be.”
passages.vernacular: 「愛麗絲小姐喺家從來不快樂,自從佢父親再婚以來。佢被輕視,喺任何事情上都冇發言權,但直到佢喺一個朋友家遇到弗勒先生之後,事情才對佢真正變壞。據我所能了解,愛麗絲小姐根據遺囑有佢自己嘅權利,但佢咁安靜、有耐心,佢從冇提過一個字,只係把一切留喺魯卡斯爾先生手中。佢知道同佢喺一起係安全嘅;但係當有機會有一個丈夫出現,會要求法律會畀佢嘅一切時,佢父親就認為係時候阻止喇。佢要佢簽一份文件,咁樣不管佢結不結婚,佢都可以使用佢嘅錢。佢唔肯咁樣做,佢就一直煩佢,直到佢得咗腦熱病,有六個星期瀕臨死亡。然後佢終於好喇,整個人瘦成咗影子,美麗嘅頭髮被剪掉喇;但呢對佢嘅年輕人冇任何改變,佢對佢始終忠誠,忠誠得再冇邊個男人能比。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「愛麗絲小姐在家從來不快樂,自從她父親再婚以來。她被輕視,在任何事情上都沒有發言權,但直到她在一個朋友家遇到弗勒先生之後,事情才對她真正變壞。據我所能了解,愛麗絲小姐根據遺囑有她自己的權利,但她那麼安靜、有耐心,她從沒提過一個字,只是把一切留在魯卡斯爾先生手中。他知道同她在一起是安全的;但是當有機會有一個丈夫出現,會要求法律會給他的一切時,她父親就認為是時候阻止了。他要她簽一份文件,這樣不管她結不結婚,他都可以使用她的錢。她不肯這樣做,他就一直煩她,直到她得了腦熱病,有六個星期瀕臨死亡。然後她終於好了,整個人瘦成了影子,美麗的頭髮被剪掉了;但這對她的年輕人沒有任何改變,他對她始終忠誠,忠誠得再沒有哪個男人能比。」

passages.original: “Ah,” said Holmes, “I think that what you have been good enough to tell us makes the matter fairly clear, and that I can deduce all that remains. Mr. Rucastle then, I presume, took to this system of imprisonment?”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,」福爾摩斯講,「我想你好心告訴我哋嘅,把事情講得相當清楚,我可以推論出剩下嘅一切。我想魯卡斯爾先生於是採取咗呢種囚禁嘅辦法?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,」福爾摩斯說,「我想你好心告訴我們的,把事情說得相當清楚,我可以推論出剩下的一切。我想魯卡斯爾先生於是採取了這種囚禁的辦法?」

passages.original: “Yes, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生。」

passages.original: “And brought Miss Hunter down from London in order to get rid of the disagreeable persistence of Mr. Fowler.”
passages.vernacular: 「並且把亨特小姐從倫敦帶下嚟,以擺脫弗勒先生令人不快嘅糾纏。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「並且把亨特小姐從倫敦帶下來,以擺脫弗勒先生令人不快的糾纏。」

passages.original: “That was it, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「就係咁樣,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是這樣,先生。」

passages.original: “But Mr. Fowler being a persevering man, as a good seaman should be, blockaded the house, and having met you succeeded by certain arguments, metallic or otherwise, in convincing you that your interests were the same as his.”
passages.vernacular: 「但弗勒先生係個有毅力嘅人,像一個好水手應該有嘅,封鎖咗房子,遇見你之後,憑某些論據,金屬嘅或其他嘅,成功地講服你,你嘅利益同佢嘅係一樣嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但弗勒先生是個有毅力的人,像一個好水手應該有的,封鎖了房子,遇見你之後,憑某些論據,金屬的或其他的,成功地說服你,你的利益和他的是一樣的。」

passages.original: “Mr. Fowler was a very kind-spoken, free-handed gentleman,” said Mrs. Toller serenely.
passages.vernacular: 「弗勒先生係個講話好客氣、出手大方嘅先生,」托勒太太平靜地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「弗勒先生是個說話非常客氣、出手大方的先生,」托勒太太平靜地說。

passages.original: “And in this way he managed that your good man should have no want of drink, and that a ladder should be ready at the moment when your master had gone out.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁樣佢設法讓你嘅好男人不缺酒,並且讓一架梯子喺你嘅主人出去嘅嗰一刻準備好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這樣他設法讓你的好男人不缺酒,並且讓一架梯子在你的主人出去的那一刻準備好。」

passages.original: “You have it, sir, just as it happened.”
passages.vernacular: 「您講對喇,先生,正是咁樣發生嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您說對了,先生,正是這樣發生的。」

passages.original: “I am sure we owe you an apology, Mrs. Toller,” said Holmes, “for you have certainly cleared up everything which puzzled us. And here comes the country surgeon and Mrs. Rucastle, so I think, Watson, that we had best escort Miss Hunter back to Winchester, as it seems to me that our locus standi now is rather a questionable one.”
passages.vernacular: 「托勒太太,我確信我哋欠您一個道歉,」福爾摩斯講,「因為您確實澄清咗所有使我哋困惑嘅事。鄉村外科醫生同魯卡斯爾太太嚟喇,所以我想,華生,我哋最好護送亨特小姐回溫徹斯特,因為喺我睇來,我哋而家嘅立足點相當可疑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「托勒太太,我確信我們欠您一個道歉,」福爾摩斯說,「因為您確實澄清了所有使我們困惑的事。鄉村外科醫生和魯卡斯爾太太來了,所以我想,華生,我們最好護送亨特小姐回溫徹斯特,因為在我看來,我們現在的立足點相當可疑。」

passages.original: And thus was solved the mystery of the sinister house with the copper beeches in front of the door. Mr. Rucastle survived, but was always a broken man, kept alive solely through the care of his devoted wife. They still live with their old servants, who probably know so much of Rucastle’s past life that he finds it difficult to part from them. Mr. Fowler and Miss Rucastle were married, by special license, in Southampton the day after their flight, and he is now the holder of a government appointment in the island of Mauritius. As to Miss Violet Hunter, my friend Holmes, rather to my disappointment, manifested no further interest in her when once she had ceased to be the centre of one of his problems, and she is now the head of a private school at Walsall, where I believe that she has met with considerable success.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣,門前有銅山毛櫸嘅不祥房子之謎就解開喇。魯卡斯爾活咗下嚟,但始終係個垮掉嘅人,僅憑佢忠誠妻子嘅照料維持住生命。佢哋仍同佢哋嘅老僕人住喺一起,佢哋大概對魯卡斯爾嘅過去生活知道得咁多,佢覺得好難同佢哋分開。弗勒先生同魯卡斯爾小姐喺佢哋逃走嘅第二天,憑特別許可證,喺南安普敦結咗婚,佢而家喺毛里求斯島擔任政府職務。至於維奧萊特·亨特小姐,我嘅朋友福爾摩斯,有點令我失望嘅係,一旦佢唔再係佢某個問題嘅中心,就冇對佢表現出進一步嘅興趣,佢而家係沃爾索爾一所私立學校嘅校長,我相信佢喺嗰度取得咗相當大嘅成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣,門前有銅山毛櫸的不祥房子之謎就解開了。魯卡斯爾活了下來,但始終是個垮掉的人,僅憑他忠誠妻子的照料維持著生命。他們仍與他們的老僕人住在一起,他們大概對魯卡斯爾的過去生活知道得那麼多,他覺得很難同他們分開。弗勒先生和魯卡斯爾小姐在他們逃走的第二天,憑特別許可證,在南安普敦結了婚,他現在在毛里求斯島擔任政府職務。至於維奧萊特·亨特小姐,我的朋友福爾摩斯,有點令我失望的是,一旦她不再是他某個問題的中心,就沒有對她表現出進一步的興趣,她現在是沃爾索爾一所私立學校的校長,我相信她在那裡取得了相當大的成功。
